docs.title: NL2SQL Platform Documentation
docs.text: This documentation describes the current runtime behavior of NL2SQL as implemented in code, including the parts that are not implemented yet. It is written for engineers and contributors who need a precise mental model of the architecture, contracts, and operational behavior. Where a page states a limitation, the limitation is the fact; nothing here describes intent.

docs.title: Problem this system solves
docs.text:
NL2SQL converts natural language requests into validated SQL across one or more datasources. The model emits a typed AST, never SQL text; the AST is checked against the retrieved schema and the caller's RBAC policy before any SQL is generated. The system is built for multi-datasource environments where correctness and inspectable failure matter more than conversational flexibility.

Model output itself is not reproducible; see Determinism for exactly which parts of a run are stable and which are not.

docs.title: Design philosophy
docs.text:
• Determinism where it is achievable: stable content-hashed IDs, sorted DAG layering, and a fixed graph topology. The LLM's output is not part of that guarantee.
  • Schema grounding: planning is constrained by a schema snapshot retrieved via structured chunks.
  • Explicit validation gates: logical validation enforces schema and RBAC constraints before execution.
  • Modularity: adapters, subgraphs, and executors are capability-driven and replaceable.
  • Bounded waiting: a global timeout bounds how long the caller waits for a run, not how long the work runs (on expiry the caller gets PIPELINE_TIMEOUT and the worker thread winds down in the background); each run carries a per-run cancellation token, and the graph itself runs in-process on a thread pool.
  • Observability: structured logging always; events on every run, which observers turn into logs, an audit log under storage.path and, with the otel extra, OpenTelemetry metrics and traces. See Observability Stack.

docs.title: Non-functional goals
docs.text:
• Reliability under partial failures (a circuit breaker on vector retrieval, SQL-agent retry semantics, errors returned as state rather than raised).
  • Extensibility via plugins and registries (datasources, subgraphs, executors).
  • Cost awareness (a row limit is baked into every generated statement; max_bytes is reported, not enforced).
  • Authorization at planning time (RBAC policy-based table access). The role is supplied by the caller, so the deployer owns authentication; see Security Model.

docs.title: High-level flow
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    User[User Query] --> Resolver[DatasourceResolverNode]
    Resolver --> Decomposer[DecomposerNode]
    Decomposer --> Router[Scan Layer Router]
    Router --> Subgraph[SQL Agent Subgraph]
    Subgraph --> Router
    Router --> Aggregator[EngineAggregatorNode]
    Aggregator --> Synthesizer[AnswerSynthesizerNode]

docs.title: Benchmark Results
docs.text: Recorded eval runs of the engine on the Chinook and routing suites. Generated by nl2sql eval publish from the records in benchmarks/; do not edit by hand. Grouped by mode and database, newest first; the runs 0.6's tier 2 recorded are mode full runs. Accuracy is execution accuracy (result_match and outcome, the measure 0.6 published), with its 95% Wilson interval. "Δ vs previous" is the change against the previous run of the same config, and how many cases flipped each way with McNemar's exact p-value on them: with a suite this size a few points either way is noise, so read the flips and the p-value, not the headline. Runs on another suite (@digest), another schema or, for mode full, other roles or curated answers on are not comparable and start a new series. See the Chinook suite and the routing suite.

docs.title: Core concepts
docs.text:
• ArtifactRef: Metadata reference to persisted query results (URI, backend, schema_version).
  • Chunk: Typed, vector-indexed schema slice used for retrieval (datasource, table, column, relationship).
  • ExecutionDAG: Deterministic logical DAG of scan/combine/post operations.
  • GraphState: Shared state across the control graph pipeline.
  • SchemaContract: Canonical schema structure for a datasource (tables, columns, foreign keys).
  • SchemaMetadata: Descriptive metadata and statistics for schema elements.
  • SchemaSnapshot: Pair of SchemaContract + SchemaMetadata.
  • SubQuery: Decomposed, datasource-scoped query intent from the decomposer.
  • Subgraph: LangGraph subgraph that handles a specific execution capability (e.g., SQL agent).
  • ResultFrame: Adapter response containing rows/columns, row_count, and error metadata.
  • IndexStore: the store that keeps the index entries, in a namespace per embedding model, and each datasource's live build pointer (chroma by default).
  • Retriever: the engine's MMR searches over the index store's live builds, pinned per run.
  • RBAC: Role-based access control enforcing datasource/table permissions.

docs.title: Supported Adapters
docs.text: The NL2SQL Platform supports a variety of datasources through specialized adapters. Each adapter is designed to handle the specific idiosyncrasies of its underlying database engine, from connection strings to catalog row estimates.

docs.title: SQL Adapters
docs.text:
We provide first-class support for the following SQL databases via SQLAlchemy.

Adapter Description Status PostgreSQL Full support including catalog row estimates, JSONB, and SSL. 🟢 Stable MySQL Support for 5.7+ and 8.0. Includes MAX_EXECUTION_TIME management. 🟢 Stable Microsoft SQL Server Enterprise support via pyodbc and T-SQL dialect. 🟡 Beta SQLite File-based local development. 🟢 Stable DuckDB In-process analytical engine over local files. 🟢 Stable

docs.title: Core Libraries
docs.text:
For developers building their own adapters, we provide detailed reference documentation for our core SDKs.

  • SDK Reference: The core interface (DatasourceAdapter, from nl2sql-sdk) that all adapters must implement.
  • SQLAlchemy Adapter Reference: The base class in the SDK (nl2sql_sdk.sqlalchemy.SQLAlchemyAdapter) for building SQL-based adapters.

docs.title: Missing your database?
docs.text: Can't find what you need? Check out the Building Adapters guide to see how to implement your own.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
All adapters are configured in the datasources section of nl2sql.yaml, usually one file per datasource in datasources/ (see Datasources).

# datasources/sales_db.yaml   (id defaults to the file name)
type: postgres
connection:
  host: "${env:DB_HOST}"
  port: 5432
  # ... see specific adapter docs for full reference

docs.title: Plugin / Adapter Architecture
docs.text: Adapters integrate NL2SQL with external datasources. Each adapter implements a protocol contract, is found by name in the registry (nl2sql.registry, built from Python entry points), and is registered in the DatasourceRegistry.

docs.title: Discovery and registration
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    Config["nl2sql.yaml: datasources"] --> Registry[DatasourceRegistry]
    Registry --> Lookup["Registry.load('adapter', type)"]
    Lookup --> EntryPoints["nl2sql.adapters entry points, or a class registered in code"]
    EntryPoints --> AdapterClass[Adapter Class]
    AdapterClass --> Validate["connection validated against connection_model"]
    Validate --> AdapterInstance["adapter_cls(id, connection, limits, folder=...)"]

docs.title: Core adapter contract
docs.text:
classDiagram
    class DatasourceAdapter {
        +interface_version 2
        +title
        +connection_model
        +capabilities() Set
        +get_dialect() str
        +default_schema() str
        +test_connection() ConnectionCheck
        +fetch_schema_snapshot(IndexScope) SchemaSnapshot
        +execute(AdapterRequest) ResultFrame

    }
    class AdapterRequest {
        +plan_type
        +payload
        +limits
    }
    class ResultFrame {
        +success
        +columns
        +rows
        +row_count
        +error
    }

See sdk.md for the authoritative adapter interface reference and required fields/methods.

docs.title: Capability-driven routing
docs.text:
Adapters expose capabilities (supports_sql, supports_bound_parameters, enforces_read_only, enforces_timeout). The registry reads them once, at registration, and DatasourceRegistry.supports(datasource_id, *capabilities) is the one check every consumer asks. It fails closed: an unknown datasource, or an adapter whose capabilities() is missing or raises, supports nothing. These capabilities drive:

  • Subgraph selection (resolve_subgraph() in routing).
  • Executor selection (ExecutorNode._supports_sql() and SqlExecutorService.validate_request(), gating the SQL executor).
flowchart TD
    Adapter[DatasourceAdapter] --> Caps["capabilities(), read once"]
    Caps --> Check["DatasourceRegistry.supports() (fails closed)"]
    Check --> Exec[ExecutorNode capability gate]
    Check --> Subgraph[resolve_subgraph()]
    Exec --> Service[SqlExecutorService]
    Subgraph --> Graph[Subgraph Selection]

docs.title: Multi-datasource routing
docs.text: The control graph can resolve multiple datasources for a single user query. DecomposerNode produces sub-queries scoped to individual datasources. Each sub-query is then routed to a subgraph that matches its adapter capabilities.

docs.title: Extensibility model
docs.text:
To add a new adapter:

  1. Implement DatasourceAdapter (or extend a base adapter), with a connection_model.
  2. Publish the adapter class as an nl2sql.adapters entry point, or register it in code (see Adding a New Adapter).
  3. Configure the datasource in the datasources section of nl2sql.yaml, with type: set to the adapter's name.
