docs.title: NL2SQL.run_query
docs.text:
Source: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/public_api.py, packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/api/query_api.py

Signature: run_query(question: str, *, datasource_id: Optional[str] = None, execute: bool = True, user_context: Optional[UserContext] = None, cancellation_token: Optional[CancellationToken] = None, plan: Optional[SuppliedPlan] = None, approvals: Optional[Sequence[Approval]] = None, clarify: bool = True, choice: Optional[ClarificationChoice] = None, answer: bool = True) -> QueryResult

Every argument after the question is keyword-only. run_query passes the runtime's artifact store to result_from_state, so each sub-query carries a capped row sample alongside its artifact reference.

Parameters: | name | type | required | meaning | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | question | str | yes | The question, in plain language. | | datasource_id | Optional[str] | no | Datasource override; otherwise resolved. | | execute | bool | no | Whether to execute SQL against datasource. | | user_context | Optional[UserContext] | no | RBAC context. Omitted (or None), the run starts with an empty UserContext, a caller with no roles, and RBAC treats it exactly as it treats any roles list it has no policy for. Pass one with a role to be granted anything. | | cancellation_token | Optional[CancellationToken] | no | A token (from nl2sql import CancellationToken) the caller cancels from another thread to stop the run. No further step and no further model call starts once it is cancelled; the step in flight finishes, and the result carries one CANCELLED error. The playground cancels it when the browser drops the request. | | plan | Optional[SuppliedPlan] | no | A plan the caller holds (from nl2sql import SuppliedPlan): a whole run (decomposition and plans), or a verified query (verified and verified_datasource_id). See Running a plan you hold. A datasource_id passed with it must be the datasource of every sub-query of the plan, or the call raises ValueError before anything runs. | | approvals | Optional[Sequence[Approval]] | no | Approvals for an earlier run's approvals_needed. See Approval. | | clarify | bool | no | Default True: a question the planner reads two or three ways ends needs_clarification with the options instead of running the most likely one. False runs the most likely reading and lists the others as assumptions. The prompts are the same either way. See Clarification. | | choice | Optional[ClarificationChoice] | no | The caller's pick from an earlier run's clarification (from nl2sql import ClarificationChoice: request, option_id). Ask the same question as the same caller: the chosen option's plan runs through the validator and the generator without routing, decomposing or planning. See Asking again. Not with plan or approvals. | | answer | bool | no | Default True. False skips the answer synthesizer: the run ends at the aggregator, final_answer is None and no model is called to write prose. With plan= that is a run with no model call at all, which is how a dashboard refresh re-runs a stored plan. The rows, the SQL and the explanation are the same. See Running without an answer. |

docs.title: Running a plan you hold
docs.text:
run_query(question, plan=SuppliedPlan(...)) runs a plan without routing or planning: the curated matcher, the datasource resolver, the decomposer and the planner's model call are skipped. A SuppliedPlan is a whole run, shaped on the pinned run the approval re-run uses, and is exactly one of:

  • decomposition (a DecomposerResponse, its combine groups and post-combine steps included) and plans, the plan of every sub-query keyed by its id; or
  • verified (a VerifiedRef: the verified query's id and its bound params) and verified_datasource_id.

SuppliedPlan.for_sub_query(sub_query, plan) is the common case, one sub-query run standalone. A plan missing for a sub-query, a plan for a sub-query that is not there, or both forms at once is a ValidationError when the SuppliedPlan is built. What is not skipped:

  • Every datasource of the decomposition is checked against user_context's scope, as the resolver would; a datasource the caller may not read ends the run with SECURITY_VIOLATION before anything runs.
  • The plan passes the plan.after hooks, the logical validator (so a table outside the caller's scope is refused) and the generator, like any plan.
  • It is never written to the plan cache, and a validator failure ends the sub-query with the validator's error: the refiner is never asked for a different plan. A database error is not retried either.

The sub-query's plan_source is "supplied". The question is still asked: the answer is written for it (unless answer=False). The same entry serves the approved re-run ("approved") and, in Wave B, a plan the asker chose ("chosen").

A supplied verified query is run by the curated matcher with its values, and it never falls back to a model run (a dashboard refresh uses no tokens). The call raises ValueError, before anything runs, when execute is False, no curated file with a verified query is loaded, or datasource_id is not verified_datasource_id. Where an approved pin would fall back to generation, a supplied one ends the run with an error and makes no model call: SECURITY_VIOLATION (the role may not read the datasource or a table the query reads), EXECUTION_FAILED (the query failed) or INVALID_STATE (an unknown query id, or a value that is missing or out of bounds).

docs.title: Running without an answer
docs.text:
run_query(question, plan=plan, answer=False, user_context=...) is a run with no model call. It is how a stored plan is re-run to refresh a chart: the graph is built without the answer synthesizer, so the run ends at the aggregator and final_answer is None (a stopped or timed-out run too: it has no stop text), timings has no answer_synthesizer and a streamed run emits no answer.delta. answer is recorded in the trace's request, so a replay runs the same graph. On its own, answer=False still routes, decomposes and plans with the models; pair it with plan= for a run that calls none.

Hooks still apply. While a hook is attached at answer.after, a model-free step runs it with final_answer=None, so a Deny withholds the rows and the result manifest as it does after an answer, and stream_query sends the result.manifest event only once the hook has allowed it.

docs.title: Approval
docs.text:
A hook at execute.before may answer NeedsApproval(reason). The run then ends with status: "needs_approval", the error NEEDS_APPROVAL and one ApprovalRequest per pending sub-query in approvals_needed: the question, the asker's user_id and tenant_id, the hook, the datasource, the run's decomposition, the sub-query and its plan (or, on the verified path, the verified query's id and values), the SQL and its SHA-256, the reason, and the roles that may approve (for display). Its id is a SHA-256 over a fixed list of those fields (REQUEST_ID_FIELDS: all but the reason and the roles), each without the values it holds at their defaults, so an edit shows, the same request always has the same id, and a field added in a later version keeps the ids of requests an app stored before.

An approver re-runs the question as the asker:

result = engine.run_query(question, user_context=asker)
if result.status == "needs_approval":
    approvals = [Approval(request=r, by=approver) for r in result.approvals_needed]
    result = engine.run_query(question, user_context=asker, approvals=approvals)

The engine, not the hook, checks each approval. An approval pins nothing when its request was edited (its id no longer matches), its sql is not the SQL of its sql_sha256 (the SQL an approver reads is the SQL whose hash is checked), it is for another question or another asker, its hook is not configured, or by holds none of that hook's approver roles. Then the run plans as usual and the hook asks again. Otherwise the re-run takes the request's decomposition and plan (plan_source: "approved", no resolver, decomposer or planner call) and validates and generates the SQL again. At execute.before the approval counts as the hook's Allow only when it is for that hook and datasource, the hash of the SQL just generated equals the request's (and, on the verified path, the values are the same), and by holds one of the hook's configured approver_roles (by default policies.admin_roles), never the roles the request lists. Then the next hook still runs. Anything else asks again: the run ends needs_approval with a new request. Nothing is stored, and an Approval is not signed and does not expire: it is trusted as far as the user_context a caller passes. See Hooks.

Returns: QueryResult, built from the pipeline graph state by result_from_state.

Raises: No exceptions are raised by run_query; errors are returned in QueryResult.errors.

Side Effects: - Pipeline execution, LLM calls, optional database execution.

Idempotency: - Not guaranteed; execution can depend on external systems and time.

docs.title: Execution Lifecycle
docs.text:
• Use the caller's CancellationToken, or create one per run, and install signal / Ctrl+X handlers bound to it.
  • Pass the graph a callback that raises RunCancelled at the next node start or model call once the token is cancelled.
  • Build LangGraph pipeline from build_graph.
  • Execute graph in thread pool with timeout.
  • On timeout/cancel, return PipelineError with appropriate ErrorCode.

docs.title: QueryResult
docs.text:
Source: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/api/query_api.py

Fields: | name | type | required | meaning | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | sub_queries | List[SubQueryResult] | no | One entry per decomposed sub-query. | | final_answer | Optional[Dict[str, Any]] | no | Answer synthesizer payload (summary, format_type, content, warnings, and truncated: True when a result was cut at the row limit). | | errors | List[Dict[str, Any]] | no | Pipeline errors (node, message, error_code, severity, provider, provider_response). provider and provider_response are set for a PROVIDER_* code and null otherwise; see provider failures. | | trace_id | str | no | Trace identifier. | | reasoning | List[Dict[str, Any]] | no | Reasoning events/logs. | | warnings | List[RunWarning] | no | What the answer should say without failing the run. See Warnings. | | artifact_refs | Dict[str, ArtifactRef] | no | Result artifact references keyed by execution node id. | | status | Optional[RunStatus] | no | "success", "plan_only", "error", "needs_approval", "stopped", "needs_clarification", or None when nothing ran and nothing failed. See below. | | timings | Dict[str, float] | no | Wall-clock seconds per graph node, plus LangGraph for the whole run. | | usage | QuestionUsage | no | LLM calls, tokens and model time per node and for the whole question. See below. | | trace_path | Optional[str] | no | Where this run's trace file was written, or None when TRACE_MODE did not write one. See Debugging a Run. | | truncated | bool | no | True when any sub-query's result reached its row limit, so rows may be missing. See sub_queries[].truncated. | | result_manifest | List[ResultSummary] | no | The run's saved results, one per terminal DAG node (node_id, columns, row_count, truncated, column_kinds): the manifest the aggregator writes beside them. column_kinds maps a column to its type category (number, text, temporal, boolean, other); the aggregator fills it from the saved file's column types, so engine.results.chart can choose a chart without reading rows. Never the rows; see Reading a run's saved results. Empty when nothing was saved. | | source | AnswerSource | no | Where the answer came from: type "verified" with the verified query's id, datasource_id and the params it ran with, or type "generated" with the other fields None. See Curated answers. | | stop | Optional[RunStop] | no | Set when status is "stopped": the limit the run reached (max_llm_calls or max_cost_usd), its configured value, and what was spent. | | approvals_needed | List[ApprovalRequest] | no | Set when status is "needs_approval": one request per sub-query a hook asked a person to approve, with the SQL, its SHA-256, the reason and the asker. Re-run the question with an Approval for each. | | clarification | Optional[ClarificationRequest] | no | Set when status is "needs_clarification": the phrase, and two or three readings, each a label, a validated plan and its explanation. See Clarification. | | explanation | Optional[Explanation] | no | The run's plan in plain English, rendered from the typed plans with no model call: one step per sub-query with its tables, joins, filters, groupings, measures, order, glossary terms, rules and assumptions; a verified answer is one step naming the verified query. Only steps that passed validation are explained (a success or plan_only run's, and the successful steps of a partly failed one); None when no step did, when a hook ended the run, or when it cannot be rendered. See Explanation. | | decomposition | Optional[DecomposerResponse] | no | The run's whole decomposition (sub-queries and combine groups), set on every run that has one and withheld, like the data, when a hook ended the run. With each sub-query's plan it rebuilds the run: a dashboard chart stores both (Wave C). |

errors holds the ERROR and CRITICAL entries, and the one INFO entry NEEDS_CLARIFICATION of a run that asked which reading was meant; WARNING-severity pipeline errors are appended to warnings as RunWarnings.

A sub-query that succeeded contributes nothing to errors: the errors of the attempts it recovered from are in warnings with detail.recovered true, and its warnings with an empty detail, each with its sub_query_id. The run trace and subgraph_outputs[<id>].errors keep every attempt's errors for debugging. A sub-query that failed without a blocking error of its own (it ended with no SQL on warnings alone) adds a MISSING_SQL error, so the run reports "error".

status is derived: "needs_approval" when a hook asked for approval (approvals_needed), "stopped" when the run reached a per-question limit (stop), "needs_clarification" when the run asked which reading was meant (clarification), otherwise "error" when any blocking error is present, otherwise "plan_only" when no sub-query produced rows or an artifact (an execute=False run), otherwise "success". A state with no sub-queries and no errors leaves it None. Hooks, approval and the caps that produce "needs_approval" and "stopped" arrive with release 0.7 (see Wave A).

Only a capped sample of the rows is inlined, in sub_queries[].rows. The full result set lives in artifact storage, addressed through artifact_refs; each combined result is listed in result_manifest and read back by the run's trace_id with the methods below.

docs.title: Clarification
docs.text:
When the planner reads a phrase of the question in more than one way that changes the result ("sales": the invoice total or the invoiced amount), it names the phrase and gives up to two other readings beside its most likely one. The clarifier step, after the logical validator, runs each other reading through the validator's own checks with the caller's scope and drops any that fail, so an option never names a table the caller cannot read, then merges readings that render to the same SQL. When two or three readings remain, the question has exactly one sub-query, clarify is on and settings.clarify.enabled is on (the default), the run ends before the generator: nothing is executed, aggregated or synthesized.

result = engine.run_query("What were sales last year?", user_context=ana)
if result.status == "needs_clarification":
    for option in result.clarification.options:
        print(option.id, option.label, option.explanation.text)

The result then has:

  • status "needs_clarification" and one errors entry, NEEDS_CLARIFICATION (INFO, never retried);
  • final_answer a fixed sentence: "This question can be read more than one way. Choose one: Sales: total of invoice total; Invoiced amount.";
  • clarification, a ClarificationRequest (from nl2sql import ClarificationRequest): id (SHA-256 of every other field, 32 hex, so a mixed-up or edited request is recognised), question (as passed, before any run.before hook), asker_user_id, asker_tenant_id, phrase, datasource_id, schema_version, knowledge_digest, sub_query and options;
  • each option a ClarificationOption: id ("a" is the most likely reading, then "b", "c"), label, plan (the plan as JSON) and explanation (an ExplainedStep, as in Explanation). The planner gives no label for its most likely reading, so a is named by the glossary term its plan reads, else its first measure, filter or table;
  • explanation None, and the sub-query's status "needs_clarification" with no SQL: nothing ran, so the options carry the explanations.

Otherwise the most likely reading runs, and the readings that passed the checks are listed as assumptions in its explanation step ("'sales' was read one way; it could also mean Invoiced amount."). That happens with clarify=False, with more than one sub-query, when only one reading passed, and on a re-plan after an attempt already executed (a sanity check's retry), so the answer is never the flagged attempt's rows. clarification.requested (sub_query_id, phrase, options) is published on the engine's bus when a run asks; it is an operator event, not on the stream. Evals run with clarification off, so a case measures the most likely reading; a case may expect clarify, and the clarify suite does.

docs.title: Asking again
docs.text:
choice = ClarificationChoice(request=result.clarification, option_id="b")
answer = engine.run_query("What were sales last year?", user_context=ana, choice=choice)

The re-ask is stateless: the caller holds the request and sends it back, and nothing is stored. The engine checks, before anything runs:

Check Failure The request's id is the hash of its content; its question is the question as passed now (before any run.before hook); its asker is this caller; option_id is one of its options CLARIFICATION_INVALID (CRITICAL). The id is an unkeyed hash, a check against mixed-up requests, not tamper evidence: the validator, run on the chosen plan with the caller's scope, is the guard against an edited plan The datasource is in the caller's scope, the request's schema_version is the live one and its knowledge_digest the live glossary's CLARIFICATION_STALE (ERROR, never retried): the data or the glossary changed since the options were offered; ask again No approvals come with it CLARIFICATION_INVALID: pass the approval alone

A refused choice ends the run with that one error (status "error") and calls no model. A plan or a pinned passed with a choice is a ValueError at the call. Otherwise the run enters at Wave A's pinned entry with one sub-query, standalone: no resolver, decomposer or datasources.after. The planner step returns the chosen plan with plan_source "chosen" and no model call; then it is an ordinary run: plan.after, the validator with the caller's scope, the generator, execute.before. A chosen plan is one person's reading and is never cached. The sub-query's plan_source is "chosen" and its explanation says "You chose: Invoiced amount".

If a hook (the cost guard, say) answers needs_approval on the chosen plan, the run ends needs_approval with an ApprovalRequest for the chosen plan; the approver's re-run passes approvals only.

engine.knowledge.save_choice(choice, user_context=ana) files the pick as a term proposal, so an admin can make the phrase part of the glossary: see the review queue.

docs.title: Warnings
docs.text:
QueryResult.warnings is a list of RunWarning (from nl2sql import RunWarning):

name type meaning code str An ErrorCode value, such as VALUE_NOT_FOUND, JOIN_FAN_OUT, ALL_NULL_COLUMN, JOIN_KEY_UNCONVERTED, RESULT_TRUNCATED or HOOK_DENIED; CURATED_FALLBACK when a verified query failed and the question was generated instead. node str The node that found it. message str What the answer says. sub_query_id Optional[str] The sub-query it is about, when it is about one. detail Dict[str, Any] What a program may branch on: recovered: true for an earlier attempt's error a retry replaced; the column, counts and type of a JOIN_KEY_UNCONVERTED. Never result rows or sample values.

The answer sanity checks (a missing filter value, a join that repeated the rows an aggregate counted, a column with no value) add theirs, and the answer synthesizer says them; see the executor's sanity checks. settings.pipeline.sanity_checks: false turns those checks off.

0.7 changed this shape: a warning was a dict with error_code and severity, and is now a RunWarning with code, and detail.recovered where severity said ERROR. A run's state is never kept across an upgrade (a run that ended needs_approval is asked again, not resumed; see Wave A, D10), so no older warning is ever read back.

docs.title: Explanation
docs.text:
QueryResult.explanation answers "why this answer" for a business reader. It is rendered by nl2sql/explain/ when the result is assembled (result_from_state), from each sub-query's typed plan, the knowledge its prompt carried (sub_queries[].knowledge_used), the planner's readings it did not ask about, the row cap and the run's warnings. No model is called, and the same plan and knowledge always give the same words. The answer synthesizer is not given it: the explanation describes the query, the answer describes the rows.

Only a sub-query that passed validation is explained. A plan the validator or a hook refused, and a dropped sub-query, get no step: their tables, and their glossary descriptions, would confirm what the refusal withholds. A run a hook ended (HOOK_DENIED, HOOK_FAILED, NEEDS_APPROVAL, COST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED) has no explanation, as it has no rows. An explanation never fails a run: one that cannot be rendered (a stored plan an older version wrote, say) is None, and the error is logged.

The glossary that names tables and tells a glossary join from a declared key is the caller's: every caller of result_from_state (run_query, stream_query, evals, trace replay and the trace itself) passes the knowledge filtered by the caller's scope (caller_knowledge in nl2sql/knowledge/scope.py), so a description that mentions a table the caller cannot read never reaches the explanation. It is the knowledge and snapshot the run pinned (run_with_graph hands back its pinned runtime as pinned_runtime), so a reload during the run does not change the words.

Explanation has steps (one ExplainedStep per sub-query, in the decomposition's order) and combined: how the steps' results were put together ("The results of a and b were joined on country."), or None for a single step. An ExplainedStep:

name type meaning sub_query_id Optional[str] The sub-query it explains. datasource_id str Its datasource. source str Where the plan came from: generated (the planner), cache, supplied (run_query(plan=...)), approved, chosen (a clarification pick) or verified (a verified query, with no plan). tables List[str] Each table, qualified as the plan names it, with its glossary description's first clause when there is one: "Invoice: one row per customer invoice (glossary)". joins List[str] Each join and the relationship it used: "each InvoiceLine to its Invoice, on InvoiceId (declared key)", or (glossary) for a join the glossary declares. filters List[str] Each condition of the WHERE, then each of the HAVING as "for each group, ...". groupings List[str] "by Customer country". measures List[str] Each aggregate the plan selects, by its alias: "revenue: total of InvoiceLine unit price times InvoiceLine quantity". order Optional[str] "highest revenue first, top 10". terms List[TermUse] The glossary terms sent with the step whose columns the plan reads: term, definition, source. rules List[str] The business rules sent with the step, by text. assumptions List[str] What the answer took for granted, all deterministic: a reading not chosen when an ambiguity was not asked about; a filter value the column did not have ('Brasil' is not in Customer country; 'Brazil' was used instead. when the final plan filters on a suggested value, else ...; the question was planned again.); the sanity checks' warnings (VALUE_NOT_FOUND, JOIN_FAN_OUT, ALL_NULL_COLUMN, JOIN_KEY_UNCONVERTED), and the row cap when the result was cut. planner_note Optional[str] The plan's own reasoning: model text, kept apart and labelled as the planner's. It appears in no other field. text str The step in two to four sentences: what it shows, what it reads and filters, which groups it keeps, and its order.

Names are the glossary description's first clause when there is one, else the name split into words (InvoiceDate on Invoice is "Invoice date"); a table the plan reads twice is named with its alias ("Track (t3)"). Each expression kind has a phrase (= "is", IN "is one of", LIKE "matches", IS NULL "is empty", SUM "total of", COUNT with distinct "number of different", DATE_PART('year', d) "the year of d", a case "depending on: ..."); a function without one is written as its name and arguments.

result_from_state(state, ..., knowledge=None) takes knowledge, a mapping from datasource id to its glossary (DatasourceKnowledge) as the caller's scope filters it; without it, names are the split names and every join is a declared key. A run on the Chinook suite's gold plans renders as the files in packages/nl2sql/tests/unit/explain/golden/, which are compared on every test run, so a change to the wording is a reviewed diff. Design: Wave B, section 8.

docs.title: NL2SQL.stream_query
docs.text:
Source: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/api/query_api.py, step events in packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/events.py, the allow-list in packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/events/catalog.py

Signature: stream_query(question: str, *, datasource_id: Optional[str] = None, execute: bool = True, user_context: Optional[UserContext] = None, cancellation_token: Optional[CancellationToken] = None, plan: Optional[SuppliedPlan] = None, approvals: Optional[Sequence[Approval]] = None, clarify: bool = True, choice: Optional[ClarificationChoice] = None, answer: bool = True) -> Iterator[Event]

The same run as run_query, with the same parameters, yielded as it happens: the run's own events on the engine's bus (Events), from the caller-safe allow-list. nl2sql run shows its live progress from them.

from nl2sql import NL2SQL, UserContext

engine = NL2SQL.from_config("nl2sql.yaml")
for event in engine.stream_query("Which genre sells the most tracks?",
                                 user_context=UserContext(roles=["admin"])):
    if event.name == "node.finished":
        print(f"{event.data['node']} took {event.data['seconds']} s")
    elif event.name == "answer.delta" and event.data["field"] == "summary":
        print(event.data["text"], end="", flush=True)
    elif event.name == "run.finished":
        result = event.data["result"]   # run_query's QueryResult, as JSON

An Event (nl2sql.Event, from nl2sql_sdk.events) has a name, at (UTC), the run's trace_id, its tenant_id and a JSON-ready data dict; event.sse() is the event as one Server-Sent Event (event: <name>, and the whole event as JSON on the data line), which is how nl2sql-api and the playground send it.

name data when run.started question, user_id, tenant_id, roles, datasource_id, execute The run began. Always first. node.started node, sub_query_id A pipeline step began (the SQL agent's steps once per sub-query, and again on a retry). sub_query_id is None outside a sub-query. node.finished node, sub_query_id, seconds, ok The step ended; ok is False when it raised. result.manifest results The aggregator saved the results: results is the run's result_manifest and the event's trace_id its request_id, so engine.results.page can be called before the answer is written. answer.delta field, text The next piece of final_answer.summary or final_answer.content, as the answer model writes it. sanity.flagged, run.limit_reached see Events Published by the sanity checks and the caps when they arrive (Wave A's S1 and E3). run.finished the run's summary (status, duration_s, usage, error_codes, source, datasources, tables, result_manifest, user_id, roles) plus result The run finished. result is exactly what run_query returns, as JSON; it is on the stream's copy only, never on the bus. A refusal, a provider failure, a timeout or a cancel is a run.finished with status: "error", as run_query returns it. run.failed message, error_code The run could not start or finish (an exception outside the pipeline, such as a missing API key when the graph is built).

Every stream ends in exactly one run.finished or run.failed. Operator events (policy.decision, hook.decision, llm.call, plan_cache.lookup) are never on it: a denial would tell a denied caller which table exists, and the rest are operator data. An operator reads them with engine.events.subscribe.

How it works:

  • The run goes on a thread of its own, started on the first next(); the caller's context goes with it, so request-scoped keys (nl2sql.llm.request_key) reach the graph as they do in run_query.
  • Every run (streamed or not) has a RunScope, and QueryAPI.open_scope attaches a RunEvents to it: a LangChain callback the graph gets with the scope's callbacks, which publishes through the scope. A node's own run (its name is its langgraph_node) is a node.started / node.finished; the runnables inside a node are not events. The aggregator's end publishes result.manifest. The stream subscribes to its scope's events from the allow-list (nl2sql.events.STREAM_EVENTS), so it yields exactly what the bus carries, in publish order, and then its own run.finished with the result.
  • run_with_graph(stream_answer=True) asks the answer synthesizer to stream: its chain is streaming_structured (nl2sql.llm.wires) instead of structured, the same request with stream on. Each piece of the answer's tool call reaches on_llm_new_token; RunEvents parses the arguments so far as partial JSON and publishes what summary and content gained as answer.delta. The pieces are joined into one message before the parser sees it, so the answer, and the token usage the call reports, are the unstreamed call's. On the Anthropic wire the joined message gets the same tool-call repair as an unstreamed one.
  • Closing the iterator before the last event (a client that went away) cancels the run's token, so it stops before its next step or model call.

Token by token, per wire: both the OpenAI wire (OpenAI, OpenRouter, Ollama, any OpenAI-compatible endpoint) and the Anthropic wire stream the answer's forced tool call, so the answer streams on every provider; how finely is the provider's choice, and one that sends the whole answer at once gives one answer.delta per field. The other model steps return a typed object the next step needs whole, and are not streamed. FakeLLMServer streams both wires, a word at a time, so replay mode and the keyless tests stream too.

docs.title: Reading a run's saved results
docs.text:
The aggregator saves each terminal result of a run as <tenant_id>/<request_id>/result_<node_id>.parquet and writes manifest.json beside them (see Artifact Store → The result manifest). While a hook is attached at answer.after, the manifest is written only once those hooks allowed, so a run's results are not readable before that, and never for a run a hook ended (What withholding guarantees). engine.results reads them back by the run's trace_id (its run_id, the request_id of the REST routes). They read lazily from the parquet file: a page reads only its slice, and the CSV export reads and yields a slice at a time (CSV_CHUNK_ROWS, 10,000 rows), so neither holds the whole result in memory.

method returns meaning results.manifest(run_id, tenant_id=None) ResultManifest request_id and results: List[ResultSummary], the same entries as QueryResult.result_manifest. results.page(run_id, result_id, offset=0, limit=100, tenant_id=None) ResultPage Rows offset to offset + limit of the result whose node_id is result_id. limit above MAX_RESULT_PAGE_SIZE (1,000) is cut to it, and the page's limit says so. A page past the end has no rows. next_offset is where the next page starts, None at the end. A negative offset or a limit below 1 raises ValueError. results.csv(run_id, result_id, tenant_id=None) Iterator[bytes] The whole result as UTF-8 CSV, header first, one chunk per slice. The ids are checked before the iterator is returned, so a missing result raises before any byte is sent.

ResultPage has request_id, result_id, columns, rows (rows[i] is row offset + i), offset, limit, total_rows and next_offset.

Scope: results are read from one tenant's folder, tenant_id or else the engine's own TENANT_ID, the tenant every run of this engine writes under. Each of these raises ResultNotFound (a LookupError, exported from nl2sql): an unknown run_id, a run in another tenant's folder, a result_id the run's manifest does not list, and an id that is not a plain token (letters, digits, _, -; at most 128 characters). Ids are checked before any path is built, and the parquet path is rendered from the artifact template, never read from the manifest, so no id reaches a file outside the run's folder. Nothing else guards a result yet: any caller who knows a trace_id can read it.

result = engine.run_query("List every genre.", user_context=UserContext(roles=["admin"]))
[saved] = result.result_manifest                   # node_id, columns, row_count, truncated
page = engine.results.page(result.trace_id, saved.node_id, offset=0, limit=20)
with open("genres.csv", "wb") as out:
    for chunk in engine.results.csv(result.trace_id, saved.node_id):
        out.write(chunk)

nl2sql-api serves these as GET /api/v1/query/{request_id}/results/{result_id} and .../{result_id}.csv; the playground serves the same two under /api/query/....

docs.title: SubQueryResult
docs.text: name type required meaning id str no Sub-query identifier. intent str no Semantic intent of the sub-query. sql str no SQL generated for the sub-query (subgraph_outputs[<id>].sql_draft). datasource_id str no Datasource the sub-query targets. schema_version str no Schema version used for planning. plan Optional[Dict[str, Any]] no The validated PlanModel, dumped. validation List[ValidationCheck] no name, passed, message per validation gate. rows Optional[RowSample] no Capped row sample; None when nothing executed or the artifact could not be read. status str no "success" or "error" for this sub-query, from its final attempt: "success" when it ended with SQL and, if executed, a result; otherwise "error". A retry that recovers reports "success". "dropped" when a hook denied it with scope="sub_query": the run went on without it. retry_count int no Plan/SQL refinement attempts made. plan_source "llm" \| "cache" \| "verified" \| "supplied" \| "approved" \| "chosen" no "cache" when the plan came from the plan cache (no planner LLM call; still validated, generated and executed), "verified" when a verified query answered (no plan; sql is the verified query's own), "supplied" for a plan passed as run_query(plan=...), "approved" for an approval's pinned plan ("chosen" is reserved for Wave B), otherwise "llm". Only an "llm" plan is ever cached. See Determinism → The plan cache. row_cap Optional[int] no The row limit that bounded this sub-query's SQL (the datasource's row_limit, bounded by RESULT_ROW_LIMIT), or None when the plan's own LIMIT was smaller. truncated bool no True when the result has row_cap rows: it was cut at the limit and may be missing rows. A result of exactly row_cap rows may be whole; it is counted as cut. knowledge_used Optional[KnowledgeUsed] no The glossary terms and rules this sub-query's prompts carried, and what the block's cap dropped. Only items within the caller's scope: none names a table the caller cannot read. Filled by the schema retriever (Wave B's K2); None when no term or rule matched, and for a plan served from the plan cache, which sent no prompt. estimate Optional[Estimate] no The database's estimate of the rows this sub-query reads, when the cost rule asked for one. rows is what the query is expected to read; cost is the database's own units, for display. None when the cost rule asked for none: no policies.cost limit applies to the caller, or the run did not reach execute.before. Present too when the rule then refused or asked for approval.

docs.title: RowSample
docs.text: name type required meaning columns List[str] no Column names, in result order. rows List[List[Any]] no At most sample_rows rows (default 50). total_rows int no Row count of the whole result, not of the sample.

docs.title: State mapping
docs.text:
result_from_state normalises the raw graph state (LangGraph may return dicts or model instances for nested values):

QueryResult field Graph state source sub_queries[].sql subgraph_outputs[<id>].sql_draft sub_queries[].id / .intent / .datasource_id / .schema_version subgraph_outputs[<id>].sub_query sub_queries[].plan / .validation / .status / .retry_count / .plan_source / .row_cap / .truncated subgraph_outputs[<id>] usage.plan_cache_hits count of sub_queries[] with plan_source == "cache" sub_queries[].rows artifact_store.read_result_frame(subgraph_outputs[<id>].artifact) final_answer answer_synthesizer_response.final_answer source verified_match (set by the curated matcher on a verified answer; absent means generated) errors, reasoning, warnings, trace_id, artifact_refs, timings, usage top-level state

errors are projected onto a client-safe summary; stack_trace and details are deliberately not exposed.

result_from_state(state, artifact_store=None, sample_rows=50) reads rows only when an artifact store is supplied. A failed read is not fatal: rows stays None and a warning is appended.

timings is collected by NodeTimingCallback (packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/timing.py), a LangChain callback handler that run_with_graph always attaches. It keys on metadata["langgraph_node"] where LangGraph provides it, so the keys are node names such as ast_planner, logical_validator, generator and executor.

docs.title: Usage: tokens, calls and model time
docs.text:
usage is collected by TokenUsageCallback (packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/services/callbacks/token_handler.py), which run_with_graph attaches to every run, so the Python API, the REST API, the CLI and the demo playground all report it. It is also filled in, with whatever had been recorded, on a timed-out or cancelled run.

QuestionUsage:

name type meaning total UsageTotals The whole question. nodes Dict[str, UsageTotals] Keyed by graph node: datasource_resolver (the answerability check), decomposer, ast_planner, refiner, answer_synthesizer. calls List[LLMCallUsage] Every model call in order, with its node and model. plan_cache_hits int Sub-queries whose plan came from the plan cache. A hit makes no planner call, so it adds no ast_planner calls or tokens; a question answered entirely from the cache has no ast_planner entry in nodes.

UsageTotals:

name type meaning calls int LLM calls. The planner and refiner run once per retry, so a sub-query retried once shows ast_planner.calls == 2. input_tokens Optional[int] Prompt tokens, including cached ones. cached_input_tokens Optional[int] Input tokens served from the provider's prompt cache (a subset of input_tokens). cache_write_input_tokens Optional[int] Input tokens written to the prompt cache (Anthropic reports these; OpenAI does not, so it is null there). output_tokens Optional[int] Completion tokens, including reasoning ones. reasoning_tokens Optional[int] Reasoning ("thinking") tokens (a subset of output_tokens). total_tokens Optional[int] As the provider reports it; input + output if it does not. latency_s float Seconds spent waiting on the model, summed over calls. The node's wall-clock time, which includes its non-LLM work, is in timings. cost Optional[float] Dollars, when every call counted here has a cost; otherwise null. Each call is priced from llm.prices, then the dated price table: cache reads at cached_input, cache writes at cache_write (Claude's are 1.25x input), the rest of input_tokens at input and output_tokens at output; see Prices.

A token count in UsageTotals is the sum of what the calls reported, and null when no call reported it: an unknown count is never 0.

LLMCallUsage has the same token fields plus node, model (the model the provider says served the call, e.g. gpt-4o-2024-08-06), latency_s, cost, usage_reported and error.

Tokens are read by the adapter of the wire type that served the call (read_usage in nl2sql/llm/wires/openai.py or anthropic.py), picked by the model_provider the client stamps on the response; TokenUsageCallback only asks it. Both read LangChain's AIMessage.usage_metadata (input_token_details.cache_read, input_token_details.cache_creation, output_token_details.reasoning) into the same fields, and differ where their providers differ, as below. A detail the provider did not report is null, never 0. A call whose result carried no usage at all is recorded with every count null and usage_reported: false; a failed call is recorded the same way, with its latency and error.

For OpenAI through langchain-openai (verified against the pinned 1.6.x by packages/nl2sql/tests/unit/test_fake_llm_server.py): prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_tokens, prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens and completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens all arrive. OpenAI's chat completions API reports no cache-write count, so cache_write_input_tokens is null there.

For Claude through langchain-anthropic (provider: anthropic; verified against the fake Anthropic endpoint by packages/nl2sql/tests/unit/test_llm_wire_contract.py, which runs the same usage tests against both wires), Anthropic's usage maps as follows:

Anthropic usage field here cache_read_input_tokens cached_input_tokens cache_creation_input_tokens, or its per-TTL split cache_creation.ephemeral_5m_input_tokens + ephemeral_1h_input_tokens cache_write_input_tokens input_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens input_tokens output_tokens output_tokens

Anthropic's own input_tokens counts only the uncached tail of the prompt; langchain-anthropic adds the cache reads and writes back, so input_tokens here is the whole prompt, counted once, and both cache fields stay subsets of it. When the write is reported per TTL, langchain-anthropic sets the generic cache_creation detail to 0 and puts the tokens under the TTL keys, which are summed here.

Cost is (input - cached - cache_write) * input_price + cached * cached_input_price + cache_write * cache_write_price + output * output_price, per million tokens; a cache count the provider did not report is not split out of input. Prices are looked up in llm.prices by the served model name, then by the configured one, and only then in the dated table by either, by exact match only, so a gpt-4o price never prices gpt-4o-mini. A call with no price, or no input or output count, has a null cost. See Prices.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: engine.results: the results a run saved, read back by its trace_id, and the chart their data is drawn as.

docs.title: Key Modules
docs.text:
• packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/api/results_api.py (ResultsAPI, internal)
  • packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/execution/artifacts/results.py (ResultManifest, ResultPage, ResultReader)
  • packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/charts/spec.py (ChartSpec)

docs.title: Public Surface
docs.text:
Method What it does manifest(run_id, tenant_id=None) -> ResultManifest Which results the run saved: per result its node id, columns, row count and truncated flag. Never the rows. page(run_id, result_id, offset=0, limit=100, tenant_id=None) -> ResultPage Rows offset to offset + limit of one saved result, read lazily from its parquet file. csv(run_id, result_id, tenant_id=None) -> Iterator[bytes] The whole result as UTF-8 CSV, a slice at a time. chart(result, result_id=None, *, kind=None, tenant_id=None) -> ChartSpec The chart the result is drawn as (Charts): a ChartSpec chosen by rules from the saved result's column kinds, with no model call. result is a QueryResult (a single sub-query's plan refines the kinds, and its intent titles the chart) or a trace_id. result_id may be left out when the run saved one result. kind forces line, bar, big_number or table; one the data cannot draw is a ValueError naming those it can. Raises ResultNotFound as page does, and also when a QueryResult has an empty result_manifest (a run a hook withheld) or its result_id is not in it: the chart is drawn only from results the caller was given. A trace_id alone is checked like page, by tenant and run id; a run a hook withheld is ResultNotFound for every read, as manifest, page and csv also raise it.

The first three are described with run_query in Query API.

docs.title: REST API (FastAPI)
docs.text: This section documents the nl2sql-api FastAPI package that exposes the core engine over HTTP. Implementation lives in packages/api/src/nl2sql_api/.

docs.title: Application lifecycle
docs.text:
Source: packages/api/src/nl2sql_api/main.py

  • lifespan configures logging, loads the .env next to nl2sql.yaml (never overriding a variable already set), builds one engine with NL2SQL.from_config() (the file NL2SQL_CONFIG names, else ./nl2sql.yaml) and calls engine.check() before it serves. A required datasource that fails, or no datasource ready at all, raises EngineNotReady and the server does not start; an optional one that fails leaves it serving the others. The engine is stored in app.state.engine and closed at shutdown. Logs are text, or JSON lines with NL2SQL_LOG_FORMAT=json.
  • Retention: the lifespan calls engine.storage.purge() once before it serves and then once a day (purge_daily, every PURGE_INTERVAL_S seconds), so traces and results older than their store's max_age_days are deleted (see Storage → Retention). A failed purge is logged and never stops the server.
  • The package imports the engine only through the top-level nl2sql namespace (from nl2sql import NL2SQL, QueryResult, UserContext, configure_logging, ...), never an engine submodule. packages/api/tests/test_architecture.py enforces it.
  • Routers are included under /api/v1.
  • CORS is restricted to the origins in api.cors_origins (see CORS origins); with none configured, no cross-origin browser access is allowed.

docs.title: Dependency injection
docs.text:
Source: packages/api/src/nl2sql_api/dependencies.py

  • get_engine(request) returns the singleton NL2SQL instance.
  • Service providers (DatasourceService, QueryService, LLMService, IndexingService, HealthService) are created per-request with the engine.
  • get_user_context(request) (in nl2sql_api/auth.py) returns the caller's UserContext; see Caller role.
  • require_admin(request) (same module) guards the routes that change datasources, LLMs or the index; see Admin routes.

docs.title: Interactive docs
docs.text:
FastAPI serves Swagger UI at /docs, ReDoc at /redoc and the OpenAPI schema at /openapi.json, with a summary, description and tag on every route. Start the server on a config:

NL2SQL_CONFIG=nl2sql-demo/nl2sql.yaml nl2sql-api --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000   # then open http://localhost:8000/docs

docs.title: API Index
docs.text: API Router Path Purpose Health routes/health.py Liveness/readiness checks. Query routes/query.py Execute natural language queries, whole or streamed as Server-Sent Events; page through or download a run's saved result. Datasource routes/datasource.py Manage datasource configs. LLM routes/llm.py Replace the LLM (PUT /settings/llm) and inspect each agent's model. Indexing routes/indexing.py Index management and status.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
FastAPI routers wrap most failures in HTTPException(status_code=500, detail=str(e)). Datasource and delete endpoints, and GET /api/v1/llm/{agent}, map ValueError to HTTP 404. PUT /api/v1/settings/llm answers a config error as HTTP 422 with its text.

POST /api/v1/query is the exception: pipeline errors are returned as a normal HTTP 200 inside QueryResponse.errors, and an unexpected failure returns a generic HTTP 500 with the traceback logged server-side rather than returned. POST /api/v1/datasource does the same: its exception can carry a connection string, password included, so the response says only that it failed and the cause goes to the server log.

Route handlers that call blocking engine code are declared with def rather than async def, so Starlette runs them in its threadpool instead of blocking the event loop.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: The REST API is configured by the same nl2sql.yaml as the engine. Beyond the runtime server options in nl2sql_api.server (--host, --port, --reload), its own settings are the api section of that file (see The api section), and the admin roles are policies.admin_roles. The engine validates the api section and never reads it.

docs.title: CORS origins
docs.text:
api.cors_origins lists the browser origins allowed to call the API cross-origin. Each entry is a full origin (scheme, host and, if non-default, port).

# api.yaml
cors_origins: [https://bi.corp.example, http://localhost:3000]

With one or more origins configured, only those origins are accepted and credentialed requests (cookies, Authorization) are permitted.

With none, no origins are allowed and credentials are disabled. That is the intended default, not a misconfiguration: a browser page served from another origin cannot call the API until you opt it in. The list is read from the engine's config, which is loaded at startup, so changing it requires restarting the server.

This setting governs the browser same-origin policy only. Non-browser clients -- curl, server-side callers, the Python SDK -- do not send an Origin header and are unaffected by it; use authentication and network controls to restrict those.

docs.title: Caller role
docs.text:
The engine enforces RBAC; the API only decides which role a request carries. It does not authenticate callers, and it never takes the role from the request body unless a dev flag says so. The get_user_context dependency reads, first match wins:

api key Role source role_header The name of a header a trusted proxy sets, e.g. X-NL2SQL-Role. Comma-separated values are several roles. Configure it only when the proxy authenticates the caller and overwrites the header on every request; otherwise any client can pick its own role. role One static role for every request, e.g. admin for a single-tenant deployment or the demo. trust_body_role true takes user_context from the request body. For local testing only: any client can choose any role. The server logs a warning at startup when it is on.

With no role from any of them, POST /api/v1/query and the result routes answer HTTP 401 with a message naming these keys; the engine never runs.

# api.yaml for the demo: every request runs as admin.
role: admin

# api.yaml behind an authenticating proxy that sets X-NL2SQL-Role.
role_header: X-NL2SQL-Role

This is a seam, not an auth provider: to integrate one, override the get_user_context dependency (app.dependency_overrides[get_user_context] = ...) or put the provider in the proxy.

docs.title: Admin routes
docs.text:
The routes that change the running process need an admin role, checked by the require_admin dependency in nl2sql_api/auth.py:

  • POST /api/v1/datasource and DELETE /api/v1/datasource/{datasource_id}
  • PUT /api/v1/settings/llm
  • POST /api/v1/index/{datasource_id}, POST /api/v1/index-all and DELETE /api/v1/index
Key Default Meaning policies.admin_roles [admin] The roles that may call the admin routes.

The roles come from the same sources as Caller role. A request whose roles include one in policies.admin_roles is let through; one with roles but none of them admin is HTTP 403; one with no role is HTTP 401.

With none of api.role_header, api.role or api.trust_body_role set, admin routes answer only clients on loopback (127.0.0.1, ::1) and return HTTP 403 to everyone else, with a message naming the keys to set. A fresh local install can still register and index datasources, and a port published by mistake does not hand them out. Two consequences:

  • In Docker, a request through a published port arrives from the bridge gateway, not loopback, so admin routes need a role setting there.
  • A reverse proxy on the same host makes every request look like loopback. Behind one, configure api.role_header.

The read-only routes (/health, /ready, GET /datasource, GET /llm, which never returns API keys, and GET /index/status) need no role.

# The proxy sets X-NL2SQL-Role; only "ops" may change datasources and the index.
# api.yaml
role_header: X-NL2SQL-Role
# policies.yaml (with the roles)
admin_roles: [ops]

docs.title: Request/Response Models
docs.text: Source: packages/api/src/nl2sql_api/models/datasource.py

docs.title: DatasourceRequest
docs.text: field type required meaning config Dict[str, Any] yes One datasource, in the shape of a datasources entry of nl2sql.yaml: id, type, connection, and optionally description, limits, preferred_tables, sample_questions, required. See Datasources.

docs.title: DatasourceResponse
docs.text: field type required meaning success bool yes Operation status. message str yes Result message. datasource_id Optional[str] no Datasource ID.

docs.title: POST /api/v1/datasource
docs.text:
Source: packages/api/src/nl2sql_api/routes/datasource.py

Request model: DatasourceRequest

Response model: DatasourceResponse

Admin only: see Admin routes.

Execution flow: - Validates config as a Datasource and delegates to engine.datasources.add(...): the adapter is built (not connected) and the datasource joins engine.config. Nothing is written to the config files and nothing is indexed.

Errors: - No role -> HTTP 401; a role not in policies.admin_roles -> HTTP 403. - A failure to add -> HTTP 500 with a generic message. The exception, which can hold the connection string, is logged server-side and never returned.

docs.title: GET /api/v1/datasource
docs.text:
Response: {"datasources": [...]}, engine.datasources.list(): every configured datasource with its id, type, description, status (ready, failed with a reason, or unchecked), capabilities and connection with every secret masked. No role needed.

{"datasources": [
  {"id": "shop", "type": "postgres", "description": "Orders and customers", "status": "ready",
   "capabilities": ["supports_sql"], "connection": {"host": "db", "user": "app", "password": "***"},
   "reason": null}
]}

docs.title: GET /api/v1/datasource/{datasource_id}
docs.text:
Response: one datasource, as the list shows it (engine.datasources.get(...)).

Errors: - An unknown id -> HTTP 404.

docs.title: DELETE /api/v1/datasource/{datasource_id}
docs.text:
Admin only: see Admin routes.

Execution flow: - Delegates to engine.datasources.remove(...): the datasource leaves routing and engine.config, and its connection pool is closed. Nothing is written to the config files, and its index entries stay until the next full index.

Response: {"success": true, "message": "...", "datasource_id": "..."}.

Errors: - An unknown id -> HTTP 404. - Other exceptions -> HTTP 500.

docs.title: GET /api/v1/health
docs.text:
Source: packages/api/src/nl2sql_api/routes/health.py

Response model: SuccessResponse

Returns: {"success": true, "message": "NL2SQL API is running"}

docs.title: GET /api/v1/ready
docs.text:
Source: packages/api/src/nl2sql_api/routes/health.py

Response model: SuccessResponse

Returns: {"success": true, "message": "NL2SQL API is ready"}

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text: POST /api/v1/index/{datasource_id}, POST /api/v1/index-all and DELETE /api/v1/index are admin only (see Admin routes); GET /api/v1/index/status is open.

docs.title: POST /api/v1/index/{datasource_id}
docs.text:
Execution flow: - Delegates to engine.index.build([datasource_id]): the new entries are written beside the live ones and switched in when all are written. No model is called: a build embeds the schema, the glossary and the verified queries.

Response: {"success": true, "datasource_id": "...", "indexing_stats": {...}, "message": "..."}

Errors: - A datasource that fails to index (unknown, unavailable, unreadable) -> HTTP 500 naming the reason. It keeps its previous entries.

docs.title: POST /api/v1/index-all
docs.text:
Execution flow: - Delegates to engine.index.build(), every configured datasource.

Response: {"success": <every datasource indexed>, "indexing_results": {"stats": [...], "empty": [...], "errors": [...]}, "message": "..."}. A datasource that fails is in errors (datasource_id, error) and keeps its previous entries.

docs.title: DELETE /api/v1/index
docs.text: Execution flow: - Delegates to engine.index.clear().

docs.title: GET /api/v1/index/status
docs.text:
Execution flow: - Delegates to engine.index.health() (see Indexing API → index.health), the same report the playground's index panel shows.

Response (illustrative):

{
  "status": "ok",
  "total": 162,

docs.title: LLM API
docs.text: Source: packages/api/src/nl2sql_api/routes/llm.py

docs.title: PUT /api/v1/settings/llm
docs.text:
Replaces the engine's whole llm section in the running process, through engine.llm.replace (see LLM API → llm.replace).

Admin only: see Admin routes.

Request body: the llm section as JSON, the same shape as llm.yaml (see LLM configuration).

{
  "provider": "openai",
  "model": "gpt-5.4",
  "api_key": "${env:OPENAI_API_KEY}",
  "agents": {"ast_planner": {"model": "gpt-5.5"}}
}

Execution flow: - The body is checked exactly as llm.yaml is: strict keys with "did you mean", the section's validators, and the providers resolved through the engine's registry. A ${provider:key} reference is kept in a secret field (api_key) and resolved by the engine's secret manager, so the body can name a variable or a secret rather than carry a key. A reference anywhere else is an error: the server's environment is never read into the config. - Every agent's API key must resolve. No model is called. - The new clients are built, then swapped in with engine.config.llm as one step. Questions already running finish on the old LLM. - The change is logged (one INFO line on nl2sql.llm) and audited, naming the caller's roles, via: "api", and each agent's old and new provider and model. Nothing is written to disk: a restart reads llm.yaml again.

Response (200): the change, never a key.

{
  "by": {"user_id": null, "roles": ["admin"], "via": "api"},
  "changes": {
    "default": {"old": "openai/gpt-5.4", "new": "anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5"},
    "ast_planner": {"old": "openai/gpt-5.4", "new": "anthropic/claude-opus-5-5"}
  }
}

Errors: - No role -> HTTP 401; a role not in policies.admin_roles, or a remote client with no role source configured -> HTTP 403. - A section that is not valid, a provider that is not installed, or a key that does not resolve -> HTTP 422, whose detail is the config error's text. Nothing changes.

HTTP 422
{"detail": "LLM has 1 problem:\n\n  LLM → llm.agents.ast_planer\n    Unknown key. Did you mean 'ast_planner'?"}

docs.title: GET /api/v1/llm
docs.text: Response: {"llms": {...}}, engine.llm.list(): each agent by its name in the llm section (default first) with its provider, model, temperature and inherited (True when it sets nothing of its own). Never a key. No role needed.

docs.title: GET /api/v1/llm/{agent}
docs.text:
Response: one agent's entry, engine.llm.get(agent).

Errors: - An unknown agent -> HTTP 404, naming the agents.

docs.title: Request/Response Models
docs.text: Source: packages/api/src/nl2sql_api/models/query.py

docs.title: QueryRequest
docs.text: field type required meaning natural_language str yes User query. datasource_id Optional[str] no Datasource override. execute bool no Execute SQL against datasource (default true). user_context Optional[Dict[str, Any]] no Ignored unless api.trust_body_role is true (local testing only); then an RBAC payload such as {"roles": ["admin"]}. See Caller role.

docs.title: SubQueryResponse
docs.text:
Derives from nl2sql.SubQueryResult, so it has exactly the engine's fields.

field type required meaning id str no Sub-query identifier. intent str no Semantic intent of the sub-query. sql str no SQL generated for the sub-query. datasource_id str no Datasource the sub-query targets. schema_version str no Schema version used for planning. plan Optional[Dict[str, Any]] no The validated plan, dumped. validation List[ValidationCheck] no Validation checks (name, passed, message). rows Optional[RowSample] no Capped row sample (columns, rows, total_rows). status str no "success" or "error" for this sub-query, from its final attempt: "success" when it ended with SQL and, if executed, a result; otherwise "error". A retry that recovers reports "success". "dropped" when a hook denied it with scope="sub_query": the run went on without it. retry_count int no Plan/SQL refinement attempts made. plan_source "llm" \| "cache" \| "verified" \| "supplied" \| "approved" \| "chosen" no "cache" when the plan came from the plan cache (no planner call; still validated and executed), "verified" when a verified query answered (there is no plan; sql is the verified query's own, with its :name placeholders), "supplied" or "approved" for a pinned plan (see Query API → Running a plan you hold), otherwise "llm". row_cap Optional[int] no The row limit that bounded this sub-query's SQL, or null when the plan's own LIMIT was smaller. truncated bool no True when the result reached row_cap, so rows may be missing.

docs.title: QueryResponse
docs.text:
Derives from nl2sql.QueryResult (only sub_queries is narrowed to SubQueryResponse), so the HTTP response cannot drift from what the engine returns.

field type required meaning sub_queries List[SubQueryResponse] no One entry per decomposed sub-query, each with its SQL. final_answer Optional[Dict[str, Any]] no Answer synthesizer payload (summary, format_type, content, warnings, truncated). errors List[Dict[str, Any]] no Pipeline errors (node, message, error_code, severity, provider, provider_response). provider and provider_response are set for a PROVIDER_* code and null otherwise; see provider failures. trace_id str no Trace identifier. reasoning List[Dict[str, Any]] no Reasoning events/logs. warnings List[RunWarning] no What the answer should say without failing the run: code, node, message, sub_query_id, detail. See Warnings. artifact_refs Dict[str, ArtifactRef] no Result artifact references keyed by execution node id. status str no "success", "error" or "plan_only" for the run. timings Dict[str, float] no Wall-clock seconds per graph node. usage QuestionUsage no LLM calls, input/cached/output/reasoning tokens and model time per node (nodes) and for the question (total), plus every call (calls) and the number of plans served from the plan cache (plan_cache_hits). The same model as QueryResult.usage; see the core query API. trace_path Optional[str] no Where the run's trace file was written on the server, or null. See Debugging a Run. truncated bool no True when any sub-query's result was cut at its row limit. result_manifest List[ResultSummary] no The run's saved results, one per terminal DAG node: node_id, columns, row_count (the whole result's), truncated (a sub-query feeding it was cut at its row limit) and column_kinds (each column's type category: number, text, temporal, boolean or other, read from the saved file's column types). Never the rows: read those with the two result routes below, result_id being the node_id. Empty when nothing was saved (execute: false, or the run failed before aggregation). source AnswerSource no Where the answer came from: {"type": "verified", "id", "datasource_id", "params"} when a verified query from curated.yaml answered, with the values it ran with; {"type": "generated"} (the other fields null) otherwise. The last event of POST /query/stream carries it too.

Only a capped sample of the rows is inlined, in sub_queries[].rows. The full result set is written to artifact storage and addressed through artifact_refs (uri, format, row_count, columns). The run's combined results are listed in result_manifest and read back, a page at a time or as CSV, with GET /api/v1/query/{request_id}/results/{result_id} and .../{result_id}.csv.

docs.title: ResultPage
docs.text:
field type meaning request_id str The run's trace_id. result_id str The result's node_id from result_manifest. columns List[str] Column names, in row order. rows List[List[Any]] rows[i] is row offset + i of the result. offset int The first row returned, from 0. limit int The page size used, after the cap of 1,000. total_rows int Rows in the whole result. next_offset Optional[int] Where the next page starts, or null when this page reaches the end.

An errors[] entry for a key the provider rejected:

{
  "node": "datasource_resolver",
  "message": "OpenAI rejected the API key.",
  "error_code": "PROVIDER_AUTH_FAILED",
  "severity": "ERROR",
  "provider": "OpenAI",
  "provider_response": "HTTP 401 (invalid_api_key): Incorrect API key provided: [redacted key]. You can find your API key at https://platform.openai.com/account/api-keys."
}

Branch on error_code, show message, and keep provider_response for a "provider response" disclosure. The codes are listed under provider failures.

docs.title: POST /api/v1/query
docs.text:
Source: packages/api/src/nl2sql_api/routes/query.py

Request model: QueryRequest

Response model: QueryResponse

Execution flow: - The get_user_context dependency supplies the caller's UserContext (see Caller role); with no role it answers HTTP 401 before the engine runs. - Delegates to engine.run_query(...), which returns a QueryResult. - Returns that QueryResult as a QueryResponse (its subclass); there is no field mapping.

The handler is declared with def, not async def: the pipeline performs blocking LLM and database calls, so Starlette runs it in its threadpool instead of on the event loop.

Errors: - Pipeline failures are a normal HTTP 200 carrying errors; they are not HTTP failures. - Genuinely unexpected failures return HTTP 500 with a generic detail; the traceback is logged server-side rather than returned to the client. - No role for the request returns HTTP 401 with a message naming the settings. - An invalid request body returns HTTP 422 (FastAPI validation).
