Dependencies pydantic>=2.0 unchanged: pydantic and the standard library only Engine dependency nl2sql-adapter-sdk~=0.1 nl2sql-sdk~=0.5.0: the engine's own version as a compatible release, on a line release-please bumps Entry points nl2sql.adapters unchanged. Entry point groups name the engine's extension points, not the SDK package.

What has to change:

File Change packages/sdk/pyproject.toml name = "nl2sql-sdk", include = ["nl2sql_sdk*"], description "Interfaces for nl2sql extensions: adapters and secret providers" packages/nl2sql/pyproject.toml the dependency; every nl2sql_adapter_sdk import in the engine (67 files, mechanical) release-please-config.json extra-files path packages/sdk/pyproject.toml. The version stays in lockstep with the other two packages, so the first nl2sql-sdk release is 0.5.0. .github/workflows/publish_pypi.yaml the build loop path; the smoke install dist/nl2sql_sdk-*.whl; the matrix entry package: nl2sql-sdk, stem: nl2sql_sdk; environment: pypi-nl2sql-sdk .github/workflows/test.yml pip install -e packages/sdk (twice) and the wheel smoke test packages/api/Dockerfile COPY ./packages/sdk and install it tests/architecture/test_boundaries.py SDK path, the allowed set, ADAPTER_LIBRARIES Docs adapters/sdk.md, adapters/development.md, adapters/architecture.md, adapters/index.md, adapters/sqlalchemy.md, extensions/add-adapter.md, architecture/invariants.md, development/releasing.md, CLAUDE.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, README.md, packages/sdk/README.md

Before the first 0.5 release, the owner must do two things by hand. These are not code: - on PyPI, add a pending trusted publisher for the new project nl2sql-sdk (workflow publish_pypi.yaml, environment pypi-nl2sql-sdk); - on GitHub, create the environment pypi-nl2sql-sdk.

Without them, the SDK leg of the release fails. Because the matrix is fail-fast: false, the other two packages would still publish against an SDK that is not on PyPI, so docs/development/releasing.md gets this as a checklist item. nl2sql-adapter-sdk is simply not published again. With no users, yanking it adds nothing.

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
Built: nl2sql config check (PR 8)

See the note in Loading.

Built: the callers on the new config (PR 7b)

The CLI takes one global --config; --env, --env-file, every per-command path flag and nl2sql setup are gone. The CLI, nl2sql-api and nl2sql demo load the .env next to nl2sql.yaml (nl2sql.config.load_env_file, never overriding a set variable) and call engine.check() at startup. ConfigManager, the nl2sql/configs/ file envelopes, sample_questions.py, nl2sql._legacy and every 0.4 file in the repository's configs/ are deleted. Building it settled these details:

  • load_env_file is exported from nl2sql too: nl2sql-api imports only the top-level package.
  • The curated checks that need the datasources (check_curated, inspect_verified_sql) moved to nl2sql/config/curated.py, with sqlglot imported inside them. AgentConfig and LLMFileConfig (the set of agents the benchmark compares, now built with LLMFileConfig.from_llm(llm)) moved to nl2sql/llm/models.py.
  • A command that only needs the stores (trace show, cache clear, feedback, curated proposals export) reads storage.path from the config without building the engine. run, index, trace replay and benchmark build it and check() it; policy validate and curated validate/test build it without connecting first. curated proposals export refuses to write nl2sql.yaml or any file it includes.
  • nl2sql doctor reports Python, the adapters' drivers, which provider key variables are set, and the configured engine's check() report.
  • BenchmarkConfig lost its path fields. A --llm PATH.yaml file, the built-in presets and --bench-config-path hold llm sections.
  • configure_llm_from_config(path) and reload_llm_config(path) take an nl2sql.yaml and replace every agent with its llm section, until PR 9 and 10 bring llm.replace. add_datasource takes a Datasource only, and so does POST /api/v1/datasource.
  • nl2sql-api reads api.cors_origins per request from the engine's config: the engine is built in the lifespan, after the middleware stack.

Built: nl2sql init (PR 6)

nl2sql init is in the CLI (PR 7b removed setup). The engine writes the files: nl2sql.config.init_project(folder, demo=, provider=, force=) returns the paths it wrote, after loading them with load_config. nl2sql.config.demo_config(llm=, path=, data_dir=) builds the demo Config that NL2SQL.demo() (PR 7a) uses, and init --demo writes that same config out, so the two cannot drift. Building it settled these details:

  • The demo's datasources, roles, sample questions and verified queries moved from nl2sql.cli.demo to nl2sql.datasets (chinook, support, webanalytics, demo), in the nl2sql.yaml shape, so the engine can build the demo without importing the CLI.
  • --provider accepts the providers with a default model (openai, anthropic, openrouter). llm.yaml gets that model and the provider's default temperature (none for Anthropic).
  • If any file init would write exists, it names them all and writes nothing. .gitignore is never overwritten: the missing lines are appended.
  • A demo datasource's database is written as data/<name>.sqlite, relative to nl2sql.yaml. load_config keeps connection as written, so the runtime (PR 7a) has to resolve a relative SQLite path against the config's folder, as it does storage.path. demo_config() points at the packaged files instead.
Change Detail One global --config PATH On the app callback, before the subcommand: nl2sql --config prod/nl2sql.yaml index. Without it, NL2SQL_CONFIG, then ./nl2sql.yaml. .env and startup Before building the engine, the CLI loads the .env next to the chosen nl2sql.yaml without overriding variables already set. Commands that query or index call engine.check() and stop on EngineNotReady. Flags removed --env, --env-file, and every per-command path flag: --config (meaning the datasource file), --secrets-config, --llm-config, --policies-config, --vector-store, and curated's and policy's --curated, --config, --secrets and --policies. nl2sql init [DIR] [--demo] [--provider NAME] [--force] Non-interactive. Writes the split layout below into DIR (default .), validates it with load_config and prints the next steps. It refuses to overwrite a file without --force. --provider (default openai) picks the llm.yaml provider and its default model. nl2sql config check [--connect] Loading, step "CI". It prints problems grouped by file and exits 0 or 1. nl2sql setup removed init replaces it, including setup --demo (owner decision 5). The guided flow (connect, scan, draft, review) comes in Phase 4. nl2sql doctor Reports Python, installed packages and extras, and provider keys present. Config problems are config check's job. nl2sql list-adapters Reads Registry.default().names("adapter") and marks each installed or missing its driver.

What nl2sql init writes (with --demo shown in comments):

nl2sql.yaml            # the table of contents
datasources/
  example.yaml         # a commented sqlite example   (--demo: chinook.yaml, support.yaml, webanalytics.yaml)
llm.yaml               # provider + model; no key, the standard variable is the fallback
embeddings.yaml        # provider: local
policies.yaml          # allow_all: true              (--demo: admin, analyst, viewer roles)
storage.yaml           # path: .nl2sql
curated.yaml           # --demo only: the demo verified queries
data/                  # --demo only: the three bundled SQLite files, copied
.gitignore             # .nl2sql/ and .env

docs.title: Demo and playground
docs.text:
Built (PR 7b)

As designed, with these details:

  • The demo writes the llm section to its own llm.yaml rather than building the LLM in code: the playground's settings panel edits that file and reloads the engine's LLMs from it, so the two must agree. In replay and record mode it points base_url at the local replay server or the recording proxy with the placeholder api_key that endpoint takes (replay, proxy); live, it names no key, so the provider's variable is read. A real key is never written into YAML.
  • Keys still reach os.environ in two places until PR 10 and 13: a key from --api-key or the demo's .env, and one saved in the settings panel. --record turns the plan cache off in the engine's own config (settings.pipeline.plan_cache), not through the environment; hosted mode never turned it off, so nothing changes there.
  • What 0.4's .env.demo set is now in the demo's config: demo_config(), and so init --demo (which writes it as settings.yaml), carries settings.pipeline.timeout_s: 300, settings.traces.mode: always and policies.refusal_names_tables: true.
  • --questions-per-minute and --questions-per-session replace the NL2SQL_DEMO_* variables, and NL2SQL_DEMO_HOSTED is gone: --hosted is the only switch.
  • nl2sql demo runs init --demo into nl2sql-demo/ the first time, builds the index if check() reports it missing, then serves the playground on NL2SQL.from_config("nl2sql-demo/nl2sql.yaml").
  • A key the demo is given is written to nl2sql-demo/.env (it was .env.demo) and passed into the LLM it builds. Nothing goes into os.environ.

Built: keys without the environment (PR 13)

nl2sql demo --api-key writes the key to the demo's .env and passes it to _build_engine as api_keys (provider -> key), which puts it into the engine's llm section in memory with nl2sql.cli.demo.llm_config.with_api_keys: the top level gets its provider's key unless it names one, and an agent on another provider gets that provider's key, or explicitly none, so it never inherits a key for a provider it does not run on. llm.yaml still never holds a key. A key in .env from an earlier run reaches the engine through load_env_file, as for every entry point; the flag wins over an exported variable because it travels as a value, which the engine prefers to the environment. The settings panel keeps the same api_keys, adds each key saved in it, and passes them with every engine.llm.replace; it shows a key masked from there or from the environment. Hosted mode used to remove the provider key variables from its own environment; it now refuses to start when one is set, since a public server must not hold a key and the demo no longer writes the environment to drop it.

  • Replay mode keeps its local fake server. The demo points the config at it with LLM(provider="openai", base_url="http://127.0.0.1:<port>/v1", api_key="replay") instead of setting OPENAI_API_KEY=replay.
  • PLAN_CACHE_ENABLED=false in hosted mode becomes settings.pipeline.plan_cache: false in the hosted demo's config.
  • CLAUDE.md's rule "never read nl2sql-demo*/ or any .env" stays as it is. Only its mention of .env.demo changes.

docs.title: 11. PR plan
docs.text:
Each PR is written test-first and updates the docs it affects. "Depends on" means the PR must be merged first. At most four PRs are open at once.

flowchart TD
  P0["0. This design doc"] --> P1["1. SDK rename"]
