Graph construction and routing: - packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/graph.py - packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/routes.py - packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/graph_utils.py

Subgraph state and execution: - packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/subgraphs/sql_agent.py - packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/subgraphs/schemas.py

Mutators / consumers: - packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/nodes/datasource_resolver/node.py - packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/nodes/decomposer/node.py - packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/nodes/aggregator/node.py - packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/nodes/answer_synthesizer/node.py - packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/nodes/schema_retriever/node.py - packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/nodes/ast_planner/node.py - packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/nodes/validator/node.py - packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/nodes/generator/node.py - packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/nodes/executor/node.py - packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/nodes/refiner/node.py

docs.title: Indexing, Chunking, and Retrieval Architecture
docs.text: This document describes current indexing behavior as implemented in code. Indexing transforms schema snapshots into typed chunks that the engine embeds and writes to the index store (storage.index, the built-in chroma store by default; see Storage). Retrieval uses these entries as candidates and then resolves authoritative schema details from the state store (storage.state; see ../schema/store.md for schema contracts and store behavior).

docs.title: Indexing flow
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    Adapter[Datasource Adapter] --> Snapshot[Schema Snapshot]
    Snapshot --> Register[StateStore.put_snapshot]
    Register --> Chunker[SchemaChunkBuilder]
    Knowledge[The glossary] --> Chunker
    Curated[curated.yaml] --> CChunker[CuratedChunkBuilder]
    Chunker --> Embed[The engine's embedder]
    CChunker --> Embed
    Embed --> Add[IndexStore.add: a new build]
    Add --> Switch[IndexStore.set_pointers: the commit]

The adapter reads only what the datasource's index scope wants, so an excluded schema costs no query. The built-in adapters reflect each schema once, take row counts from the catalog's estimates (counting rows only where the database keeps none, and only under profile: stats), profile each column on its own by type, and keep text values only with index.sample_values (off by default; the demo turns it on). A column, row count or table the database cannot read is indexed without it rather than failing the datasource's index, and is an IndexIssue on the snapshot: the build returns the issues in the datasource's stats under issues, and nl2sql index prints them (see Reading a schema).

docs.title: What is indexed today
docs.text:
Schema-derived chunks, the verified queries of curated.yaml when the file exists, and knowledge: the glossary's descriptions in the table and column entries, its terms, its joins and its example questions (Knowledge in the index). There is no symbolic index, behavioral index, or other catalog in the current implementation.

The stored schema snapshot holds only what the database said (B31): a table or column comment the adapter read. A person's words stay in the glossary, and a description a model drafts is a proposal in the review queue that reaches nothing until a person accepts it. nl2sql index calls no model.

docs.title: Chunk types and contracts
docs.text:
Chunk types are defined in nl2sql.indexing.models:

  • DatasourceChunk (schema.datasource): datasource description and domains. The description is the one the datasource was registered with (description: in the datasources config, or the description of a Datasource passed to engine.datasources.add); the orchestrator reads it from the datasource registry, falling back to the datasources file only when the registry has none. It lives in the config rather than the database, so the orchestrator writes it into the snapshot's metadata, where it takes precedence over any description the adapter produced.
  • DatasourceExampleChunk (schema.datasource_example): one example question the datasource answers, one entry per question, so the fifth question moves routing as much as the first (in the datasource entry's one text it barely moved the vector). build_example_chunks(datasource_id, questions, schema_version) builds them from a list the caller assembles: the datasource's sample_questions and the glossary's examples (SchemaChunkBuilder joins them). A blank or repeated question is skipped. Ids: schema.datasource_example:<datasource_id>:<12 hex of the question's SHA-256>:<schema_version>.
  • TableChunk (schema.table): table name, PKs, column list, FK summaries, row counts, and the chosen description (the glossary's, else the database's comment).
  • ColumnChunk (schema.column): column type, stats, PII flags, the chosen description, synonyms (the database's and the glossary's) and the role a person set in the glossary (a Role: line; a role derived from the schema is not written).
  • RelationshipChunk (schema.relationship): FK relationships, columns, cardinality, and origin (database, or glossary for a join a person wrote).
  • TermChunk (knowledge.term): a glossary term, its synonyms and its definition. Metadata: id, type, datasource_id, term, schema_version. Id: knowledge.term:<datasource_id>:<12 hex of the lower-cased term's SHA-256>:<schema_version>.
  • MetricChunk (schema.metric): defined but not emitted by SchemaChunkBuilder.
  • VerifiedQueryChunk (curated.verified_query): one phrasing of a verified query, or its description, built by CuratedChunkBuilder (nl2sql.indexing.curated). Each {placeholder} is filled with the param's example, else its default, else its own name, because a raw {n} embeds poorly: "Best {n} customers in {year}" is embedded as "Best 10 customers in 2012". Metadata: id, type, datasource_id, query_id, schema_version. Ids: curated.verified_query:<datasource_id>:<query_id>:<n>, the phrasings in order, then the description. The SQL is never indexed.

Chunk models live in nl2sql.indexing.models and are Pydantic models. IDs are deterministic and include schema_version.

docs.title: Verified queries
docs.text:
Verified query entries are written in the same build as the datasource's schema entries: IndexingOrchestrator.index_datasource() appends them to the schema chunks before it writes the build. A build replaces every entry of its datasource, so curated entries written on their own would be deleted by the next schema re-index.

The build's pointer also records curated_hash, a SHA-256 of that datasource's verified queries as canonical JSON (metrics are left out; nothing indexes them yet). Index health compares it with the file as it is now (see Index health).

Changing curated.yaml or the glossary does not re-read the schema. nl2sql index --refresh (engine.index.refresh(), IndexingOrchestrator.refresh()) writes a new build for each datasource the usual way, except that every entry's text is rendered again from the live build's stored snapshot, the current verified queries and the current knowledge, and the pointer keeps its schema version: no schema read, no snapshot registered, no model call. An entry whose text and metadata equal the live build's keeps its stored vector; only the changed and new entries are embedded, and an entry no longer written is dropped. The switch and the clean-up are the ones described below, so the refresh is just as safe. It needs the datasource to have been indexed once; otherwise that datasource fails with a message saying to run nl2sql index.

docs.title: Knowledge in the index
docs.text:
Prompts read the in-memory knowledge, so an accepted change is effective in the next run. The index carries knowledge for ranking (D56): the chosen descriptions and synonyms in the table and column entries, a knowledge.term entry per term, a relationship entry per glossary join that resolves (with its cardinality and origin: glossary), and the glossary's examples among the example questions. Names that do not resolve against the snapshot are left out, as engine.knowledge.show reports them.

A term is also matched by similarity: Retriever.retrieve_term_candidates(query, datasource_id, k, terms=None) returns the term entries nearest the sub-query's intent (only the named terms when given: the ones the caller's scope shows), and the schema retriever keeps the ones at or above settings.knowledge.match_floor (0.6) whose term the caller's scope shows, beside the terms whose name or synonym appears in the text. The search is a plain similarity search over the live build, embeds nothing when the datasource has no term entry, and a failure leaves the match by name.

The build's pointer records knowledge_hash, the datasource's knowledge digest, beside curated_hash. Index health compares it with the digest of the live knowledge: a glossary changed since the build makes the index stale (below), and nl2sql index --refresh clears it without reading the schema.

Retriever.retrieve_verified_query_candidates(question, datasource_ids, k) returns the verified queries a question most resembles. It is a plain similarity search, not MMR, because several phrasings of one query are exactly what should match: it reads the live builds of the given datasources only, fetches k × 10 entries, keeps each query's best phrasing (by cosine similarity), and returns the best k (CURATED_MATCH_TOP_K, 5), each with its score and the phrasing that won. With no verified query entry among those datasources it returns nothing without embedding the question. Given an explain list, it appends a record shaped like the MMR one below. Nothing in the pipeline calls it yet; the matcher that will is described in Curated Answers (design).

docs.title: Chunk → index mapping (actual)
docs.text:
The engine embeds each chunk with its own embedder and hands the index store an Entry (nl2sql_sdk.stores):

  • Entry.text = chunk.get_page_content()
  • Entry.vector = the embedder's vector for that text
  • Entry.metadata = chunk.get_metadata(), with empty values left out, plus build_id. An entry holds scalars only, so a relationship's from_columns and to_columns are stored comma-joined; the retriever splits them again.

The store never embeds and never depends on LangChain. build_id is stripped from retrieved entries, because retrieved metadata reaches the planner's prompt and a build id would change it on every rebuild.

docs.title: One namespace per embedding model
docs.text:
Entries live in a namespace per embedding model: nl2sql__<model slug>__<dimension>, for example nl2sql__local-all-minilm-l6-v2__384 (the slug is the provider and model, lower case; Runtime.namespace). Every datasource of one model shares its namespace; the chroma store keeps one collection per namespace.

  • Changing the embedding model opens a new, empty namespace. Health reports missing with "run nl2sql index", and nl2sql index fills it. Nothing refuses the change, and no special rebuild is needed.
  • Switching back finds the old namespace still built.
  • nl2sql index prune (engine.index.prune()) drops every namespace but the current one, including 0.5's nl2sql_store collection, which this version never reads.

docs.title: The build pointer is the commit
docs.text:
Re-indexing never deletes anything first. Each datasource is built on its own (IndexingOrchestrator):

flowchart TD
    A[Read the schema; store the snapshot as version v2] --> B[Embed and write every entry under a new build_id]
    B --> C{All entries written?}
    C -->|no| D[Raise: the pointer still names the previous build and v1]
    C -->|yes| E[set_pointers: datasource to the new build and v2]
    E --> F[Delete the datasource's builds older than the one replaced]
    F --> H[If v2's structure differs from v1's: store the diff, publish schema.drifted]
    H --> G[keep_snapshots: delete the snapshots nothing can read any more]
  • Each datasource's BuildPointer names its live build_id and the schema_version the build was made from, with built_at and curated_hash. Switching the pointer is the commit. A snapshot stored by a build that then fails is referenced by no pointer, so no reader ever sees it: readers resolve "live" through the pointer, never through the state store's newest snapshot (bug B5). The failed build's entries are deleted by the next build of that datasource.
  • A run pins the pointers. A run reads the pointers once, when it starts (Runtime.pin_index(), called by run_with_graph), as it pins its LLM set. The resolver, the schema retriever, the curated matcher and the decomposer's context all use that build and that schema version. A build keeps the build it replaces and deletes only older ones, so a run in flight never loses its entries, and nothing has to hold questions back around the switch.
  • Other datasources are never read, deleted or rewritten by a datasource's build. nl2sql index --datasource X rebuilds only X; nl2sql index rebuilds each configured datasource in turn, and a failure keeps that datasource's previous build live and exits 1.
  • nl2sql.indexing.rebuild.rebuild_index, behind engine.index.build, is the one entry point for nl2sql index, the demo's startup repair, the playground's Rebuild and the REST index routes. Its on_datasource callback gets an IndexProgress per datasource (started, then done with the entry counts or failed with the reason): nl2sql index prints a line from it.
  • One build at a time. rebuild_index holds the state store's index lock (a lease that expires after an hour), so nl2sql index is safe while nl2sql-api serves the same storage.path. A build started while another holds it fails every datasource at once, with the reason.
  • Snapshots are immutable, and after a build only the snapshots a pointer names (in any namespace), the one just replaced and the newest settings.schema.max_versions are kept. See The state store.
  • A structural change is recorded. When the new version's structure differs from the one it replaced, the diff between them is stored beside it and schema.drifted is published; nothing else happens. See Schema Drift, which also covers nl2sql index --check.
  • engine.datasources.schema(), engine.curated.validate() and an eval report's database identity read the snapshot the live pointer names too.

docs.title: Index health
docs.text: nl2sql.indexing.health judges the index of the configured embedding model by its contents, never by whether a folder exists (the demo once had a data/vector_store_demo folder holding 0 entries). Only the builds the pointers name are counted. Status, worst first: missing (the model has no namespace yet: never indexed, or the model changed), empty (no live entries), stale (a configured datasource has no live build, its build's snapshot is gone from the state store, or its glossary changed since the build: "The glossary changed for 'chinook' since it was indexed; run nl2sql index --refresh --datasource chinook"), ok. It reports entry counts by type, the schema version each live build was made from (index_version), when each was built, the embedding model and the namespace. warnings never change the status: a datasource whose curated.yaml section has changed since it was indexed (its pointer's curated_hash differs from the file's) gets "curated.yaml changed for 'chinook' since it was indexed; run nl2sql index --refresh --datasource chinook". Questions keep working meanwhile; the stale entries still name queries that exist. A preferred_tables entry missing from the datasource's live snapshot is a warning too. nl2sql doctor prints it under Index, nl2sql demo rebuilds at startup when it is not ok, and the playground and GET /api/v1/index/status show it (through engine.index.health()), the playground with a Rebuild button.

docs.title: Chunking strategy (as implemented)
docs.text:
Chunking is aligned to planning intent:

  • Routing uses the datasource and example entries, the verified queries, and the table and column entries as votes (see Routing).
  • Schema context uses table/metric chunks.
  • Planning context uses columns and relationships for specific tables.

If retrieval returns no candidates, the retriever falls back to full schema enumeration.

docs.title: Retrieval pipeline (staged, code-accurate)
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    SubQuery --> SemQuery[_build_semantic_query]
    SemQuery --> L1[retrieve_schema_context (tables/metrics)]
    L1 -->|no tables| L2[retrieve_column_candidates]
    L2 --> L3[retrieve_planning_context (columns/relationships)]
    L3 --> Snapshot[SchemaStore.get_snapshot]
    Snapshot --> Tables[relevant_tables for planner]

docs.title: Stages
docs.text:
1. Schema context: retrieves table/metric chunks.
  2. Column candidates: fallback to column chunks when no table matches.
  3. Planning context: retrieves columns/relationships for the selected tables.
  4. Authoritative resolution: resolves tables/columns from SchemaStore snapshot.

docs.title: Authoritative vs semantic sources
docs.text:
• Semantic candidates come from the index store (vector search over entries).
  • Authoritative schema is resolved from SchemaStore snapshots.
  • Index content is never treated as authoritative.

docs.title: Metadata propagation
docs.text:
• datasource_id and schema_version are included in all chunk metadata.
  • TableChunk includes primary_key, columns, row_count, and FK summaries.
  • ColumnChunk includes dtype, pii, description, and stats when available.
  • RelationshipChunk includes join column pairs and cardinality.

Metadata is consumed by SchemaRetrieverNode to construct Table objects for planning and by LogicalValidatorNode to validate joins and filters.

docs.title: Versioning and determinism
docs.text:
• Schema snapshots are fingerprinted and versioned (YYYYMMDDhhmmss_<fp8>).
  • Chunk IDs embed schema_version for deterministic indexing.
  • Retrieval uses the SubQuery.schema_version when available; otherwise the version the run's pinned pointer names.
  • MMR ranking may introduce non-determinism in ordering for similar scores.

docs.title: Retrieval: MMR, not a re-ranking model
docs.text:
Every vector search in the engine is one maximal marginal relevance (MMR) search over the current namespace's live builds, which hold every datasource (the demo's three databases: 3 datasource, 20 table, 121 column and 18 relationship entries, 162 in all, of which Chinook is 87). There is no re-ranking model. What is sometimes called re-ranking is this:

  1. Embed the query text with the engine's embedder (the local all-MiniLM-L6-v2 costs nothing per query).
  2. Fetch the pool: the fetch_k = 4 * k entries nearest to it, filtered by entry type, datasource and live build (IndexStore.query with a Filter).
  3. Pick k of them one at a time, in the engine, on the vectors the store returned. The first pick is the entry most similar to the query (cosine similarity). Every later pick is the pool entry with the highest 0.7 * similarity(entry, query) - 0.3 * max similarity(entry, earlier picks), so an entry that nearly repeats an earlier pick loses to a less similar one that adds something. lambda_mult = 0.7 is the weight on similarity.

The documents come back in pool order (nearest first), not pick order.

Caller Search Entry types k Pool SchemaRetrieverNode tables table, metric table_k (8) 32 SchemaRetrieverNode, when tables finds nothing columns column table_k (8) 32 SchemaRetrieverNode, over the tables found planning column, relationship planning_k (12) 48

table_k and planning_k are settings.retrieval settings (see Settings). The resolver's routing searches are not MMR; they are described below.

The schema retriever runs none of these when the schema has SCHEMA_RETRIEVAL_FULL_SNAPSHOT_MAX_TABLES tables or fewer (15 by default, so each of the demo's three schemas, at 11, 4 and 5 tables, is always sent whole); the resolver runs none when the request names a datasource_id or only one datasource is registered. The demo is no longer such a case: with three datasources registered, the resolver searches on every question.

A datasource's preferred_tables change the order but not the searches: on either path they come first, and on the retrieval path a preferred table the tables search scored within 0.05 of its least similar pick is added (see SchemaRetrieverNode).

Retriever.mmr in nl2sql.indexing.retrieval is the one implementation: it asks the index store for the pool with its vectors, runs MMR in numpy, and returns the documents with a record of the search (the query, the pool with similarity, the store's distance and type, the picks in order with the score each won with, and what was dropped). The record comes from numbers MMR computes anyway, so it costs no second search. Nodes put it in their run trace (see Debugging a run), and the playground's Retrieval inspector (engine.index.inspect) runs the same search for any text, with k, lambda, entry types and datasource exposed. That inspector is the tool for chunking experiments: change the chunks, rebuild, search the same text, and diff the Copy as text output. It is run as a caller (user_context is required): entries the caller's scope hides are left out of the pool.

docs.title: Routing: five signals, fused
docs.text:
Retriever.route(question, datasource_ids, explain, *, limit, floor_ratio, allows) ranks the datasources a question most likely needs, as a list of RouteCandidate:

  • datasource_id;
  • score, its fused score;
  • ranks, its rank in each signal that ranked it;
  • similarity, its best entry's cosine similarity to the question.

The resolver calls it with the datasources the caller's scope reaches, and only those: a datasource the role may not read is never searched, so it never ranks. It also passes allows, its entry check:

  • A table or column entry votes only when its table is one of that datasource's visible tables in the live snapshot. The check is on the (datasource, table) pair, because two datasources can hold a table of the same name.
  • A verified query votes only when every table its SQL reads is visible. A query whose SQL does not parse never votes.

An entry allows refuses is dropped before anything is ranked or recorded, so a denied table never votes and never appears in the trace. The searches fetch more until they hold VOTE_K allowed entries or the index runs out.

route embeds the question once and runs five searches over the reachable datasources' live builds (ROUTE_SIGNALS). Each ranks datasources by their best entry:

Signal Entries Search description schema.datasource every entry, exactly examples schema.datasource_example the nearest VOTE_K (20) curated curated.verified_query the nearest VOTE_K tables schema.table the nearest VOTE_K columns schema.column the nearest VOTE_K

Fusion. The ranks are fused with reciprocal rank fusion (fuse): score(ds) = sum over the signals of 1 / (RRF_K + rank), with RRF_K = 60.

  • A datasource a signal did not rank gets the rank after the last one it did rank (len(ranked) + 1). It has no entry of that type, or none among the nearest. Having entries of a type is therefore not a vote: only ranking well in a signal is.
  • Without that penalty, the one datasource with verified queries would collect a curated vote on every question and win nearly all of them.
  • A signal that ranked nothing is skipped.
  • A datasource with no example questions is still routed by its description, tables and columns.

Shortlist. shortlist then keeps the top limit (settings.routing.candidates, 3). It also drops any datasource whose best similarity is under floor_ratio (settings.routing.floor_ratio, 0.5) times the most similar candidate's.

  • The floor is on similarity, not on the fused score. With a handful of datasources every reciprocal-rank score is within a few percent of the best, so a floor on the score would never fire.
  • VOTE_K and RRF_K are constants on Retriever until the routing suite shows a reason to tune them.

The description search is exact: instead of the store's nearest-neighbour query it reads every live schema.datasource entry (IndexStore.get) and scores each by cosine similarity. There is one such entry per datasource among hundreds of others. An approximate (HNSW) search under a filter that selective can return fewer entries than exist, which would cost a datasource its vote. So every datasource the caller reaches is ranked at least once. The other four searches are approximate.

Given an explain list, route appends:

  • One record per signal: route.description, route.examples, route.curated, route.tables and route.columns. Each holds the pool by similarity, with each datasource's best entry marked picked, and is recorded as a search with lambda_mult 1.
  • Then a routing record:
  • rrf_k, vote_k, candidates and floor_ratio;
  • each signal's datasource ranking (signals);
  • the fused datasources (fused: score, ranks, best similarity), also given as a pool so a search view can draw it;
  • the datasources kept (picks);
  • those dropped and why (dropped: floor or limit).

The records name datasources and the ids of allowed entries, never entry text.

docs.title: Tenant isolation (current state)
docs.text:
Tenant scoping is not implemented in indexing:

  • No tenant_id field exists in chunk metadata.
  • Vector store queries do not filter by tenant.
  • Schema store is global.

docs.title: Failure modes and fallbacks
docs.text:
Current failure behaviors:

  • Vector store retrieval wrapped by VECTOR_BREAKER; failures fast‑fail.
  • Vector retrieval errors in SchemaRetrieverNode return empty results with warnings.
  • If no candidates are found, the retriever falls back to full schema snapshot.
  • Indexing calls no model, so a missing API key never affects it. Descriptions a model drafts are proposals (the profiler), not part of the index or the snapshot, until a person accepts them into the glossary.
  • A changed embedding model reads its own, empty namespace: health says missing and nl2sql index builds it. Nothing is refused.
  • When the resolver finds no datasource and the index is empty, its SCHEMA_RETRIEVAL_FAILED error says so and names nl2sql index, instead of "No datasource candidates resolved."
  • A failed rebuild leaves the previous build and schema version live (see above).

docs.title: Performance characteristics (current)
docs.text:
• Embedding uses the engine's own embedder, built from its embeddings section: OpenAI or OpenAI-compatible embeddings, or the local ONNX all-MiniLM-L6-v2 model with provider: local.
  • Vector search is MMR (lambda_mult=0.7, fetch_k = 4*k); see Retrieval.
  • No caching or sharding layers are implemented.
  • Index refresh re-embeds every entry of the datasource being re-indexed; other datasources are untouched. nl2sql index --refresh embeds only the entries whose text changed and keeps the stored vectors of the rest.

docs.title: Observability hooks
docs.text:
• VECTOR_BREAKER logs breaker state changes.
  • Indexing and retrieval log errors; no metrics are emitted in indexing code.

docs.title: Source references
docs.text:
• Chunk models: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/indexing/models.py
  • Chunk builder: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/indexing/chunk_builder.py
  • Verified query entries and their hash: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/indexing/curated.py
  • Retrieval and MMR: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/indexing/retrieval.py
  • The chroma index store: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/storage/chroma.py
  • The store interfaces: packages/sdk/src/nl2sql_sdk/stores.py
  • Schema retriever: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/nodes/schema_retriever/node.py
  • Indexing orchestrator: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/indexing/orchestrator.py
  • Index health: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/indexing/health.py
  • The local embedder: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/embeddings/local.py

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: These invariants capture rules that are enforced by the code paths responsible for planning, validation, and execution. They exist to keep the system deterministic, secure, and stable under malformed input or misconfiguration.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text: Sub-query intents and post-combine operations must not contain SQL. Each text field (intent, metric names, filter, group-by and order-by attributes, expected-schema names) is checked on its own and rejected if it opens with a SELECT ... FROM statement, or contains a statement terminator (;) or a comment marker (--, /*, */). English words that happen to be SQL keywords are allowed: "customers from Brazil" and "tracks where the genre is Rock" are valid intents.

docs.title: Enforcement Points
docs.text:
• SubQuery.validate_semantic_only() in nl2sql.pipeline.nodes.decomposer.schemas
  • PostCombineOp.validate_semantic_only() in nl2sql.pipeline.nodes.decomposer.schemas

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text: Raises ValueError ("contains SQL syntax") when a field matches; the decomposer response fails validation.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: Prevents physical SQL leakage into semantic planning stages and keeps decomposer output safe to interpret downstream.

docs.title: Combine Groups Require Roles and Typed Join Keys
Definition
docs.text: Combine groups with compare or join operations must include a role for every input, at most one left-hand input (left, base or primary) and one right-hand input (right, compare or secondary), and at least one join key pair; a group with only one side is refused by the decomposer node. Each key names a column in the expected_schema of its side's sub-query, that column declares a dtype, and the two sides' dtypes can be coerced to each other: a number or a boolean never joins a date (Wave A, D30). The aggregator casts both sides of each key to one type before the join, in polars; a value that does not convert joins nothing and is a JOIN_KEY_UNCONVERTED warning.

docs.title: Enforcement Points
docs.text:
• CombineGroup.validate_roles() and DecomposerResponse.validate_join_key_types() in nl2sql.pipeline.nodes.decomposer.schemas
  • LogicalValidatorNode (validator/join_keys.py): a join-key column whose database type cannot be coerced to its declared dtype is a retryable JOIN_KEY_TYPE_MISMATCH. The check lives in the validator, not the aggregator, because the validator has the retry edge.

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text: Raises ValueError when roles, join keys or their types are missing or cannot meet; parse-and-retry sends it back to the model.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: Ensures combine operations are well-defined and deterministic for aggregation. A text key from one database joined to an integer from another used to fail in the aggregator, terminally, or match nothing (B30).

docs.title: Definition
docs.text: Combine-group inputs must reference existing subqueries, and post-combine ops must reference existing combine groups.

docs.title: Enforcement Points
docs.text: • DecomposerResponse.validate_references() in nl2sql.pipeline.nodes.decomposer.schemas

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text: Raises ValueError for unknown subquery or group references.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: Prevents invalid execution graphs and dangling references.

docs.title: Expression AST Must Match Its Kind
Definition
docs.text: Expression nodes must satisfy kind-specific required fields (e.g., binary ops require left/right and an operator).

docs.title: Enforcement Points
docs.text: • Expr.model_post_init() in nl2sql.pipeline.nodes.ast_planner.schemas

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text: Raises ValueError when required fields are missing or operators are invalid.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: Guarantees the AST is structurally complete before SQL generation.

docs.title: Plan Model Is Strict and Read-Only
Definition
docs.text: Plan fields are schema-validated with no unknown fields, and query type must be READ.

docs.title: Enforcement Points
docs.text:
• ConfigDict(extra="forbid") on plan models in nl2sql.pipeline.nodes.ast_planner.schemas
  • PlanModel.query_type: Literal["READ"] in nl2sql.pipeline.nodes.ast_planner.schemas, which pydantic enforces before any node sees the plan (the plan cache re-validates on read, so a cached plan is covered too)

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text: Pydantic validation errors for extra/invalid fields and for any query_type other than READ; the plan never reaches the validator. LogicalValidatorNode no longer re-checks it — the branch was unreachable.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: Prevents mutation or unknown plan constructs from entering execution.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text: Each table alias in the plan must be unique.

docs.title: Enforcement Points
docs.text: • LogicalValidatorNode._alias_collision() in nl2sql.pipeline.nodes.validator.node

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text: Returns PipelineError with INVALID_PLAN_STRUCTURE.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: Prevents ambiguous column resolution.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
Every func expression names a function from ALLOWED_FUNCTIONS in nl2sql.pipeline.nodes.ast_planner.functions, written as a plain identifier (any case).

The only date functions on the list are the ones the planner prompt offers: DATE_PART and DATE_TRUNC, plus YEAR, QUARTER, MONTH, DAY and EXTRACT, which are read as DATE_PART. STRFTIME is still accepted as a legacy name (LEGACY_FUNCTIONS): a recorded demo answer and three of the Chinook suite's hand-written plans call it. Nothing offers it to the model, and the validator's rejection message leaves it out of the functions it lists.

docs.title: Enforcement Points
docs.text:
• LogicalValidatorNode._unsupported_functions() in nl2sql.pipeline.nodes.validator.node
  • packages/nl2sql/tests/unit/test_date_functions_agree_with_prompt.py reads the allow-list and the planner prompt together, so a date function cannot be allowed by one and forbidden by the other

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text: Returns PipelineError with UNSUPPORTED_FUNCTION (severity ERROR, so the refiner can retry).

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: func_name is model text that becomes the function's name in the SQL. Without the check, any text, including a second statement, reached the query.

docs.title: Expected Schema Must Match Select List
Definition
docs.text: When expected_schema is provided, the plan’s select_items count and aliases must match it.

docs.title: Enforcement Points
docs.text: • LogicalValidatorNode._validate_static() in nl2sql.pipeline.nodes.validator.node

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text: Returns PipelineError with INVALID_PLAN_STRUCTURE.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: Keeps multi-stage subqueries contractually aligned.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text: All column references must map to declared table aliases and be unambiguous.

docs.title: Enforcement Points
docs.text:
• LogicalValidatorNode._validate_columns() in nl2sql.pipeline.nodes.validator.node, which resolves the plan with sqlglot.optimizer.qualify.qualify() against the schema retrieved for the query
  • LogicalValidatorNode._validate_static() converts resolution failures to PipelineError

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text: Returns PipelineError with COLUMN_NOT_FOUND: a retryable ERROR by default, a WARNING that does not block when logical_validator_strict_columns is turned off.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: Prevents queries from referencing non-existent or ambiguous columns.

docs.title: Joins Must Be Valid and Schema-Backed
Definition
docs.text: Join aliases must exist, join conditions must reference both sides, must include an equality pair, and must match allowed schema relationships.

docs.title: Enforcement Points
docs.text: • LogicalValidatorNode._validate_static() join checks in nl2sql.pipeline.nodes.validator.node

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text: Returns PipelineError with INVALID_PLAN_STRUCTURE or JOIN_TABLE_NOT_IN_PLAN.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: Prevents invalid joins and enforces schema-authorized relationships.

docs.title: Knowledge Is Data: the Validator and Scope Decide
Definition
docs.text: The glossary (Wave B's knowledge) reaches a model only as JSON values: inside the schema block, and inside [BUSINESS_CONTEXT], one JSON object on one line in the planner's and refiner's human messages, so a newline or a block marker in a definition stays inside one JSON string. Every item and the whole block are capped (settings.knowledge.item_max_chars, block_max_chars), and notes never reach a model. Knowledge is filtered by the caller's Scope before it reaches a prompt, knowledge_used, knowledge.used or the explanation: an item naming a table the caller cannot read, or whose text mentions one as a whole word, is left out, and so is a database comment that mentions one. The prompt says it is data. Encoding does not stop a model from obeying a sentence it reads; the guarantee is that whatever the model plans under any knowledge is a typed plan, validated with the caller's scope. A glossary join only adds a relationship between two tables the caller may read, which the validator's existing join check matches.

docs.title: Enforcement Points
docs.text:
• visible() and caller_knowledge() in nl2sql.knowledge.scope; schema_knowledge() in nl2sql.pipeline.nodes.schema_retriever.node
  • render_business_context() and fit_business_context() in nl2sql.knowledge.render
  • Planner instruction 15 (ast_planner/prompts.py) and refiner instruction 5 (refiner/prompts.py)
  • LogicalValidatorNode with the caller's Scope, as for every plan
  • packages/nl2sql/tests/unit/knowledge/test_injection.py

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text: An item over the cap is a load error naming it. A plan on a denied table, written under any glossary, is refused with SECURITY_VIOLATION exactly as without one.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: A glossary is written by people other than the caller, and may be wrong or hostile. It may inform a plan; it may never widen what the caller can read.

docs.title: Residual Risk
docs.text: A paraphrase ("the pay table"), a plural or singular ("salary" for salaries) and a name inside a longer identifier cannot be caught by the mention check. The validator still refuses any plan on the table.

docs.title: Policy Enforcement Is Namespaced and Fail-Closed
Definition
docs.text: A role allows and denies tables with patterns that are *, datasource or datasource.schema.table (each part a glob, matched regardless of case); a two-part pattern is rejected when the config loads. Policy checks fail if the datasource ID is missing. Access is decided on datasource, schema and table: a table the plan names without a schema is in the adapter's default schema. Deny beats allow within a role; across roles a table is readable when some role allows it and that same role does not deny it. Every place that decides table access asks one Scope (PolicyEngine.scope(user, datasource_id) in nl2sql.policies), engine.datasources.schema(..., user_context=) included, and nothing outside nl2sql/policies/ matches a policy pattern. A run builds each datasource's scope once and keeps it. An optional policy check (nl2sql_sdk.policy.PolicyCheck) is asked once per caller and datasource per run; its grant is intersected with the roles, so neither widens the other, and any exception from it denies the datasource for the run: it never fails open.

docs.title: Enforcement Points
docs.text:
• Role in nl2sql.config.models (the pattern shape, through nl2sql.policies.patterns.parse_pattern)
  • LogicalValidatorNode._validate_policy() in nl2sql.pipeline.nodes.validator.node
  • Scope and PolicyEngine in nl2sql.policies.scope, asked with the same datasource, schema and table by the datasource resolver, the curated matcher, the schema retriever (which hides denied tables from the planner), the validator, the executor's value check and engine.policies.allows()
  • test_every_access_decision_goes_through_scope in packages/nl2sql/tests/architecture/test_boundaries.py

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text: ValueError for an invalid pattern; PipelineError with SECURITY_VIOLATION if datasource ID is missing or a table is not allowed. An unknown role, or no role, allows nothing and is refused the same way, never with VALIDATOR_CRASH. The user-facing refusal names no table unless policies.refusal_names_tables is set; the table, the roles and the rule are in the error's details.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: Ensures access control boundaries are explicit and enforced.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text: Only datasources the caller's scope reaches (Scope.reaches_datasource()) may be selected or resolved.

docs.title: Enforcement Points
docs.text:
• DatasourceResolverNode._get_allowed_datasource_ids() and __call__() in nl2sql.pipeline.nodes.datasource_resolver.node
  • CuratedMatcherNode._searchable() and _check_access() in nl2sql.pipeline.nodes.curated_matcher.node: the verified-query search covers only datasources the role may read, and every table a verified query's SQL reads must pass Scope.allows()

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text: Returns PipelineError with SECURITY_VIOLATION if no allowed datasource is available. The check runs before the resolver's answerability LLM call, so a denied caller triggers no model call and the model only ever sees datasources the role may read. It runs on every path, including the single-datasource shortcut that skips the vector search. The curated matcher refuses nothing itself: a verified query on a datasource or table the role may not read is never offered or never run, and the run falls back (policy_denied) to the resolver, which refuses as above.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: Prevents execution against unauthorized datasources.

docs.title: Events Carry No Rows, and the Stream Carries No Operator Data
Definition
docs.text: No event on the engine's bus carries result rows, sample values, keys or header values; the question and the answer text are carried and may hold values from the data. Every published name is in the event catalog, whose model for it forbids extra keys. A caller's own stream (stream_query) yields only its run's events on the caller-safe allow-list (STREAM_EVENTS, the catalog entries marked stream); the full QueryResult is only on the stream's copy of run.finished, never on the bus.

docs.title: Enforcement Points
docs.text:
• EventBus.publish and the catalog in nl2sql.events (CATALOG, STREAM_EVENTS)
  • QueryAPI.stream_query in nl2sql.api.query_api (subscribes to its scope with the allow-list only)
  • test_no_bus_event_carries_rows in packages/nl2sql/tests/e2e/test_run_events_fake_llm.py, test_stream_never_yields_policy_or_hook_or_llm_call_events in packages/nl2sql/tests/unit/test_stream_query.py, and test_every_published_event_is_in_the_catalog in packages/nl2sql/tests/architecture/test_event_catalog.py

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text: An uncatalogued name, or data its model refuses, is a ValueError or a validation error from publish: an engine bug a test sees. An event off the allow-list never reaches the stream; an operator reads it with engine.events.subscribe.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: Observers write events to logs, files and collectors outside the engine's access control, so rows must never reach them; and a stream is the caller's, so a policy denial (which would tell a denied user that a table exists), a hook's reasons or a model's cost must not reach it.

docs.title: Observers Fail Open and Never Block
Definition
docs.text: An observer (the observers section, or engine.events.subscribe) can never fail a run or an engine call: what it raises is logged once per observer and event name and skipped. It never blocks either: the bus delivers a run's events one at a time under the run's lock, so an observer that writes to disk or the network hands that work to a thread of its own (the audit observer queues its lines on a bounded queue, dropping and counting what does not fit; the otel observer records in memory and its SDK exports in the background). Hooks are the opposite: they fail closed (Hooks Modify Before the Validator, Deny After).

docs.title: Enforcement Points
docs.text:
• EventBus.publish in nl2sql.events.bus (subscribers made with fail="open", the default for observers)
  • AuditObserver in nl2sql.observers.audit (a queue and a writer thread; a failed write is logged)
  • test_observer_exception_is_logged_once_and_skipped and test_audit_never_blocks_the_publisher in packages/nl2sql/tests/unit/test_observers.py, and test_a_raising_subscriber_never_fails_the_run in packages/nl2sql/tests/unit/test_events_api.py

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text: A WARNING on logger nl2sql.events, once per observer and event name, and EventBus.failures counts it. The run goes on.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: Observing must not change the answer. A full disk, a collector that is down or a plugin bug would otherwise fail every question, and a slow write would hold every run's lock.

docs.title: SQL Execution Requires SQL, Datasource, and Capability
Definition
docs.text: Execution only proceeds when SQL text exists, a datasource ID is present, and the datasource supports SQL.

docs.title: Enforcement Points
docs.text:
• ExecutorNode.__call__() in nl2sql.pipeline.nodes.executor.node
  • SqlExecutorService.validate_request() in nl2sql.execution.executor.sql_executor

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text: Returns PipelineError with MISSING_SQL, MISSING_DATASOURCE_ID, or INVALID_STATE.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: Prevents invalid execution requests and ensures capability compatibility.

docs.title: Execution DAG Must Be Valid and Acyclic
Definition
docs.text: Post-combine ops must target known combine groups, all edges must reference existing nodes, and the DAG must be acyclic.

docs.title: Enforcement Points
docs.text:
• build_execution_dag() in nl2sql.pipeline.nodes.decomposer.dag, called by DecomposerNode.__call__()
  • ExecutionDAG._layered_toposort() in nl2sql.execution.dag

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text: Raises ValueError, leading to PipelineError with PLANNER_FAILED.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: Ensures deterministic and well-ordered aggregation execution.

docs.title: Aggregation Requires Scan Artifacts and Single-Input Post Nodes
Definition
docs.text: Scan nodes must have corresponding artifacts, and post-combine nodes must have exactly one input. The one exception is a scan a hook dropped (a deny scoped to its sub-query): it has no artifact, a join or compare group it feeds is dropped whole with its post-combine nodes, and another group goes on without it.

docs.title: Enforcement Points
docs.text:
• AggregationService.execute() in nl2sql.aggregation.aggregator (its dropped argument)
  • EngineAggregatorNode in nl2sql.pipeline.nodes.aggregator.node, which passes the sub-queries whose output is dropped

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text: Raises ValueError when artifacts are missing or post nodes have invalid inputs. A dropped group is a HOOK_DENIED warning; when hooks dropped every part of the question, the aggregator ends the run with HOOK_DENIED.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: Guarantees aggregation operates on complete, correctly wired inputs.

docs.title: An Engine Keeps Its Data Under storage.path
Definition
docs.text: storage is a required section of the config. An engine keeps its vector index in <storage.path>/index/, its schema snapshots, plan cache and feedback in <storage.path>/state.db, its traces in <storage.path>/traces/, its result files in <storage.path>/results/ and, with the audit observer, its audit log in <storage.path>/audit/. The index collection name is an internal constant.

docs.title: Enforcement Points
docs.text:
• Config in nl2sql.config (the section is required)
  • Runtime.from_config() in nl2sql.runtime (each slot's store, built with folder=storage.path)

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text: A config without storage is a ConfigError from load_config, or a validation error building Config in code.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: There is no hidden default for where data lives, and two engines with different storage.path values never share a store.

docs.title: SQL Generation Enforces a Row Limit Cap
Definition
docs.text: Generated SQL must not exceed the row limit: the datasource adapter’s row_limit, bounded by the RESULT_ROW_LIMIT ceiling (100,000), which is also the limit when the datasource sets none. A result that reaches the limit is flagged as truncated. Verified SQL is held to the same limit, but a person's SQL is never rewritten: the executor stops reading its result at the limit (ExecutorRequest.max_rows).

docs.title: Enforcement Points
docs.text:
• GeneratorNode.__call__() in nl2sql.pipeline.nodes.generator.node
  • wrap_subgraph() in nl2sql.pipeline.graph_utils sets SubgraphOutput.truncated, which QueryResult and the answer carry
  • CuratedMatcherNode._run() sets max_rows and truncated for a verified query; _Stream in nl2sql.execution.executor.sql_executor stops at max_rows and closes the adapter's stream

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text: No error; the limit is clamped to the smaller of the two. A cut result is flagged (truncated), and the answer says it was cut at N rows.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: Protects execution resources and prevents runaway result sizes, without passing off a cut result as complete.

docs.title: The Answer Model Sees a Preview, Never the Whole Result
Definition
docs.text: The answer synthesizer's prompt carries at most ANSWER_PREVIEW_ROWS (20) rows of each result, with its total row count, its column names and a partial flag. The model is told to state only numbers from the preview or the count, and not to reproduce the result.

docs.title: Enforcement Points
docs.text: • result_preview() and AnswerSynthesizerNode._serialize_result() in nl2sql.pipeline.nodes.answer_synthesizer.node

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text: None; rows past the preview are left out of the prompt.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: The prompt's size must not grow with the result: that is what kept the row limit at 1,000. The user sees the full result as a table, so the model has no need to copy it.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text: Pipeline execution must complete within settings.global_timeout_sec.

docs.title: Enforcement Points
docs.text: • run_with_graph() in nl2sql.pipeline.runtime

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text: Returns PipelineError with PIPELINE_TIMEOUT and a timeout response message.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: Ensures latency bounds and prevents hung requests.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
Dependencies point in one direction: nl2sql-sdk → nothing, nl2sql.adapters.* → the SDK, nl2sql (the engine) → the SDK, and every caller — the REST API, the CLI, the playground — → the top-level nl2sql facade.

Concretely:

  • The SDK's core imports only pydantic and the standard library. nl2sql_sdk.sqlalchemy, the SQLAlchemy base installed with nl2sql-sdk[sqlalchemy], may also import SQLAlchemy and sqlglot, and the core never imports it. nl2sql_sdk.testing, the conformance kit installed with nl2sql-sdk[testing], may import pytest and sqlglot, but not SQLAlchemy: it checks an adapter through DatasourceAdapter alone.
  • An adapter imports only the SDK, its driver, SQLAlchemy, sqlglot, pydantic and the standard library. SQLAlchemy and sqlglot are adapter-layer libraries: the shared connection layer, and the expression vocabulary the engine hands over to be rendered.
  • Nothing outside nl2sql/adapters/ (and the SDK's SQLAlchemy base) imports an adapter, SQLAlchemy or a database driver. The engine reaches an adapter through the nl2sql.adapters entry points and DatasourceAdapter.
  • Only nl2sql/storage/ imports chromadb (or langchain_chroma). The engine embeds, ranks and filters through the IndexStore interface (nl2sql_sdk.stores), so a plugin index store works the same way as the built-in chroma one. The one exception is the local embedder, nl2sql/embeddings/local.py, whose model is the ONNX all-MiniLM-L6-v2 that ships inside chromadb.
  • Only nl2sql/storage/ imports sqlite3. Schema snapshots, the plan cache, feedback and the index lock are reached through the StateStore interface, so a plugin state store works the same way as the built-in sqlite one. The SQLite adapter (its driver) reads a datasource, not the engine's state, and is exempt. An eval suite's expected rows come through the datasource's adapter, so nothing in nl2sql/evaluation/ imports sqlite3 (test_gold_does_not_import_sqlite3).
  • Nothing outside nl2sql/cli/ imports the CLI, and nl2sql.cli.demo never imports nl2sql.cli.commands.
  • nl2sql_api imports only the top-level nl2sql namespace, and so do the playground and nl2sql demo, apart from a named list of exceptions (STILL_IMPORTED_FROM_INSIDE: the provider catalogue in llm/providers.py, the hosted demo's per-request keys, and the demo's replay machinery and questions). In particular they never import nl2sql.feedback, nl2sql.tracing, nl2sql.pipeline, nl2sql.indexing or PROVIDER_PRESETS: engine.feedback, engine.traces.get, engine.about(), engine.index.inspect_defaults() and engine.llm.providers() serve them. The CLI, the playground and nl2sql_api reach the engine only through NL2SQL's public methods and namespaces, never the runtime behind them (engine._runtime, a namespace's _ctx). The MCP server (nl2sql/mcp/) imports only the top-level nl2sql and, under the same rule, never the runtime; it is the only code that imports mcp, the mcp extra (test_mcp_uses_only_the_public_api). The chat tools (nl2sql/chat_tools/, from Wave C) are held to the same rule: each tool module imports only the top-level nl2sql and its own interface module, and its __init__ also the strict model base and the conversation shapes (CHAT_TOOLS_INIT_MAY_IMPORT; test_chat_tools_use_only_the_public_api). Only nl2sql/mcp/, nl2sql/cli/demo/ and nl2sql/cli/commands/demo.py import Starlette, FastAPI or Uvicorn (test_only_mcp_and_the_demo_import_starlette_or_uvicorn). The SDK's FastMCP settings are pydantic-settings that read FASTMCP_* variables and the working directory's .env; the server passes every setting explicitly, so neither changes it, and nothing is written.
  • The runtime (pipeline, execution, indexing, datasources, llm, policies, aggregation, schema, services, context, public_api) never imports nl2sql.evaluation or nl2sql.feedback at module scope. A deferred import inside a function is fine.
  • A provider's API-key environment variable is read in nl2sql/llm/ only. PROVIDER_PRESETS (llm/registry.py) is the one table; everything the CLI, the playground, evaluation and the REST API know about providers derives from it through llm/providers.py.

docs.title: Enforcement Points
docs.text:
• packages/nl2sql/tests/architecture/test_boundaries.py — an AST import scan of packages/*/src, one test per rule
  • packages/api/tests/test_architecture.py — the REST API's own imports, and that its response model is nl2sql.QueryResult

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text: A failing test naming the rule and the file, line and import that broke it. Each documented exception is a named constant in the test module with the reason beside it.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: Each rule keeps one thing replaceable. The SDK is what a third-party adapter compiles against, so a dependency there is a dependency every adapter author inherits; an adapter that imported the engine would close the circle and make the split meaningless. Engine code that imports an adapter, or SQLAlchemy, is a second way to reach a database that no new adapter can plug into. And import nl2sql loading nl2sql.evaluation cost every SDK user the YAML loaders, the eval suites and the fake LLM before anyone asked a question.

docs.title: Example
docs.text: The playground once read engine.context.ds_registry, engine.context.schema_store and engine.context.vector_store through getattr, so the schema view, the retrieval inspector and index health existed only in the playground; nl2sql-api had a placeholder where index status should be. The fix was facade methods that both callers use. Later the CLI's run, index and trace replay built on the runtime too; they now use stream_query's events, engine.index.build's IndexProgress callback and engine.traces.replay. The playground then still imported the feedback store, the trace reader, the pipeline's step list and the provider presets; those are engine.feedback, engine.traces.get, engine.about() and engine.llm.providers() now, which nl2sql feedback uses too. The rule stops the shortcut being taken again, which is what keeps a second client cheap.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
import nl2sql loads none of chromadb, onnxruntime, sqlalchemy, psycopg2, psycopg, pymysql, pyodbc, pymssql, duckdb, duckdb_engine, textual, opentelemetry or mcp, and its imports stay under 500 ms.

Concretely:

  • nl2sql/__init__.py imports only the NL2SQL class. Every other public name (QueryResult, Event, CancellationToken, the API classes, the eval shapes) is imported the first time it is asked for, through the module's __getattr__. from nl2sql import QueryResult works as it always did.
  • nl2sql/public_api.py imports the runtime (Runtime and the API classes) inside NL2SQL.__init__, not at the top of the module.
  • Runtime modules import their heavy libraries where they are used, as the adapters already do.
  • Only nl2sql/observers/otel.py imports opentelemetry, and only inside the observer: OpenTelemetry is the otel extra, and an engine without an otel observer never loads that module.

docs.title: Enforcement Points
docs.text:
• test_only_the_otel_observer_imports_opentelemetry, test_the_otel_observer_imports_opentelemetry_only_when_it_is_built and test_building_an_engine_loads_no_otel_observer in packages/nl2sql/tests/architecture/test_boundaries.py. A built engine may still have opentelemetry in sys.modules: chromadb, a core dependency, installs its SDK, and langsmith imports it whenever it is installed. The rule holds the engine's own code.
  • test_importing_nl2sql_loads_no_heavy_library in packages/nl2sql/tests/architecture/test_boundaries.py — imports nl2sql in a fresh interpreter and checks sys.modules
  • test_import_nl2sql_stays_within_its_time_budget in the same module — the cumulative figure python -X importtime reports for nl2sql, best of five, under 500 ms. It measures imports only, not wall-clock time, so a busy runner does not fail it.

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text: A failing test naming the heavy libraries that were loaded, or the import time against the budget.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: Code that only needs a name — a type hint, nl2sql --help, a config check in CI, a REST client building a request — should not pay for a vector store, a database driver and a tracing stack. import nl2sql used to load chromadb, duckdb, opentelemetry, langgraph, langchain_openai and polars and took about 2.2 seconds; it now takes about 15 ms. The cost moves to NL2SQL(...), which needs the runtime anyway.

docs.title: An Engine Owns Its Config: No Process Globals
Definition
docs.text:
Everything an engine reads comes from its own Config, handed down through the runtime (ctx.settings, ctx.config) or passed as a parameter. Nothing is process-global, so two engines in one process share nothing.

Concretely:

  • There is no settings singleton. A module with no runtime takes the value it needs as a parameter (run_date(today), PlanCache(store, enabled=..., today=...)).
  • No module writes the process environment: no os.environ assignment, pop or update, no os.putenv. Keys and options travel in the Config. nl2sql demo --api-key and a key saved in the playground's settings panel are written to the demo's .env and given to the engine as a value in its LLM config, never put in os.environ; nl2sql demo --hosted refuses to start when a provider key variable is set rather than drop it.
  • The environment is read from an allow-list only: NL2SQL_CONFIG (nl2sql/config/), NL2SQL_LOG_LEVEL and NL2SQL_LOG_FORMAT (configure_logging), the provider key variables (nl2sql/llm/, through PROVIDER_PRESETS), ${env:VAR} references (nl2sql/config/ and the env secret provider), the trace redactor, which masks every value the environment holds, and, from Wave C, DATABASE_URL, read by nl2sql/cli/commands/launch.py alone (nl2sql launch offers it as a candidate; it is also an entry point that loads the .env it has just written). Anything else is configuration and is written in nl2sql.yaml, as ${env:VAR} where it should come from the environment.
  • Only the entry points load a .env file: the CLI, nl2sql demo and nl2sql-api call nl2sql.config.load_env_file(), which loads the .env next to nl2sql.yaml and never overrides a variable already set. It is the one place that calls load_dotenv. The library never reads a .env; a Python caller who wants one loads it before NL2SQL.from_config().
  • Runs that need different settings (evaluation, trace replay) take a run-scoped runtime with a derived config (ctx.derive(...)) instead of editing shared state.

docs.title: Enforcement Points
docs.text:
• test_no_module_writes_the_environment, test_environment_reads_only_from_the_allow_list and test_only_entry_points_load_dotenv in packages/nl2sql/tests/architecture/test_boundaries.py, an AST scan of packages/*/src (READS_THE_ENVIRONMENT names each allowed reader and why); the first also scans scripts/, so a maintenance script passes keys as arguments instead of writing the environment
  • packages/nl2sql/tests/e2e/test_two_engines_fake_llm.py — two engines in one process, each with its own row limit, plan cache, LLM, embedder and storage, and os.environ unchanged afterwards

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text: A failing test naming the file, line and the write or read that broke the rule.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: 0.4 kept its settings in a process-global object that every module imported, and carried keys and options through os.environ. Two engines in one process (a test, a server with two configs, an evaluation run beside live traffic) then read each other's values, an evaluation that pinned a setting raced every other query, and a key set for one engine leaked into every other engine and child process.

docs.title: Dialect Knowledge Lives in the Adapter
Definition
docs.text: No engine module names a database dialect or writes one database's SQL. The plan says what; the adapter says how. An adapter declares its dialect with get_dialect(), which must return a name sqlglot.Dialect.get_or_raise accepts, and may override render_sql() for what sqlglot cannot express.

docs.title: Enforcement Points
docs.text:
• test_no_dialect_name_outside_the_adapters and test_no_dialect_specific_sql_outside_the_adapters in packages/nl2sql/tests/architecture/test_boundaries.py — a scan of every non-docstring string literal, f-string chunks included
  • test_get_dialect_is_a_sqlglot_dialect, over every nl2sql.adapters entry point
  • The plan's one function vocabulary: ALLOWED_FUNCTIONS in nl2sql.pipeline.nodes.ast_planner.functions (see Plan Functions Are Known Functions)

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text: A failing test naming the literal and where it was written. The documented exceptions are the engine's own state store, a SQLite file by default (storage/sqlite.py), the in-process polars/DuckDB compute engine (aggregation/engines/polars_duckdb.py), and the plan's function allow-list.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: SQL that only one database understands, written in the engine, is wrong for every other database — and it is wrong silently, because it parses. A dialect name in engine code is worse: it is a switch statement that every future adapter has to be added to, in a repo whose point is that adapters are pluggable.

docs.title: Example
docs.text: The planner prompt asked for STRFTIME('%Y', o.order_date) to get a year. On SQLite that works; on Postgres and SQL Server it is a call to a function that does not exist, and on MySQL it means something else. The fix was not to teach the prompt about dialects but to move the decision: the plan asks for DATE_PART('year', x), the generator builds a typed sqlglot node, and SQLiteAdapter.render_sql() rewrites it to STRFTIME for SQLite only. Related: get_dialect() returned SQLAlchemy's postgresql and mssql, which sqlglot rejects, so no SQL could be generated for either datasource — a one-word bug that the entry-point contract test now catches.

docs.title: The Validator Rejects Everything the Generator Can
Definition
docs.text: Anything the generator can refuse, the logical validator must refuse first. The validator is the last node with a retry edge back to the planner; the generator runs after it.

docs.title: Enforcement Points
docs.text:
• packages/nl2sql/tests/unit/test_logical_validator_generator_parity.py — each case asserts both halves: the generator rejects the plan, and so does the validator, with a retryable code
  • LogicalValidatorNode._validate_static() in nl2sql.pipeline.nodes.validator.node

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text: A structural mistake is returned as a retryable PipelineError from the validator, so check_logical_validation sends the plan back to the refiner and the planner sees the message. The same mistake reaching the generator is a terminal SQL_GEN_FAILED.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: A check that lives only in the generator is a dead end rather than a retry. The model produced a fixable plan and got a hard failure, one node past the only gate that could have asked it to try again.

docs.title: Example
docs.text: The validator resolves columns against a throw-away query in which every table is CROSS JOINed — correct for column resolution, and deliberately blind to join topology. So a plan declaring three tables and joining only two validated CLEAN, then failed in the generator with "Table alias(es) t3 are declared in the plan but never joined to the FROM table." Three more join-shape mistakes behaved the same way. Every one is a pure function of plan.tables and plan.joins — no schema, no dialect — so each belongs in the validator, where the message reaches the planner.

docs.title: Verified SQL Is Human-Authored, Read-Only and Parameter-Bound
Definition
docs.text: A verified query's SQL is written by a person in curated.yaml, or proposed (from a thumbs-up or a correction) and reviewed and accepted by a person through the review queue. The model picks a verified query by id and supplies parameter values; it never writes or edits the SQL. The SQL must be exactly one read-only query whose :name placeholders are exactly its declared params. Values are typed and checked by code (type, min/max, choices, required) and bound by the adapter's driver, never interpolated into the SQL text. A query with params runs only on an adapter that declares SUPPORTS_BOUND_PARAMETERS.

docs.title: Enforcement Points
docs.text:
• VerifiedQuery and ParamSpec in nl2sql.config.curated, and inspect_verified_sql() and check_curated_queries() in nl2sql.configs.curated, at startup, in nl2sql curated validate, and in nl2sql curated test (CuratedAPI.test()), which runs only queries that pass them, with their values bound
  • resolve_params() in nl2sql.pipeline.nodes.curated_matcher.params
  • CuratedMatcherNode._match() in nl2sql.pipeline.nodes.curated_matcher.node: parses the SQL read-only again before running, and checks the capability
  • SQLAlchemyAdapter._run() in nl2sql_sdk.sqlalchemy.adapter: conn.execute(text(sql), parameters); without parameters the call is exactly conn.execute(text(sql))
  • packages/nl2sql/tests/sqlalchemy_base/test_bound_parameters.py: a value 1; DROP TABLE x is compared as a value and the table survives

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text: A broken file fails startup. At question time a bad value, a denied table, a missing capability or a failed run falls back to the generated pipeline with a reason code in the matcher's trace record; it is never an error of the run. A hook's deny at execute.before or execute.after is different: it ends the run with HOOK_DENIED and does not fall back, because a deny means no.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: The model emits a typed plan, never SQL holds on this path too: no model wrote the SQL, and a value cannot change what the query does.

docs.title: Hooks Modify Before the Validator, Deny After
Definition
docs.text: A hook may change what a run carries only through a Modify, and only at the three points before the logical validator: the question at run.before, the datasources at datasources.after (a subset only, checked against the caller's scope again) and the plan at plan.after. A plan a hook changed is validated like any other. At execute.before, execute.after and answer.after a hook may only allow or stop the run (or, at execute.before, ask for approval). Hooks fail closed: an exception, a value that is not a decision, or a decision the point does not allow denies with HOOK_FAILED; on_error: open lets an exception through as an allow, never a disallowed decision. The plan cache stores the planner's plan, never a hook's change of it.

docs.title: Enforcement Points
docs.text:
• HOOK_POINTS in nl2sql.hooks.points (what each point allows) and HookRunner.call() in nl2sql.hooks.runner
  • ASTPlannerNode.after_plan() in nl2sql.pipeline.nodes.ast_planner.node: every plan the validator gets (the planner's, a cached one, a supplied one) passes plan.after there
  • wrap_subgraph() in nl2sql.pipeline.graph_utils caches ASTPlannerResponse.planner_plan
  • HookRunner.call() hands hooks deep copies of the plan, the caller, the sub-query and the values, so a hook that changes one in place changes nothing: test_a_hook_changing_the_callers_roles_in_place_changes_nothing, test_a_hook_changing_the_plan_in_place_changes_nothing, test_a_shallow_copy_modify_leaves_the_planners_plan_alone and test_a_hook_changing_the_params_in_place_changes_nothing in packages/nl2sql/tests/unit/test_hook_points.py
  • test_hooks_modify_only_before_the_validator in packages/nl2sql/tests/architecture/test_hooks_boundary.py: the point table, an AST scan of every runner call (each names its point as a literal, and no other call passes a point name along), and the SQL agent graph, in which every path from the planner to the generator passes the validator

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text: A deny is HOOK_DENIED, a hook error HOOK_FAILED (its message names the hook and the point only; the exception goes to the log and hook.decision), an approval request NEEDS_APPROVAL; the built-in cost hook's deny is COST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED; none is retried. A run-scoped one ends the run once the step in flight is done, and its result carries no rows, artifact references or result manifest. A deny scoped to a sub-query drops it (and a join or compare group it feeds), and the answer says what went unanswered.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: The validator rejects everything the generator can would mean nothing if code could change the plan or the SQL after the validator: a hook could otherwise route around the policies, including a table the role may not read.

docs.title: Only an Accept Writes a Person's File
Definition
docs.text: The engine writes two files a person owns, and only from the review queue's accept: the first yaml knowledge source's glossary.yaml and the curated section's own file. An accept needs by with one of policies.admin_roles (any caller under allow_all). For each file it takes the state store's lock accept:<real path>, refuses when the file's SHA-256 is no longer the one the engine loaded, applies every accepted item, runs the item's checks (the glossary's validation; the curated checks for a verified query), and rewrites the file once, canonically and atomically (a temporary file renamed over the real path, through a symlink). An inline curated section, a config built in code, or a project without a yaml knowledge source is never written. Nothing a model or a thumbs-up produced reaches either file, or a prompt, before an accept.

docs.title: Enforcement Points
docs.text:
• accept() in nl2sql.review.accept, through engine.proposals.accept and apply; the admin check is require_admin() in nl2sql.review.queue
  • write_glossary() in nl2sql.knowledge.yaml_source and write_curated() in nl2sql.review.curated_file: the hash check, the atomic rewrite
  • test_only_accept_writes_a_persons_file in packages/nl2sql/tests/architecture/test_boundaries.py: an AST scan allowing calls of the two writers only in nl2sql/review/accept.py. Wave C's amended list (PERSONS_FILE_WRITERS, D123) also names write_project (only config/project.py and nl2sql launch) and write_env_values (only datasources.save and nl2sql launch); the definition above is amended when they are built (L2)
  • packages/nl2sql/tests/unit/test_review_queue.py: the admin role, the hash check, the lock, an inline section, the curated checks

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text: ReviewError with NOT_AUTHORIZED, NOT_WRITABLE or FILE_CHANGED, and nothing written: every file is locked and checked before the first write. Each file's items are recorded as accepted under its lock right after its write, so the queue always matches the files: if a later write fails, the items already written stay accepted and the rest stay proposed. An item whose change fails its checks stays proposed and is named in AcceptReport.refused; the others are written.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: The glossary and the curated answers are what people know and vouch for. An engine that edited them on its own would turn a model's guess into a fact without anyone deciding so, and two writers that did not check the file would lose a person's edit.

docs.title: Saved Answers Run as the Caller
Definition
docs.text: A conversation stores what a turn said and found, never a permission. Every method of engine.conversations takes the caller, and each turn's questions run through run_query with the user_context passed to that call, not the one the conversation was started with: a role taken away applies at the next turn. A conversation belongs to the (tenant_id, user_id) that started it; any other caller is told it does not exist. A caller with no user_id is refused (TypeError), never mapped to a shared owner. A stored step keeps its plan, SQL and explanation but never the rows of its sub-queries, and a stored tool output never holds rows either: a chart output has an empty data.rows and the report tool's body has no row tables or takeaways, so reading a result again goes through engine.results (and conversations.report, which reads it). engine.results does not check the caller: it reads a run's results by tenant and trace id alone, so the trace id is the only access control until the separate row that records the asker in the manifest lands. The model sees summaries and column names, never rows. (Dashboards extend this rule in Wave C's D rows.)

docs.title: Enforcement Points
docs.text:
• ConversationStore.get in nl2sql.conversations.store: the owner check behind every method
  • Conversations._ask in nl2sql.conversations.api: each step calls run_query with the turn's caller; strip_rows removes the rows before a step is stored
  • test_other_users_conversation_is_not_found, test_turn_runs_with_the_callers_roles_not_the_starters, test_stored_turn_has_no_rows, test_model_never_sees_rows in packages/nl2sql/tests/unit/test_conversations.py; test_owned_and_privileged_methods_require_a_caller in the boundary test

docs.title: Failure Behavior
docs.text: ConversationNotFound for an id that is missing or another owner's, with the same message for both.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: A conversation outlives the request that began it. If it carried the starter's roles, a person who lost access, or anyone who learned its id, would keep reading what the roles allowed.

docs.title: Categories
docs.text:
• State: Plan Model Is Strict and Read-Only; Context Requires Vector Store and Schema Store Configuration
  • Execution: SQL Execution Requires SQL, Datasource, and Capability; Execution DAG Must Be Valid and Acyclic; Aggregation Requires Scan Artifacts and Single-Input Post Nodes; Pipeline Execution Is Time-Bounded
  • Security: Policy Enforcement Is Namespaced and Fail-Closed; Datasource Access Is Policy-Gated; Plan Model Is Strict and Read-Only; Verified SQL Is Human-Authored, Read-Only and Parameter-Bound; Hooks Modify Before the Validator, Deny After; Only an Accept Writes a Person's File; Saved Answers Run as the Caller
  • Determinism: Expected Schema Must Match Select List; Joins Must Be Valid and Schema-Backed
  • Resource bounds: SQL Generation Enforces a Row Limit Cap; The Answer Model Sees a Preview, Never the Whole Result; Context Requires Vector Store and Schema Store Configuration
  • Boundaries: Package Boundaries Are One-Way; Importing nl2sql Is Light; An Engine Owns Its Config: No Process Globals; Dialect Knowledge Lives in the Adapter
  • Retryability: The Validator Rejects Everything the Generator Can; Plan Functions Are Known Functions
  • Observability: Events Carry No Rows, and the Stream Carries No Operator Data; Observers Fail Open and Never Block

docs.title: Gaps
docs.text:
• Column existence enforcement degrades to warnings when settings.pipeline.strict_columns is turned off (it is on by default), so missing columns then do not always block execution.
  • Semantic-only checks are pattern based: they block a field that opens with SELECT ... FROM, a statement terminator and comment markers, rather than parsing for every possible SQL construct. An intent that literally reads "select ... from ..." is rejected as SQL.
