docs.title: Phase 2: test bed, storage, providers, policies and adapter SDK v2 (design)
docs.text:
Status: design

This page is the design for Phase 2 of the redesign, which ships as release 0.6. Nothing on it is built yet. Each pull request in the PR plan adds a "Built" note to the sections it builds, as Phase 1 did. Phase 1 is described in Configuration v2 and the extension registry.

docs.title: Principles
docs.text:
The Phase 1 principles still hold, and the owner restated them for Phase 2:

  • No users yet, so design it correctly, not compatibly. No shims, no aliases, no deprecation periods. Where a 0.5 shape is wrong, 0.6 replaces it.
  • Never over-engineer. Ship what 0.6 needs. Anything that can wait, does.
  • Prefer extension points over built-ins. A small interface and a way to register your own beats another built-in we have to maintain.
  • No database-specific code outside adapters. The plan says what; the adapter says how.
  • The package is the product. The CLI, nl2sql-api and the playground use the public API only.

One more rule comes from how Phase 2 was ordered: nothing about a real database is designed from memory. Until now every test ran against SQLite, DuckDB and mocks. Phase 2 builds a test bed with real PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQL Server first, and the adapter work is proven on it.

docs.title: Owner decisions
docs.text:
The owner answered every question this design raised, and confirmed the choices it made on its own. Each answer is written into the section it affects.

# Decision Where 1 No Cloud SQL. A stopped Cloud SQL instance still bills its public IPv4 address, so the test bed is one compose file instead, run locally, in CI and on one small GCP VM. The real-database test bed 2 CI runs the real databases only when they matter: on pull requests that change database-facing code, nightly on main, and on demand before a release. A small gate job that always runs is the required check, so a skipped run passes honestly. The containers run on GitHub's runners. CI: the realdb workflow 3 The GCP test bed is one small VM running the same compose file, started and stopped on demand, with an ephemeral external IP, no public database port, and access through IAP tunnels. A nightly scheduler job stops it. There are no GitHub-to-GCP credentials: it is run by hand, at least before each release. The GCP VM 4 SQL Server declares ENFORCES_READ_ONLY false, check() warns, and the docs recommend a login with only db_datareader. Read-only and timeouts, honestly 5 Two-part policy patterns are rejected, with the fix in the message. Pattern rules 6 No S3 or ADLS result store in 0.6. The ResultStore interface ships with a docs example; a community plugin can come later. The interfaces 7 Built-in LLM providers stay minimal: openai, anthropic and openai_compatible. There is no azure_openai; Azure's v1 endpoint, vLLM, LiteLLM and any other OpenAI-style server use openai_compatible with a base_url. openrouter and ollama stay as named presets of openai_compatible: a fixed base_url and key variable, with no code path of their own. Everything else is a plugin through the provider interface and the registry. The same holds for embeddings. LLM and embeddings providers 8 Read-only always. There is no per-datasource read_only setting: every adapter makes its session read-only whenever it can. Read-only and timeouts, honestly 9 Sample values are off by default (index.sample_values: false); the demo turns them on. IndexScope: what gets indexed 10 Policy patterns match regardless of case, so a deny cannot be dodged by Orders against orders. Pattern rules 11 A PolicyCheck is called once per user and datasource per run, with no cache across runs. The PolicyCheck extension point 12 The runtime price table moves to Phase 3 with the cost observer, and the REST routes for Connect a database to Phase 4; Phase 2 ships the package methods. Not in Phase 2

docs.title: Where Phase 1 left us
docs.text: Area What 0.5 has What is still wrong Config One typed Config from nl2sql.yaml and split files; strict keys; ${provider:key} references Nothing for Phase 2 to fix Registry Registry.default(), add_* and decorators for adapters, LLMs, embeddings and secrets No store or policy-check kinds yet Storage storage.path only. Under it: Chroma in index/, state.db, traces/, results/ One store class per thing, opened by path, Chroma private attributes used throughout, and bug B5 LLMs openai, anthropic, openrouter, ollama; per-agent provider, model, temperature, key and base_url No general OpenAI-compatible provider that the presets build on; one malformed structured answer ends the run Embeddings local and openai No base_url; a model change is refused instead of building a new index Policies allow_all, default_role, admin_roles, refusal_names_tables, roles with allowed_datasources and allowed_tables No deny; no globs; five call sites of table_allowed; denied tables still shown to the planner; no extension point Adapters Interface version 1 with driver_modules and install_hint; typed connection models hidden inside each adapter Unknown connection keys are ignored, read-only is enforced only on SQLite with an option, test_connection returns a bool, profiling reflects twice and counts every row

docs.title: What ships in 0.6
docs.text: Goal What it means A real-database test bed PostgreSQL with Pagila, MySQL with Sakila and SQL Server 2022 with AdventureWorksLT, plus a generated schema of 1,200 tables in 20 schemas. One docker-compose.yml runs them locally, on GitHub's runners in CI, and on one small GCP VM started on demand. A realdb pytest marker and fixtures point the same tests at any of them. Four stores storage gets index, state, traces and results, each with a type, behind four small interfaces in the SDK. The index's build pointer is the commit, which fixes bug B5. The index has one namespace per embedding model. A general LLM provider openai, anthropic and openai_compatible (any server with an OpenAI-style API at a base_url: Azure's v1 endpoint, vLLM, LiteLLM), with openrouter and ollama kept as named presets of it. Each provider declares how it returns structured output, and a malformed answer is retried with the error fed back. Embeddings providers local, openai and openai_compatible, base_url on the hosted ones, and a known model and dimension for every embedder. Policies, step 1 Allow and deny globs over datasource.schema.table, one Scope object used at every place access is decided, denied tables hidden from the planner, and a PolicyCheck extension point. Adapter SDK v2 A typed ConnectionModel per adapter (which also drives a generated form), IndexScope, type-aware profiling with catalog row estimates, honest read-only and timeout capabilities checked against real servers, test_connection that names the failed stage, the SQLAlchemy base made public as an SDK extra, and a conformance kit run against all five built-in adapters. Connect a database, in the package engine.datasources.types(), test() and add(): the package methods a Connect-a-database form calls.

docs.title: Not in Phase 2
docs.text: Later Why it waits Where it goes PostgreSQL state store and pgvector index (multi-replica) Single replica is enough until someone runs several. The interfaces are written so these are plugins or built-ins later. Later (owner) deny_columns, row filters, user attributes Step 2 and 3 of the policy ladder Later (owner) JWT and identity-provider groups mapped to roles They belong to the API's role resolver Phase 4 (apps), JWT later (owner) dbt as a knowledge source Needs the knowledge-source interface Later (owner) Async hooks; any event bus or hook Nothing in Phase 2 consumes events Phase 3, designed as Wave A Snowflake and BigQuery adapters The conformance kit comes first; a community package passes it, then is adopted Later (owner) S3 or ADLS result stores The results interface ships with a docs example; remote stores come as plugins (owner decision 6) Later The runtime price table owned by llm/ It belongs with the cost observer Phase 3 REST routes and forms for Connect a database, datasources.scan() and draft() The package methods ship first; the apps render them Phase 4 Retrieval limits as settings, incremental re-indexing The wide schema in the test bed measures the problem first After 0.6

docs.title: 2. Order of work
docs.text:
Phase 2 runs in two waves, in this order because until now there was no real database to test against.

flowchart LR
  subgraph A["Wave A"]
    T["Track 1: the real-database test bed<br/>one compose file, CI, GCP VM, realdb marker"]
    N["Track 2: work that needs no real database<br/>stores, providers, policies"]
  end
  T --> B["Wave B: adapter SDK v2<br/>built and proven on the test bed"]
  N --> R["Release 0.6"]
  B --> R
  • Wave A, track 1 builds the test bed. Nothing else depends on the GCP part; the CI containers and fixtures are what Wave B needs.
  • Wave A, track 2 changes code that SQLite, DuckDB and the fake LLM can test: storage, LLM and embeddings providers, and policies.
  • Wave B starts once track 1's CI job is merged. It may overlap the end of track 2.
  • Release 0.6 follows the last Wave B pull request.

docs.title: 3. The real-database test bed
docs.text:
Built: the compose file, the realdb marker and the CI workflow (PR T1)

testbed/ holds the compose file, wide_schema.py, samples.py (the pinned samples with their checksums), passwords.py, the servers' init scripts and gate.py; packages/nl2sql/tests/realdb/ holds the fixtures; and .github/workflows/realdb.yml runs them. Four details differ from the first draft of this section. The passwords have no default: testbed/passwords.py writes random ones to the git-excluded testbed/.env, and CI generates new ones per run, so no password is written in the repository. Pagila is pinned to commit 5ba5a57, because later commits need PostgreSQL 18. The audit schema is a small 21st schema beside the 20 numbered ones that hold the 1,200 tables. datasource() defaults to the server's own sample database (Pagila, Sakila or AdventureWorksLT) and passes other keywords to Datasource, since Datasource.index arrives with B1. The GCP VM and scripts/testbed.py are PR T2. See The real-database test bed.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text:
One file, testbed/docker-compose.yml, defines the whole test bed. The same file runs in three places (owner decision 2):

Where When Cost Your machine whenever you want free GitHub's runners (CI) pull requests that change database-facing code, nightly on main, and on demand before a release free; no IP address involved One small GCP VM by hand, at least once before each release about $0.07 an hour running; disk only (about $1 to $2 a month) when stopped Server Sample database Generated schema PostgreSQL 16 Pagila wide (1,200 tables, 20 schemas) MySQL 8.0 Sakila wide_s01 ... wide_s20 (MySQL's schemas are databases) SQL Server 2022 AdventureWorksLT 2022 wide SQLite, DuckDB the conformance kit's own seed, in process, in the unit job —

The generated schema is loaded on all three servers everywhere, because IndexScope and catalog row estimates are per adapter, and one compose file means one behaviour.

There is no Cloud SQL. An earlier draft of this page used three Cloud SQL instances; a stopped Cloud SQL instance still bills its public IPv4 address, and a VM running the same compose file is cheaper, simpler and identical to CI.

docs.title: The sample databases and their licences
docs.text:
The compose file's samples service downloads each sample from a pinned URL and checks its SHA-256. Nothing is committed to the repository, so we never redistribute the files. If we ever vendor one, its licence file goes beside it.

Sample Files Source Licence What we must do Pagila pagila-schema.sql, pagila-insert-data.sql github.com/devrimgunduz/pagila PostgreSQL License (copyright Devrim Gündüz) Keep the notice if the files are ever copied Sakila sakila-schema.sql, sakila-data.sql downloads.mysql.com (sakila-db.tar.gz) New BSD (stated on the Sakila licence page) Keep the notice if copied AdventureWorksLT 2022 AdventureWorksLT2022.bak github.com/microsoft/sql-server-samples, release adventureworks MIT (the repository's licence) Keep the notice if copied

The server images have their own terms. The SQL Server image runs the free Developer edition, which needs ACCEPT_EULA=Y and is licensed for development and testing, which is all we do with it. The PostgreSQL and MySQL images are used as they are.

docs.title: The generated wide schema
docs.text:
testbed/wide_schema.py --dialect postgres|mysql|tsql --seed 7 writes one SQL file. The same seed always gives the same schema. It has:

Feature Count What it tests Schemas 20 (sales_01 ... ops_20, plus audit) IndexScope include and exclude, policy globs Tables 1,200, with 5 to 30 columns each Reflecting once, catalog-only indexing, retrieval at scale Views 2 per schema Views are indexed Odd column types boolean, uuid, json, binary, xml or array where the server has it Type-aware profiling never aborts Comments on 30% of tables and columns Descriptions come from the database Foreign keys within each schema Join paths Mixed-case names 10 tables, such as "CustomerAccounts" Quoting Rows 3 tables with 1,000,000 rows, 50 with 1,000, the rest empty Row estimates, max_profile_rows

The big tables are filled on the server with a series function (generate_series, a recursive CTE, or a numbers table), so the file stays small. That SQL lives in the test bed, which is test code, not engine code.

docs.title: The compose file
docs.text:
docker compose -f testbed/docker-compose.yml up -d --wait starts and loads everything. Loading happens once per data volume, so a second up is quick.

Service Image What it does samples python:3.12-slim One-shot. Downloads the pinned samples, checks them, runs wide_schema.py for the three dialects, and writes the files into the samples volume. Skips what is already there. postgres postgres:16 Starts after samples. Its first start runs Pagila and the wide schema from /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d, the image's own init mechanism. mysql mysql:8.0 The same, with Sakila. The image's init uses the mysql client, which handles DELIMITER blocks. mssql mcr.microsoft.com/mssql/server:2022-latest Starts the server. mssql-init the same image (it ships sqlcmd) After mssql starts. Restores AdventureWorksLT from the .bak, loads the wide schema, and creates the test logins. Skips each step whose database already exists. Then it idles, healthy, instead of exiting: nothing waits for it to complete, and --wait fails on an exited container, which a skipping second up would otherwise produce.

Every service has a healthcheck, so --wait returns only when every server is loaded. Each server also gets a login nl2sql_reader with read grants on its sample database only; the conformance kit uses it for the permission stage of test_connection.

The file reads four variables. The bind address has a default; the passwords do not, so no password is written in the repository:

Variable Default On the GCP VM TESTBED_BIND 127.0.0.1 0.0.0.0 (the firewall admits only IAP, see below) TESTBED_POSTGRES_PASSWORD none: required; testbed/passwords.py makes random ones, and CI makes new ones per run from Secret Manager TESTBED_MYSQL_PASSWORD none: required; testbed/passwords.py makes random ones, and CI makes new ones per run from Secret Manager TESTBED_MSSQL_PASSWORD none: required; testbed/passwords.py makes random ones, and CI makes new ones per run from Secret Manager Service Published port User postgres 15432 postgres mysql 13306 root mssql 11433 sa

The ports avoid a clash with a database already installed locally.

docs.title: Local use
docs.text:
python testbed/passwords.py > testbed/.env               # once
docker compose -f testbed/docker-compose.yml up -d --wait
set -a; . testbed/.env; set +a
REALDB=compose pytest -m realdb
docker compose -f testbed/docker-compose.yml down        # add -v to drop the data

docs.title: CI: the realdb workflow
docs.text:
A new workflow, .github/workflows/realdb.yml, with three jobs (owner decision 2):

Job Runs What it does changes always Works out whether the pull request touches database-facing code (the paths below) realdb on a pull request when changes says so; nightly on main (schedule); on demand (workflow_dispatch), which is run before every release docker compose ... up -d --wait on the runner, installs Microsoft's msodbcsql18 for pyodbc, installs packages/nl2sql[postgres,mysql,mssql,duckdb], then pytest -m realdb with REALDB=compose and REALDB_REQUIRED=1 realdb-gate always (if: always()), after the other two Passes when realdb passed or was skipped because nothing database-facing changed; fails when it failed or was cancelled. This is the required check, so a skipped job is an honest pass and never mistaken for one that ran.

The paths that make realdb run:

packages/sdk/**
packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/adapters/**
packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/indexing/**
packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/storage/**        (and schema/** until S3 moves it)
packages/nl2sql/tests/realdb/**
testbed/**
.github/workflows/realdb.yml

REALDB_REQUIRED=1 turns a skipped realdb test into a failure: a green run that skipped the real databases proves nothing. The unit job in test.yml changes to pytest -m "not integration and not realdb". The containers run on GitHub's runners; no cloud credentials are involved.

docs.title: The realdb marker and fixtures
docs.text:
pytest.ini registers the marker:

realdb: needs a real PostgreSQL, MySQL or SQL Server (the test bed). Start
    testbed/docker-compose.yml and set REALDB=compose, or run it through
    scripts/testbed.py for the GCP VM.

The fixtures live in packages/nl2sql/tests/realdb/conftest.py:

Variable Meaning REALDB=compose The compose servers on 127.0.0.1, at the published ports, with the passwords in TESTBED_*_PASSWORD REALDB_POSTGRES, REALDB_MYSQL, REALDB_MSSQL A URL for one server, such as postgresql://postgres:<password>@127.0.0.1:15432/, with the password percent-encoded. It wins over REALDB=compose. scripts/testbed.py run sets these. REALDB_REQUIRED=1 A missing server is a failure, not a skip 
@pytest.fixture(params=["postgres", "mysql", "mssql"])
def server(request) -> RealServer: ...            # skips loudly, or fails under REALDB_REQUIRED

def datasource(server, database="pagila", **index) -> Datasource:
    """A Datasource for one test-bed database, built from the server's URL."""

@pytest.fixture
def engine_on(server, tmp_path) -> Callable[..., NL2SQL]: ...   # an engine on that server, fake LLM

The skip message names the fix: "realdb: no PostgreSQL. Run docker compose -f testbed/docker-compose.yml up -d --wait and set REALDB=compose, or run python scripts/testbed.py run -- pytest -m realdb."

Test code may name dialects and use SQLAlchemy directly. The boundary tests cover packages/*/src, not the tests.

docs.title: The GCP VM
docs.text:
One small VM, nl2sql-testbed in nl2sql-testbed-261014 (zone us-central1-a), runs the same compose file (owner decision 3). It is started for a session and stopped after it.

Setting Value Machine e2-standard-2 (2 vCPU, 8 GB: SQL Server alone wants 2 GB) Image Debian 12, with Docker and the compose plugin installed once by its startup script Disk 30 GB standard persistent disk: the images and the data volumes, kept while stopped, so a later session skips the load External IP Ephemeral only, for outbound traffic (image pulls, sample downloads). It is released, and free, while the VM is stopped. Inbound No public database port. The VM sits in its own VPC, nl2sql-testbed, so the default network's open SSH and RDP rules do not apply, and one firewall rule admits TCP 22, 15432, 13306 and 11433 from IAP's range 35.235.240.0/20 only. Access gcloud compute start-iap-tunnel, which forwards localhost:15432, 13306 and 11433 on the caller's machine to the VM Passwords Secret Manager: the existing testbed-postgres-root-password, testbed-mysql-root-password and testbed-mssql-root-password. Never in the repository. Bucket gs://nl2sql-testbed-261014-samples is not needed: the VM downloads the samples itself, once

There are no GitHub-to-GCP credentials. The owner, or an agent the owner asks, runs the VM by hand.

scripts/testbed.py is Python, not a shell script, because the owner works on Windows and CI runs Linux. It calls gcloud (found with shutil.which, so gcloud.cmd works) and never writes its own process's environment.

Command What it does up Starts the VM (gcloud compute instances start). Copies testbed/ to it (gcloud compute scp --tunnel-through-iap). Runs docker compose up -d --wait on it over gcloud compute ssh --tunnel-through-iap, with TESTBED_BIND=0.0.0.0 and the three passwords from Secret Manager passed on that command's environment only (they travel on its stdin, never on a command line). Then opens the three IAP tunnels in the background and waits until each local port answers. run -- <cmd> up, then runs <cmd> with REALDB_POSTGRES, REALDB_MYSQL and REALDB_MSSQL (pointing at the local tunnel ports) in the child's environment only, then closes the tunnels and stops the VM in a finally: also on Ctrl-C, a failing command or a failed up. It exits with the command's code. down Closes any tunnels it opened, runs docker compose stop on the VM (bounded; a failure is reported, not fatal) so SQL Server shuts down cleanly, then stops the VM. Safe to run again. status The VM's state, how long it has been running, and whether the tunnels are open. Never a password.

Passwords are read with gcloud secrets versions access latest into memory, and are never written to a file or printed.

The nightly backstop. If testbed.py is killed hard, or the VM is started by hand, it would keep billing. One Cloud Scheduler job calls the Compute Engine API directly at 03:00 UTC, with an OAuth token for a service account that may only stop instances in this project: POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/nl2sql-testbed-261014/zones/us-central1-a/instances/nl2sql-testbed/stop. Stopping a stopped VM does nothing, so the job needs no logic, and one job is inside Cloud Scheduler's free tier.

docs/testing/test-bed.md gives the commands for the owner to create the VM, the firewall rule and the scheduler job once. Nothing in the repository creates cloud resources by itself.

docs.title: Cost controls
docs.text:
Control Why The VM is stopped whenever no session runs A running VM bills by the hour Ephemeral external IP only Released, and free, while stopped No public database port; IAP's range only Nothing else can reach the servers run always stops the VM in a finally A failed test cannot leave it running The nightly stop at 03:00 UTC The backstop for everything above CI runs on GitHub's runners Free, and only when database-facing code changes, nightly, or on demand Budget of $10 a month with alerts The last line Item Approximate cost (check the billing report after the first month) Stopped the 30 GB disk: about $1 to $2 a month Running about $0.07 an hour

So even a daily session stays well inside $10.

docs.title: 4. Storage: four stores
docs.text:
Built: the interfaces, config and registry kind (S1)

nl2sql_sdk.stores holds the four protocols with Entry, Hit, Filter and BuildPointer; StoreConfig and the four Storage sub-blocks are in nl2sql/config/models.py; the store registry kind (add_store, @registry.store, group nl2sql.stores) and the slot check are in nl2sql/registry.py and nl2sql/storage/__init__.py. The built-ins, nl2sql/storage/{chroma,sqlite,files,local}.py, are thin wrappers that build today's VectorStore, SqliteSchemaStore and ArtifactStore and hold the traces folder; Runtime.index, .state, .traces and .results are built through the registry. Building it settled these details:

  • IndexStore.query returns Hit (id, text, metadata, distance, and vector only when with_vectors), which the sketch below used without defining.
  • Until S2 to S4 move the engine onto each interface, the engine reads a slot only through its built-in store, and a plugin store in that slot is a ConfigError at storage.<slot> rather than silently unused.
  • max_age_days arrives with retention in S4; until then files and local take no keys.

Built: the index store and the pointer as the commit (S2)

nl2sql/storage/chroma.py is the chroma index store on Chroma's public client API, one collection per namespace, with each datasource's BuildPointer in the collection's metadata. The engine embeds and ranks: nl2sql/indexing/retrieval.py holds the Retriever (MMR in numpy over the vectors query returns) and namespace_for; indexing/vector_store.py, retrieval_trace.py, indexing/embeddings.py (the local embedder moved to embeddings/local.py), staging, full, switch_guard, EmbeddingModelMismatchError, get_latest_snapshot/get_latest_version and settings.schema.version_mismatch are deleted. Runtime.vector_store is a Retriever on the live pointers, Runtime.pin_index() pins them for a run (run_with_graph calls it), and the index slot takes any IndexStore. engine.index.prune() and nl2sql index prune are added. Building it settled these details:

  • Entry.metadata holds scalars only, so a relationship entry stores from_columns and to_columns comma-joined and the retriever splits them; empty values are left out.
  • The local embedder uses chromadb's bundled ONNX model function, so embeddings/local.py is the one exception to "only nl2sql/storage/ imports chromadb". langchain-chroma is no longer a dependency.
  • Health keeps index_version per datasource (the pointer's schema version, which the playground shows) and drops snapshot_version; stale now means a datasource without a live build, or whose snapshot is gone.
  • The chroma store opens index/ on the first write; reads of a missing folder or namespace create nothing.
  • Snapshot immutability and keep_snapshots (so eviction never removes a pointed version) are S3's: until then settings.schema.max_versions still evicts the oldest versions, and an unchanged structure still refreshes its stored metadata in place.

Built: the trace and result stores, and retention (S4)

nl2sql/storage/files.py is the files TraceStore and nl2sql/storage/local.py the local ResultStore, each with max_age_days (14 and 7, at least 1) and purge. The run trace is written through Runtime.traces, engine.traces.get reads through it, and ArtifactStore(results, path_template) writes Parquet and the manifest through Runtime.results; ArtifactStoreConfig and Runtime.traces_dir are deleted, and the traces and results slots take any store. engine.storage.info() and purge(), nl2sql storage purge and the API's startup and daily purge are added. No S3 or ADLS store is built in; storage/artifact-store.md has an S3 example. Building it settled these details:

  • ArtifactRef.uri is the result's key in the results store (<tenant_id>/<request_id>/<sub_query_id>.parquet), not a file path, and ArtifactRef.backend is deleted.
  • Reading a result: when ResultStore.open returns a local file, as local does, polars scans the file in place; any other stream is read into memory first, since a scan outlives the call that opened it.
  • purge() purges a store that has a max_age_days attribute and leaves one without it alone; it returns the counts per slot purged.
  • QueryResult.trace_path is the file the files store wrote, and None with another trace store; trace_id always names the trace.
  • nl2sql trace show <id> reads through engine.traces.get. Runtime.stores (StorePaths) stays for the state store's callers until S3.

Built: the state store, migrations and the lock (S3)

nl2sql/storage/sqlite.py is the sqlite state store: immutable snapshots (a trigger refuses any UPDATE), the plan cache, feedback, nl2sql_meta migrations (1 adopts 0.5's three tables, 2 adds the later feedback columns, 3 adds the trigger and the locks table) and the lease. schema/sqlite_store.py, schema/in_memory_store.py, schema/store.py, schema/protocol.py (the fingerprint moved to schema/fingerprint.py) and feedback/store.py are deleted; Runtime.schema_store is gone and the engine reads Runtime.state through StateStore, so the state slot takes any state store. The runtime calls migrate() when it opens the stores; the store opens its file on first use. health.py, nl2sql cache clear (through the new engine.clear_plan_cache()) and nl2sql curated proposals export (through engine.feedback.list()) go through the engine. Building it settled these details:

  • StateStore.list_versions(datasource_id), newest first, is added: the engine needs it to keep "the newest max_versions".
  • put_snapshot returns the stored version when the contract and metadata are identical, and stores a new version otherwise, so a re-index whose statistics changed gets a new version and a cold plan cache for that datasource (the cache is already keyed on the run date).
  • After a build, keep is every version a pointer names in any namespace, the version the build replaced (runs in flight may have pinned it, as with builds), and the newest max_versions.
  • engine.index.build() holds the index lock with a one-hour lease; a build started while it is held fails every datasource at once with the holder's expiry. A store's lock() raises when the lease is held.
  • The engine builds the feedback row (nl2sql.feedback.rated_row) and the store keeps it as given, so add_feedback needs no rating rules.
  • With every slot read through its interface, the runtime's "built-in only" slot check, Runtime.stores (StorePaths) and the CLI's store_paths are deleted.

docs.title: The config
docs.text:
Every sub-block is optional. A config with only path stays valid and means the built-ins below.

# storage.yaml
path: .nl2sql
index:   { type: chroma }                       # <path>/index/
state:   { type: sqlite }                       # <path>/state.db
traces:  { type: files, max_age_days: 14 }      # <path>/traces/
results: { type: local, max_age_days: 7 }       # <path>/results/

A plugin store takes its own keys, validated by its config_model:

index: { type: qdrant, url: "http://qdrant:6333", api_key: "${env:QDRANT_KEY}" }

The same in Python, by name or with an object:

from nl2sql import Storage, StoreConfig

Storage(path=".nl2sql")
Storage(path=".nl2sql", traces=StoreConfig(type="files", max_age_days=30))
Storage(path=".nl2sql", index=MyQdrantIndex(url="http://qdrant:6333"))   # any IndexStore object
Field Type Default path Path required (Phase 1) index StoreConfig \| IndexStore {type: chroma} state StoreConfig \| StateStore {type: sqlite} traces StoreConfig \| TraceStore {type: files} results StoreConfig \| ResultStore {type: local}

StoreConfig is like SecretProviderConfig: type, plus the store's own keys, which keep their references until the store is built. max_age_days is a key of the files and local stores, not of every store.

Names. Store names share one entry point group, nl2sql.stores (owner decision), so they are unique across the four slots. Each store class says which slot it fills (slot = "index"), and the engine checks it: "chroma is an index store; results needs a results store. Installed: local."

Slot Built-in Location under path index chroma index/ state sqlite state.db traces files traces/ results local results/

docs.title: The interfaces
docs.text:
They live in nl2sql_sdk.stores, so they need only pydantic and the standard library. Each has interface_version = 1, a slot, a config_model and from_config(cfg, *, folder: Path), where folder is storage.path.

class Entry(BaseModel):          # one index entry
    id: str
    text: str
    vector: list[float]
    metadata: dict[str, str | int | float | bool]

class Filter(BaseModel):         # what the engine filters on today, and nothing more
    eq: dict[str, Scalar] = {}
    ne: dict[str, Scalar] = {}
    in_: dict[str, list[Scalar]] = Field({}, alias="in")

class BuildPointer(BaseModel):   # which build of one datasource is live
    build_id: str
    schema_version: str
    built_at: datetime
    curated_hash: str | None = None

class IndexStore(Protocol):
    slot: ClassVar[Literal["index"]]
    def open(self, namespace: str, dimension: int) -> None: ...
    def add(self, namespace: str, entries: Sequence[Entry]) -> None: ...
    def query(self, namespace: str, vector: Sequence[float], k: int, where: Filter | None = None,
              with_vectors: bool = False) -> list[Hit]: ...        # MMR needs the vectors
    def get(self, namespace: str, where: Filter, with_vectors: bool = False) -> list[Entry]: ...
    def delete(self, namespace: str, where: Filter) -> int: ...
    def pointers(self, namespace: str) -> dict[str, BuildPointer]: ...        # by datasource id
    def set_pointers(self, namespace: str, updates: dict[str, BuildPointer | None]) -> None: ...  # atomic
    def namespaces(self) -> list[str]: ...
    def drop(self, namespace: str) -> None: ...
    def close(self) -> None: ...

class StateStore(Protocol):
    slot: ClassVar[Literal["state"]]
    def migrate(self) -> list[str]: ...                       # applied migration names
    def put_snapshot(self, snapshot: SchemaSnapshot) -> str: ...      # returns schema_version
    def get_snapshot(self, datasource_id: str, schema_version: str) -> SchemaSnapshot | None: ...
    def list_versions(self, datasource_id: str) -> list[str]: ...              # newest first (S3)
    def keep_snapshots(self, datasource_id: str, keep: set[str]) -> int: ...   # deletes the rest
    def get_plan(self, key: str, datasource_id: str, schema_version: str) -> str | None: ...
    def put_plan(self, key: str, datasource_id: str, schema_version: str, plan_json: str) -> None: ...
    def clear_plans(self) -> int: ...
    def add_feedback(self, row: dict) -> dict: ...
    def list_feedback(self, limit: int | None = None) -> list[dict]: ...
    def clear_feedback(self) -> int: ...
    def lock(self, name: str, ttl_s: int) -> ContextManager[None]: ...
    def close(self) -> None: ...

class TraceStore(Protocol):
    slot: ClassVar[Literal["traces"]]
    def write(self, trace_id: str, document: dict) -> None: ...
    def get(self, trace_id: str) -> dict | None: ...
    def purge(self, older_than: datetime) -> int: ...

class ResultStore(Protocol):     # bytes only: the engine keeps writing Parquet
    slot: ClassVar[Literal["results"]]
    def write(self, key: str, chunks: Iterable[bytes]) -> int: ...
    def open(self, key: str) -> BinaryIO: ...
    def exists(self, key: str) -> bool: ...
    def purge(self, older_than: datetime) -> int: ...

Design notes:

  • The engine embeds. Today Chroma's LangChain wrapper embeds documents itself. In 0.6 the engine embeds with its own embedder and hands the store vectors, so a store never depends on LangChain, and MMR runs in the engine on the vectors query returns.
  • No staging or rename in the interface. A rebuild writes a new build beside the live one and switches a pointer, so no backend has to rename anything.
  • The filter is small on purpose. eq, ne and in (combined with "and") are all the engine uses today. Each backend translates them.
  • ResultStore stores bytes. The engine still writes Parquet and the manifest; the store only puts and gets them. A remote store (S3, ADLS) then needs four methods and no Polars knowledge.
  • The lock is a lease in the state store: in SQLite, a locks row taken in a BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction, with an expiry so a crashed holder cannot block forever. It makes nl2sql index safe to run while nl2sql-api serves the same storage.path, and needs no new dependency.

docs.title: The build pointer is the commit (bug B5)
docs.text:
The bug. Indexing registers the schema snapshot in the state store before it writes the index (indexing/orchestrator.py), and the resolver, retriever, curated matcher and datasources.schema() read the state store's latest snapshot. If the index build fails, the "latest" snapshot describes a schema the live index was never built from. Today this only produces a warning (settings.schema.version_mismatch).

The fix. A snapshot is an immutable row keyed by schema_version. The index's BuildPointer records the schema_version the build was made from, and every reader resolves "live" through the pointer. Switching the pointer is the commit.

sequenceDiagram
  participant I as Indexing
  participant S as State store
  participant X as Index store
  participant R as A run
  I->>S: put_snapshot(snapshot) returns v42 (nothing reads it yet)
  I->>X: add(entries tagged build b7)
  I->>X: set_pointers(sales to build b7 and schema v42)
  Note over X: the commit
  R->>X: pointers() once, at the start of the run
  R->>S: get_snapshot(sales, v42)
  R->>X: query(where build_id = b7)
  • A failed build leaves an unreferenced snapshot and entries that no pointer names. The next build of that datasource deletes them.
  • get_latest_snapshot and get_latest_version are deleted, so no reader can ask the wrong question. settings.schema.version_mismatch is deleted, because the mismatch can no longer happen.
  • keep_snapshots keeps every version a pointer names, plus the newest settings.schema.max_versions.
  • It works for any pair of backends (Chroma and SQLite today, pgvector and PostgreSQL later) without a transaction across the two.

docs.title: A run pins the pointers
docs.text: A run reads pointers() once, when it starts, the way it already pins its LLM set. Every step of the run uses that build and that schema version. To make that safe, a new build deletes only the builds before the previous one, so an in-flight run never loses its entries. That replaces switch_guard and the playground's RunGate for index switches.

docs.title: One namespace per embedding model
docs.text:
The index namespace is nl2sql__<model slug>__<dimension>, for example nl2sql__local-all-minilm-l6-v2__384. The slug and dimension come from the embedder (see section 5).

  • Changing the embedding model opens a new, empty namespace. check() reports the index as missing for the new model, with "run nl2sql index". EmbeddingModelMismatchError and the dimension check are deleted.
  • Switching back to an earlier model finds its namespace still built.
  • engine.index.prune() and nl2sql index prune drop every namespace except the current one, including 0.5's nl2sql_store collection, which 0.6 never reads.
  • A full rebuild no longer needs a staging collection: index.build() with no ids builds every datasource in the current namespace. The full argument, create_staging, promote and discard are deleted.

docs.title: Migrations and retention
docs.text:
• Migrations. The SQLite state store keeps a nl2sql_meta table and applies numbered migrations at startup. Migration 1 creates 0.5's three tables if they do not exist, so a 0.5 state.db is adopted as it is. The feedback store's ad-hoc ALTER TABLE statements move into migrations.
  • Retention. files traces and local results take max_age_days (defaults 14 and 7). engine.storage.purge() deletes what is older and returns the counts. nl2sql storage purge calls it, and nl2sql-api calls it at startup and once a day. Feedback and snapshots have no age limit: feedback is cleared by hand, and snapshots by keep_snapshots.

docs.title: The facade
docs.text: Method What it does engine.storage.info() Each slot's type and location, and the current index namespace engine.storage.purge() Retention, as above engine.index.prune() Drops the namespaces of other embedding models engine.index.build(datasource_ids=None, *, curated_only=False, enrich=False, on_datasource=None) full and switch_guard are gone

docs.title: What changes in existing code
docs.text:
Today 0.6 indexing/vector_store.py (855 lines, Chroma private attributes throughout) nl2sql/storage/chroma.py, the chroma index store, on Chroma's public client API. Retrieval and MMR move to indexing/retrieval.py, on IndexStore. schema/sqlite_store.py, schema/in_memory_store.py, schema/protocol.py, feedback/store.py nl2sql/storage/sqlite.py, the sqlite state store (snapshots, plan cache, feedback, migrations, locks). Tests use it on :memory:. execution/artifacts/store.py writing files itself Writes Parquet through the ResultStore; nl2sql/storage/local.py is the local store Trace documents written by tracing/document.py Through the TraceStore; nl2sql/storage/files.py is the files store Runtime.stores (StorePaths) Runtime.index, .state, .traces, .results, built through the registry indexing/rebuild.py staging and promote Deleted indexing/health.py opening state.db and importing chromadb Reads through the stores get_latest_snapshot / get_latest_version callers Resolve through the pinned pointer

A new boundary test: only nl2sql/storage/ imports chromadb or sqlite3.

docs.title: 5. LLM and embeddings providers
docs.text:
Built: LLM providers and agent fields (PR L1)

openai_compatible, with openrouter and ollama as its presets; structured_output, max_tokens, timeout_s, max_retries and headers on LLM and AgentLLM; LLMProvider on interface version 2. See LLM configuration.

Built: parse-and-retry (PR L2)

parse_retries on LLM and AgentLLM; structured() and streaming_structured() retry an answer that does not parse; StructuredOutputError and MODEL_OUTPUT_INVALID. See Parse-and-retry.

docs.title: The LLM config
docs.text:
Phase 1's llm section stays flat. Six fields are added to LLM and to AgentLLM, and an agent inherits each one it does not set:

# llm.yaml
provider: openai_compatible
base_url: http://vllm:8000/v1
model: qwen3-32b
api_key: "${env:VLLM_KEY}"          # optional for this provider
structured_output: json_schema      # tool_calling | json_schema | json_mode
parse_retries: 1
max_tokens: 8000
timeout_s: 60
max_retries: 2
headers: { X-Team: analytics }
agents:
  ast_planner: { provider: anthropic, model: claude-opus-5, max_tokens: 16000 }
  answer_synthesizer:
    provider: openai_compatible     # Azure OpenAI's v1 endpoint
    base_url: https://my-resource.openai.azure.com/openai/v1/
    api_key: "${env:AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY}"
    model: gpt-5-4-prod             # the Azure deployment name

from nl2sql import LLM, AgentLLM

LLM(provider="openai_compatible", base_url="http://vllm:8000/v1", model="qwen3-32b",
    structured_output="json_schema",
    agents={"ast_planner": AgentLLM(provider="anthropic", model="claude-opus-5", max_tokens=16000)})
New field Type Default Notes structured_output "tool_calling" \| "json_schema" \| "json_mode" \| None the provider's How structured answers are asked for parse_retries int >= 0 1 Retries of a malformed structured answer max_tokens int \| None the provider's Today fixed at 16,000 for Anthropic and unset for OpenAI timeout_s float \| None the client library's Per request max_retries int \| None the client library's Network and rate-limit retries, done by the client headers dict[str, Secret] {} Values may be references; they never print

The client cache key already covers every field of the agent model, so these need no change there.

docs.title: Providers
docs.text:
The built-ins stay minimal (owner decision 7):

Provider Wire Key variable base_url Default structured_output openai OpenAI OPENAI_API_KEY optional tool_calling anthropic Anthropic ANTHROPIC_API_KEY optional tool_calling openai_compatible OpenAI none: write api_key (usually ${env:...}) if the server needs one required json_schema openrouter preset of openai_compatible OPENROUTER_API_KEY fixed: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 tool_calling ollama preset of openai_compatible none fixed: http://localhost:11434/v1 (a base_url may override it) tool_calling
  • openai_compatible is any server with an OpenAI-style chat API: Azure OpenAI's v1 endpoint (https://<resource>.openai.azure.com/openai/v1/, with model as the deployment name), vLLM, LiteLLM, LM Studio, llama.cpp's server or a company gateway. Without api_key it sends a placeholder, because the OpenAI client refuses to start without one. Its default is json_schema because local servers support schema-guided decoding more often than tool calls; set tool_calling for Azure.
  • openrouter and ollama stay, as named presets of openai_compatible: a PROVIDER_PRESETS row each, with a fixed base_url, a key variable (or a placeholder key for Ollama) and a default structured_output, and no code path of their own. nl2sql init --provider openrouter and the demo's sk-or- key detection keep working. PROVIDER_PRESETS stays the one table of key variables.
  • Anything else is a plugin: a class implementing LLMProvider, registered with registry.add_llm or the nl2sql.llms entry point group. An Azure provider with Entra ID sign-in, Bedrock or Gemini would each be one.

docs.title: Structured output, and parse-and-retry
docs.text:
Every structured call already goes through one function, structured() in llm/wires/__init__.py. Phase 2 changes it:

  1. Ask with the agent's structured_output method. For json_mode, the schema is added to the prompt, since JSON mode alone does not carry it.
  2. If the answer does not parse (OutputParserException, a pydantic ValidationError, no tool call, or None), ask again, up to parse_retries times. Each retry adds the model's answer and the validation errors to the messages: "Your answer did not match the schema: steps[0].op: field required. Answer again with only PlanModel."
  3. If it still fails, raise StructuredOutputError(agent, schema, attempts). provider_error() maps it to a new ErrorCode.MODEL_OUTPUT_INVALID, whose message names the agent and suggests another structured_output or a stronger model.

The method is not switched automatically: the agent's setting is what runs. Retries are counted in the run's trace and in token usage. A streamed answer that fails to parse is retried without streaming.

docs.title: Embeddings
docs.text:
Built: embeddings providers v2 (PR E1)

openai_compatible, base_url and dimension on the embeddings section, EmbeddingInfo and describe() on interface version 2, and the one-call probe as Runtime.embedding_info. The index does not read it yet: namespaces per model come with S2. See Embeddings.

# embeddings.yaml
provider: openai_compatible
base_url: http://ollama:11434/v1
model: nomic-embed-text
dimension: 768            # optional: otherwise asked of the provider, or probed with one call
Field Type Default Notes provider str \| None required unless instance Phase 1 model str \| None the provider's default Phase 1 api_key Secret \| None the provider's variable Phase 1 instance embeddings object None Phase 1 (code only) base_url str \| None None For openai and openai_compatible. An error for local. dimension int \| None None Needed only when the provider does not know it and you want to skip the probe Provider Default model Dimension known? local all-MiniLM-L6-v2 yes, 384 openai text-embedding-3-small yes, for OpenAI's own models openai_compatible none: model is required only with dimension:; otherwise probed an instance its own probed

Model and dimension. The engine needs both to name the index namespace. The embedder reports them as EmbeddingInfo(provider, model, dimension). When the dimension is unknown, the engine embeds the text "dimension probe" once, at the first index build or query, and remembers the answer for the engine's life. Writing dimension: skips that one paid call.

docs.title: Interface changes
docs.text:
Interface 0.5 0.6 LLMProvider version 1, create(agent) version 2: adds structured_output (the default method); ResolvedAgent carries the new fields EmbeddingsProvider version 1, create(cfg) version 2: adds describe(cfg) -> EmbeddingInfo (the dimension may be None, meaning "probe")

As in Phase 1, the engine accepts exactly the version it was built for.

docs.title: What changes in existing code
docs.text: Today 0.6 structured() with no retry Parse-and-retry as above openrouter and ollama as their own providers on the OpenAI wire Presets of openai_compatible: same names, same key variables, one code path Anthropic max_tokens fixed at 16,000 max_tokens from the agent embeddings/openai.py without base_url base_url passed through; openai_compatible added beside it (Azure, Ollama and other servers use it) VectorStore dimension checks and the model-mismatch error Deleted: the namespace carries the model and dimension

docs.title: 6. Policies, step 1
docs.text:
Built: globs and Scope (PR P1)

allow and deny on Role, the pattern rules, PolicyEngine.scope and Scope in nl2sql/policies/ (which replaces nl2sql/auth/), a run's scopes pinned (PolicyEngine.run), every call site on Scope, the retriever hiding denied tables, and the demo roles rewritten. Beyond the table below, engine.policies.allowed() is replaced by engine.policies.scope(), since a flat table list cannot say what a deny does. See Policies.

Built: PolicyCheck (PR P2)

nl2sql_sdk.policy (UserContext, Grant, PolicyCheck), the policies.check block (or a check object), the intersection with the roles, failing closed, and the policy_check registry kind. The runtime builds the block through the registry, and PolicyEngine.run makes the check asked once per caller and datasource per run. A grant that returns something other than a Grant, or a pattern that does not parse, fails closed like an exception. See A policy check.

docs.title: The config
docs.text:
# policies.yaml
default_role: viewer
admin_roles: [admin]
refusal_names_tables: false
roles:
  admin:
    description: Everything
    allow: ["*"]
  analyst:
    description: Sales, except the audit schema and PII tables
    allow: [sales]
    deny:  [sales.audit.*, "sales.*.*_pii"]
  viewer:
    description: Reporting views and support tickets
    allow: [sales.reporting.*, support.public.tickets]
check:                                 # optional: a registered PolicyCheck
  type: corp_iam
  url: "${env:IAM_URL}"

from nl2sql import Policies, Role

Policies(default_role="viewer", admin_roles=["admin"],
         roles={"analyst": Role(description="Sales", allow=["sales"], deny=["sales.audit.*"])},
         check=MyIamCheck())             # an object, or a {type: ...} block

allow_all, default_role, admin_roles and refusal_names_tables are Phase 1's and do not change. nl2sql-api already reads admin_roles for its admin routes. Role.allowed_datasources and Role.allowed_tables are replaced by allow and deny.

docs.title: Pattern rules
docs.text: Rule Detail Shape * (everything), ds (a whole datasource), or ds.schema.table. Each part is an fnmatch glob: sales.audit.*, sales.*.*_pii. Two parts Rejected, with a fix: "sales.orders has two parts: write sales.<schema>.orders, or sales.<schema>.*". Owner decision 5. Schemas SQLite and DuckDB tables are in main. A plan table with no schema is in the adapter's default schema (public, dbo, main), as in 0.5. Case Matching ignores case, so a deny cannot be dodged by Orders against orders. Within a role Deny beats allow. Across roles A caller may read a table if some role allows it and that same role does not deny it. That keeps 0.5's union. Datasource access Implied: a role reaches a datasource when any of its allow patterns can match inside it. Unknown datasources A pattern naming a datasource that is not configured is a policies.validate() problem, not a startup error, because datasources can be added at runtime.

docs.title: One Scope
docs.text:
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Scope:
    datasource_id: str
    def reaches_datasource(self) -> bool: ...
    def allows(self, schema: str | None, table: str) -> bool: ...
    def rule_for(self, schema: str | None, table: str) -> str | None: ...   # the deny or missing allow, for the log

PolicyEngine.scope(user, datasource_id) -> Scope builds it from the roles, allow_all, default_role and the optional check. A run builds each datasource's Scope once and keeps it, so every step decides the same way.

Where 0.5 0.6 Datasource resolver get_allowed_datasources scope.reaches_datasource() before any model call Curated matcher table_allowed on the verified SQL's tables scope.allows on the same tables Schema retriever strips sample values and statistics of denied tables, but shows their structure drops denied tables entirely (below) Logical validator table_allowed on each plan table scope.allows; refuses with SECURITY_VIOLATION Executor's value check probes allowed tables only scope.allows engine.policies.allows() RBAC.is_allowed the same Scope Decomposer context datasource descriptions and table names filtered by scope too

table_allowed, RBAC, RolePolicy and default_schema() in auth/ are deleted. nl2sql/auth/ becomes nl2sql/policies/.

docs.title: Denied tables are hidden from the planner
docs.text:
The owner decided (D7) that denied tables are hidden by default. In 0.5 the planner sees every table's name, columns and keys ("structure yes, data no"). In 0.6 the retriever filters entries through the Scope before it takes the top k, fetching more candidates when needed, so a schema with many denied tables still fills the prompt with readable ones.

What the user sees changes: a question that needs only denied tables gets "no data for that question" from the planner rather than a refusal. A plan that names a hidden table anyway is still refused by the validator. With refusal_names_tables: true the refusal names the table, for debugging.

docs.title: The PolicyCheck extension point
docs.text:
# nl2sql_sdk.policy
class UserContext(BaseModel):          # moves here from nl2sql.auth.models
    user_id: str | None = None
    tenant_id: str | None = None
    roles: list[str] = []

class Grant(BaseModel):
    allow: list[str] = []              # the same patterns as policies.yaml
    deny: list[str] = []

class PolicyCheck(Protocol):
    interface_version: ClassVar[int]   # 1
    config_model: ClassVar[type[BaseModel]]
    @classmethod
    def from_config(cls, cfg: BaseModel) -> "PolicyCheck": ...
    def grant(self, user: UserContext, datasource_id: str) -> Grant: ...
Rule Detail Combined by intersection The effective scope allows a table only if the YAML roles allow it and the check's Grant does. Neither can widen the other. With allow_all: true and a check, the check alone decides. Fails closed Any exception from grant denies that datasource for the run, and is logged with the check's name. There is no fail-open option. How often Once per user and datasource per run. No cache across runs. Timeouts The check owns them (an HTTP client timeout). The pipeline's timeout_s bounds the run anyway. Registration registry.add_policy_check(name, cls), @registry.policy_check(name), or the nl2sql.policy_checks entry point group. No built-in: OPA, Cedar, OpenFGA, Unity Catalog or an internal service are each a plugin.

The docs page gets a 30-line example that calls an HTTP service.

docs.title: 7. Adapter SDK v2 (Wave B)
docs.text:
Wave B is built on the test bed. Every behaviour below that touches a database has a realdb test.

Built: B1, the contract

ConnectionModel, Limits, IndexScope, ConnectionCheck, IndexIssue, the two enforcement capabilities and DatasourceAdapter version 2 are in nl2sql_sdk; the five built-ins declare public, strict connection models (B18) and build their engine on first use; a datasource has index:; the engine validates connection against the adapter's model. Filled in on the way: the SQLAlchemy base already applies IndexScope's schema, table and column rules, SQLite is already always mode=ro (its options bag went with strict keys), and test_connection returns a ConnectionCheck with the driver's message and no stage yet (B3 classifies). The pool settings, profile, sample_values and max_profile_rows come with B2.

Built: B2, the SQLAlchemy base in the SDK

nl2sql_sdk.sqlalchemy (the nl2sql-sdk[sqlalchemy] extra) holds SQLAlchemyAdapter, SQLAlchemyConnection with pool, ColumnProfile and column_profile; the five built-ins import it, and the engine's adapters/sqlalchemy_base/ is gone with dry_run, explain and cost_estimate (B22, B23, B24). A snapshot reflects each schema once, after IndexScope has dropped what it does not want, takes row counts from row_estimates (PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, DuckDB; SQLite counts), profiles by column_profile, keeps values only with sample_values, and reports failures as IndexIssues, which index.build() returns and nl2sql index prints. Filled in on the way: IndexScope.wants_schema, which also leaves out a schema no include_tables pattern names; SQLite and DuckDB connections have no pool (a file has no server to protect); a schema-wide estimate failure is an issue on schema.*. session_setup and classify come with B3. Not done here: the scope is not yet part of the snapshot's fingerprint, which lives in the state store (S3).

Built: B3, honest enforcement and stages

session_setup and classify are on the SDK's base; the five built-ins declare ENFORCES_READ_ONLY and ENFORCES_TIMEOUT as the table below says, SQLite stops a slow statement with a progress handler (B20), and check() reports the adapter's stage (B26) and warns about a session that can write. Filled in on the way: test_connection also lists the schemas, so a login that connects but cannot read the catalog is permission; an error the adapter cannot place has no stage rather than connect; DuckDB's :memory: cannot be opened read-only, so it does not declare ENFORCES_READ_ONLY; the warning says "a login that can only read", since the engine names no database, and the SQL Server page recommends db_datareader.

docs.title: The contract
docs.text:
# nl2sql_sdk (core: pydantic and the standard library)
class ConnectionModel(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", hide_input_in_errors=True)
    # SecretStr fields are secrets. Field(title, description, examples) and
    # json_schema_extra={"group": "advanced"} drive the generated form.

class Limits(BaseModel):               # moves here from nl2sql.config
    row_limit: PositiveInt | None = None
    timeout_ms: PositiveInt | None = None
    max_bytes: PositiveInt | None = None

class IndexScope(BaseModel):           # a datasource's `index:` block
    include_schemas: list[str] = []    # globs; empty means every non-system schema
    exclude_schemas: list[str] = []
    include_tables: list[str] = []     # "schema.table" globs
    exclude_tables: list[str] = []
    exclude_columns: list[str] = []    # "schema.table.column" globs
    profile: Literal["catalog", "stats"] = "stats"
    sample_values: bool = False
    max_profile_rows: PositiveInt = 1_000_000
    def wants_table(self, ref: TableRef) -> bool: ...    # one matcher for every adapter
    def wants_column(self, ref: TableRef, column: str) -> bool: ...

class ConnectionCheck(BaseModel):
    ok: bool
    stage: Literal["config", "driver", "network", "auth", "database", "permission"] | None = None
    message: str | None = None
    fix: str | None = None
    server_version: str | None = None

class IndexIssue(BaseModel):           # a table or column indexed without something
    table: str
    column: str | None = None
    stage: Literal["reflect", "estimate", "profile", "values"]
    message: str

class DatasourceCapability(str, Enum):
    SUPPORTS_SQL; SUPPORTS_BOUND_PARAMETERS
    ENFORCES_READ_ONLY                 # new: the session cannot write
    ENFORCES_TIMEOUT                   # new: a statement over limits.timeout_ms is stopped by the server or driver
    # SUPPORTS_REST is removed: nothing uses it

class DatasourceAdapter(Protocol):     # replaces DatasourceAdapterProtocol
    interface_version: ClassVar[int]   # 2
    title: ClassVar[str]               # "PostgreSQL", for the form
    connection_model: ClassVar[type[ConnectionModel]]
    driver_modules: ClassVar[tuple[str, ...]]
    install_hint: ClassVar[str]

    def __init__(self, datasource_id: str, connection: ConnectionModel, limits: Limits,
                 *, folder: Path | None = None) -> None: ...      # never connects
    def capabilities(self) -> set[DatasourceCapability]: ...
    def get_dialect(self) -> str: ...                  # a sqlglot name, unchanged
    def default_schema(self) -> str | None: ...
    def test_connection(self) -> ConnectionCheck: ...
    def fetch_schema_snapshot(self, scope: IndexScope,
                              on_table: Callable[[str], None] | None = None) -> SchemaSnapshot: ...
    def execute(self, request: AdapterRequest) -> ResultFrame: ...
    def close(self) -> None: ...

SchemaSnapshot gains issues: list[IndexIssue], and TableMetadata gains row_count_source: "catalog" | "exact" | None. The optional StreamingAdapterProtocol and SqlRenderingAdapterProtocol do not change.

What goes from version 1: connect() (an adapter connects on first use, and test_connection connects), datasource_engine_type, connection_args, statement_timeout_ms, row_limit and max_bytes (now limits), and the unused dry_run, explain and cost_estimate.

docs.title: ConnectionModel and the generated form
docs.text:
Each built-in declares its model publicly. For example:

class PostgresConnection(SQLAlchemyConnection):     # SQLAlchemyConnection adds `pool`
    host: str = Field(title="Host", examples=["db.internal"])
    port: int = Field(5432, title="Port")
    database: str = Field(title="Database")
    user: str = Field(title="User")
    password: SecretStr = Field(title="Password")
    sslmode: Literal["disable", "prefer", "require", "verify-full"] = Field(
        "prefer", json_schema_extra={"group": "advanced"})
  • Strict. extra="forbid": hostname: is now an error with "did you mean 'host'", where 0.5 silently ignored it (bug B18).
  • Validated at build. The engine resolves the references in connection, then validates against the adapter's model. Python callers may pass a dict or a model instance: Datasource(connection=PostgresConnection(...)).
  • The form. connection_model.model_json_schema() is the form. A SecretStr field is "format": "password", "writeOnly": true, which a form renders as a password input. A field in the advanced group is folded away. A new adapter gets a form for nothing.
  • Pool. SQLAlchemyConnection adds pool: {size: 5, max_overflow: 0, timeout_s: 30, recycle_s: 1800}. With no overflow, the pool size is also the cap on concurrent queries against that database, so NL2SQL cannot overload a production server.

docs.title: IndexScope: what gets indexed
docs.text:
# datasources/sales.yaml
type: postgres
connection: { host: db.internal, database: sales, user: nl2sql, password: "${env:SALES_DB_PASSWORD}" }
index:
  include_schemas: [public, reporting]
  exclude_tables: ["*.*_audit", "public.tmp_*"]
  exclude_columns: ["public.customers.email"]
  profile: stats
  sample_values: false
Field Default Meaning include_schemas every schema except the adapter's system schemas Globs exclude_schemas none Globs, applied after include include_tables, exclude_tables all, none schema.table globs exclude_columns none schema.table.column globs: the column is not indexed or profiled. This is not access control; deny_columns is a later policy step. profile stats catalog: names, types, keys, comments and catalog row estimates, with no query against table data. stats: also each column's null share, distinct count and min/max. sample_values false Store each text column's values (all of them when 50 or fewer distinct, otherwise the five most frequent). Off by default (owner decision D18): values reach the index, prompts and the provider. NL2SQL.demo() and init --demo turn it on. max_profile_rows 1,000,000 A table estimated above this gets catalog profiling and an IndexIssue saying so

The filter runs before any per-table query, so an excluded schema costs nothing. The scope is part of the snapshot's fingerprint, so changing it makes a new schema_version.

docs.title: Profiling and row estimates
docs.text:
The SQLAlchemy base changes how it reads a schema:

  • Reflect once. inspector.get_multi_columns, get_multi_pk_constraint and get_multi_foreign_keys per schema, instead of reflecting the whole database twice table by table. The wide schema measures it: the target is a catalog snapshot of 1,200 PostgreSQL tables in under 60 seconds in CI.
  • Catalog row estimates. An overridable row_estimates(conn, schema) -> dict[str, int] | None: PostgreSQL pg_class.reltuples, MySQL information_schema.tables.table_rows, SQL Server sys.partitions, DuckDB duckdb_tables().estimated_size. SQLite returns None, and gets COUNT(*) under profile: stats. Nothing counts every row of every table any more.
  • Type-aware statistics. An overridable column_profile(sa_type) -> ColumnProfile(min_max, distinct, values). No MIN/MAX on boolean, uuid, json, binary, xml or arrays; values only for text and only with sample_values. This makes 0.4.1's skip list a public rule.
  • Isolation. Each column's statistics query is isolated as today (a rollback after a failure), and a failure becomes an IndexIssue instead of a log line, so index.build() can report it.

docs.title: Read-only and timeouts, honestly
docs.text:
Each adapter does its session setup in one place, session_setup(dbapi_conn), run on every new pooled connection. A capability is declared only when the conformance kit proves it on a real server.

Adapter Read-only Timeout ENFORCES_READ_ONLY ENFORCES_TIMEOUT PostgreSQL SET default_transaction_read_only = on SET statement_timeout yes yes MySQL SET SESSION TRANSACTION READ ONLY SET SESSION MAX_EXECUTION_TIME (applies to SELECT, which is all the engine runs) yes yes SQL Server none at session level: ApplicationIntent=ReadOnly only routes to a readable replica pyodbc's query timeout (the client cancels) no yes DuckDB read_only=True on the connection interrupt after the deadline (0.4.1) yes yes SQLite mode=ro always, not only with options.read_only a progress handler that stops a statement after the deadline (today it is only a lock wait, bug B20) yes yes

There is no read_only setting: the engine never writes, so every adapter always makes its session read-only when it can. When it cannot (SQL Server), engine.check() adds a warning to that datasource's status: "sales (mssql): this adapter cannot make the session read-only. Connect with a login that has only db_datareader." The typed plan and the validator still block every write. This is owner decision 4.

docs.title: test_connection: which stage failed
docs.text:
Stage Means Example fix config The connection does not validate against the model the field and "did you mean" driver A module in driver_modules is missing the install_hint network The host or port cannot be reached "check the host, port and firewall" auth The login was refused "check the user and password" database The database does not exist "check database" permission Connected, but the catalog cannot be read "grant read access to the schemas you index"

Mapping a driver error to a stage is the adapter's job: an overridable classify(exc) on the SQLAlchemy base reads the SQLSTATE class (08 connection, 28 authorization, 3D database) and each adapter adds its own codes (MySQL 1045 and 1049, SQL Server 18456 and 4060). check()'s DatasourceStatus.stage is now one of these, where 0.5 always said connect.

docs.title: The SQLAlchemy base, public
docs.text:
BaseSQLAlchemyAdapter moves from the engine to nl2sql_sdk.sqlalchemy, installed with nl2sql-sdk[sqlalchemy], as SQLAlchemyAdapter with SQLAlchemyConnection. The five built-ins import it from there.

  • The SDK core still imports only pydantic and the standard library. The sqlalchemy subpackage may also import SQLAlchemy and sqlglot, and the boundary test says so.
  • Its overridable methods are the whole extension surface: url(connection) (with sqlalchemy.engine.URL.create, so credentials are escaped), session_setup, row_estimates, column_profile, classify, system_schemas and render_sql.
  • The docs' "build an adapter" page shows a complete adapter in about 40 lines.

docs.title: The conformance kit
docs.text:
nl2sql_sdk.testing, installed with nl2sql-sdk[testing] (adds pytest and sqlglot), ships AdapterConformance, a test class an adapter author subclasses. The author provides three fixtures:

Fixture What it gives adapter_factory Builds the adapter for a ConnectionModel and Limits seed A function that runs DDL with a writable connection outside the adapter. The kit's seed (two schemas, a view, mixed-case names, boolean, uuid and json columns) is written once and transpiled to the adapter's dialect with sqlglot. sleep_sql A query that takes a given number of seconds on this database

What it checks:

Check Pass means Dialect get_dialect() is a name sqlglot.Dialect.get_or_raise accepts Connection model Unknown keys fail; a password with @ : / # % connects; no secret appears in repr, str or an error Stages Good settings give ok; a wrong password gives auth; a closed port gives network; a missing database gives database Scope System schemas are left out; include and exclude rules hold; views are included; mixed-case names keep their case Odd columns Profiling a boolean, uuid or json column gives statistics or an IndexIssue, never an exception Row estimates Every table has a row count and says where it came from Bound parameters 1; DROP TABLE x passed as a parameter is a value Read-only If declared: an INSERT and a CREATE TABLE through execute fail and change nothing. If not declared: the test is reported as skipped with the reason. Timeout If declared: sleep_sql(5) with a 1-second limit fails within 3 seconds, with a timeout error code Errors A query naming a missing column is retryable; a permission error is not Streaming If execute_batches exists, its frames match execute's result

The kit proves itself on the five built-ins: SQLite and DuckDB in the unit job, PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQL Server in the realdb job.

Built: B4

nl2sql_sdk.testing.AdapterConformance, with the testing extra and a boundary test (pytest, sqlglot, pydantic, the SDK core and the standard library only). Filled in on the way: the kit also takes a connection fixture (the stage checks vary it) and an optional limited_login, a second login whose password holds @ : / # % and that cannot read kit_b, for the password and permission checks, since each needs a login of its own; the test bed's nl2sql_reader cannot read the seed, so the realdb tests make nl2sql_kit. schemas and column_types adapt the seed to a database with one schema (SQLite) or without a type (MySQL's uuid, SQL Server 2022's json). The "timeout error code" is a new QUERY_TIMEOUT from the SQLAlchemy base. The kit found two misclassified refusals, fixed in the base: MySQL's "command denied" (SQLSTATE 42000) and DuckDB's write to a read-only file were both retryable. It also found that SQLAlchemy 2.1 breaks every DuckDB snapshot (duckdb-engine inherits PostgreSQL reflection, which now queries pg_collation). The DuckDB adapter now reads DuckDB's own catalog through the base's schema_names and reflect hooks, so it runs on SQLAlchemy 2.1.

docs.title: engine.datasources: the methods behind Connect a database
docs.text:
Built: B5

types() returns DatasourceTypes (exported from nl2sql), test() takes an id or a Datasource, and add() validates index as an IndexScope again, since model_copy(update=...) skips validation. Filled in on the way: Registry.load(..., require_installed=False) and missing_modules describe an adapter without its driver; a Datasource that cannot be built fails test() at config (unknown type, or a connection the model rejects) or driver (the install hint is the fix), and an adapter that names no stage still reports connect until B3 classifies. The REST routes and the form are Phase 4.

Method What it does types() -> list[DatasourceType] Every adapter the engine's registry can name: name, title, installed (its driver modules are found), install_hint, and connection_schema (the model's JSON Schema). Adapter modules import without their driver, so the schema is there even before the driver is installed. test(datasource: Datasource \| str) -> DatasourceStatus With an id, as in 0.5. With a Datasource that is not added: builds the adapter, runs test_connection, closes it, and registers nothing. The status carries the ConnectionCheck's stage, message and fix. add(datasource) As in 0.5, now validating connection against the adapter's model and index as an IndexScope

These are what the Phase 4 form, the terminal app and nl2sql datasources add will call. Saving the result to a file stays the calling app's job, as Phase 1 decided.

docs.title: What changes in existing code
docs.text: Today 0.6 adapters/sqlalchemy_base/ in the engine nl2sql_sdk/sqlalchemy/ Private *ConnectionConfig models with extra: ignore Public *Connection models with extra: forbid construct_uri with per-adapter URL.create url(connection) on the base fetch_schema_contact and fetch_schema_metadata, each reflecting everything One reflection pass per schema, filtered by IndexScope _get_row_count with COUNT(*) row_estimates, with COUNT(*) only where there is no catalog estimate dry_run, explain, cost_estimate, adapters/sqlalchemy_base/models.py Deleted test_connection() -> bool -> ConnectionCheck DatasourceRegistry passing connection_args and keyword limits Builds adapter_cls(id, connection_model(**resolved), limits, folder=...) cli/demo and datasets setting SQLite options.read_only Gone: SQLite is always read-only

docs.title: 8. The registry after Phase 2
docs.text:
Kind Entry point group Interface Version in 0.6 Built-ins adapter nl2sql.adapters nl2sql_sdk.DatasourceAdapter 2 sqlite, postgres, mysql, mssql, duckdb llm nl2sql.llms nl2sql.llm.LLMProvider 2 openai, anthropic, openai_compatible, and its presets openrouter and ollama embeddings nl2sql.embeddings nl2sql.embeddings.EmbeddingsProvider 2 local, openai, openai_compatible secrets nl2sql.secrets nl2sql_sdk.secrets.SecretProvider 1 env, aws, azure, hashicorp store nl2sql.stores nl2sql_sdk.stores (four protocols) 1 chroma, sqlite, files, local policy check nl2sql.policy_checks nl2sql_sdk.policy.PolicyCheck 1 none

New on Registry: add_store, add_policy_check, and the store and policy_check decorators. Hooks, observers, scorers and knowledge sources stay in later phases.

docs.title: 9. Events and hooks
docs.text:
Phase 2 adds no event bus and no hooks: nothing in 0.6 would consume them. Where Phase 3 will emit an event, Phase 2 returns the data instead, so Phase 3 only has to publish it.

Phase 2 returns Where Phase 3 event IndexIssue list in the snapshot, and in IndexProgress index.build(on_datasource=...) index.column_failed ConnectionCheck datasources.test(), check() datasource.failed Parse retries, in the trace structured() llm.parse_retry The rule that denied a table, in the log and the trace Scope.rule_for policy.decision The pointer switch, in the log IndexStore.set_pointers index.swapped Purge counts storage.purge() retention.purged

Built: the events published (Wave A, E4)

Wave A publishes each of these (wave_a.md, row E4). Engine events go on the runtime's bus (ctx.bus), since an index build, a datasource check and a purge run outside any question: rebuild_index publishes index.started and index.failed, IndexingOrchestrator publishes one index.column_failed per IndexIssue (the issue only, never a sample value) and index.swapped from _commit, Runtime.check_datasource and try_datasource publish datasource.failed, and engine.storage.purge() publishes retention.purged with the counts it returns. Run events go through the run's scope: structured() publishes llm.parse_retry before each retry, with the validation messages only, and policy.decision is published for a denial at the logical validator, the curated matcher and the datasource resolver (when it refuses every candidate), never by Scope itself. The data Phase 2 returns is unchanged.

docs.title: 10. Bugs Phase 2 fixes
docs.text:
# Bug Evidence Fixed by B5 The snapshot is registered before the index switch, and readers use the "latest" snapshot indexing/orchestrator.py (register_snapshot before refresh_schema_chunks); get_latest_* in the resolver, retriever, curated matcher and datasources.schema() S2 B18 Every adapter's connection model ignores unknown keys, so a typo is silent model_config = {"extra": "ignore"} in all five adapters B1 B19 pytest.ini tells you to run nl2sql setup --demo, which 0.5 removed pytest.ini, the integration marker T1 B20 SQLite's "timeout" is a lock wait, so a slow query is never stopped adapters/sqlite/adapter.py B3 B21 Read-only is enforced only on SQLite, and only with options.read_only adapters/*/adapter.py B3 B22 Indexing reflects the database twice and runs COUNT(*) on every table sqlalchemy_base/adapter.py (fetch_schema_contact, fetch_schema_metadata, _get_row_count) B2 B23 Text values are always collected into the index and prompts sqlalchemy_base/adapter.py (_get_sample_values) B2 B24 explain and cost_estimate are broken and have no callers adapters/mssql, adapters/sqlite, sqlalchemy_base/models.py B2 B25 Changing the embedding model is refused instead of building a new index EmbeddingModelMismatchError in indexing/vector_store.py S2 B26 check() reports every connection failure at stage connect test_connection() -> bool B3

The rest of the original list: B1 to B4, B6 to B12 and B15 to B17 were fixed in 0.4.1 and 0.5. B13 (results readable by anyone with the request id) is a later policy step, and B14 (OpenTelemetry only on the CLI path) is Phase 3.

docs.title: 11. Boundary and invariant changes
docs.text: Rule Change The SDK imports only pydantic and the standard library Still true of nl2sql_sdk. nl2sql_sdk.sqlalchemy may also import SQLAlchemy and sqlglot; nl2sql_sdk.testing may also import pytest and sqlglot. An adapter imports only the SDK, its driver, SQLAlchemy, sqlglot, pydantic and the standard library Unchanged Nothing outside nl2sql/adapters/ imports SQLAlchemy or a driver Unchanged. New: only nl2sql/storage/ imports chromadb or sqlite3. No dialect name outside the adapters nl2sql/storage/ joins the scanned folders. storage/sqlite.py is an exception, as schema/sqlite_store.py is today: it names the engine's own metadata store, not a datasource. The import-time rule import nl2sql still loads no driver, chromadb or onnxruntime. Stores are imported when built. New Every place that decides table access calls a Scope; nothing outside nl2sql/policies/ matches policy patterns.

docs.title: 13. Release 0.6
docs.text:
• release-please opens the release PR as usual. Releasing is the owner's act (see Releasing); no agent merges it.
  • docs/releases/0.6.0.md is written with the release-notes process. Its "breaking changes" table covers: the storage sub-blocks and the new index namespace (run nl2sql index after upgrading), the policy pattern rules (allow/deny replace allowed_datasources/allowed_tables; two-part patterns are rejected), denied tables hidden from the planner, sample_values off by default, strict connection keys, adapter interface version 2, LLM and embeddings provider interface version 2, and the deleted index.build(full=..., switch_guard=...) arguments and settings.schema.version_mismatch.
  • Before tagging, the realdb workflow is run on demand on main, and the owner runs python scripts/testbed.py run -- pytest -m realdb once on the GCP VM. Both results go in the release notes.
