docs.title: Pipeline Architecture
docs.text: This document consolidates the LangGraph pipeline architecture as implemented in code. It describes the control graph, logical DAG, routing, and execution/aggregation flow. Node and subgraph details live in their respective sections.

docs.title: End-to-end flow
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    Resolver[DatasourceResolverNode] --> Decomposer[DecomposerNode]
    Decomposer --> Router[layer_router]
    Router --> SqlAgent[SQL Agent Subgraph]
    SqlAgent --> Router
    Router --> Aggregator[EngineAggregatorNode]
    Aggregator --> Synthesizer[AnswerSynthesizerNode]

docs.title: Control graph nodes
docs.text:
• CuratedMatcherNode: the entry point when curated answers are configured; a verified answer goes straight to the aggregator
  • pinned_entry (PinnedEntryNode in nl2sql.pipeline.pinned): the entry point of a pinned run's graph (build_graph(ctx, pinned=True): a plan passed as run_query(plan=...), or an approval's); it checks each datasource against the caller's scope and goes to the layer router, so no curated matcher, resolver or decomposer runs
  • DatasourceResolverNode
  • DecomposerNode
  • layer_router (routing function, not a node class)
  • EngineAggregatorNode
  • AnswerSynthesizerNode

docs.title: Entry points
docs.text:
• build_graph(ctx) builds the control graph in nl2sql.pipeline.graph.
  • run_with_graph(ctx, user_query, ...) executes the graph with timeouts and cancellation in nl2sql.pipeline.runtime.

docs.title: Control graph and logical DAG
docs.text:
The system uses two orchestration layers:

  • Control graph (LangGraph StateGraph): runtime nodes and routing.
  • Logical DAG (ExecutionDAG): deterministic compute plan, built by the decomposer (nodes/decomposer/dag.py::build_execution_dag) from the sub-queries it just wrote, not by a node of its own.
graph TD
    Scan1[scan:subquery_1] --> Combine[combine:group_1]
    Scan2[scan:subquery_2] --> Combine
    Combine --> PostAgg[post_aggregate]
    PostAgg --> PostSort[post_sort]

ExecutionDAG.layers are computed deterministically by _layered_toposort() and consumed by the router to dispatch scan nodes.

docs.title: ExecutionDAG node kinds (actual)
docs.text:
ExecutionDAG nodes are LogicalNode instances with:

  • kind: scan, combine, post_filter, post_aggregate, post_project, post_sort, post_limit
  • inputs: upstream node IDs
  • attributes: operation-specific metadata for a combine or post-combine node (join keys, filters, metrics). A scan node carries none: its ID is its sub-query's ID, so everything about it is one lookup away in decomposer_response.

docs.title: Routing and subgraph selection
docs.text:
build_scan_layer_router() selects the next scan layer with missing artifacts and dispatches subgraphs in parallel using Send(). A scan node's ID is its sub-query's ID, so the datasource comes from that SubQuery.

Subgraph selection is capability-based via resolve_subgraph():

flowchart TD
    DatasourceId[DatasourceId] --> Capabilities[DatasourceCapability set]
    Capabilities --> SubgraphRegistry[SubgraphRegistry]
    SubgraphRegistry --> Match{RequiredSubset}
    Match -->|yes| Subgraph[SelectedSubgraph]
    Match -->|no| Error[PipelineExecutionError]

If no compatible subgraph is found, routing raises PipelineExecutionError (an NL2SQLError carrying the PipelineError payload on .error) and terminates the pipeline. A router may only return routing decisions, so it cannot report the failure as a PipelineError value in state the way a node does.

docs.title: SQL agent subgraph lifecycle
docs.text:
The only registered subgraph today is sql_agent (build_sql_agent_graph()).

See subgraphs/sql_agent.md for full lifecycle, retry semantics, and node wiring.

docs.title: Execution, artifacts, and aggregation
docs.text:
Executors produce ResultFrame objects, which are persisted via ArtifactStore and referenced by ArtifactRef. Aggregation reads artifacts and applies the logical DAG.

sequenceDiagram
    participant Adapter as DatasourceAdapter
    participant Exec as SqlExecutorService
    participant Store as ArtifactStore
    participant Agg as AggregationService

    Adapter->>Exec: ResultFrame
    Exec->>Store: create_artifact_ref(ResultFrame)
    Store-->>Exec: ArtifactRef
    Exec-->>Agg: ArtifactRef
    Agg->>Agg: load_scan / combine / post_op
    Agg-->>Exec: aggregated rows

Aggregation uses AggregationService(PolarsDuckdbEngine()) and executes layers sequentially.

docs.title: State model
docs.text:
Shared and subgraph state models are defined in graph_state.md. The pipeline uses:

  • GraphState for control graph execution and aggregation.
  • SubgraphExecutionState for subgraph-local execution.
  • wrap_subgraph() to merge subgraph outputs back into GraphState.

docs.title: Determinism
docs.text: Determinism guarantees and non-determinism sources are centralized in determinism.md.

docs.title: Known limitations (current)
docs.text:
• There is no execution sandbox; the SQL executor runs in-process on the pipeline thread pool (see ../execution/isolation.md).
  • VECTOR_BREAKER is the only circuit breaker. LLM calls and SQL execution are not breaker-guarded.

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text:
The engine's HookRunner (ctx.hooks, built by the runtime from the hooks section) is called at six points of every run; see Hooks.

Point Called from run.before run_with_graph's worker, before graph.invoke; a Modify rewrites user_query, a deny returns before the graph runs datasources.after DatasourceResolverNode, on the datasources it forwards plan.after ASTPlannerNode.after_plan(), on the planner's or the cache's plan, before the validator execute.before, execute.after ExecutorNode, and CuratedMatcherNode for a verified query answer.after AnswerSynthesizerNode, once the answer is written

A hook that stops the run (HOOK_DENIED, HOOK_FAILED, NEEDS_APPROVAL, or the cost rule's COST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED) ends it at the layer router once the layer in flight is done. A sub-query a hook dropped (scope="sub_query") reports status: "dropped" from wrap_subgraph(), with its reason as a HOOK_DENIED warning; the router still sends the run to the aggregator, which drops a join or compare group that needs it. SubgraphExecutionState.user_query carries the run's question (after run.before) into each sub-query for the hooks there.

A NEEDS_APPROVAL ending also puts an ApprovalRequest in the state's approvals_needed (built by wrap_subgraph(), or by the curated matcher on the verified path), so the result's status is needs_approval. The approved re-run pins the request's decomposition and plan through the pinned entry (plan_source="approved"); the hooks at execute.before see the run's approvals and the runner checks them. See Query API → Approval.

docs.title: Observability hooks (current)
docs.text: Observability stack and callback behavior are documented in ../observability/stack.md.

docs.title: Wave A: events, observers, hooks, evals and routing (design)
docs.text:
Status: design

This page is the design for Wave A of the product redesign, which ships as release 0.7. Each pull request in the PR plan adds a "Built" note to the sections it builds, as Phase 1 and Phase 2 did; A0 (the foundation), E1, H1, H2, V1, E2, V2, E4, S1 and D1 are built. Phase 1 is Configuration v2 and the extension registry; Phase 2 is Phase 2: test bed, storage, providers, policies and adapter SDK v2. Wave A is what those pages called "Phase 3", plus the cross-database routing work ("Phase R") and three smaller tracks.

docs.title: Principles
docs.text:
The owner restated them for Wave A, and they rank above everything below:

  • The package is the product; the playground only demonstrates it. Every capability is a public facade method or an extension point first. The CLI, nl2sql-api, the playground and the MCP server use the public API only, and nothing in this design exists only in one of them.
  • No active users: design it correctly, not compatibly. No shims, no aliases, no deprecation paths. Where a 0.6 shape is wrong, 0.7 replaces it.
  • Never over-engineer. Ship what 0.7 needs; the cut lists below are part of the design.
  • Everything is configurable in nl2sql.yaml (and its section files) or in code with dependency injection, extensible through the registry, and events and observability apply everywhere: a question on the generated or the verified-query path, an index build, a purge, an LLM swap, from the CLI or the server. Hooks apply to every run, on both paths; there is no hook on an index build in 0.7.

Two older rules shape this wave in particular: the model emits a typed plan, never SQL (it decides how evals are seeded), and anything the generator can reject, the validator rejects first (it decides where the join-key check and the hook boundary live).

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
The owner was asleep when this design was written and asked that its recommendations be used, each marked for confirmation. D9 to D13 were already on record from the final redesign; D14 onwards are new. Each decision is written into the section it affects. An independent review of the first draft (PR #308) changed several of them; those are marked amended after review and are still the owner's to confirm.

# Decision Status Where D9 Hooks fail closed; observers fail open. A hook that raises denies, unless that hook is configured on_error: open. An observer that raises is logged and skipped; it can never fail a run. decided overnight, owner to confirm Hooks, Observers D10 Approval ends the run, and the re-run pins what was approved. A hook at execute.before may answer needs_approval; the run ends with status needs_approval and an ApprovalRequest that carries the decomposition, the sub-query, its validated plan and the SQL's hash, bound to the asker. An approver re-runs the question with an Approval; the re-run uses the pinned decomposition and plan, validates and generates again, and compares the SQL's hash. Nothing is queued or stored. decided overnight, amended after review, owner to confirm Approval D11 A dated price table ships in llm/; a model it does not list has a null cost. llm.prices in the config adds or overrides rows. decided overnight, owner to confirm Cost and caps D12 Evals use curated answers by default and record each answer's source; every case a verified query answered is also run with curated answers off, so the report has a generated-only accuracy over every case. Modes plans and retrieval always run with curated answers off, and mode full with the plan cache off, as tier 1 and tier 2 do today. decided overnight, amended after review, owner to confirm Evals D13 No masking at execute.after on day one. After the validator a hook may only allow, deny or ask for approval. decided overnight, owner to confirm Hooks D14 Event and the Observer interface live in the SDK (nl2sql_sdk.events, pydantic only), so an observer plugin depends on the SDK alone. Hook and Scorer live in the engine, because they see engine types (a plan, a QueryResult). decided overnight, owner to confirm The event bus D15 Events never carry result rows, sample values, keys or header values. They carry the question, SQL, table names and counts; the question and the answer text (answer.delta) are carried and may contain values from the data. The full QueryResult is never published on the bus: only the stream's own terminal event holds it. decided overnight, amended after review, owner to confirm The catalog D16 policy.decision is published for denials, at the enforcement points only: the validator's table refusal, the curated matcher's refusal of a verified query, and the resolver's datasource refusal. Scope itself publishes nothing, because it is also asked to filter (the retriever, the value check), which would flood the bus with tables nobody asked for. decided overnight, amended after review, owner to confirm The catalog D17 stream_query yields bus Events, from a caller-safe allow-list: run.*, node.*, answer.delta, result.manifest, sanity.flagged and run.limit_reached. QueryEvent and its six type names are deleted, with no alias. Operator events (policy.decision, hook.decision, llm.call and the rest) are reached only through engine.events.subscribe. decided overnight, amended after review, owner to confirm The run's stream D18 OpenTelemetry becomes the otel extra and an observer. settings.observability is replaced by an observers: section; with no section the engine runs log and audit. decided overnight, owner to confirm Observers D19 The audit log moves under storage.path (audit/, JSON lines, 90 days, purged by engine.storage.purge()), written by the audit observer: one summary line per run (who, which datasources and tables, status, source) plus the denials, approvals, limits and changes. common/event_logger.py is deleted (bug B27). decided overnight, amended after review, owner to confirm Built-in observers D20 Caps: max_llm_calls defaults to 60, max_cost_usd to none. A cost cap with a configured model the price table cannot price is a ConfigError when the engine is built. decided overnight, owner to confirm Per-question caps D21 The six hook points are run.before, datasources.after, plan.after, execute.before, execute.after and answer.after. The first three may modify; the last three may not. decided overnight, owner to confirm The six points D22 No built-in hooks in 0.7. The docs carry a 30-line example; the tests use fakes. decided overnight, owner to confirm Hooks D23 Hooks run in config order. The first deny ends the point; modifications chain, each hook seeing the previous one's output. decided overnight, owner to confirm Hook decisions D24 An approval is bound to the asker and checked by the engine. The request's id hashes the question, the asker's user_id and tenant_id, the hook, the datasource, the plan and the SQL's hash; the engine recomputes it, and an approval for another asker or another request is refused. Approvers are the hook's approver_roles, by default policies.admin_roles. An approved decision counts as Allow, and the next hook at the point still runs. An Approval is not signed and does not expire: it is trusted exactly as far as the UserContext a caller passes is trusted today. decided overnight, amended after review, owner to confirm Approval D25 engine.evals only. No top-level engine.evaluate (the top level stays questions only). engine.benchmark, BenchmarkAPI, BenchmarkConfig and nl2sql benchmark are deleted. decided overnight, owner to confirm The facade D26 Seeding asks the model for questions and typed plans, never SQL, five per call, under a cost cap (max_cost_usd, by default evals.yaml's). The engine's validator and generator turn each plan into SQL, the adapter runs it read-only, and the case is written with status: draft. decided overnight, amended after review, owner to confirm Seeding D27 regenerate runs gold SQL through the datasource's adapter. evaluation/gold.py's direct sqlite3 use and its boundary exemption go. decided overnight, owner to confirm Regenerating expected rows D28 Routing fuses five signals with reciprocal rank fusion (k = 60), keeps the top 3 (candidates defaults to 3), and drops a datasource whose best entry similarity is under half the most similar datasource's: the floor is on similarity, not on the fused score, because the fused scores of a handful of datasources are always within a few percent of each other. A datasource a signal did not rank gets the rank after the last one it did, so having entries of a type (only one datasource with verified queries, say) is not a vote. Only entries the caller's scope allows vote: a hidden table or column, or a verified query that reads a hidden table, never votes or reaches the trace. candidates, max_datasources, max_sub_queries and floor_ratio are settings; the vote depth and the fusion constant stay constants until a measurement asks for a knob. decided overnight, amended after review (twice: the floor on similarity, the absent rank, table scope, after the review of PR #316), owner to confirm Phase R D29 A decomposition over max_sub_queries ends the run with QUESTION_TOO_BROAD, whose message asks for a narrower question. It is not retried. decided overnight, owner to confirm Limits D30 Join keys are coerced, not just checked. The engine's aggregator casts both sides of a join key to the declared dtype (in polars, so no dialect is involved), and a value that does not convert is a warning. The validator rejects only categories that cannot be coerced (temporal against number or boolean); an unknown type is not checked. The plan has no CAST, so the validator never asks the model for one. decided overnight, amended after review, owner to confirm The join-key type check D31 Structural diffs are stored with the new version in the state store (store interface version 2). A rename is reported as a drop and an add. index.check() never re-indexes. decided overnight, owner to confirm Schema drift D32 Sanity checks: a missing filter value with a close match, and a confirmed fan-out under COUNT (repairable as COUNT(DISTINCT ...)), are retried once. A fan-out under SUM or AVG (the plan has no derived tables to repair it), an all-null column, a missing value with no close match, and any check with no retry left are warnings. Many-to-many sums are one case of JOIN_FAN_OUT, not a code of their own. decided overnight, amended after review, owner to confirm Answer sanity checks D33 MCP is stdio only in 0.7, behind the mcp extra; the caller's role comes from nl2sql mcp --role, by default policies.default_role, and with neither the server refuses to start, except under policies.allow_all, where it starts and logs a warning that every table is readable; an unknown --role is refused, allow_all included. Over MCP a refusal is always the generic one, whatever refusal_names_tables says. engine.datasources.schema() requires a user_context and hides denied tables (bug B29); there is no default admin view, and the playground's /api/schema requires its role. decided overnight, amended after review (twice: the second after the attack review of PR #325), owner to confirm MCP server D34 QueryResult.warnings is typed (RunWarning: code, node, message, sub_query_id, detail), replacing the list of dicts. It lands with the sanity checks (S1), the PR that adds warnings, not in the foundation. decided overnight, amended after review, owner to confirm Answer sanity checks D35 The first PR adds the shared shapes, and only those: the SDK's Event and Observer, the bus, the catalog, RunScope with its publish slots, the registry kinds, the config shapes, the error codes, the new status, stop and approvals_needed result fields, and stub engine.events and engine.evals namespaces. The parallel PRs then never edit config/models.py, common/errors.py, events/run.py or public_api.py's namespace list; the overlaps that remain are listed in the PR plan. decided overnight, amended after review, owner to confirm PR plan

docs.title: Where 0.6 leaves us
docs.text: Area What 0.6 has What is still wrong Events stream_query yields six QueryEvent types from a LangChain callback (pipeline/events.py). Phase 2 returns, but does not publish, the data for six more (phase2.md, section 9). No bus. Nothing outside a streamed question can observe the engine: an index build, a purge, an LLM swap. Logs TraceContextFilter and trace_context() in common/logger.py trace_context() is never called, so every log line's trace_id is null (the rest of bug B14). OpenTelemetry Three instruments in common/metrics.py; configure_metrics Configured only in cli/commands/run.py, so nl2sql-api and the playground never export. opentelemetry is a hard dependency, loaded by the runtime through pipeline/plan_cache.py and services/callbacks/token_handler.py (B14). Audit common/event_logger.py: one llm.changed record per LLM swap A module-global logger that creates logs/audit_events.log in the process's working directory (B27). Cost TokenUsageCallback prices calls from llm.prices, which is empty by default; evaluation/prices.py holds a dated table that only tier 2 reads A run's usage.cost is null unless the user writes prices (B28). No cap on a question's cost or calls. Hooks None Nothing can veto or rewrite a step, or ask for a person's approval. Evals engine.benchmark: tier 1 (gold plans, fake LLM), tier 2 (real model, dollar cap, baseline gate), retrieval recall; chinook_gold.yaml; nl2sql benchmark Chinook only, one fixed file shape, no scorer interface, gold rows produced with sqlite3 outside the adapter, and no way to build a gold set for your own database. Curated answers are off by default in tier 2. Routing One schema.datasource index entry per datasource (description, domains and every sample question in one text); retrieve_datasource_candidates(k=5); the answerability verdict already returns a list One phrasing dilutes the others; tables and columns never vote; no fusion, no floor, no limit on datasources or sub-queries; TABLE_K, PLANNING_K and k=5 are constants; join keys across datasources are not type-checked. Drift Immutable snapshots with a structural fingerprint (schema/fingerprint.py), the last max_versions kept, the plan cache keyed on schema_version Health is stale only without a build or after a curated.yaml change. Nothing compares the live database with the build, and no diff between versions exists. Sanity VALUE_NOT_FOUND: an empty result filtered on a value its column lacks (executor/value_check.py), retried once with the closest values Nothing catches join fan-out, sums over many-to-many joins, or all-null columns. Warnings are untyped dicts. MCP None

docs.title: What ships in 0.7
docs.text: Goal What it means An event bus Synchronous and in process. Typed events for a run and its steps, model calls, hook and policy decisions, index builds, drift, purges, LLM swaps and evals. engine.events.subscribe(); stream_query yields the run's events, each ready to send as a Server-Sent Event. Observers A registry kind (nl2sql.observers). Built-in log (correlated: every line carries its trace_id), audit and otel (the otel extra). import nl2sql loads no opentelemetry. Observers fail open. Cost and caps A dated price table in llm/. A cap on each question's cost and on its model calls, ending the run as stopped with a typed reason. Hooks Six points through a run, a registry kind (nl2sql.hooks), fail closed with a per-hook on_error: open. Modify before the validator, deny only after it, held by an architecture test. Approval A run that ends needs_approval, and a re-run that carries the approval. Evals as a product engine.evals, evals.yaml and suite files, five scorers behind a Scorer interface (nl2sql.scorers), regenerate through the adapter, the regression gate, nl2sql eval, and seeding a draft gold set from your own database. The Chinook gold set moves over unchanged. Phase R Routing on one entry per example phrasing, table and column votes and reciprocal rank fusion; up to 3 datasources and 6 sub-queries per question; retrieval limits as settings; join keys coerced in the aggregator and checked in the validator; routing evals beyond Chinook as the gate. Schema drift, measured engine.index.check() and nl2sql index --check, a stored structural diff per version, its impact on verified queries and policies, and a schema.drifted event. Answer sanity checks Join fan-out, many-to-many sums, all-null columns and missing filter values, as typed warnings or one retry. An MCP server nl2sql mcp over stdio with ask, list_datasources and describe_table, on the public facade only.

docs.title: Not in Wave A
docs.text: Later Why it waits Hooks on every event; an async bus; a stored event log; webhooks; /metrics Cut from the final design. Observers cover what an event is for; a stored log and webhooks are a product of their own. Masking result values at execute.after D13: deny first, masking once deny is proven A hook on an index build No use for one yet; events cover observing a build Repairing a SUM or AVG fan-out The plan has no derived tables; splitting the question in the decomposer is a Wave B idea (D32) Approval expiry D24: nothing is stored, so there is nothing to expire An approval queue, signed approvals D10, D24: the run ends and is asked again; nothing is stored Pluggable result comparators, a built-in LLM judge, an eval scheduler, a leaderboard UI Cut from the final design. A scorer plugin can do the first two. Automatic re-indexing on drift, scheduled checks Drift is measured first (owner) MCP over HTTP with auth Wave C REST routes for evals, approval and drift Wave D (API parity) Glossary, knowledge sources, clarification results Wave B; see the preview at the end of this page

docs.title: 2. Order of work
docs.text:
One foundation PR, then four tracks that touch different files, then three smaller tracks for whichever agent frees up first.

flowchart LR

docs.title: The event
docs.text:
# nl2sql_sdk.events (pydantic and the standard library only, D14)
class Event(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)
    name: str                    # "node.finished", from the catalog
    at: datetime                 # UTC
    trace_id: str | None = None  # the run's id; None for an engine event (an index build)
    tenant_id: str | None = None
    data: dict[str, Any] = {}    # JSON-ready; the catalog's model for this name, dumped

    def sse(self) -> str:        # "event: <name>\ndata: <json>\n\n"
        ...

class Observer(Protocol):
    interface_version: ClassVar[int]           # 1
    config_model: ClassVar[type[BaseModel]]
    events: ClassVar[frozenset[str] | None]    # the names it wants; None means every event
    @classmethod
    def from_config(cls, cfg: BaseModel, *, folder: Path) -> "Observer": ...   # folder: storage.path
    def on_event(self, event: Event) -> None: ...
    def close(self) -> None: ...

trace_id is the name the facade already uses for a run (QueryResult.trace_id, engine.traces.get, engine.results), so an event, a log line, a trace and a result page all join on one value.

docs.title: The bus
docs.text:
# nl2sql/events/bus.py
class EventBus:
    def subscribe(self, fn: Callable[[Event], None], names: Iterable[str] | None = None,
                  *, fail: Literal["open", "raise"] = "open") -> Subscription: ...
    def publish(self, name: str, data: BaseModel | Mapping[str, Any] = {}, *,
                trace_id: str | None = None) -> Event: ...
    def close(self) -> None: ...               # closes every observer it built
Rule Detail Synchronous, in process publish calls each subscriber in subscription order, on the publishing thread, and returns. There is no queue and no worker. A slow observer slows the run; the docs say so, and otel exports in its SDK's own background thread. One bus per engine Runtime.bus, built with the runtime. Two engines in one process share nothing (the invariant An Engine Owns Its Config). Observers fail open (D9) An exception from a subscriber is caught, logged once per subscriber and event name at WARNING, and counted (EventBus.failures). The bus never raises into the engine. The internal run collectors subscribe with fail="raise", because a broken collector is an engine bug a test must see. Thread safety Sub-queries run on LangGraph's worker threads, so publish is called concurrently. The bus holds its subscriber list immutably (copy on subscribe); an observer that keeps state locks it. Checked names publish refuses a name the catalog does not list (a ValueError: an engine bug), and validates data against the name's model. A test scans every publish("...") call site for catalogued names.

Engine events go through ctx.bus. Code that runs outside a question (an index build, storage.purge, replace_llm, index.check, a datasource check, an eval run) publishes with ctx.bus.publish(...) explicitly; it always holds the runtime.

Run events go through the run's scope. A RunScope (nl2sql/events/run.py) is the life of one question on the bus. Where it sits follows from the code as it is:

  1. It is opened by the caller that builds the result: QueryAPI.run_query and stream_query, and the eval runner. run_with_graph returns graph state; the QueryResult is built afterwards by result_from_state in QueryAPI (api/query_api.py), so only there can run.finished be published with the result's summary. The scope makes the run's trace_id and hands it to run_with_graph, which puts it in GraphState.
  2. Its context is entered inside the worker. run_with_graph submits the graph to its own ThreadPoolExecutor with the caller's copy_context() (pipeline/runtime.py; 0.6 submitted it without one), so the worker inherits the caller's context variables (a request's keys, the run's pinned LLM set), and policy_engine.run() is entered inside _invoke. The scope's context variables (the trace_id, the tenant_id and the scope itself) are entered there too, beside it; LangGraph's own worker threads then inherit them, as they already inherit current_datasource_id. Code deep in a run (the structured-output retry in llm/wires/, the hook runner, the budget, the enforcement points) publishes with the module function nl2sql.events.publish(name, data), which reads the scope from the context and is for code inside a RunScope only: outside one it does nothing. The same context variable is what TraceContextFilter reads, which fixes the null trace_id on every log line (B14).
  3. It closes exactly once. run.finished (with the summary) when QueryAPI has the result, or run.failed when run_with_graph raised or the result could not be built. Both are published on the bus, so the audit observer and the otel run span see a crashed run too.
  4. A closed scope drops what comes after. A timed-out run is answered while its graph winds down in the background (run_with_graph's TimeoutError branch); the llm.call and node.* events it publishes after run.finished are dropped and counted (RunScope.late_events), so no observer sees a run continue after it ended. The usage in run.finished is what was spent until the answer; the docs say a timed-out run may spend a little more.

RunScope is also where the run-scoped pieces attach and detach (RunScope.attach): the stream's queue, the usage collector, the budget, and the trace's event list. It is the one place later PRs plug a run-scoped piece into, so they do not each edit run_with_graph or QueryAPI.

docs.title: The catalog
docs.text:
nl2sql/events/catalog.py lists every event the engine publishes, with a pydantic model for its data. engine.events.catalog() returns it (name, description, the data's JSON Schema), so an observer author and the docs page read the same list. Events never carry result rows, sample values, keys or header values (D15); the question and the answer text are carried and may contain values from the data. test_no_bus_event_carries_rows runs a demo question with a capturing subscriber and checks that no rows key appears at any depth of any event.

Run events (they have a trace_id):

Name Data Published by run.started question, user_id, tenant_id, roles, datasource_id, execute RunScope, when it opens run.finished A summary, never rows: status (success, plan_only, error, needs_approval, stopped), duration_s, usage totals with cost, error_codes, source (verified, generated), datasources used, tables read (datasource.schema.table), result_manifest, user_id, roles RunScope, once, last run.failed message, error_code RunScope: the run could not start, or crashed outside the pipeline (today's stream error event) node.started node, sub_query_id The LangChain callback in pipeline/events.py node.finished node, sub_query_id, seconds, ok The same answer.delta field (summary, content), text The same result.manifest results (ResultSummary list: columns, row counts, truncated) The same, after the aggregator llm.call node, agent, model, the six token counts, latency_s, cost, usage_reported, error (redacted) TokenUsageCallback, per finished call llm.parse_retry agent, schema, attempt, errors (validation messages only) structured() in llm/wires/__init__.py (phase2.md, section 9) plan_cache.lookup datasource_id, hit pipeline/plan_cache.py (replaces its OpenTelemetry counter) policy.decision datasource_id, schema, table (None for a datasource), rule, step; denials only (D16) The enforcement points only: LogicalValidatorNode._validate_policy, CuratedMatcherNode._check_access and the resolver's datasource refusal (phase2.md, section 9) hook.decision hook, point, decision (allow, modify, deny, needs_approval, approved, error), reason, sub_query_id, approver (for approved), seconds The hook runner run.limit_reached limit (max_cost_usd, max_llm_calls), value, spent The budget sanity.flagged code, sub_query_id, retry The sanity checks

Engine events (no trace_id, except where a run caused them):

Name Data Published by datasource.failed datasource_id, stage, message, fix Runtime.check_datasource and try_datasource (phase2.md, section 9) index.started datasource_id, namespace indexing/rebuild.py index.column_failed datasource_id, table, column, stage, message the orchestrator, one per IndexIssue (phase2.md, section 9) index.swapped datasource_id, namespace, build_id, schema_version, replaced_build_id, replaced_schema_version, counts IndexingOrchestrator._commit (phase2.md, section 9) index.failed datasource_id, reason indexing/rebuild.py schema.drifted datasource_id, from_version, to_version (None for the live database), detected_by (check, build), the diff's counts index.check() and the orchestrator retention.purged counts per slot engine.storage.purge() (phase2.md, section 9) llm.changed by, changes (old and new provider and model per agent; never a key) Runtime.replace_llm (configuration_v2.md, section 7) eval.case suite, case_id, role, pass, source, scores, cost engine.evals.run eval.finished suite, cases, accuracy, accuracy_generated, cost, gate engine.evals.run

docs.title: The run's stream
docs.text:
engine.stream_query yields Events (D17). QueryEvent, its type literal and the names node_started, node_finished, result_manifest, answer_delta, final and error are deleted. event.sse() is the event as one Server-Sent Event, which is all nl2sql-api's POST /query/stream sends.

The stream is the caller's, so it carries only what the caller may see. It yields its own run's events from an allow-list, in publish order: run.started, node.started, node.finished, answer.delta, result.manifest, sanity.flagged, run.limit_reached, and then exactly one of run.finished or run.failed. policy.decision would tell a denied user which table exists (the validator names no table unless policies.refusal_names_tables is set, for exactly that reason), and hook.decision and llm.call are operator data (hook names and reasons, models and cost). Those reach an operator through engine.events.subscribe only. test_stream_never_yields_policy_or_hook_or_llm_call_events holds it.

The terminal event holds the result, on the stream only. The stream's run.finished is the bus event's summary plus data.result, the QueryResult as JSON (as final holds it today). QueryAPI adds the result to the stream's copy; the event published on the bus never has it (D15).

0.6 0.7 QueryEvent(type="node_started", data={"node"}) Event(name="node.started", data={"node", "sub_query_id"}) answer_delta answer.delta result_manifest result.manifest final (the QueryResult as JSON) run.finished, whose data.result is the QueryResult as JSON (stream only) error run.failed (none) run.started, sanity.flagged, run.limit_reached

The CLI's nl2sql run, the playground and nl2sql-api move to the new names in the same PR.

docs.title: The facade
docs.text:
Method What it does engine.events.subscribe(fn, names=None) -> Subscription A function (or an Observer) called for every event, or for names: the operator's view of every run and of the engine. Subscription.close() detaches it. Fails open. engine.events.catalog() -> list[EventInfo] Every event name, its description and its data's JSON Schema engine.stream_query(...) -> Iterator[Event] As above

Event is exported from nl2sql (from nl2sql_sdk.events, lazily).

Built: the event, the bus, the catalog and the run scope (A0)

nl2sql_sdk/events.py holds Event (with sse(), whose data line is the whole event as JSON) and the Observer protocol. nl2sql/events/ holds EventBus (bus.py; publish also takes tenant_id), the catalog with a strict model per event and catalog() returning EventInfo (catalog.py, which also defines RunStatus), and RunScope, current_scope() and the module publish (run.py). Runtime.bus is built with the runtime and closed with it. QueryAPI.open_scope(question, datasource_id=, execute=, user_context=) makes the scope, with the run's usage collector, and calls start() (which publishes run.started); QueryAPI.close_scope(scope, result) closes it with finish(result, tables=...), or fail(message, code) when the summary cannot be built, and a result built without a graph run is accepted. run_query and stream_query open their own scope, or take an open one as scope= (internal; Wave C's turn opens it before its rewrite call) and close it. RunScope.callbacks() is the usage collector and the LangChain handlers attached (the budget, from E3): a model call made in the run but outside the graph passes them, inside entered(), so it counts in the run's usage and carries its trace_id. run_with_graph takes scope=, uses its trace_id and its usage collector, enters it beside policy_engine.run() in _invoke (submitted with the caller's copy_context()) and adds its callbacks() to the graph's. That is all of Wave C's A2 need (wave_c.md); E1 keeps scope= when it moves stream_query to Events. The scope sets the context TraceContextFilter reads, so log lines written during a run carry its trace_id and tenant_id. attach takes a function or an object with on_event (subscribed to this run's events with fail="raise"), a LangChain callback handler (added to the graph's callbacks) and anything with close (closed with the scope); a closed scope refuses attach with RuntimeError. Closing detaches every subscription and calls every close even when an attached piece raised on the terminal event. run_query and stream_query close the scope with run.failed on any BaseException (a KeyboardInterrupt too) and re-raise it. The scope holds its lock while the bus delivers each of its events, so run.finished is always last; the cost is that a run's events reach subscribers one at a time and finish (a timed-out run's too) waits for the delivery in flight, so an observer must never block (the Observer and RunScope docstrings say so; E2's audit and otel hand slow work to a queue). run.finished's usage and result_manifest copy only the catalog models' own fields, so a field added to UsageTotals or ResultSummary never fails a run. run.finished's tables come from each sub-query's plan, or a verified query's SQL, as datasource.schema.table. engine.events and engine.evals are empty namespaces; E1 adds subscribe and catalog.

Built: run events, the stream and engine.events (E1)

pipeline/events.py's RunEvents(publish) is a LangChain callback that publishes node.started, node.finished (each with its sub_query_id, from the sub-query subgraph's subgraph_id and inherited by the runs inside it), result.manifest (results only; the event's trace_id is the request_id) and answer.delta. QueryAPI.open_scope attaches one to every scope (scope.attach(RunEvents(scope.publish))), so every run publishes its steps, streamed or not, and scope.callbacks() is now the usage collector, the RunEvents, then whatever was attached. QueryEvent is deleted, with its export. The allow-list is one definition: each catalog entry (EventSpec) has stream and audit flags, and nl2sql.events.STREAM_EVENTS (D17) and AUDIT_EVENTS (D19, which E2's audit observer reads; of hook.decision it keeps the decisions the entry's description names) are derived from them; EventInfo reports both. A later event joins a list by its own catalog entry (Wave B's events stay off the stream). The stream: QueryAPI.stream_query(..., scope=None, names=STREAM_EVENTS) yields Events. RunScope.follow(fn, names) replays what the scope already published (RunScope.events, a new list of every event the scope published, in order) and attaches fn, both under the scope's lock, so an event published meanwhile is neither lost nor doubled; the stream follows its scope with names minus run.finished, and puts its own run.finished: the summary close_scope (which now returns the published event) returned, plus data.result. So a scope opened before the stream (Wave C's turn, need A2) still gives the stream its run.started and anything the turn published in it, and names (internal) is where Wave C's conversations.stream adds conversation.rewritten (need A4); it appends conversation.turn after the stream's run.finished itself. The stream ends with exactly one terminal event whatever breaks: when no run.failed reached it (the scope could not open, was already closed, or a collector raised on its terminal event), it ends with a run.failed built in place, with the scope's trace_id when there is a scope. A KeyboardInterrupt ends it the same way. scope= is kept on run_query and stream_query; a closed scope= is a ValueError at the call. engine.events.subscribe(fn, names=None) subscribes to Runtime.bus (fail open) and catalog() returns catalog(). The trace document has events (the scope's events but answer.delta); since run_with_graph writes the trace before run.finished is published, the list ends before it. That reads scope.events in pipeline/runtime.py (one argument to write_run_trace), not tracing/recorder.py, a small difference from the file list above. nl2sql run, the playground (app.py and web/playground/src/stream.js, rebuilt) and nl2sql-api's stream route read the new names; each SSE data line is the whole event. The invariant Events Carry No Rows, and the Stream Carries No Operator Data is in invariants.md.

Built: the Phase 2 events, published (E4)

Engine events go through ctx.bus explicitly, never a context variable, because an index build and a purge run outside any RunScope; each carries the engine's tenant_id. rebuild_index wraps its on_datasource callback, so every IndexProgress it reports started publishes index.started (with ctx.namespace) and every failed one index.failed (a datasource that is unavailable, unknown, locked out by another build, or whose build raised). IndexingOrchestrator keeps ctx.bus and ctx.tenant_id: index_datasource publishes one index.column_failed per IndexIssue before the commit (table, column, stage, message: the issue, never the column's statistics or sample values, D15), and _commit publishes index.swapped after the pointer switch, with counts by entry type and the replaced pointer's build_id and schema_version (None on a first build), so a curated-only refresh publishes it too. Runtime._published(status) publishes datasource.failed for a failed DatasourceStatus; check_datasource returns through it, and try_datasource is now _published around _try_datasource (the old body), which is the whole runtime.py change. StorageAPI.purge publishes retention.purged with the counts it returns (audited, so the audit observer writes it to the current day's file after deleting the old ones). Run events use the module publish: structured()'s retry loop publishes llm.parse_retry before each retry (attempt 1 is the first retry; errors are pydantic's path: message lines, or the exception's type name, never the model's answer). policy.decision is published at the three enforcement points only (D16 amended): LogicalValidatorNode._validate_policy per refused table (step: logical_validator, schema the table's or the scope's default), CuratedMatcherNode._check_access on the refused table (step: curated_matcher; it now asks scope.rule_for, which allows wraps), and the resolver when the role check refuses every datasource it was asked about: every registered one before the routing search (R1's scope filter), or the explicit or only one (_publish_refusals, one per datasource, schema and table None, step: datasource_resolver, rule naming the roles or the policy check). The resolver's re-check after datasources.after hooks publishes nothing; the hook's own hook.decision covers it. After review: datasource.failed (message, fix), index.failed and index.column_failed run their text through nl2sql.tracing.trace.redact_for(ctx, text) (the trace's Redactor with collect_secrets(ctx); its patterns now also catch a bare user:password@host). For the values and profile stages, index.column_failed's message is a fixed sentence plus the new IndexIssue.error_type (SDK, optional, set by the SQLAlchemy base), so a cast error quoting a cell value never reaches the bus. The rule comes from the new Scope.datasource_rule() (reaches_datasource is datasource_rule() is None), which names a failed policy check, and the validator publishes once per (schema, table, rule). Test fakes that build an orchestrator or call rebuild_index need bus and tenant_id (tests/unit/index_helpers.py's TestIndex has them). Tests: tests/unit/test_phase2_events.py.

docs.title: The registry kind and the config
docs.text:
Kind Entry point group Interface Version Built-ins observer nl2sql.observers nl2sql_sdk.events.Observer 1 log, audit, otel

registry.add_observer(name, cls), @registry.observer(name). An observer is "attached, many" (configuration_v2.md, section 6): the config lists any number.

# nl2sql.yaml
observers: observers.yaml

# observers.yaml
- type: log
  level: INFO                     # node.started and answer.delta are logged only at DEBUG
- type: audit
  max_age_days: 90
- type: otel                      # needs nl2sql-engine[otel]
  endpoint: http://collector:4317
  metrics: true
  traces: true
- type: corp_siem                 # a plugin; its config_model checks the rest
  url: "${env:SIEM_URL}"

from nl2sql import Config, ObserverConfig
Config(..., observers=[ObserverConfig(type="log"), MyObserver()])   # a {type: ...} block or an object
Rule Detail No section observers absent means [{type: log}, {type: audit}] (D18). observers: [] means none. Objects skip the registry As every other kind: an Observer object is used as given. Validation type is resolved and the block validated by the observer's config_model at NL2SQL(...), with the usual "did you mean". otel without the extra installed is a ConfigError naming pip install "nl2sql-engine[otel]". Built when the engine is Subscribed to Runtime.bus in config order, and closed by engine.close(). settings.observability Deleted. exporter: otlp and otlp_endpoint become an otel block. Its two readers go with it in A0: cli/commands/run.py (configure_metrics) and cli/common/engine.py (JSON logs under otlp). Between A0 and E2 nothing exports to OpenTelemetry; no release falls in between.

Built: the observer kind and the section (A0)

The observer registry kind (add_observer, @registry.observer) and the observers section (ObserverConfig, or an object with on_event) are accepted and validated; nothing builds an observer yet (E2). Config.observers is None when the section is absent, which E2 reads as log and audit. settings.observability and its readers (nl2sql run's configure_metrics, the CLI's and nl2sql-api's switch to JSON logs) are gone. nl2sql --log-format text|json and NL2SQL_LOG_FORMAT choose the log format; configure_logging(json_format=None) reads the variable.

docs.title: Built-in observers
docs.text:
Observer What it does Keys log One log line per event on logger nl2sql.events: the name and a short summary of data. node.started and answer.delta are logged only when level is DEBUG, so the default adds about one line per step, not one per token. The trace_id reaches the line through the context, so with configure_logging(json_format=True) every line, the engine's own included, carries it. level (INFO), events (a list; by default all but the two above) audit JSON lines in <storage.path>/audit/<date>.jsonl. One summary line per run.finished and run.failed (trace_id, user, roles, datasources, tables read, status, source; never rows), so the log answers "who read payroll.salaries" without a line per allowed table. And one line per llm.changed, hook.decision with deny, needs_approval, approved or error, policy.decision, run.limit_reached, index.swapped, retention.purged and schema.drifted. Replaces common/event_logger.py (B27, D19). engine.storage.purge() deletes files older than max_age_days. max_age_days (90, at least 1) otel Metrics: nl2sql.node.duration, nl2sql.token.usage and nl2sql.plan_cache.lookups (as today, from node.finished, llm.call and plan_cache.lookup), and nl2sql.run.cost. Traces: one span per run (run.started to run.finished) with a child span per node, keyed by trace_id and sub_query_id. Sets its own MeterProvider and TracerProvider for its exporter rather than the process-global ones, so two engines can export to two collectors. endpoint (http://localhost:4317), exporter (otlp, console), metrics, traces, service_name (nl2sql)

opentelemetry-api, -sdk and -exporter-otlp move from the engine's dependencies to the otel extra. Only nl2sql/observers/otel.py imports them, and only when the observer is built. common/metrics.py is deleted: plan_cache.py and token_handler.py publish events instead of adding to counters.

Built: the observers (E2)

nl2sql/observers/ holds build_observers (__init__.py, with DEFAULT_OBSERVERS, log then audit), log.py (LogObserver, LogConfig), audit.py (AuditObserver, AuditConfig) and otel.py (OtelObserver, OtelConfig), declared in the nl2sql.observers entry point group. Runtime.components builds them after every other component (a problem is one more line of the one ConfigError, and a built observer is closed again), keeps them as Runtime.observers and subscribes them to Runtime.bus in config order; engine.close() closes them through the bus. The registry checks an observer's requires like an LLM provider's, so otel without the extra is a ConfigError ending in pip install "nl2sql-engine[otel]". What is audited is the catalog's: EventSpec.audit, and a new EventSpec.audit_only (a field name to the values written; hook.decision's is decision: deny, needs_approval, approved, error), applied by EventSpec.audited(data) and reported in EventInfo.audit_only. The observer reads the audited names from the catalog when it is built, so Wave C's datasource.saved, api_key.created, api_key.revoked and mcp.denied join the log with audit=True on their own entries. run.failed gained user_id and roles (two lines in RunScope.fail), so a failed run's line names its user too. The audit observer queues each line and writes on its own daemon thread, started by the first audited event, opening and closing the day file per batch. Its queue is bounded (MAX_QUEUE, 10,000): a line that does not fit is dropped, counted in dropped and warned about once. close writes what is queued, and what arrived while it closed; an atexit hook (through a weak reference, unregistered by close) does the same for a process that never closes its engine. RunScope.fail passes message through redact_keys (D15). engine.storage.purge() adds audit (day files older than max_age_days) when the engine runs an audit observer. otel records in memory on its own MeterProvider and TracerProvider (a BatchSpanProcessor, a PeriodicExportingMetricReader) and never sets the global ones, and close bounds the providers' flush at 5 seconds; nl2sql.token.usage lost its datasource_id attribute, which llm.call does not carry. TokenUsageCallback publishes llm.call per finished call through nl2sql.events.publish (with the client's nl2sql_agent metadata as agent), PlanCache.get publishes plan_cache.lookup, and Runtime.replace_llm publishes llm.changed on ctx.bus with the engine's tenant_id; common/metrics.py and common/event_logger.py are deleted, and opentelemetry is the otel extra (CI's unit and integration jobs install it). One test differs from the plan: test_building_an_engine_loads_no_opentelemetry cannot hold, because chromadb (a core dependency) installs the OpenTelemetry SDK and langsmith, under langchain, imports it whenever it is installed; test_building_an_engine_loads_no_otel_observer checks what the engine controls, beside the two AST tests on nl2sql/observers/otel.py. The page is Observers.

docs.title: The run collectors
docs.text:
Three things the engine already builds for every run become run-scoped bus subscribers attached by RunScope, not configurable observers, since the result depends on them:

Collector Fills Today Usage QueryResult.usage (tokens, calls, cost) and the budget TokenUsageCallback keeps its LangChain hooks (the only place usage is visible) and publishes llm.call (E2, which deletes the OpenTelemetry counter it fed); the roll-up reads the events (E3) Timings QueryResult.timings NodeTimingCallback, from node.finished Trace The trace document's new events list (every run event but answer.delta) TraceRecorder keeps the per-node records; the events are added beside them

docs.title: Logs with correlation (B14)
docs.text:
• RunScope sets the run's trace_id and tenant_id in the context variables TraceContextFilter reads; stream_query's thread already copies the caller's context, and so does every LangGraph worker.
  • configure_logging stays an entry point's call (nl2sql, nl2sql demo, nl2sql-api, nl2sql mcp), as the invariant on process globals says: logging handlers are global by nature. It installs the filter on its handler, as today. A library caller who configures logging their own way adds nl2sql.TraceContextFilter to their handler; the docs say so.
  • cli/common/engine.py stops switching to JSON logs when OpenTelemetry is configured; --log-format json (and NL2SQL_LOG_FORMAT) chooses it for any command. NL2SQL_LOG_FORMAT joins READS_THE_ENVIRONMENT.

Built: log correlation (E1)

run_query and stream_query's thread run inside scope.entered() as well as the graph's worker, so every log line written during a run, on the caller's thread or a LangGraph worker thread, carries its trace_id and tenant_id (test_every_log_line_in_a_run_has_its_trace_id, test_log_lines_on_worker_threads_have_the_trace_id). docs/observability/events.md shows a library caller adding TraceContextFilter.

docs.title: 5. Cost, the price table and per-question caps
The price table
docs.text:
evaluation/prices.py moves to nl2sql/llm/prices.py (D11). It keeps its shape: PRICES_CHECKED_ON, and per model input, cached_input, cache_write, output (USD per million tokens), verified and source.

# nl2sql/llm/prices.py
PRICES_CHECKED_ON = "2026-09-21"
PRICES: dict[str, ModelPrice] = {...}            # dated and sourced; updated by hand

def price_for(model: str, overrides: Mapping[str, Price]) -> ModelPrice | None:
    """The config's llm.prices row, else the table's, by exact name; None when neither has it."""
Rule Detail Overrides llm.prices (Phase 1's field) adds a model or replaces a row. A negotiated rate or a fine-tune goes there. Exact names No prefix matching (gpt-5.4 must not price gpt-5.4-mini). A call is priced by the model name the provider reported, then by the name configured, as token_handler._cost does today, so a dated variant the provider reports (gpt-5.4-2026-03-05) is priced by its configured name. Unknown model Cost None, for the call and for any total that includes it. Never zero. Facade engine.llm.prices() returns the effective table: checked_on, each row with its source (table or config), so a UI can show "prices as of 2026-09-21".

Evals keep tier 2's rule: a run with max_cost_usd refuses to start if a model it would call has no price.

docs.title: Per-question caps
docs.text:
# settings.yaml
pipeline:
  timeout_s: 60
  max_llm_calls: 60       # model calls per question, parse retries included; null: no cap
  max_cost_usd: 0.50      # dollars per question; null (the default): no cap
Rule Detail Defaults (D20) max_llm_calls: 60, max_cost_usd: null. 60 covers the largest legitimate run: resolver, decomposer, six sub-queries each with a planner call and three refiner and planner retries, the answer, and parse retries. Enforced before each call, through the token The budget is a run-scoped callback (nl2sql/limits.py, attached by RunScope). On on_chat_model_start it compares the usage collector's totals with the caps. When the next call would exceed the call cap, or the spent cost has reached the cost cap, it cancels the run's CancellationToken with a reason, RunStop(limit, value, spent), and then raises, as _StopWhenCancelled does. Raising alone is not enough: the nodes wrap their model calls in except Exception (the planner turns any failure into a retryable PLANNING_FAILURE, and the decomposer and answer synthesizer catch too), so the raise would be retried and end as a planner error. The cancelled token is what ends it: the SQL agent's routers check it before every retry and end the sub-query, and _StopWhenCancelled refuses every later step and call. CancellationToken.cancel(reason=None) gains the optional reason. Overshoot The call in flight finishes, so a run can overshoot the cost cap by the calls in flight: at most one per running sub-query. The docs say so. A cap needs prices With max_cost_usd set, every model the config names must have a price; otherwise NL2SQL(...) raises a ConfigError listing them, with the fix "add llm.prices.". Since a call falls back to its configured name, every call of such an engine is priced. How the run ends run_with_graph already maps a cancelled token to its cancelled outcome; a token cancelled with a RunStop reason maps instead to QueryResult.status = "stopped", QueryResult.stop = RunStop(limit, value, spent), an error RUN_LIMIT_REACHED (not retryable) whose message names the limit and the setting, and the answer "This question reached its limit of 60 model calls (settings.pipeline.max_llm_calls)." run.limit_reached is published, and the audit observer records it. test_cap_hit_inside_the_planner_ends_stopped_not_planning_failure holds it. Evals An eval run's own max_cost_usd is across the run, as tier 2's is; the per-question caps apply inside it too.

Built: the price table, cost and caps (E3)

nl2sql/llm/prices.py holds PRICES_CHECKED_ON, PRICES (the five rows moved unchanged), ModelPrice (a NamedTuple: input, cached_input, cache_write, output, verified, source; a config row has source="config" and may leave the two cache rates None), price_for(model, overrides) (the llm.prices row, else the table's, by exact name), call_cost(price, *, input_tokens, output_tokens, cached_input_tokens=None, cache_write_input_tokens=None, cache_write_multiplier=1.0) (None when the input or output count is unknown; a cache count not reported is not split out of input; a config row's missing cache_write is input times the wire's multiplier, so Anthropic's 1.25x from #193 holds) and effective_prices(overrides). evaluation/prices.py is deleted with no alias; evaluation/run.py's check_prices(configs, prices=None) and question_cost(usage, cfg, prices=None) take llm.prices as overrides (run_evals passes the engine's), and the UnknownPriceError fix names llm.prices. TokenUsageCallback(prices=llm.prices) prices every call with price_for by the served name, then the configured one, and gained spent() (the dollars of the calls with a known cost). Unknown counts are None, never 0 (an owner requirement after the design): the wires' usage() takes Optional counts (opt_int, sum_known in wires/base.py; as_int is gone), so an unreported cache read, cache write (OpenAI reports none) or reasoning count is None, and a call with no usage (a failed call) has every count None and a null cost. LLMCallUsage, UsageTotals and the catalog's LLMCall and UsageTotalsData have Optional[int] token fields; a total is the sum of what was reported, None when nothing was; the otel observer skips a None count. engine.llm.prices() returns {"checked_on", "models": {name: {input, cached_input, cache_write, output, verified, source, citation}}} (source is table or config; citation the table row's source). nl2sql/limits.py holds Budget, LimitReached, describe and stop_answer beside RunStop. Budget(max_llm_calls=None, max_cost_usd=None, usage=None, token=None, setting="settings.pipeline") is a LangChain callback (raise_error = True): on on_chat_model_start and on_llm_start it refuses the call when the calls it let start have reached max_llm_calls or usage.spent() has reached max_cost_usd; on the first refusal it sets budget.stop, cancels every bound token with the RunStop (CancellationToken.cancel(reason=None) keeps the first reason in token.reason), publishes run.limit_reached through the module publish (nothing outside a run), and raises LimitReached(stop, setting) (not a ValueError, so the parse-retry loop never swallows it); every later call is refused with the same stop. Work that is not a question (Wave B's profiler, V3's seeding) opens its own Budget(..., setting="evals"), makes its calls with budget.callbacks() (the budget, then its usage collector), and reads budget.stop or catches LimitReached. Budget.for_question(pipeline, usage) is None when both caps are off. The budget reads the usage collector directly, not the llm.call events, because a budget outside a question has no scope to read events from (a difference from the file list's "usage collector on llm.call"). QueryAPI.open_scope attaches the question's budget after the RunEvents, so scope.callbacks() is the usage collector, the RunEvents, the budget, then anything attached later; run_with_graph binds every attached Budget to the run's token (budget.bind(token)), and a token cancelled with a RunStop maps to _stopped: stop, the one error RUN_LIMIT_REACHED ("The question reached its limit of 60 model calls (settings.pipeline.max_llm_calls)."), the answer "This question reached its limit of 60 model calls (settings.pipeline.max_llm_calls)." (or "its cost limit of $0.50 (settings.pipeline.max_cost_usd)"), and the trace outcome stopped. Runtime.components and Runtime.replace_llm raise a ConfigError per unpriced model (llm.model, llm.agents.<agent>.model; a model object by its model_name) when max_cost_usd is set, with the fix add llm.prices.<model> .... Tests: tests/unit/test_cost_and_caps.py. After review (PR #326): a call is priced by price_for_call(served, configured, overrides), every llm.prices override (served name, then configured name) before the table for either name; Price's four rates are NonNegativeFloat; a timeout that fires while a budget stop unwinds reports stopped; mode full counts a call with no token counts in EvalReport.unknown_cost_calls (new unknown_cost_calls(usage), one warning per run) instead of adding 0; the OpenAI rows are marked for the owner to re-verify.

docs.title: 6. Hooks
docs.text: A hook is code the operator registers that sees a run at fixed points and may let it continue, change what it carries, stop it, or ask for approval. No hook ships built in (D22).

docs.title: The six points
docs.text:
flowchart TD
  Q["question"] --> P1(["run.before"])
  P1 --> CM["curated matcher"]
  CM -->|"no match"| RES["datasource resolver"]
  RES --> P2(["datasources.after"])
  P2 --> DEC["decomposer"]
  DEC --> PL["planner, or the plan cache"]
  PL --> P3(["plan.after"])
  P3 --> VAL["logical validator"]
  VAL --> GEN["generator"]
  GEN --> P4(["execute.before"])
  CM -->|"verified query"| P4
  P4 --> EX["executor"]
  EX --> P5(["execute.after"])
  P5 --> AGG["aggregator"]
  AGG --> ANS["answer synthesizer"]
  ANS --> P6(["answer.after"])
  P6 --> R["QueryResult"]
Point When The hook sees It may answer Called from run.before Once, before the first step question, user, datasource_id, execute allow, modify (question), deny run_with_graph's _invoke in pipeline/runtime.py, before graph.invoke (the events package never depends on hooks) datasources.after The resolver chose its datasources, before the decomposer + datasource_ids allow, modify (datasource_ids: a subset only), deny DatasourceResolverNode plan.after Per sub-query and attempt: a plan from the planner or the plan cache, before the validator + sub_query, plan allow, modify (plan), deny ASTPlannerNode, on both paths execute.before Per sub-query: validated, generated SQL, or a verified query's SQL with its bound values, before the adapter runs it + datasource_id, sql, params, tables allow, deny, needs_approval ExecutorNode and CuratedMatcherNode execute.after Per sub-query, after it ran + result: the ResultSummary (columns, row count, truncated); never rows allow, deny ExecutorNode and CuratedMatcherNode answer.after The answer is written, before it is returned + final_answer, the sub-query summaries allow, deny AnswerSynthesizerNode
  • Modify before the validator, deny only after (D21, D13). A plan a hook changed at plan.after is validated like any other, so a hook can never smuggle in what the validator forbids, including a table the role may not read. After the validator nothing may change the SQL, the plan or the result; a hook may only stop it. datasources.after may only remove datasources: the resolver re-applies the scope check to what the hook returns, and an added id is a hook error.
  • The verified path has no routing and no plan, so only run.before, execute.before, execute.after and answer.after apply. A deny there ends the run; it does not fall back to the generated path, because a deny means no.
  • A plan-only run (execute=False) never reaches the execute.* points.
  • Deny scope. A deny at a per-sub-query point (plan.after, execute.before, execute.after) may name scope="sub_query", which drops that sub-query (the answer says so) and lets the others continue; the default is scope="run". This is the only narrowing after the validator. A sub-query that feeds a join or compare combine group cannot be dropped alone, since the group would have one side: the whole group is dropped, with its post-combine operations, and the answer says which part of the question went unanswered and why.
  • The plan cache keeps the planner's plan. graph_utils caches the planner's response after a clean execution. It stores the plan the planner (or the cache) produced, before any plan.after hook changed it, and plan.after runs on every cache hit. So a hook's change is never cached, is applied fresh on each run, and stops applying the moment the hook config changes. test_cached_plan_is_the_planners_not_the_hooks holds it.

docs.title: The interface
docs.text:
# nl2sql/hooks/__init__.py (engine: the context holds engine types, D14)
HookPoint = Literal["run.before", "datasources.after", "plan.after",
                    "execute.before", "execute.after", "answer.after"]

class HookContext(BaseModel):          # frozen; fields beyond the point's are None
    point: HookPoint
    trace_id: str
    question: str
    user: UserContext
    datasource_id: str | None
    datasource_ids: list[str] | None
    sub_query: SubQuery | None
    plan: PlanModel | None
    sql: str | None
    params: dict[str, Any] | None
    tables: list[str] | None           # datasource.schema.table, read by the SQL
    result: ResultSummary | None
    final_answer: dict | None
    approvals: list[Approval]          # what the run was re-run with (section 7)

class Allow(BaseModel): ...
class Modify(BaseModel):  question: str | None = None; datasource_ids: list[str] | None = None; plan: PlanModel | None = None
class Deny(BaseModel):    reason: str; scope: Literal["run", "sub_query"] = "run"
class NeedsApproval(BaseModel): reason: str
Decision = Allow | Modify | Deny | NeedsApproval

class Hook(Protocol):
    interface_version: ClassVar[int]           # 1
    config_model: ClassVar[type[BaseModel]]
    points: ClassVar[frozenset[HookPoint]]     # where it may be attached
    @classmethod
    def from_config(cls, cfg: BaseModel) -> "Hook": ...
    def __call__(self, ctx: HookContext) -> Decision: ...

docs.title: Decisions and the runner
docs.text:
nl2sql/hooks/runner.py holds HookRunner.call(point, ctx) -> Decision, built once per engine from the config, and the table of points (HOOK_POINTS: each point's allowed decisions and the fields Modify may set there).

Rule Detail Order (D23) Hooks run in config order. A Modify replaces the fields it sets, and the next hook sees the result. The first Deny, or NeedsApproval without a matching approval, ends the point; later hooks are not asked. A NeedsApproval the run's approvals cover counts as Allow, and the next hook still runs (D24). Fails closed (D9) An exception, a return value that is not a Decision, or a decision the point does not allow (a Modify at execute.before, a NeedsApproval at plan.after) is a hook error, which denies with HOOK_FAILED and the hook's name. With on_error: open on that hook, an exception is logged and treated as Allow; a disallowed decision still denies, because it is a bug in the hook, not an outage. Timeouts The hook owns them, as a PolicyCheck does; the pipeline's timeout_s bounds the run anyway. Events Every call publishes hook.decision; the audit observer keeps the denials, approvals and errors. Errors Deny becomes a PipelineError HOOK_DENIED (CRITICAL, not retryable) whose message is the hook's reason, and whose details name the hook and the point. A run-scoped deny ends the run with status: "error".

docs.title: The config
docs.text:
# nl2sql.yaml
hooks: hooks.yaml

# hooks.yaml (a list; order matters)
- type: corp_sql_review           # a registered hook
  points: [execute.before]        # a subset of the hook's own points; all of them by default
  on_error: closed                # closed (the default) | open
  approver_roles: [dba]           # who may approve its needs_approval; default policies.admin_roles
  url: "${env:REVIEW_URL}"        # the hook's own keys, checked by its config_model
- type: question_rewriter
  points: [run.before]

from nl2sql import Config, HookConfig
Config(..., hooks=[HookConfig(type="corp_sql_review", points=["execute.before"]), MyHook()])
Kind Entry point group Interface Version Built-ins hook nl2sql.hooks nl2sql.hooks.Hook 1 none

registry.add_hook(name, cls), @registry.hook(name). A point the hook does not declare is a ConfigError at build.

Built: the hook kind and the section (A0)

The hook registry kind and the hooks section are accepted and validated: HookConfig (points, on_error, approver_roles, and the hook's own keys) or an object with __call__. HookPoint, the six point names, is defined in nl2sql/config/models.py, where the config and the hook.decision event both read it, and re-exported from nl2sql.hooks, where H1 imports it.

docs.title: The architecture test
docs.text:
test_hooks_modify_only_before_the_validator holds the boundary three ways:

  1. HOOK_POINTS allows Modify at run.before, datasources.after and plan.after only.
  2. An AST scan finds every hooks.call("<point>", ...) call site: a point that allows Modify may be called only from pipeline/runtime.py, datasource_resolver/node.py and ast_planner/node.py, and the generator, executor, curated matcher, aggregator and answer synthesizer may call only points that do not.
  3. The SQL agent graph, built with fakes, has exactly one path from ast_planner to generator, and it passes logical_validator.

Built: the runner, the six points and the boundary test (H1)

nl2sql/hooks/: the interface in __init__.py (HookContext, Allow, Modify, Deny, NeedsApproval, Decision, Hook; HookPoint is re-exported from nl2sql.config.models), points.py (HOOK_POINTS, a PointRule per point: decisions, modifies, per_sub_query) and runner.py. The shapes differ from the sketch above in four places:

  • HookRunner(bindings) takes a list of HookBinding(name, hook, points, on_error, approver_roles) from the runtime (Runtime._build_hooks, build_hook per entry, in config order) and reads no config, so a built-in hook (Wave B's policy.cost) goes first with its own approver_roles. ctx.hooks is the engine's runner; hooks_of(ctx) gives NO_HOOKS for a stand-in runtime.
  • HookRunner.call(point, **fields) builds the context from deep copies of fields (a hook changing the plan or the caller in place changes nothing) and returns a HookVerdict: ctx after every Modify, modified, and the decision and hook that stopped the point (allowed, scope, error(node), the PipelineError; a hook error's message names only the hook and the point). With no hook at a point, nothing is validated. HookRunner.attached(point) says whether any hook runs there: while one runs at answer.after the answer is not streamed (no answer.delta), RunEvents(..., hold_manifest=True) holds result.manifest until the answer is allowed (dropped on a deny), and result_from_state drops the rows, artifact_refs and result_manifest of a run a hook ended.
  • HookContext adds conversation_id: str | None (Wave C's A3), execute (run.before) and results (the run's ResultSummarys at answer.after, the "sub-query summaries" of the table).
  • NeedsApproval at execute.before stops the SQL with NEEDS_APPROVAL (status error) until H2 adds the request and the re-run; so NEEDS_APPROVAL left DECLARED_AHEAD here with HOOK_DENIED and HOOK_FAILED.

The call sites: run.before in run_with_graph's worker; datasources.after in DatasourceResolverNode._after_hooks (the one addition to the resolver; R1 rebases on it); plan.after in ASTPlannerNode.after_plan(state, plan, plan_source), which the planner's and the cache's plan go through and which a supplied plan (H2's approved, Wave B's chosen, Wave C's supplied) calls the same way; ASTPlannerNode.check_plan(state, plan) is one plan's verdict, for Wave B's alternatives. ASTPlannerResponse.planner_plan is the plan before the hooks, and wrap_subgraph caches it. execute.before and execute.after in ExecutorNode and CuratedMatcherNode (each a self.hooks.call("<point>", **self._hook_fields(...)); a deny on the verified path ends the run, as _ended, never a fallback); answer.after in AnswerSynthesizerNode. A sub-query a hook dropped has SubgraphOutput.status == "dropped" and a HOOK_DENIED warning; build_scan_layer_router (in pipeline/routes.py, a small addition the file list missed) ends the run on a hook's error and still aggregates when a sub-query was dropped; AggregationService.execute(..., dropped=) drops a join or compare group whole; the answer's warnings name what was dropped. SubgraphExecutionState.user_query (in pipeline/state.py, also not in the file list) carries the question to the sub-query's hooks. The architecture test is tests/architecture/test_hooks_boundary.py: every runner call names its point as a literal; its graph check asks that every path from ast_planner to generator pass logical_validator, so Wave B's clarifier may sit between the validator and the generator.

docs.title: 7. Approval
docs.text:
A hook at execute.before answers NeedsApproval("Reads payroll.salaries"). The minimal shape (D10, D24):

class ApprovalRequest(BaseModel):          # on QueryResult.approvals_needed
    id: str                                # sha256 over every field below except reason and approver_roles, hex
    question: str
    asker_user_id: str | None              # the run's UserContext
    asker_tenant_id: str | None
    hook: str
    point: Literal["execute.before"]
    datasource_id: str
    decomposition: DecomposerResponse | None   # generated path: the run's decomposition
    sub_query: SubQuery | None                 # generated path: the sub-query the SQL answers
    plan: PlanModel | None                     # generated path: its validated plan
    verified: VerifiedRef | None               # verified path: the query id and its bound params
    sql: str
    sql_sha256: str
    reason: str
    approver_roles: list[str]              # for display; the engine checks the hook's configured roles

class Approval(BaseModel):                 # passed back on the re-run
    request: ApprovalRequest
    by: UserContext                        # the approver
  1. The run ends. The sub-query does not run, the others finish the step they are on, nothing is aggregated or synthesized, and the result has status: "needs_approval", approvals_needed (one ApprovalRequest per pending sub-query), an error NEEDS_APPROVAL and the answer "This question needs approval before it runs: Reads payroll.salaries." hook.decision is published and audited.
  2. The approver re-runs it. An app shows the request to someone with an approver role, who calls engine.run_query(question, user_context=<the asker>, approvals=[Approval(request=..., by=<the approver>)]). run_query and stream_query gain the approvals argument.
  3. The re-run pins what was approved. The plan cache cannot do it: it holds only plans that executed cleanly (pipeline/graph_utils.py), which a sub-query stopped at execute.before never did, and its key is the decomposer's intent text, which is model output and can change. So:
  4. Generated path. The run takes the request's decomposition instead of calling the resolver and decomposer. Each datasource in it is checked with scope.reaches_datasource() as the resolver would, and datasources.after is not called (there is no routing, as on the verified path). The approved sub-query's planner step returns the pinned plan with plan_source="approved", as a cache hit returns a cached one; other sub-queries plan as usual. The pinned plan still goes through plan.after, the validator and the generator, so a plan the policies or the code no longer accept is refused like any other. An approved plan is never written to the plan cache.
  5. Verified path. The curated matcher runs the request's verified query with its bound params, with no matching call.
  6. The approval is checked by the engine, not the hook. When a hook answers NeedsApproval at execute.before, the runner looks for an Approval whose request has the same hook and datasource and whose sql_sha256 equals the hash of the SQL just generated, and accepts it only if: the engine's recomputation of the request's id matches (the request was not edited); the request's question, asker_user_id and asker_tenant_id are this run's; and by holds one of the roles the hook is configured with (approver_roles, by default policies.admin_roles), not the roles the request lists. An accepted approval counts as Allow: hook.decision is published with decision: "approved" and the approver, and the next hook at the point still runs. The hook also sees ctx.approvals, so a hook that wants a stricter rule can apply it.
  7. Different SQL asks again. If the regenerated SQL's hash differs (the generator changed, or a plan.after hook changed the plan), the run ends needs_approval again with the new SQL: an approval never covers SQL nobody saw.

Built: the shapes on the result (A0)

ApprovalRequest, Approval and VerifiedRef (id, params) are in nl2sql/hooks/approval.py, and RunStop in nl2sql/limits.py; all are exported from nl2sql. QueryResult.status is a RunStatus (success, plan_only, error, needs_approval, stopped, and needs_clarification, reserved for Wave B), or None when nothing ran and nothing failed (0.6's ""). result_from_state reads the state's approvals_needed and stop, and sets the status from them before looking at errors, so H2 and E3 put those keys in the state and touch no result code. The error codes HOOK_DENIED, HOOK_FAILED, NEEDS_APPROVAL, RUN_LIMIT_REACHED and QUESTION_TOO_BROAD (never retried), JOIN_KEY_TYPE_MISMATCH and JOIN_FAN_OUT (retried) and JOIN_KEY_UNCONVERTED and ALL_NULL_COLUMN (warnings) are in ErrorCode; DECLARED_AHEAD in test_boundary_tidy_ups.py lists each with the PR that raises it, which takes it off the list.

Nothing is stored: no queue, no expiry, no table. The asking app holds the request until someone acts on it. An Approval is not signed and does not expire (D24): it is trusted as far as the user_context a caller passes is trusted today, which is the application's responsibility (nl2sql-api resolves both from its auth). The REST shape is Wave D.
