docs.title: Addendum: the pinned-plan entry is public
docs.text:
Decided after this design merged, with the Wave B to D reviews: the entry the approved re-run uses is built once and is public. run_query(question, plan=SuppliedPlan(datasource_id, sub_query, plan)) (and stream_query) runs a plan the caller holds. It skips the curated matcher, the resolver, the decomposer and the planner's model call; checks the datasource against the caller's scope; sets plan_source="supplied"; runs plan.after, the validator, the generator and the executor; is never cached; and never asks the refiner on a validator failure (the sub-query fails with the validator's error). The run's state carries the pin as a PinnedRun whose source is a PinnedSource: supplied, approved (this section's re-run) or chosen (Wave B's clarification re-ask, which may not be combined with approvals). SuppliedPlan is exported from nl2sql.

Changed in Wave C (C0b)

SuppliedPlan is no longer (datasource_id, sub_query, plan). It is a whole run, shaped on PinnedRun: a decomposition with the plans of every sub-query, or a verified query with its verified_datasource_id; exactly one. SuppliedPlan.for_sub_query(sub_query, plan) builds the old one-sub-query case. run_query and stream_query also take answer=False, which skips the answer synthesizer. See Query API and Wave C.

Built: approval and the pinned-plan entry (H2)

  • The entry. nl2sql/pipeline/pinned.py: PinnedSource, SuppliedPlan, PinnedRun (source, decomposition, plans keyed by sub-query id, or verified with verified_datasource_id), PinnedRun.supplied(plan), pinned_from_approvals(approvals, question=, user=) and PinnedEntryNode. build_graph(ctx, execute, pinned=True) builds a pinned run's graph, whose entry is pinned_entry (with no curated matcher); every other run's graph is unchanged and has no such node. run_with_graph builds the pinned graph for a supplied pin, or, for an approval's pin (known only after run.before), inside the worker. The pinned_entry node scope-checks every datasource of the decomposition (SECURITY_VIOLATION otherwise, routes.pinned_route ends the run) and goes to the layer router. build_scan_payload hands each sub-query its pinned_plan and pinned_source; the planner returns it through after_plan(state, plan, source). The SQL agent reads a pinned sub-query's retries as spent, so neither a validator nor a database error is retried, and the executor's value check never asks for a retry on it. The schema retriever gives a pinned plan every table the caller may read, with no search, for the validator. check_pinned(pinned, approvals, datasource_id) refuses, with a ValueError at the call (QueryAPI.run_query and stream_query, before the run's scope opens), a chosen pin with approvals and a datasource_id that is not the pinned plan's datasource. QueryAPI.run_query(..., pinned=) (internal) takes a pin of another source; Wave B passes its chosen plan there.
  • The request. ApprovalRequest.build(...) computes sql_sha256 and id; expected_id() recomputes it: SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of the fields in REQUEST_ID_FIELDS only, each dumped without the values it holds at their defaults. The rule for Wave D's store: a field added later, to the request or with a default to a nested model, keeps the ids of stored requests; changing a default or the meaning of a listed field changes them, and a test pins one id (GOLDEN_ID) so that never happens by accident. wrap_subgraph builds the request for a sub-query that ended NEEDS_APPROVAL (the error's details now carry the reason) into GraphState.approvals_needed; the curated matcher does the same with a VerifiedRef. One difference from the sketch above: the request pins the plan as plan.after received it (planner_plan), not the plan the hooks let through, because the re-run passes it through plan.after again; pinning the hooked plan would apply a hook's Modify twice and the SQL would never match the hash. What the approver approves is the SQL, and it is the same.
  • The check. HookRunner(bindings, admin_roles=) (the runtime passes policies.admin_roles), HookRunner.approver_roles(hook). On a NeedsApproval the runner looks for an approval in ctx.approvals with no approval_problem(...): unedited, this run's question (after run.before) and asker, this hook and datasource, the hash of the SQL just generated, the same verified values, and an approver holding one of the hook's configured roles. A match publishes hook.decision with decision: "approved" and the approver, and the next hook runs. request_problem refuses an edited request, a request whose sql is not the SQL of its sql_sha256 (so the SQL an approver reads is the SQL whose hash is checked), and another question or asker. pinned_from_approvals(approvals, question=, user=, hooks=) pins only an approval with no request_problem, for a configured hook, whose by holds one of that hook's approver roles; so a forged approval, an approver without the role, or a request the asker built with no approval hook configured, pins nothing and covers nothing: the run plans as usual and asks again, and plan_source is never "approved" for it.
  • The verified path. A pinned verified request takes the default entry; the curated matcher runs that query with its values (_run_pinned), with no search and no model call, through the same access checks and hooks. If it is no longer available, the matcher falls back as usual.
  • Not done: the result's final_answer stays None on a needs_approval run (the error's message is the answer text), as on every run a hook ended; nothing is stored (Wave D).

docs.title: 8. Evals as a product
docs.text: engine.benchmark becomes engine.evals (D25). What 0.6 calls tier 1, tier 2 and retrieval recall become three modes of one run over one case format, scored by registered scorers.

docs.title: The files
docs.text:
# nl2sql.yaml
evals: evals.yaml

# evals.yaml: the section
suites: [evals/chinook.yaml, evals/routing.yaml]
scorers: [result_match, outcome, faithfulness, retrieval_recall, routing]   # the default: all five
curated: true                       # D12
max_cost_usd: 5.00                  # across a run in mode full; required for it
gate:
  max_regressions: 2
  alpha: 0.05
  max_cost_increase: 0.20

# evals/chinook.yaml: a suite
version: 1
cases:
- id: chinook_001
  question: How many customers do we have, by country?
  datasources: [chinook]
  status: approved                  # draft | approved | retired; only approved cases run
  origin: hand                      # hand | seeded
  difficulty: easy
  tags: [aggregation, rbac-denial]
  paraphrase_group: null
  outcome: {admin: allowed, analyst: allowed, viewer: refused}
  tables: [Customer]
  columns: [Customer.Country, Customer.CustomerId]
  order_matters: false
  sql: |
    SELECT Country, COUNT(CustomerId) AS customer_count
    FROM Customer GROUP BY Country ORDER BY customer_count DESC, Country
  rows: [...]                       # written by regenerate, never by hand
  alt_sql: []                       # reviewed alternatives
  alt_rows: []                      # written by regenerate
  plan: {...}                       # optional: the hand-written gold plan, for mode plans
Field Was (chinook_gold.yaml) Notes datasources datasource (one) A list, so a cross-database case can say where it should go. The routing scorer reads it. status, origin none New. Every moved Chinook case is approved, hand. origin is hand, seeded or feedback. outcome expected The same map of role to allowed, refused or unanswerable tables, columns needed_tables, needed_columns sql, rows, alt_sql, alt_rows gold_sql, gold_result, alt_gold_sql, alt_gold_result Same values plan chinook_gold_plans.yaml, by id Folded into the case

Built: the section and the settings (A0)

EvalsConfig (with EvalGate) is Config.evals, from evals.yaml; suites are paths relative to nl2sql.yaml, resolved by V1. The settings the other tracks read are in place with their defaults: settings.pipeline.max_llm_calls, max_cost_usd and sanity_checks, settings.routing, and settings.retrieval.table_k, planning_k and decomposer_tables; eval_seeder is in AgentName.

evals.yaml is a config section file like the others: strict keys, loaded with the config. A suite file is data: it is read when a run asks for it, not when the engine starts, so a thousand cases cost an engine start nothing. The suites the package ships (Chinook, routing) live in nl2sql/evaluation/suites/; nl2sql init --demo copies them next to the demo's nl2sql.yaml.

The Chinook gold set moves unchanged. The PR that moves it computes a SHA-256 over every case's question, SQL, alternatives, rows, outcomes and needed tables and columns, read from chinook_gold.yaml and chinook_gold_plans.yaml with the old loader, and pins it in test_chinook_suite_holds_the_gold_data_unchanged, which computes the same digest from the new suite. Then the old files are deleted. No question, SQL or row changes; only the keys around them do. docs/testing/evaluation-dataset.md and the rule in CLAUDE.md move to the new names (alt_sql).

Feedback drafts move to the case format too. engine.feedback.export writes rated runs as gold drafts today, through GoldQuestion and the gold file's dumper (feedback/drafts.py, api/feedback_api.py). They become cases with status: draft and origin: feedback, so a person reviews them the same way as seeded ones.

docs.title: The facade
docs.text:
Method What it does engine.evals.load(path=None) -> list[EvalSuite] The suites named in evals.yaml, or one file engine.evals.run(suites=None, *, mode="full", llm=None, cases=None, roles=None, scorers=None, curated=None, passes=1, max_cost_usd=None, on_case=None) -> EvalReport Runs every approved case, once per role in its outcome map, passes times. cases narrows by id or tag. llm is None (the engine's own llm section), one LLM, or a mapping of names to LLMs, which tier 2 compares today: each config runs on its own derived runtime over the same cases, and the report compares them. None arguments take evals.yaml's values. engine.evals.gate(report, baseline) -> GateResult The regression gate below engine.evals.regenerate(path) -> RegenerateReport Runs each case's sql and alt_sql through its datasource's adapter and writes rows and alt_rows engine.evals.seed(datasource_id, *, count=20, out, user_context, max_cost_usd=None) -> SeedReport Draft cases from a datasource's schema, as the caller sees it engine.evals.scorers() -> list[str] The registered scorer names Mode What runs Model calls Was full The whole pipeline, on the configured LLM yes; needs max_cost_usd tier 2 plans Each case's gold plan through the validator, generator and executor, with the gold-plan fake LLM none tier 1 retrieval Datasource routing and schema retrieval only none (the local or configured embedder) retrieval recall

full runs on a derived runtime (ctx.derive, as tier 2 does), so the engine serving traffic is untouched, and that runtime has the plan cache off, as tier 2's does, so a second pass asks the planner again rather than measuring the cache. Modes plans and retrieval run with curated answers off, whatever curated says: the curated matcher makes a model call the gold-plan fake cannot answer, and a verified hit would skip the gold plan or the retrieval being measured. The named LLM configs in evaluation/presets/ stay, and nl2sql eval run --llm takes a preset name or a file holding an llm section. Each case runs under its own RunScope. Every finished case publishes eval.case; the end publishes eval.finished.

Curated answers (D12). curated: true is the default in mode full. Each case result records its source (verified or generated). A case a verified query answered is run a second time with curated answers off, and that result is scored as its generated answer. The report carries accuracy (what users see), accuracy_generated (every case on the generated path: the model's own skill, comparable across configs) and both split by source. Only the curated hits pay the second run.

docs.title: Scorers
docs.text:
# nl2sql/evaluation/scorers/__init__.py (engine: it sees QueryResult, D14)
class Score(BaseModel):
    value: float | None        # 0..1; None when the scorer does not apply to this case
    passed: bool | None
    detail: dict[str, Any] = {}

class CaseRun(BaseModel):      # what a scorer is given
    case: EvalCase
    role: str
    result: QueryResult        # with the run's trace when one was kept
    rows: list[list[Any]]      # the first terminal result, read from the results store

class Scorer(Protocol):
    interface_version: ClassVar[int]     # 1
    config_model: ClassVar[type[BaseModel]]
    modes: ClassVar[frozenset[str]]      # the modes it can score
    @classmethod
    def from_config(cls, cfg: BaseModel) -> "Scorer": ...
    def score(self, run: CaseRun) -> Score: ...
Scorer Pass means Modes From result_match The rows match rows or any alt_rows (order when order_matters, the numeric tolerance and the period rules of today's ModelEvaluator) full, plans evaluation/evaluator.py outcome The role's outcome is the case's: allowed ran and answered, refused ended SECURITY_VIOLATION, unanswerable ended QUESTION_NOT_ANSWERABLE full, plans the same retrieval_recall Value: the share of tables and columns the schema retriever picked; passes at 1.0 full, retrieval evaluation/retrieval_recall.py faithfulness Every number the answer states is in the result or its count full evaluation/faithfulness.py routing The datasources the run used are exactly datasources; in retrieval mode, all of them are among the fused top max_datasources full, retrieval new (Phase R) Kind Entry point group Interface Version Built-ins scorer nl2sql.scorers nl2sql.evaluation.scorers.Scorer 1 the five above

A case passes when every scorer that applies to it passes. A scorer that raises scores the case as an error (passed: None, the message in detail) and the run continues; the report counts errors apart from fails.

docs.title: Regenerating expected rows
docs.text:
regenerate replaces python -m nl2sql.evaluation.gold (D27). For each approved case it asks the case's datasource adapter, through the engine's DatasourceRegistry, to run sql and every alt_sql (read-only, with the datasource's limits), and writes the rows back into the suite in the order the SQL returns them, keeping the file's formatting rules from gold.py's dumper. A case whose SQL fails is reported and left unchanged. evaluation/gold.py stops importing sqlite3, and its entry in STATE_LIBRARY_EXCEPTIONS is removed: the Chinook gold rows now come from the same adapter questions run on. Gold data is never edited by hand: a new accepted answer is a reviewed alt_sql, then regenerate.

Built: evals core (V1)

nl2sql/evaluation/ is reorganised as the section says:

  • The case format. suite.py holds EvalCase, EvalSuite, load_suite, select_cases and write_suite. outcome also takes clarify, which runs only with engine.evals.run(clarify=True); Wave B's clarification produces it.
  • The Chinook suite moved. suites/chinook.yaml holds the gold data unchanged, pinned by test_chinook_suite_holds_the_gold_data_unchanged. Rows stay {column: value} maps, as the old file wrote them.
  • The run and the report. run.py (run_evals) runs the three modes. report.py holds EvalReport and the boards, from tier 2's scoreboard.
  • The scorers. scorers/ holds Score, CaseRun, Scorer and the five built-ins, declared as nl2sql.scorers entry points.
  • Rows through the adapter. regenerate.py returns a RegenerateReport.
  • The gold-plan fake. gold_llm.py answers from one table, RESPONSES, keyed by structured-output schema name. Wave B's PlannerAnswer is one more entry there.
  • The gate's statistics. gate.py holds tier 2's question_flips, mcnemar_exact, compare_with_baseline and check_baseline, unchanged except that the deprecated max_accuracy_drop is gone. V2 builds engine.evals.gate on them.

engine.evals has load, run, regenerate and scorers. run takes clarify: bool = False. With curated on in mode full, a curated hit's record carries generated, and each board carries accuracy.generated. CaseRun also carries mode, columns, retrieval (what the retriever sent) and routed (mode retrieval's ranking). In mode full, retrieval is read from the run's schema retriever node.

Deleted: engine.benchmark, BenchmarkAPI, BenchmarkConfig, benchmark_runner.py, tier1.py, tier2.py, types.py, gold.py, retrieval_recall.py (now scorers/retrieval_recall.py, with sent, routed and retrieval_settings), datasets/ and nl2sql benchmark. records.py keeps its page texts, which still name nl2sql benchmark, so the committed pages stay byte-identical until V2 rewires publishing.

After review:

  • Each board also reports accuracy.execution. It counts only result_match and outcome, the 0.6 tier 2 measure, so the published series stays comparable.
  • Mode retrieval cases open a run scope too.
  • regenerate refuses a packaged suite unless allow_packaged=True.
  • feedback export refuses a configured suite and any file holding approved cases.

docs.title: The regression gate
docs.text:
nl2sql/evaluation/gate.py takes tier 2's gate as it is (compare_with_baseline, check_baseline): at most max_regressions cases that passed in the baseline and fail now, a one-sided test at alpha on the accuracy difference, and at most max_cost_increase more cost per case. It compares accuracy_generated and, separately, accuracy, and only compares reports of the same suite digest and mode (a changed suite is a series break, as records.py already reports). GateResult(ok, regressions, series_break).

Where Gate CI, every pull request mode: plans on Chinook (today's tier 1 test) and mode: retrieval on Chinook and routing, against benchmarks/ baselines. Free. Before a release, by the owner mode: full with a key, against the last published record. Asked for explicitly: it spends the owner's key.

Built: the gate (V2)

engine.evals.gate(report, baseline) -> GateResult(ok, regressions, series_break, compared), with evals.yaml's gate settings, built on V1's statistics in nl2sql/evaluation/gate.py (gate, load_baseline). Where the code differs from the section above, after the owner's decision of 2026-10-15:

  • It reads execution accuracy, not overall. A case passes the gate on result_match and outcome only (nl2sql.evaluation.report.execution_passed), the measure 0.6's tier 2 published, so a faithfulness miss is never a regression and a 0.7 run compares with the 0.6 history. "Both accuracies" are that measure as users see it and on the generated path (each case's generated run), the second only when the run had curated answers on. Mode retrieval has no execution and is read by status.
  • A baseline is a report, a record or a benchmarks/ folder (the newest record of the run's mode, database and config). A record 0.6 wrote has no scores; its status was execution accuracy and is read so.
  • A series break is not ok. The gate uses the history's own rule, records.series_key (mode, suite digest, schema fingerprint and, in mode full, roles and curated answers), plus the roles each run actually ran. A series break compares nothing for that config, and nl2sql eval run exits 2 after printing the other configs' regressions.
  • The allowance is per mode. max_regressions and McNemar (two-sided, counted only when more cases were lost than gained) apply to mode full. Modes plans and retrieval run no model and allow no flip.
  • A missing or unreadable baseline exits 2 with a one-line error.
  • Routing has no suite yet (Phase R adds it), so CI gates mode retrieval on Chinook only. R3 added it: see the routing gate.

docs.title: The CLI
docs.text:
Command Calls nl2sql eval run [--suite PATH] [--mode full\|plans\|retrieval] [--llm NAME=PRESET_OR_FILE ...] [--cases ID/TAG ...] [--max-cost USD] [--baseline FILE] [--out FILE] engine.evals.run, then gate with --baseline; exit 1 on a regression, 3 when stopped at the cost cap nl2sql eval regenerate PATH engine.evals.regenerate nl2sql eval seed --datasource ID [--count N] [--role R] [--max-cost USD] --out PATH engine.evals.seed, as the caller --role names nl2sql eval publish Writes the report as a record under benchmarks/ and refreshes the README block (today's benchmark publish)

nl2sql benchmark and all its subcommands are deleted.

Built: the CLI and the records (V2)

nl2sql eval run, regenerate and publish are in cli/commands/eval.py. Where they differ from the table:

  • run also takes --passes. --llm takes PRESET, FILE.yaml, NAME=PRESET or NAME=FILE. The report goes to --out, by default eval_<mode>.json next to nl2sql.yaml, with a run stamp (when, and which engine version and commit) for publish. Exit codes: 0, 1 on a regression, 2 on a usage error or a baseline that cannot be compared, 3 at the cost cap. Mode full refuses to start with CI set (the one CI read, in READS_THE_ENVIRONMENT).
  • publish [REPORT ...] [--note] [--from DIR ...] writes one record per config of each report, then rebuilds docs/benchmarks.md and the README block from every record. With no report it only rebuilds the pages, as benchmark publish did.
  • Records are keyed by mode and suite digest: benchmarks/<mode>/<database>/...json, kind the mode and dataset the suite's name and digest (several suites: their digests joined and hashed, report.suite_identity). Every mode is recorded; a record keeps the config's whole board.
  • The headline accuracy is execution accuracy (metrics.accuracy is accuracy.execution), so the published series reads the same as 0.6's; accuracy_all_scorers and accuracy_generated sit beside it.
  • 0.6's records stay readable. Kind tier2 is read as mode full (records.mode_of), so the history shows those runs in the mode full table, as a new series (the suite changed).
  • Records are slim: one compact JSON line, each case's verdicts and cost only (records.slim_result). The full report is CI's eval-reports artifact. A retrieval record names its embedder.
  • CI's baselines are recorded on CI (ubuntu-latest, Python 3.12): the integration job uploads eval_plans.json and eval_retrieval.json, and nl2sql eval publish records them from that artifact, the run's URL in the note. The steps are in benchmarks/README.md; a suite, schema or routing change re-records both the same way.

docs.title: Seeding: benchmark your own database
docs.text:
engine.evals.seed("sales", count=20, out="evals/sales.yaml") (D26):

  1. A new agent, eval_seeder (added to AgentName), is shown the datasource's live snapshot, filtered by the caller's scope: tables, columns, keys, descriptions, and sample values only where the datasource has sample_values on. It is asked for questions of mixed difficulty, each with a typed PlanModel, never SQL, five per call, until count are written or the budget is spent: twenty plans in one structured answer would be fragile to parse, and one bad plan would cost the other nineteen. Each call goes through parse-and-retry as every structured call does.
  2. Seeding has its own cost cap. It runs outside a question, so no per-question cap applies; it runs under the same budget (nl2sql/limits.py) with max_cost_usd, by default evals.yaml's, and a model with no price refuses to start, as an eval in mode full does. When the budget is spent, the cases so far are written and the report says it stopped.
  3. Each plan goes through the engine's LogicalValidatorNode and GeneratorNode, so the SQL is the engine's own rendering in the adapter's dialect. A plan the validator rejects is dropped and counted.
  4. The SQL runs through the adapter, read-only and within the datasource's limits, to confirm it executes and returns rows. A failure or an empty result drops the case and is counted.
  5. Survivors are appended to out with status: draft, origin: seeded, sql, plan, tables, columns (from the plan) and outcome set to the caller's role allowed. A question already in the file is skipped. rows are left empty.
  6. A person reads each draft, fixes the question or the SQL, and sets status: approved; regenerate then writes the rows. Drafts never run in an eval.

SeedReport(written, dropped_invalid, dropped_failed, dropped_empty, dropped_duplicate, stopped_at_cost_cap, usage).

Built: seeding (V3)

engine.evals.seed(datasource_id, *, count=20, out, user_context, max_cost_usd=None) -> SeedReport and nl2sql eval seed, in evaluation/seed.py and evaluation/prompts.py (EVAL_SEEDER_PROMPT). The user guide is Benchmark your own database. Where the code differs from the steps above:

  • The caller is required and checked first. No user_context, no role, or a role whose scope does not reach the datasource (or none of its tables) is a PermissionError before any call. The model is shown the tables through SchemaRetrieverNode.visible_tables(user_context, datasource_id), new and public: the planner's own rendering for that caller. outcome marks allowed each of the caller's roles whose own scope reads every table of the plan (after review of PR #328); other roles get no entry.
  • Plans go through the pinned-plan entry. Each proposed plan runs as run_query(question, plan=SuppliedPlan(...), execute=False, user_context=...): plan.after, the validator and the generator under the caller's scope, with no model call, in a run scope of its own (run.started and run.finished). The draft keeps the plan that produced the SQL (result.sub_queries[0].plan), so a plan.after change wins. A question that reads as SQL (the decomposer's SubQuery check) is dropped as invalid.
  • The SQL passes execute.before and execute.after (the session lead's decision on the review of PR #328): it is model-proposed, so an approval hook or Wave B's cost guard must see it. A deny, a hook failure or needs_approval drops the case (dropped_hooked). execute.after gets a summary of the first row (truncated: true). regenerate runs human-reviewed gold SQL and stays unhooked; both are documented in configuration/hooks.md. The rows are checked with execute_batches(request, 1) where the adapter streams; no row is kept.
  • The structured output is SeedBatch (cases: SeedCase with question, difficulty and a PlanModel), the name a fake LLM rule answers. A call whose answer never parses counts its batch as invalid.
  • The budget is Budget(max_cost_usd, max_llm_calls, setting="evals") with at most three calls per batch of five (CALLS_PER_BATCH), so a model answering nothing usable stops; the report says so (stopped_at_call_limit), and the CLI exits 3 as at the cost cap. Each call is shown the count of questions already written and the newest ten (RECENT_QUESTIONS), not all of them. max_cost_usd is required (the argument, else evals.yaml's), and an unpriced eval_seeder model is an UnknownPriceError before any call.
  • Drafts never go into reviewed cases: out may not be a packaged suite, a suite evals.yaml names, or a file holding approved cases. The guard is nl2sql.evaluation.suite.check_target(path, configured), which feedback export calls too. SeedReport also carries path, dropped_hooked and stopped_at_call_limit.
  • The CLI asks as --role, else policies.default_role, and exits 2 without one; it exits 2 on any refusal and 3 at the cost cap or the call limit, and refuses to run with CI set, as mode full does. It takes no --llm: llm.agents.eval_seeder picks the model.

docs.title: 9. Phase R: cross-database routing
docs.text: Phase R was never built: 0.6 has domains on a datasource and nothing else of it. Everything below is in indexing/ and the resolver, decomposer and validator nodes.

docs.title: One entry per phrasing
docs.text:
Today SchemaChunkBuilder._build_datasource_chunks writes one schema.datasource entry per datasource whose text holds its description, domains and every sample question, so the fifth sample question barely moves the vector.

Entry type Text Count schema.datasource description and domains one per datasource schema.datasource_example (new) one sample question (from sample_questions, or enrichment's) one per question curated.verified_query (exists) one phrasing of a verified query one per phrasing (already)

ENTRY_TYPES in api/indexing_api.py and the inspector gain the new type.

docs.title: Votes and fusion
docs.text:
Retriever.route(question, datasource_ids, explain) -> list[RouteCandidate] replaces retrieve_datasource_candidates. It runs five searches over the live builds of the datasources the caller's scope reaches (the scope filter moves before the search, so a denied datasource never even ranks), and each search ranks datasources by their best entry:

Signal Search description schema.datasource, exact over every datasource (as today) examples schema.datasource_example, top VOTE_K curated curated.verified_query, top VOTE_K tables schema.table across every datasource, top VOTE_K columns schema.column across every datasource, top VOTE_K

The ranks are fused with reciprocal rank fusion (D28):

score(ds) = sum over signals s:  1 / (RRF_K + rank_s(ds))

where rank_s(ds) is len(ranked_s) + 1 for a datasource signal s did not rank (amended after review: otherwise merely having entries of a type is a vote).

VOTE_K = 20 and RRF_K = 60 (the value the RRF literature uses) are constants on Retriever, beside FETCH_MULTIPLIER and LAMBDA_MULT, until the routing suite shows a reason to tune them.

Then the candidates are the top candidates by score, dropping any whose best entry similarity is under floor_ratio times the most similar candidate's (amended after review: a floor on the fused score never fires). The searches see only the entries the caller's scope allows: a table or column of a hidden table, or a verified query that reads one, is dropped before it can vote or be recorded. The trace records each signal's ranking and the fused scores (retrieval.searches, with a new routing record), so the playground's inspector and an eval can show why a datasource was or was not chosen.

The answerability verdict is unchanged in shape (it already returns a list): it may pick several of the candidates, and the resolver forwards at most max_datasources of them, in fused order.

Built: entries, votes, fusion and the retrieval settings (R1)

  • Entries. DatasourceExampleChunk (schema.datasource_example) in indexing/models.py; build_example_chunks(datasource_id, questions, schema_version) in indexing/chunk_builder.py takes the question list from its caller (SchemaChunkBuilder passes the orchestrator's sample_questions, or enrichment's), so Wave B adds the glossary's examples to that list without changing it. Blank and repeated questions are skipped; ids hash the question. DatasourceChunk lost examples. ENTRY_TYPES lists the new type.
  • Routing. Retriever.route(question, datasource_ids, explain=None, *, limit=3, floor_ratio=0.5, allows=None) -> list[RouteCandidate] replaces retrieve_datasource_candidates, which is deleted. limit, floor_ratio and allows (an entry check) are keyword arguments the resolver fills from settings.routing.candidates, floor_ratio and the caller's scope (the retriever reads no settings and no policy). RouteCandidate (datasource_id, score, ranks, similarity) is in indexing/models.py; ROUTE_SIGNALS, fuse(rankings, rrf_k, datasource_ids, similarity=None) (an unranked datasource gets rank len(ranked) + 1) and shortlist(fused, limit, floor_ratio) (the floor on best similarity) are module functions in indexing/retrieval.py; VOTE_K = 20 and RRF_K = 60 are on Retriever. The trace gets one route.<signal> record per signal and a routing record (signals, fused with each similarity, a pool of the fused datasources, picks, dropped with floor or limit, rrf_k, vote_k, candidates, floor_ratio).
  • Table scope (after the review of PR #316). The resolver's _route_filter passes allows: a table or column entry votes only when its (datasource, table) is visible in the live snapshot, a verified query only when every table its SQL reads is. Refused entries are dropped before ranking or recording, over-fetching so VOTE_K counts allowed entries. routing.candidates now defaults to 3, as D28 says.
  • The resolver. The scope filter runs before routing: no reachable datasource is a SECURITY_VIOLATION with no search. It forwards at most max_datasources of the accepted candidates, best by fused score; the forwarded list stays sorted by id, so the decomposer's prompt does not depend on the fused order. ResolvedDatasource.metadata is empty on every path now (it held the datasource entry's metadata, which nothing read). MAX_DECOMPOSER_TABLES is settings.retrieval.decomposer_tables.
  • The schema retriever reads settings.retrieval.table_k and planning_k; TABLE_K and PLANNING_K are deleted.
  • The retrieval scorers (evaluation/scorers/retrieval_recall.py, after V1): routed() ranks with route under settings.routing (then cut at the caller's limit, max_datasources in mode retrieval), and retrieval_settings() reads settings.retrieval.
  • Baseline. The 0.6 retrieval baseline, recorded on main before any of this changed, is benchmarks/retrieval/chinook/2026-10-15_653fa73_retrieval.json: table recall 0.9767, column recall 0.7185 and datasource_top1_accuracy 0.9535 (41 of 43 Chinook questions; the two misses went to support), over the demo's three datasources with the local embeddings.
  • Measured after the review (key-free, local embeddings). Routing top-1 over 79 questions across the demo's three datasources (the 43 Chinook gold questions, the 20 sample questions and 16 paraphrases written for this check): 0.6 75/79; R1 before the review 62/79 (the curated free vote sent 17 of the 20 support and webanalytics questions to chinook); R1 after it 77/79. The expected datasource was among the shortlisted candidates for all 79 in every version.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
# settings.yaml
routing:
  candidates: 3          # datasources shown to the answerability check
  max_datasources: 3     # datasources one question may use
  max_sub_queries: 6     # sub-queries one question may have
  floor_ratio: 0.5       # drop a candidate less similar than this share of the most similar
retrieval:
  full_snapshot_max_tables: 15     # exists
  table_k: 8                       # was SchemaRetrieverNode.TABLE_K
  planning_k: 12                   # was SchemaRetrieverNode.PLANNING_K
  decomposer_tables: 30            # was MAX_DECOMPOSER_TABLES in the resolver
  • max_datasources bounds what the resolver forwards.
  • max_sub_queries is stated in the decomposer's prompt. A decomposition over it ends the run with QUESTION_TOO_BROAD (D29): "This question needs more than 6 separate queries. Ask about fewer things at once." It is not retried: a model that ignored the limit once will usually do so again, and the question is the thing to change.

Built: the sub-query limit (R2)

DecomposerNode reads settings.routing.max_sub_queries once, in its constructor (self.max_sub_queries), and the system prompt states it as rule 10 ("Use at most 6 sub_queries"), a {max_sub_queries} template variable, so the system message stays the same for one engine. The count is of the model's own sub-queries, before any is dropped as unmapped. Over it, the node returns an empty DecomposerResponse, no DAG and one QUESTION_TOO_BROAD error (ERROR, in FATAL_ERRORS), with the message above; the model is called once.

docs.title: The join-key type check
docs.text:
A join or compare combine group joins two sub-queries' results in the aggregator on its join_keys (aggregation/engines/polars_duckdb.py, a polars join). Today nothing checks that both sides of a key have the same kind of type, so a text customer_id from one database joined to an integer from another fails in the aggregator (AGGREGATOR_FAILED, terminal) or matches nothing (B30).

A validator check alone cannot fix that case. The plan has no cast (there is no CAST in ALLOWED_FUNCTIONS, and nothing in ast_planner/schemas.py), and when one database stores the key as text there is no numeric column for the model to pick instead: a "type mismatch, try again" would turn one terminal failure into three wasted retries and then another. So the fix is in two parts (D30):

  1. The decomposer declares the type. DecomposerResponse's validator requires that each JoinKeyPair.left and .right names a column in the expected_schema of its side's sub-query, with a dtype, and that the two dtypes can be coerced to each other (the table below). A violation is a ValueError, which parse-and-retry feeds back to the model. The decomposer node then marks those columns as join keys on its own copy of each SubQuery: ExpectedColumn.join_key is excluded from the model's tool schema (SkipJsonSchema), so the model can never set it.
  2. The aggregator coerces. Before the join, the engine's aggregator casts both sides of each key to the declared dtype in polars, non-strictly. A value that does not convert becomes null, does not match, and is counted in a JOIN_KEY_UNCONVERTED warning ("3 of 412 support.customer_ref values are not numbers and joined nothing"). This is engine-side compute on result frames, so no dialect is involved.
  3. The validator rejects only what cannot be coerced. In LogicalValidatorNode._validate_static, for each select item that is a join key and a plain column reference, the column's data_type from the snapshot is parsed with sqlglot.exp.DataType.build(data_type, dialect=<the adapter's>) and put in a category: number, text, temporal, boolean, or other. Against the declared dtype:
Column \ declared number text temporal boolean number ok ok (formatted) reject ok (0 and 1) text ok (parsed) ok ok (parsed) ok (parsed) temporal reject ok (formatted) ok reject boolean ok ok reject ok

A rejected pair is JOIN_KEY_TYPE_MISMATCH, a retryable ERROR that asks for another column, never a cast: "The join key order_date is declared a date, but Orders.OrderId is a number. Select the date column for this key." A type sqlglot cannot place is other and is not checked; a computed select item is not checked.

No dialect name is written in the engine: the dialect comes from the adapter, as the generator already does. test_text_and_integer_keys_join_after_coercion is B30's test.

Built: join-key coercion and the check (R2)

  • One set of rules. nl2sql/aggregation/join_keys.py (plain Python) holds the categories, DTYPE_CATEGORY, coercible(a, b) and join_dtype(left, right), the type both sides are cast to: the shared dtype; text parsed as the other side's type; int and float meet as int (not float: a non-whole value cannot equal a whole one, and a float cannot tell ids above 2^53 apart), date and datetime as datetime, a number and bool as bool. The decomposer's schema, the aggregator and the validator all read it.
  • The decomposer. DecomposerResponse.validate_join_key_types() resolves each key against its side's expected_schema with resolve_key (so right.customer_id is customer_id); the side is the input's place in engine order (input_order). ExpectedColumn.join_key, JoinKeyPair.left_dtype and JoinKeyPair.right_dtype are SkipJsonSchema, set only by mark_join_keys() in decomposer/node.py, which replaces whatever the model sent and leaves a key it cannot find untyped rather than crash. join_key is excluded from the stable sub-query id and from the planner's expected_schema. CombineGroup.validate_roles() refuses two inputs on one side, or a third input, in a join/compare. The DAG carries the pair's dtypes in the combine node's join_keys attributes (dag.py dumps the pair, so it is unchanged).
  • The aggregator. PolarsDuckdbEngine.combine casts each side first to its own declared dtype and then to the joined one, so a value is read the way its sub-query declared it (a number goes straight to the joined number type, and two float keys over integer frames join as int). A cast nulls, never changes, a value: a float or decimal that is not whole is not an int. Timestamps of any unit or zone become naive UTC microseconds (exact dtypes are compared, not the bare pl.Datetime class); text is parsed only by the ISO formats in _DATE_FORMATS, _NAIVE_FORMATS and _OFFSET_FORMATS, never by inference; a Time key declared a date or timestamp is null. Every one of those nulls is counted, so none ends the run as AGGREGATOR_FAILED. Text is stripped on both sides, of a text key too; a text boolean is true/false/t/f/yes/no/1/0; a number cast to a boolean is 1 or 0, anything else null. PolarsDuckdbEngine.unconverted_join_keys(inputs, join_keys) counts the values that became null (it collects the key columns only), and AggregationService.execute(..., warnings=[...]) gathers them; the node turns each into a JOIN_KEY_UNCONVERTED warning on the state's warnings, naming the datasource: "1 of 3 support.customer_id values are not whole numbers and joined nothing." S1 made it a RunWarning whose detail holds column, failed, total and dtype.
  • The validator. pipeline/nodes/validator/join_keys.py, join_key_type_errors(plan, sub_query, relevant_tables, dialect), called from _validate_static before the buildability check. The column type is the schema snapshot's Column.type. sqlglot's BOOLEAN is a boolean, its numeric types a number (BIT included), its text types text, its temporal types temporal; anything else, an unparsable type or no type is other and not checked. The message is "The join key order_key is declared a date, but Orders.OrderKey is a number. Select a column that holds a date for this key."
  • The demo. test_a_key_declared_text_on_one_side_joins_after_coercion (tests/e2e/test_multi_sub_query_fake_llm.py) joins Chinook's integer CustomerId to support's customer_id declared as text and gets the SQLite answer. The demo databases store both keys as integers, so the text-against-integer case itself is the unit test above. The design lists no realdb test for R2.

docs.title: The routing gate
docs.text:
nl2sql/evaluation/suites/routing.yaml holds approved cases over the demo's three databases (chinook, support, webanalytics), single and cross-database, each with its datasources, plus cases over the test bed's 1,200-table wide schema that run in the realdb job. The routing scorer in retrieval mode is the CI gate (free); the same suite in full mode is the release check. R1 records the 0.6 baseline first, so the gate measures Phase R's change rather than asserting a number.

Built: the routing suite and gate (R3)

  • The suite. suites/routing.yaml (ROUTING_SUITE_PATH in evaluation/suite.py): 78 approved, hand-written cases asked as admin, tagged by origin and datasource. They are R1's 79-question measurement (the 43 Chinook gold questions, the demo's 20 sample questions, 12 of which are gold questions too, and 16 paraphrases) plus 8 more support and webanalytics questions and 3 cross-database ones: 47 name chinook, 14 support, 14 webanalytics, 3 two of them. Every expected datasource was read against the schema. No case names tables, so the routing scorer alone decides a case and a recall miss cannot hide a routing one (the Chinook suite's retrieval status needs both). Ten support and webanalytics cases carry reviewed SQL, with rows written by regenerate; the others are routing only, with no sql.
  • The scorer, after the owner's extra requirement. In mode retrieval routing passes a case only when routing ranks one of its datasources first (detail.top1) and shortlists all of them (detail.shortlist, as the section above said). Mode retrieval allows no flip, so the gate fails when either drops. The board gains routing (cases, top1, shortlist), and a retrieval record's metrics gain routing_top1, routing_shortlist and routing_cases, shown on the history page and the README beside recall. result_match no longer scores a case without sql: such a case says where a question goes, not what it returns.
  • Where it runs. The demo's evals.yaml still names only chinook.yaml: mode plans needs a plan for every case with SQL, and a combined run would also move the Chinook records to a new database id. nl2sql init --demo copies routing.yaml with the other suites, and it is run by name. CI's integration job adds an "Eval gate (routing)" step (eval run --mode retrieval --suite evals/routing.yaml --baseline benchmarks --out demo-ci/eval_routing.json) and uploads eval_routing.json in eval-reports; its records live under benchmarks/retrieval/chinook-support-webanalytics/.
  • Tests. tests/integration/test_routing_gate.py: test_routing_suite_cases_are_approved_and_regenerated and test_routing_recall_does_not_regress (the gate against benchmarks/).
  • The wide schema. Its cases are in tests/realdb/test_routing_wide.py (test_routing_on_the_wide_schema), not in routing.yaml: they name the test bed's datasources, which the demo does not have. Pagila and the whole wide schema are indexed side by side on PostgreSQL only, since indexing 1,200 tables takes about 17 minutes on CI's runner; four questions about films must go to Pagila and four about payroll runs, ledger entries, vendor contacts and campaign clicks to the wide schema. After review it runs only when the realdb workflow sets REALDB_WIDE_ROUTING (nightly, on demand, and on pull requests that change indexing/), and the realdb job's timeout is 60 minutes.
  • Routing cases are a kind (after review). EvalCase.kind is answer (the default, left out of a suite file) or routing. A routing case has no sql, gets no result_match verdict, and is left out of execution accuracy in every mode: the board's accuracy.execution, the record's headline metrics and flips, and the gate's execution measures. Mode retrieval still gates it by status. The loader rejects an approved answer case with an allowed role and no sql, so a missing answer can no longer pass as "any answer". Records keep each case's kind. The Chinook suite and its digest are unchanged. The three cross-database cases are tagged with both their datasources; the suite's header names the cases with two defensible answers. Both changed the suite's digest, so the routing baseline was recorded again from CI (run 38788733052, 2026-10-15_baaae0c_retrieval.json: the same 97.4% top-1 and 98.7% shortlist).
  • Measured (key-free, local embeddings). On the routing suite, routing top-1 is 76/78 and shortlist recall 77/78. The misses: "Which customers complained most about refunds?" and "How many purchases were there per month in 2013?" rank chinook first; "Which customers both raised support tickets and made a purchase on the website?" drops webanalytics at the floor. The Chinook suite's retrieval gate is unchanged by the stricter scorer (all 43 Chinook cases rank chinook first).
  • Baselines, recorded on CI (run 38778183715, ubuntu-latest, Python 3.12, the same numbers as on Windows): benchmarks/retrieval/chinook-support-webanalytics/2026-10-15_a33c8ce_retrieval.json (routing top-1 97.4%, shortlist 98.7%) and a new Chinook retrieval record, benchmarks/retrieval/chinook/2026-10-15_a33c8ce_retrieval.json, which carries the routing metrics (100% / 100%) with no flip against the last. The realdb wide-schema test passed on that run too.

docs.title: 10. Schema drift: measure first
docs.text: The owner wants drift captured and measured before anything acts on it. Nothing here re-indexes or schedules (D31).

docs.title: engine.index.check()
docs.text:
engine.index.check(datasource_ids=None) -> list[DriftReport]

class DriftReport(BaseModel):
    datasource_id: str
    status: Literal["unchanged", "drifted", "not_indexed", "failed"]
    live_version: str | None          # the build pointer's schema version
    checked_at: datetime
    diff: SchemaDiff | None           # live database against the live build
    impact: DriftImpact | None
    error: str | None

For each datasource it reflects the live database with the datasource's IndexScope (adapter.fetch_schema_snapshot, no profiling: profile: catalog for the check), fingerprints it with generate_schema_fingerprint, and compares it with the fingerprint of the snapshot the live build pointer names. Equal fingerprints are unchanged; otherwise the diff and impact are computed and schema.drifted is published with detected_by: "check". Nothing is stored and nothing is rebuilt. nl2sql index --check prints the reports and exits 0 when nothing drifted, 1 when something did, 2 when a check failed, so a cron job or CI step can act on it.

docs.title: The diff
docs.text:
class ColumnChange(BaseModel):
    table: str; column: str
    changes: dict[str, tuple[Any, Any]]     # "type", "nullable", "pk": (old, new)

class SchemaDiff(BaseModel):
    datasource_id: str
    from_version: str
    to_version: str | None                  # None: the live database
    tables_added: list[str]; tables_dropped: list[str]
    columns_added: list[ColumnRef]; columns_dropped: list[ColumnRef]
    columns_changed: list[ColumnChange]
    foreign_keys_added: list[str]; foreign_keys_dropped: list[str]
    engine_type: tuple[str, str] | None     # (old, new) when the adapter type changed
    def is_empty(self) -> bool: ...

It compares exactly what the fingerprint covers (schema/fingerprint.py): table and column names, types, nullability, primary keys, foreign keys, and the snapshot's engine_type, which the diff reports as engine_type: tuple[str, str] | None (a datasource whose type changed). The fingerprint also covers datasource_id, which is the same on both sides of any diff, so: for two snapshots of one datasource, diff.is_empty() is true exactly when the fingerprints are equal; a property test holds that. A rename is a drop and an add: there is no reliable way to tell a rename from a drop without asking someone.

Stored with the new version. When a build stores a snapshot whose fingerprint differs from the version it replaces, the orchestrator computes the diff and stores it beside the new version, then publishes schema.drifted with detected_by: "build". A version whose structure did not change (only statistics did) gets no diff. StateStore gains:

def put_schema_diff(self, diff: SchemaDiff) -> None: ...                       # keyed by datasource and to_version
def get_schema_diff(self, datasource_id: str, schema_version: str) -> SchemaDiff | None: ...

so the store kind moves to interface version 2 (the other three stores only declare it), and the sqlite store adds migration 4, a schema_diffs table that keep_snapshots prunes with its version. The diff's model lives in nl2sql_sdk.schema beside SchemaSnapshot. The version moves for all four slots, not only the state store, because the registry has one version per kind (INTERFACE_VERSIONS["store"] in registry.py) and the four slots share the nl2sql.stores group; a version per slot would be a second mechanism for one method.

Facade What it does engine.index.check(datasource_ids=None) Above engine.index.versions(datasource_id) -> list[SchemaVersionInfo] Each stored version, newest first: schema_version, created_at, fingerprint, live (a pointer names it), has_diff engine.index.diff(datasource_id, schema_version=None) -> SchemaDiff \| None The stored diff that introduced a version (the live one by default)

Measuring is then a matter of reading these: how often each datasource's structure changes between builds, and how far the live database is from the build at any check.

docs.title: Impact
docs.text:
DriftImpact lists what the diff breaks, from data the engine already has:

What How Verified queries Each query in curated.yaml whose SQL reads a dropped table or column, or a column whose type changed: the tables and columns from the same sqlglot parse nl2sql curated validate uses Policy rules Each role's allow or deny pattern that matched a dropped table and now matches nothing, from a new nl2sql.policies.patterns_matching(datasource_id, tables) (pattern matching stays in policies/, by the invariant) Preferred tables The datasource's preferred_tables that were dropped

The plan cache needs no impact entry: it is keyed on schema_version, so a rebuild already makes its plans unreachable.

Built: schema drift (D1)

nl2sql_sdk.schema holds SchemaDiff (with counts() and is_empty()), ColumnChange and ForeignKeyRef, exported from nl2sql_sdk and SchemaDiff from nl2sql too. Three shapes differ from the sketch above, so a caller's scope can filter them without parsing names: tables are TableRefs (not str), ColumnChange.table is a TableRef, and a foreign key is a ForeignKeyRef (table, columns, referred_table, referred_columns) rather than a string. A table added or dropped is listed once, without its columns or foreign keys. nl2sql/schema/diff.py has diff_contracts(old, new, *, from_version, to_version) and visible_diff(diff, allows); a seeded random property test holds that the diff is empty exactly when the fingerprints match. The store kind is at interface version 2 (INTERFACE_VERSIONS), all four built-in stores declare it, and SqliteState adds migration 0004_schema_diffs (schema_diffs, keyed by datasource and to_version; put_schema_diff replaces and refuses a diff with no to_version; keep_snapshots deletes a pruned version's diff). Wave B takes version 3 and migration 5, Wave C version 4 and migration 6. IndexingOrchestrator._record_drift runs after the commit (a failure is logged, never fails the live build) and publishes through nl2sql/schema/drift.py's publish_drift(ctx, diff, detected_by) on ctx.bus with the engine's tenant_id. The caller's scope (binding extra): engine.index.check(datasource_ids=None, *, user_context), versions(datasource_id, *, user_context) and diff(datasource_id, schema_version=None, *, user_context) all require user_context, as datasources.schema does (M1). A caller sees only the tables its Scope.allows: drift only in denied tables is unchanged (and a stored diff reads None, has_diff false); a datasource it cannot reach is left out of check() and, named, is the same ValueError as an unknown id. schema.drifted carries the whole diff's counts and no table name; it is audited and off the stream (STREAM_EVENTS). DriftReport and SchemaVersionInfo live in nl2sql/schema/drift.py; SchemaVersionInfo has schema_version, fingerprint, live, has_diff and no created_at, since the store interface records no creation time (the sqlite version string starts with one). The check reflects with the datasource's IndexScope copied to profile: catalog, sample_values: false; a failure's error is redact_for(ctx, ...). Impact: nl2sql/schema/impact.py's drift_impact(ctx, diff, tables) runs every finder in FINDERS over the (caller-visible) diff, each filling its own field of DriftImpact (verified_queries: ImpactedQuery(datasource_id, query_id, reasons); policy_rules: ImpactedRule(role, kind, pattern); preferred_tables). Wave B adds glossary_terms as one more field and one more finder appended to FINDERS; no caller changes. Verified queries are matched from inspect_verified_sql, which now also returns columns. After review: SchemaVersionInfo.fingerprint is of visible_contract(contract, scope.allows) (the denied tables and the foreign keys to them removed), so a denied-only change looks like a statistics-only one; the policy-rule impact compares against the live tables the caller may read; a check publishes schema.drifted once per drift (_publish_check_drift remembers (from_version, the diff's sha256) per datasource in a WeakKeyDictionary keyed by the runtime, so per engine and in memory only); inspect_verified_sql's columns are (schema, table, column) with the table its qualifier's alias names (or the only table read, or ""), and an unqualified column in a multi-table query is a "may read" reason. nl2sql index --check exits 2 when nothing was checked. nl2sql.policies.patterns_matching(roles, datasource_id, tables) takes policies.roles too and returns (role, kind, pattern) triples; the boundary test now flags imports of the nl2sql.policies.patterns module only (its prefix also caught patterns_matching), and api/indexing_api.py joined its access-decision list. nl2sql index --check also takes --role (repeatable, default admin as nl2sql run) and --json; a config that fails to load exits 2.

docs.title: 11. Answer sanity checks
docs.text:
Cheap checks after a sub-query runs, before the aggregator. They live in pipeline/nodes/executor/sanity/, which takes in today's value_check.py. Every probe is a sqlglot expression built from the plan and rendered by the adapter (render_sql or its dialect), bounded by the datasource's row limit, and skipped for a table the caller's scope denies, as value_check.py does today. A check that fails to run reports nothing.

Check When it runs Detects Then (D32) Missing value (exists) An empty result filtered on a string literal The column has no such value. With sample values in the snapshot the closest is taken from them with no query; otherwise from today's bounded DISTINCT probe. A close value and a retry left: retried once (VALUE_NOT_FOUND, ERROR). Otherwise a warning. Join fan-out The plan joins a table on a key that is not unique on the other side (known from the snapshot's primary and foreign keys) and aggregates SUM, AVG or COUNT over a column of the one side. This includes one table joined to two others on their many side (a many-to-many sum), which is the same probe per many side. A probe over the plan's FROM, joins and WHERE: COUNT(*) against COUNT(DISTINCT <one side's primary key>). More rows than keys confirms that each row was counted several times. Under COUNT, confirmed with a retry left: retried once (JOIN_FAN_OUT, ERROR), telling the planner to count distinct keys, which the plan can say (Expr.distinct). Under SUM or AVG: a warning only, since the repair (aggregate the many side first) needs a derived table the plan cannot express; splitting such a question in the decomposer is a Wave B idea. Otherwise a warning. All-null column A result with rows A result column whose every value is null: usually an outer join that matched nothing, or the wrong column A warning only (ALL_NULL_COLUMN): no probe, and no reliable fix to suggest

Retries are counted against settings.pipeline.retries.max, and each check retries at most once per sub-query, as VALUE_NOT_FOUND does. A verified query is not checked: a person wrote its SQL. settings.pipeline.sanity_checks: true turns them all off when false.

Typed warnings (D34). QueryResult.warnings becomes list[RunWarning], in S1, the PR that adds warnings (today's producers: result_from_state in api/query_api.py, executor/value_check.py, executor/node.py, the answer synthesizer):

class RunWarning(BaseModel):         # not Warning, which is a Python builtin
    code: str                     # an ErrorCode value: VALUE_NOT_FOUND, JOIN_FAN_OUT, ALL_NULL_COLUMN, ...
    node: str
    message: str                  # what the answer says
    sub_query_id: str | None = None
    detail: dict[str, Any] = {}

The answer synthesizer is given the warnings, as it is given VALUE_NOT_FOUND warnings today, and sanity.flagged is published for each.

Built: sanity checks and typed warnings (S1)

  • Where. pipeline/nodes/executor/sanity/: values.py (moved from executor/value_check.py), fanout.py, nulls.py, and __init__.py's run_checks(plan, *, adapter, allowed, tables, row_limit, row_count, frame, can_retry). ExecutorNode._sanity calls it after execute.after (H1's order is kept: a result a hook stopped is never checked), when settings.pipeline.sanity_checks is on and the execution succeeded. An empty result gets the value check; a result with rows the fan-out and null checks. Each check is wrapped: one that raises reports nothing.
  • Retries. can_retry(code) is true while retries remain, the plan is not pinned, and no earlier attempt of the sub-query raised that code, so each check retries at most once. Findings carry details.attempt; sql_agent.check_execution retries a VALUE_NOT_FOUND or JOIN_FAN_OUT ERROR of the current attempt (_SANITY_RETRIES).
  • Fan-out. A table is repeated when a join reaches, on its far side, columns that are not the far table's whole primary key (from relevant_tables[].primary_key; an unknown key counts as unique); every table on the near side of that join in the plan's join tree is repeated, which covers the many-to-many sum. A COUNT, SUM or AVG (not DISTINCT) of a plain column of a repeated table is confirmed by SELECT 1 FROM <the plan's FROM and joins> WHERE <the plan's WHERE> AND NOT alias.pk IS NULL GROUP BY <the plan's groups>, alias.pk HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 LIMIT 1 (after review: a COUNT(*) against COUNT(DISTINCT pk) over the whole join gave false findings on outer joins and grouped plans), built with the generator's GeneratorNode.attach_joins (now a static method) and rendered by the adapter; the key keeps its reflected case. No probe without a single-column primary key or with a table the scope denies.
  • Probes and hooks (owner's decision after review). A probe, the value check's or the fan-out check's, runs outside execute.before and execute.after. So no probe runs when any hook is attached at execute.before (run_checks(..., probes=False)): only the null check does. settings.pipeline.sanity_checks: false stays the off switch. The check lives in the executor, per sub-query, not in the aggregator beside unconverted_join_keys: the repeated rows are inside one sub-query's SQL, which the aggregator never sees.
  • All-null. check_nulls(frame) reads the saved result's null counts through ArtifactStore.scan_parquet, never its values.
  • Sample values. check_values(..., samples=) takes a column's snapshot sample values (from relevant_tables[].columns[].stats) before the DISTINCT probe; the existence probe still runs, since samples are partial.
  • RunWarning lives in nl2sql/common/errors.py, beside PipelineError, not in api/query_api.py as planned: the nodes that produce warnings must not import the API layer. It is exported as nl2sql.RunWarning. RunWarning.of(error, sub_query_id) turns an error into a warning, its details left behind; an ERROR or CRITICAL one (an attempt a retry replaced) gets detail={"recovered": True} in place of the old severity field, and the answer synthesizer skips those. GraphState.warnings and SubgraphExecutionState.warnings are List[RunWarning]; every producer builds one (the aggregator's RESULT_TRUNCATED, HOOK_DENIED and R2's JOIN_KEY_UNCONVERTED, the curated matcher's CURATED_FALLBACK, the schema retriever's fallback as SCHEMA_RETRIEVAL_FAILED, result_from_state's row-read failure as UNKNOWN_ERROR). extra="forbid", so a stray dict fails loudly.
  • The answer. The synthesizer's Data Notes now carry VALUE_NOT_FOUND, JOIN_FAN_OUT and ALL_NULL_COLUMN warnings, and each is appended to the answer's warnings.
  • sanity.flagged is published through nl2sql.events.publish for each finding: code, sub_query_id, retry (true for a retried ERROR).
  • The playground. NodeInspector.jsx reads a warning's code only, with no fallback to error_code; the bundle is rebuilt.
  • Breaking for REST clients. QueryResult.warnings[] items lost error_code and severity for code and detail.recovered. Runs are not stored across an upgrade, so no older warning is read back.
  • Tests. Every e2e test that opened the session demo's shared state.db (the fake_llm fixture, the RBAC API test, both evals tests, the temperature test) now gets a private copy.

docs.title: 12. MCP server (stdio)
docs.text:
nl2sql mcp serves the engine to an MCP client (a desktop assistant, an IDE) over stdio, using the official mcp Python SDK.

Rule Detail An extra pip install "nl2sql-engine[mcp]". import nl2sql never loads mcp; the boundary test adds it to FORBIDDEN_AT_IMPORT. Public facade only nl2sql/mcp/server.py imports the top-level nl2sql and mcp, nothing else from the engine, held by the same test that holds the API and the playground. nl2sql/cli/commands/mcp.py builds the engine and calls build_server(engine, identity).run("stdio"); identity is a UserContext or a function returning one, asked on every call, so Wave C can name a caller per HTTP request. Who is asking (D33) stdio has no authentication: the person who started the process is the caller. --role (repeatable) and --user set the UserContext; without them the role is policies.default_role. That defaults to none (config/models.py), and a caller with no role reads nothing, so nl2sql mcp with neither refuses to start, naming both fixes; getting_started/mcp.md says so. Logs To stderr only; stdout is the protocol. HTTP and auth Wave C Tool Arguments Returns Facade ask question, datasource_id (optional) status, the answer (summary, content), per sub-query its SQL, columns and the first 20 rows, truncated, source, warnings, trace_id, and approvals_needed or stop when set engine.run_query list_datasources none each datasource's id, type, description and status, for the datasources the caller's scope reaches engine.datasources.list, engine.policies.scope describe_table datasource_id, table its columns (name, type, nullable, key, description), foreign keys, row count and description; "not found" for a table the caller may not read, so a denied table is indistinguishable from a missing one engine.datasources.schema(datasource_id, user_context=...)

engine.datasources.schema(datasource_id, *, user_context) takes the caller, required, and drops the tables its scope denies (B29). There is no default: an app that forgot the argument would fail open. A caller that wants the whole schema passes an admin UserContext explicitly. The playground's schema panel passes the selected role.

Built: the MCP server and the caller's schema (M1)

nl2sql/mcp/server.py has build_server(engine, identity) -> FastMCP (official mcp SDK, the mcp extra mcp>=1.10,<2) and PREVIEW_ROWS = 20; nl2sql mcp --role ... --user ... is cli/commands/mcp.py (caller(policies, roles, user), mcp_command). Shapes the design did not fix: every tool returns a JSON object (its structured content). ask returns status (the run's RunStatus, so Wave B's needs_clarification needs no new field; its clarification gets its own key), answer (summary, content), sub_queries (id, datasource_id, sql, columns, rows, total_rows, truncated), truncated, source, warnings (code, message), trace_id, and errors (code, node, message), approvals_needed and stop when set. An error's or warning's message is kept only for the codes written for the asker (refusals, hooks, limits, providers, the answer checks); any other message is replaced by its code and the trace id, since it may carry an exception's text. An exception out of the engine is INTERNAL_ERROR, logged; ask with a datasource_id the caller cannot reach is DATASOURCE_NOT_FOUND without running. describe_table answers status: ok with the schema() table, or not_found (a denied table, a missing one and a table in an unreachable datasource alike) with the tables the caller may read, or ambiguous when a bare name matches tables in two schemas. nl2sql mcp also starts without a role under allow_all (with a warning), and refuses a role the policies do not define, under allow_all too. After the attack review of PR #325: the identity is resolved inside each tool's guard (a resolver that raises gives INTERNAL_ERROR); SECURITY_VIOLATION always carries the generic refusal (GENERIC_REFUSAL); FastMCP is built with explicit settings; and /api/schema without ?role= is a 400. datasources.schema(datasource_id, *, user_context) filters through policy_engine.scope(...).allows (schema_view(..., allows=)), drops a foreign key to a denied table, and is in the boundary test's ACCESS_DECISIONS. The playground's /api/schema requires ?role= (400 without it) and the page sends its Ask as role. mcp is in FORBIDDEN_AT_IMPORT (which is what test_import_nl2sql_does_not_load_mcp was to check), and test_mcp_uses_only_the_public_api holds nl2sql/mcp/ to the top-level nl2sql and mcp to nl2sql/mcp/.

docs.title: 13. The registry after Wave A
docs.text:
Kind Entry point group Interface Version in 0.7 Built-ins adapter nl2sql.adapters nl2sql_sdk.DatasourceAdapter 2 sqlite, postgres, mysql, mssql, duckdb llm nl2sql.llms nl2sql.llm.LLMProvider 2 openai, anthropic, openai_compatible (with openrouter and ollama) embeddings nl2sql.embeddings nl2sql.embeddings.EmbeddingsProvider 2 local, openai, openai_compatible secrets nl2sql.secrets nl2sql_sdk.secrets.SecretProvider 1 env, aws, azure, hashicorp store nl2sql.stores nl2sql_sdk.stores 2 (StateStore diffs) chroma, sqlite, files, local policy check nl2sql.policy_checks nl2sql_sdk.policy.PolicyCheck 1 none observer nl2sql.observers nl2sql_sdk.events.Observer 1 log, audit, otel hook nl2sql.hooks nl2sql.hooks.Hook 1 none scorer nl2sql.scorers nl2sql.evaluation.scorers.Scorer 1 result_match, outcome, retrieval_recall, faithfulness, routing

New on Registry: add_observer, add_hook, add_scorer and their decorators. Knowledge sources stay for Wave B.

Built: the three kinds (A0)
