    planner_note: Optional[str]  # the plan's own `reasoning`, labelled as the planner's (model text)
    text: str                  # the step as two or three sentences

class Explanation(BaseModel):
    steps: List[ExplainedStep]
    combined: Optional[str]    # how steps were combined (join, compare, union), from the decomposer's groups
Part Rendered from Names A table or column is named by its glossary description's first clause when it has one, else its name split into words (InvoiceDate as "invoice date"), with the qualified name in the structured fields Expressions One renderer per Expr kind: = "is", IN "is one of", LIKE "matches", IS NULL "is empty", SUM "total of", COUNT with distinct "number of different", DATE_PART('year', d) "the year of d", DATE_TRUNC('month', d) "the month of d", a case as "depending on"; a function on ALLOWED_FUNCTIONS without a phrase is written as its name Joins The relationship the join used, and where it came from: a declared key, or the glossary (an accepted proposal) Assumptions Deterministic only: the row cap when the result was truncated; a filter value replaced after VALUE_NOT_FOUND; Wave A's sanity warnings; the readings not chosen when an ambiguity was not asked (D47) Verified answers "Answered by the verified query top_customers_by_revenue, written by the data team, with n = 10 and year = 2012" and its description; no plan

The explanation is built when the result is assembled (api/query_api.py), for every status that has a plan (plan_only included). It reads only fields B0 adds to the state, so X1 builds and tests it with state made by hand, before K2 and L1 fill those fields. The answer synthesizer is not given it: the explanation describes the SQL, the answer describes the rows. explanation is also each clarification option's explanation. Editing the plan from this view is later.

Golden tests render every gold plan in the Chinook suite and compare with stored text, so a renderer change is a reviewed diff.

Built: why this answer (X1)

nl2sql/explain/phrases.py names tables and columns and phrases every Expr kind and operator (KIND_PHRASES, BINARY_PHRASES, UNARY_PHRASES, FUNCTION_PHRASES); nl2sql/explain/render.py has explain_plan(plan, *, datasource_id, sub_query_id=None, source="generated", knowledge_used=None, knowledge=None, assumptions=()) -> ExplainedStep, explain_verified(match, sub_query_id, assumptions) and explain_state(state, warnings=None, knowledge=None) -> Optional[Explanation]. result_from_state fills QueryResult.explanation with explain_state, importing the renderer only there, so every caller (run, stream, evals, replay) gets it. It reads SubgraphOutput only, as B0 set up. Where the build filled a gap (some after an independent review on #335):

  • Only validated steps are explained. An output whose status is not success (a plan the validator or a hook refused, a dropped sub-query) gets no step, and a run a hook ended has no explanation: naming a refused plan's tables would confirm what the refusal withholds. This narrows "every status that has a plan" above.

  • It never fails a run. An operator without a phrase is written as itself, and a state that cannot be rendered gives explanation=None with the error logged, as tables_read does.

  • The glossary is an argument. Glossary names and a join's source need the datasource's glossary, which no output carries: result_from_state(..., knowledge=) takes a mapping from datasource id to DatasourceKnowledge. Nothing passes it yet; K2, which makes glossary joins valid, passes the caller's scope-filtered knowledge (K1's scope filter), never the whole glossary, at the call sites. Without it every join is a declared key, which is true until then.

  • The default reading is "'sales' was read as revenue" when exactly one term sent with the step is read by the plan, else "was read one way"; the planner's answer has no label for its default.
  • text is two to four sentences: what it shows, what it reads and filters, the groups it keeps (HAVING), its order.
  • Assumptions from warnings are the step's own (sub_query_id): a recovered VALUE_NOT_FOUND is said from the final plan ("'Brasil' is not in Customer country; 'Brazil' was used instead." only when a suggested value is a literal of the final plan, else "the question was planned again"), never the planner's retry message; an unrecovered VALUE_NOT_FOUND, JOIN_FAN_OUT, ALL_NULL_COLUMN or JOIN_KEY_UNCONVERTED is said as is; the row cap from truncated.
  • Golden files are one JSON per gold case in tests/unit/explain/golden/; a missing one is written and the test fails, so deleting a file is how a reviewed wording change is made.

For L1: each option's explanation is explain_plan(option_plan, ...); a run that did not ask keeps ambiguous_phrase and alternatives on the output and the step lists them as assumptions. For L2: "You chose: " is passed as an assumptions entry or set on the step; the label is not on the output.

docs.title: The adapter method
docs.text:
# nl2sql_sdk
class Estimate(BaseModel):                       # nl2sql_sdk.models
    rows: Optional[int] = None                   # rows the database expects to READ: see the table below
    cost: Optional[float] = None                 # the planner's own cost units, for display: comparable within one database only
    source: str                                  # what was read, for people: "EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON) and pg_class"

class DatasourceCapability(str, Enum):
    ...
    # ``estimate`` returns the database's own estimate without running the query.
    ESTIMATES_COST = "estimates_cost"

@runtime_checkable
class EstimatingAdapterProtocol(Protocol):
    def estimate(self, sql: str, parameters: Dict[str, Any]) -> Estimate:
        """The database's estimate of the rows sql reads, without executing it. Raises on failure."""

This re-adds what Phase 2 removed as bug B24 (explain and cost_estimate, broken and uncalled), this time with a caller, a capability flag and a conformance check (D52).

rows is what the query reads. The generator's row-cap LIMIT makes the rows a query returns small, and a scan node's own row estimate is its output after the filter: a sequential scan that filters a billion rows down to ten reports ten. Neither predicts cost. So each adapter adds up, over the plan's scan operators, the rows each one reads:

Adapter Reads A full scan counts An index scan or seek counts postgres EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON), then the adapter's own row_estimates (pg_class.reltuples) for the scanned relations Seq Scan: the relation's reltuples, not its Plan Rows Index Scan, Index Only Scan, Bitmap Index Scan: the node's Plan Rows mysql EXPLAIN FORMAT=JSON access_type: ALL: rows_examined_per_scan (MySQL's estimate of rows read) rows_examined_per_scan mssql the estimated plan (SET SHOWPLAN_XML ON, on its own connection), then row_estimates (sys.partitions) Table Scan, Clustered Index Scan, Index Scan: EstimatedRowsRead where the server reports it (SQL Server 2016 SP1 and later), else the table's catalog row count Index Seek, Clustered Index Seek: EstimatedRowsRead, else EstimateRows duckdb EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON), then row_estimates (duckdb_tables().estimated_size) SEQ_SCAN / TABLE_SCAN: the scanned table's cardinality, not the operator's estimate DuckDB plans no index scans for analytic queries; any other scan counts its table sqlite does not declare ESTIMATES_COST: EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN has no row estimates

cost is the planner's total cost where the database reports one (PostgreSQL's Total Cost, MySQL's query_cost, SQL Server's StatementSubtreeCost), shown in the trace and never compared with a limit. The exact fields are proven against the test bed in C1's realdb tests before the table is final. SQL Server needs the SHOWPLAN permission; a login without it gets an error, which the rule treats as unknown. An estimate runs under the datasource's timeout_ms.

The conformance kit gains a check: when ESTIMATES_COST is declared, estimate on a seeded table returns rows >= 0 and does not run the statement (an estimate of sleep_sql(5) returns within 1 second); a filtered full scan of the kit's largest seeded table (a WHERE on an unindexed column that matches no row) reports at least half the table's row count, not the filter's output; and an estimate of SQL naming a missing table raises.

Built: estimate (C1)

estimate(sql, parameters) on the PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server and DuckDB adapters, which declare ESTIMATES_COST; SQLite does not. Each asks for the plan on the adapter's own connections (read-only and under timeout_ms), with parameters bound as execute binds them. Every failure raises RuntimeError: the database's, with the driver's first line, and a plan the adapter cannot read, with the error's class. None falls back to an operator's filtered estimate, and none reports a statement with no plan (SQL Server's WAITFOR, a parameterized RPC) as zero rows: no plan is no estimate, which the cost rule's unknown decides. The kit's sleep_sql check accepts that RuntimeError. The table above holds, with these details:

  • Per execution. Scan rows are per execution, so the inner side of a nested loop is multiplied: SQL Server by 1 + EstimateRebinds + EstimateRewinds; PostgreSQL by the outer side's Plan Rows (EXPLAIN without ANALYZE gives no loops), except below a Materialize; MySQL by the rows_produced_per_join of the tables before it, except through a join buffer (a hash join reads its table once). DuckDB plans hash joins. Not multiplied: a correlated subquery (PostgreSQL SubPlan, MySQL dependent subquery) counts one execution.
  • postgres asks EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON, VERBOSE), for each scan's Schema. A Seq Scan counts the Plan Rows of EXPLAIN SELECT * FROM its relation, the planner's reltuples scaled to the current size on disk, rather than reltuples itself: that counts a relation never analyzed on every version (-1 since 14, 0 before) and is fresher on stale statistics. Foreign Scan and Function Scan are not counted.
  • mysql skips a table with materialized_from_subquery (a derived table, named by its alias in the JSON) and <union...>, and counts what they read.
  • mssql counts Columnstore Index Scan too. SHOWPLAN is a session setting, and pyodbc's ODBC pooling hands a closed connection's session to the next connection, so invalidate() alone leaked it into later adapters (the first realdb run showed it). The estimate now runs SET SHOWPLAN_XML OFF in a finally, then invalidates the connection. Bound parameters are written in as escaped literals (inline_parameters): sent as parameters, the statement is an sp_executesql call, for which SHOWPLAN returned no plan (realdb showed rows=0). cost is StatementSubtreeCost, else the top RelOp's EstimatedTotalSubtreeCost, else None. The test bed's reader login lacks SHOWPLAN; its estimate raises.
  • duckdb reads the scan's Table as DuckDB prints it (memory.main."Big Orders") with sqlglot.exp.to_table, and a scanned table with no size in duckdb_tables() raises. A table function (range) counts its own Estimated Cardinality. DuckDB rules a scan out from its min/max statistics when a filter falls outside them, so the kit's no-match filter (amount = 50.5 on kit_orders, now 100 rows) falls inside them.

The kit's checks are test_kit_estimate_does_not_execute (two seconds, not one: SQL Server opens a fresh connection per estimate), test_kit_filtered_full_scan_reports_the_table_size and test_kit_estimate_of_a_missing_table_raises (a RuntimeError, the contract C2 relies on). cost is None on DuckDB.

docs.title: The policy rule
docs.text:
# policies.yaml
cost:                            # absent: no estimate is ever asked for
  max_estimated_rows: 5000000    # null: no limit
  over_limit: confirm            # allow | confirm | refuse
  unknown: allow                 # no estimate (not declared, failed, rows null): allow | confirm | refuse
roles:
  analyst:
    allow: ["chinook.*.*"]
    cost: { max_estimated_rows: 1000000, over_limit: refuse }
  admin:
    allow: ["*.*.*"]
    cost: { max_estimated_rows: null }
Rule Detail Where it runs (D53) A built-in hook, policy.cost (nl2sql/policies/cost.py), at Wave A's execute.before, ahead of every configured hook. It is built by the runtime from policies.cost, not listed in hooks:, and it applies to generated SQL, verified queries and a correction's check run alike. With allow_all It applies: allow_all: true opens table access, not cost. A cost block beside allow_all is valid (Policies' allow_all check forbids only roles and default_role beside it). Which rule A role's cost fields replace the top-level ones for that role. A caller with several roles gets each field's most permissive value across them: the highest max_estimated_rows, where null (no limit) wins, and the weakest over_limit and unknown (allow over confirm over refuse). Fields may therefore come from different roles; that is intended, as grants union across roles. The call Only when a limit is set and the adapter declares ESTIMATES_COST. One estimate per sub-query, before it runs. Within the limit, or allow Allow. confirm NeedsApproval("Estimated to read 12,400,000 rows (limit 5,000,000)"): the run ends needs_approval with Wave A's ApprovalRequest (hook: "policy.cost", approvers policies.admin_roles), and an approved re-run with the same SQL runs. refuse (D54) Deny with COST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED (CRITICAL, not retryable): "This query is estimated to read 12,400,000 rows, over this role's limit of 1,000,000 (policies.roles.analyst.cost). Ask about less data, for example a shorter period." The planner is not retried: planning the same question again rarely reads less. unknown The same three actions for a sub-query with no estimate.

docs.title: Trace and events
docs.text:
SubQueryResult.estimate: Optional[Estimate] carries the estimate; the executor's trace record holds it with the rule that applied and the decision. Every estimate publishes cost.estimated (datasource_id, sub_query_id, rows, cost, limit, decision); the audit observer keeps the confirm and refuse ones, and Wave A's hook.decision records the hook's decision as for any hook.

Built: the cost rule (C2)

policies.cost and a role's cost are enforced by the built-in policy.cost hook (nl2sql/policies/cost.py: CostGuard, build_cost_guard, take_record). Where the code on main differed from this page, the code won:

  • Order. Need 1 was already met: HookRunner takes the runtime's list, so Runtime._build_hooks puts build_cost_guard(...).binding() first, with approver_roles=policies.admin_roles, only when a cost block exists (at the top or on a role). Without one there is no hook, so execute.before is as configured.
  • The rule. A role's override replaces the fields in its model_fields_set; a caller's roles are user.roles, else default_role, keeping the ones policies.roles knows. Each field takes its most permissive value (null limit wins; allow over confirm over refuse); a caller with no known role gets the top-level rule. A cost on a role with no top-level block starts from CostRule() (no limit), so a caller without that role is never estimated. No limit means no estimate call; a limit with an adapter that does not declare ESTIMATES_COST, an exception or rows: None is unknown, and the exception text goes to the log only.
  • The refusal. Deny from policy.cost is COST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED: HookVerdict.error maps a deny from COST_HOOK (hooks/runner.py) to it, with the same details as HOOK_DENIED. The code joins the run endings in pipeline/routes.py, pipeline/events.py (no manifest), api/query_api.py (no rows) and the MCP caller-facing codes. The message names policies.cost or policies.roles.<role>.cost, whichever set the limit that applied.
  • The estimate on the result. The hook leaves a CostRecord (the estimate, the limit, the decision) in a context variable; the executor and the curated matcher read it with take_record(trace_id, sub_query_id) straight after execute.before and put the estimate on SubgraphExecutionState.estimate / SubgraphOutput.estimate, whether or not the SQL then ran. cost.estimated carries the decision; the trace holds the estimate through the result, not a separate record.
  • Probes. The answer sanity checks run no probe while a configured hook is attached at execute.before, or for a caller the cost rule gives a limit (CostGuard.applies(user); a probe passes no hook and would bypass the limit). A caller with no limit keeps them.
  • Names. A configured hook named policy.cost is a config error (hooks[<i>]): the name is the built-in's.
  • Corrections reach the rule with no change of their own: the hook is in the runner feedback/corrections.py already calls.

docs.title: 10. Learn from corrections
docs.text:
engine.feedback.correct(trace_id, *, sql=None, plan=None, question=None, note=None,
                        user_context) -> Proposal

A thumbs-down that comes with a fix becomes a verified_query proposal (D55). Exactly one of sql or plan is given.

  1. The run. Its trace gives the question (or question overrides it), the datasource (a run on several datasources is refused: a verified query answers from one) and the rating, which is recorded as down with the note if it was not already.
  2. A plan fix (PlanModel or its JSON) goes through the engine's LogicalValidatorNode and GeneratorNode with the corrector's scope, as Wave A's seeding does; a rejected plan is refused with the validator's messages. The SQL is the engine's rendering in the adapter's dialect.
  3. A SQL fix must parse as one read-only SELECT in the adapter's dialect (the curated config's own check), and every table it reads must be in the corrector's scope.
  4. The hooks. The SQL goes through the execute.before hooks, the built-in policy.cost first, with the corrector as the caller. A Deny, or a NeedsApproval (a correction is not re-run with an approval), refuses the correction with the hook's reason.
  5. The check. The SQL runs once through the adapter, read-only and within the datasource's limits, as nl2sql curated test runs a verified query. A failure is refused with the database's message; an empty result is allowed and recorded.
  6. The proposal has origin: correction, change in curated.yaml's shape (id slugged from the question, the question as its phrasing, no params, the SQL, description from the note or a placeholder), tables from the SQL, and evidence: the trace id, the original SQL, ran, row_count, columns. proposal.created is published.

Accepting it (engine.proposals.accept(id, by=admin, edits={id: {...}})) is the review: the reviewer usually edits the id, the description, extra phrasings and the params (replacing literals with :name), the curated checks run on the result, the verified query is written to curated.yaml, and the datasource's entries are refreshed so the next phrasing matches. Nothing is written before that accept.

Command Calls nl2sql feedback correct TRACE_ID (--sql FILE \| --plan FILE) [--question TEXT] [--note TEXT] --as ROLE engine.feedback.correct

Built: corrections (F1)

engine.feedback.correct(trace_id, *, sql=None, plan=None, question=None, note=None, user_context) -> Proposal and nl2sql feedback correct (with --user beside --as, through K1's caller) are built, in nl2sql/feedback/corrections.py (correct); FeedbackAPI.correct only calls it. Exact names, and where the code differs from the steps above:

  • Refusals. CorrectionRefused(ValueError) in feedback/corrections.py, with code (one of REFUSAL_CODES: no_run, multi_datasource, invalid_plan, not_read_only, denied, hook_denied, needs_approval, failed) and messages (the validator's, the hook's reason, the database's). It is a ValueError, so it adds no ErrorCode and no export (both B0's). No caller is a TypeError and not exactly one fix a ValueError, as Q1's methods do.
  • The run. The kept trace (request.question, the result's sub-queries) is read first; with no trace (the default settings.traces.mode keeps only failed runs), the run's rating gives the question, datasource and SQL. Neither is no_run. The run's scope comes first (after review on #341): before anything else, the corrector's Scope must reach every datasource the run read and every table its SQL read (_find_run; a run whose SQL cannot be parsed is refused), and that refusal (denied, DENIED_RUN) names no datasource, table or question. Only then is a run on several datasources refused, and the run rated down, through engine.feedback.record (or the stored row re-rated). So a refused fix still leaves the thumbs-down of a caller who could read the run, and no other caller can change a rating.
  • A plan fix is run_query(plan=SuppliedPlan(...), execute=False, user_context=corrector), as Wave A's seeding runs a plan, so run.before and plan.after see it too. A PlanModel, a dict or JSON text.
  • The SQL check is inspect_verified_sql for both fixes (the engine's rendering included), and a SQL fix with :name placeholders is not_read_only: it runs once, with no values. A trailing ; and the comment after it are dropped first (_one_statement, with sqlglot's tokenizer). A person's SQL fix is also held, in corrections.py rather than the shared curated check, to plain tables (an exp.Table whose source is not an identifier, a table-valued function such as a catalog or file reader, is refused) and to an allow-list of functions: ALLOWED_FUNCTIONS, as sqlglot names them in the datasource's dialect (_known_functions), plus STRUCTURAL_FUNCTIONS (CAST, TRY_CAST, CASE, IF, EXISTS, the current date and time). An unknown function is refused too. Both are not_read_only. The scope check asks PolicyEngine.scope (feedback/corrections.py joins ACCESS_DECISIONS in the boundary test, and FeedbackAPI.correct joins WAVE_B_READ_METHODS, so its caller is a required UserContext).
  • The hooks are hooks_of(ctx).call("execute.before", ...) with the fields a question's executor passes (trace_id the corrected run's, sub_query id correction, plan for a plan fix, params={}, tables as datasource.schema.table, approvals=[]). C2's built-in policy.cost reaches a correction once the runtime puts it in that runner: C2's test_correction_check_is_cost_guarded calls engine.feedback.correct(...) and expects CorrectionRefused with code needs_approval (over_limit: confirm) or hook_denied (refuse; the message is the hook's). execute.after is not called, as step 4 says.
  • The check runs as CuratedAPI.test does: _frames over the adapter with settings.results.fetch_batch_size, the first frame only, no artifact written. row_count is that frame's. An error the adapter did not wrap is logged and named by its type only, so no driver text (a host, a password) reaches the caller. A NEEDS_APPROVAL from a plan fix's run is needs_approval.
  • The proposal is Proposal.build(kind="verified_query", origin="correction", target=<question>, ...) filed with review.queue.propose, so a correction supersedes an open thumbs-up of the same question. change is {id, description, questions, sql} (the id feedback.proposals._slug's, the description the note else DESCRIPTION_PLACEHOLDER); created_by the corrector's user id; schema_version the run's. tables lists the tables the fix and the original SQL read, since evidence.original_sql shows the latter: a caller denied either never sees the proposal. review/queue.py propose now unions tables when the same change is filed again and its evidence is replaced (a second run's correction with the same fix), so new evidence never shows tables the row does not list.
  • Tests. tests/unit/test_corrections.py (every F1 test the row names, the visibility tests and the CLI).

docs.title: 11. Events Wave B adds
docs.text:
Added to Wave A's catalog (nl2sql/events/catalog.py) in B0, each with its data model. None carries rows or sample values (Wave A D15). None of the run events joins Wave A's caller-safe stream allow-list (D17): they carry glossary text, options and estimates, which are operator matters, and reach a subscriber through engine.events.subscribe only. A caller learns of a clarification from the result, which the stream's run.finished carries.

Name Data Published by knowledge.loaded sources (type, item counts, sha256), digests per datasource, error Runtime at build, engine.knowledge.reload() knowledge.used (run, operator) sub_query_id, datasource_id, terms (names and scores), rules (ids), dropped, digest The schema retriever clarification.requested (run, operator) sub_query_id, phrase, options (count) The clarifier cost.estimated (run, operator) above policy.cost profile.finished datasource_id, the ProfileReport's counts, stopped_by, cost, seconds engine.knowledge.profile proposal.created id, kind, datasource_id, origin the queue proposal.decided id, kind, datasource_id, decision, by, wrote accept, reject

The audit observer adds proposal.decided and the confirm and refuse cost.estimated events to what it keeps.

docs.text:
Wave B is designed on Wave A's shapes as PR #308 now states them (after its own review). These are the places where Wave B needs something Wave A does not yet say. None changes a Wave A decision; each is small enough to fold into the Wave A PR named. The single-path rule of H1's architecture test needs no change: the validator's "valid" edge always goes to the clarifier, so every path from the planner to the generator still passes the validator.

(evaluation/tier1.py) would stop answering V1 6 The eval outcome map admits clarify, and engine.evals.run takes clarify: bool = False D58 V1 7 The budget in nl2sql/limits.py can be opened outside a question for a call's own max_cost_usd, as V3's seeding opens it Section 6: drafting runs under it E3 (and V3) 8 D33's rule is stated for every method that shows schema or data, so Wave B's read methods (D60) follow a stated rule Section 3 and 5 the Wave A design (D33) 9 Wave B's run events (knowledge.used, clarification.requested, cost.estimated) stay off D17's caller-safe stream allow-list: they are operator events Section 11 E1 (the allow-list is unchanged) 10 The MCP ask tool's result admits clarification, and it takes an optional choice Section 7 M1 (or L2 adds it) 11 R1's schema.datasource_example builder takes its questions as a list the caller assembles Wave B adds the glossary's examples to the datasource's sample_questions R1 12 The store interface version: Wave A moves to 2; Wave B moves to 3. Each PR is written test-first and updates the docs it affects in the same PR. At most four PRs are open at once. B0 lands first and alone; it is small on purpose and front-loads every shared shape (D59), so the four tracks touch different files. No PR makes a real model call, and none spends the owner's key: K2 converts the demo's recorded answers mechanically (see the note under the table).

Built: knowledge sources, show and export (K1)

The engine loads, merges, resolves, scopes, shows and exports knowledge; nothing reaches a prompt or the index yet (K2, K3). Exact names, and where the code differs from this page:

  • Sources. nl2sql/knowledge/yaml_source.py: YamlKnowledgeSource (yaml, entry point nl2sql.knowledge_sources, config YamlSourceConfig(path), sha256 of the bytes it read), parse_glossary, canonical_yaml(glossary), file_sha256(path) and write_glossary(path, glossary, expected_sha256) -> str (the new hash; ReviewError(FILE_CHANGED) when the hash moved). A config built in code reads a relative path from the current folder.
  • Merge. nl2sql/knowledge/merge.py: load_knowledge(config, registry=, secrets=) -> Knowledge (raises KnowledgeLoadError(index, label, message)); Knowledge is frozen: sources (LoadedSource(type, glossary, sha256, path, loaded_at)), datasources, provenance (datasource to item key to source), digests, errors, get(ds), digest(ds). Item keys are tables.<name>.<field>, columns.<name>.<field>, joins.<from>-><to>, terms.<term>, rules.<id>, examples.<text>. Every source's glossary is checked against settings.knowledge.item_max_chars again after load(), a plugin's too. Two sources of one type are labelled yaml, yaml#2.
  • Resolve and scope. resolve.py: resolve_table, resolve_column, table_label, derived_roles(snapshot, dialect=) (a primary key or a foreign key's constrained column is identifier, a temporal type date), problems(knowledge, snapshot, dialect=). scope.py: visible(knowledge, snapshot, allows), denied_table_names, mentions_denied and with_schema_facts (database comments and derived roles, with origins). Without a snapshot nothing is visible (fails closed): show returns the datasource with only a problem saying to index it, and export and sources leave it out. K2's retriever should call visible with the run's scope and pinned snapshot.
  • Runtime. Runtime.knowledge (a Knowledge) is loaded in components(); a failing source is a ConfigError problem at knowledge[i]. Runtime.reload_knowledge() -> Optional[str] swaps under the lock (on failure the old knowledge stays, carrying errors); pin_index() keeps the knowledge the run started with. knowledge.loaded is published at build only when the knowledge section is not empty, and on every reload.
  • Facade. sources, show, export, reload as section 3 says. A user_context that is not a UserContext is a TypeError. reload needs an admin role, or allow_all; otherwise PermissionError. export writes only knowledge-source items (no derived roles, no database comments) and refuses nl2sql.yaml, every section file and every source file.
  • Appliers. nl2sql/knowledge/apply.py: apply_change(glossary, kind, datasource_id, target, change, *, item_max_chars) -> Glossary and apply_proposal(glossary, proposal, *, item_max_chars), for Q1's accept; GLOSSARY_KINDS = ("table", "column", "join", "term"). A table or column change sets its fields over the item; a join replaces the same join in place or is added; a term replaces the term of the same name (D50).
  • CLI. nl2sql knowledge show, export, sources, with --as (repeatable) and --user; cli/commands/knowledge.py's caller(engine, roles, user) builds the UserContext (P1 and Q1 can reuse it).
  • Init and the demo. nl2sql init writes knowledge.yaml and an empty glossary.yaml; --demo copies the demo glossary. The demo glossary is a canonical YAML file, nl2sql/datasets/glossary.yaml (nl2sql.datasets.DEMO_GLOSSARY_PATH), not a dict in datasets/chinook.py, so demo_config() (and NL2SQL.demo()) can name it with a yaml source; demo_config(glossary=...) overrides it.
  • Drift. DriftImpact.glossary_items and the finder _glossary_items, filtered with visible to the tables the caller reads.
  • After review (#333). sources() shows a reload's error only to a caller who may reload; others get HIDDEN_ERROR. The mention check also reads rule ids and enum codes, and visible(..., also_denied=deny_names(scope)) adds the names a role denies explicitly (a table kept out of the index). The SDK caps names at NAME_MAX_CHARS (255); the yaml source refuses a file over GLOSSARY_MAX_BYTES (5 MB). write_glossary fsyncs, keeps the file's mode and maps a PermissionError to ReviewError(NOT_WRITABLE).

engine.proposals is built; a thumbs-up files a verified_query proposal and an admin's accept writes the glossary or curated.yaml. Exact names, and where the code differs from section 5:

  • Filing. nl2sql/review/queue.py: propose(ctx, proposal) -> Proposal is how every track files a finding (P1, P2, F1, L2 build a Proposal.build(...) and call it). It keeps identity (the same change updates the open row's evidence; an accepted or rejected change is returned as it is and never re-proposed), supersedes the open row of the same kind, datasource and target (the target compared case-insensitively), revives a superseded row proposed again, and publishes proposal.created for a new or revived row only. table_names(ctx, datasource_id, pairs) turns (schema or "", table) pairs into datasource.schema.table, the adapter's default schema filling a blank. propose completes tables with named_tables(ctx, proposal): the table of a table, a column's table, both sides of a join, a term's tables and its columns' tables, and the tables a verified_query's SQL reads. A caller sees a proposal only when their scope reaches all of them, so a track that forgets one cannot leak a denied table; P1, F1 and L2 should still pass tables themselves.
  • Visibility and deciding. visible(ctx, user, proposal): the caller's Scope must reach the datasource and every name in tables (no text mention check, unlike K1's knowledge filter). caller(value) raises TypeError for anything but a UserContext; require_admin(ctx, by) raises ReviewError(NOT_AUTHORIZED). Under allow_all every caller may decide, as K1's reload does: there are no roles to hold. who(by) is what decided_by records: the user id, else the roles.
  • Accept. nl2sql/review/accept.py: accept(ctx, ids, by, edits) and reject(ctx, reasons, by) (reasons maps id to reason). Unknown or decided ids are named in AcceptReport.refused by accept; reject refuses the whole call with ReviewError(NOT_FOUND). Every lock (accept:<real path>, LOCK_TTL_S 60; a caller waits up to LOCK_WAIT_S 10 s for another) is taken and every file's hash checked before the first write. Each file's items are decided (stored, decide_proposal, proposal.decided) under the locks right after that file's write, and every item is re-read as still proposed under the locks; reject takes the same locks. So an id is accepted once, and a failed second write leaves the first file's items accepted and the second's proposed. apply passes replace=True: the file's change replaces the stored one. A per-item failure (the glossary's validation, the curated checks, a verified query id already taken) leaves that item proposed in refused. files_written and wrote are paths relative to the folder of nl2sql.yaml. The accepted row keeps its id and stores the change as accepted (edits included).
  • The curated file. nl2sql/review/curated_file.py: curated_path(config) (None when inline, absent or built in code), file_sha256, canonical_curated(curated), write_curated(path, curated, expected_sha256) -> str and loaded_sha256(config). Runtime.curated_sha256 is taken in components(): the file is read once, hashed and parsed, and when the parse is not config.curated (an edit after the config was loaded) the hash is STALE, so accept refuses with FILE_CHANGED; Runtime.replace_curated(curated, *, sha256) swaps config.curated, curated and the hash under the lock. The refresh runs rebuild_index(ctx, datasource_ids=..., refresh=True) (the index lock, IndexingOrchestrator.refresh, which section 5 names directly); a datasource that cannot be refreshed is a warning, not a failure. K3 renamed that call, in _refreshed() in review/accept.py.
  • The review file. nl2sql/review/review_file.py: render(proposals) and read(path) -> ReviewFile (ReviewItem: id, decision, reason, change; other keys ignored). apply merges an edited change over the stored one and rejects with each item's own reason, so it is one accept call and per-item rejections rather than one reject call. AcceptReport.rejected is new: the proposals apply rejected. export refuses nl2sql.yaml, its section files and knowledge source files.
  • Thumbs-up. feedback/proposals.py is skip_reason(row) and verified_query(row) (the change); FeedbackAPI.record files it with origin thumbs_up, tables from inspect_verified_sql, and evidence {trace_id, role}. SQL that is not one read-only query files nothing. build_proposals, render_proposals, write_proposals and nl2sql curated proposals export are deleted.
  • Retention, events, CLI. engine.storage.purge() returns proposals (decided rows past settings.review.max_age_days). proposal.decided is published per decision (the audit set was B0's). nl2sql review list, show, accept, reject, export, apply, with --as and --user through K1's caller. engine.proposals.current(id, *, user_context) is new (a read method, so it takes the caller): what the proposal would replace, through current_value in review/queue.py; a curated query whose SQL reads a table outside the caller's scope is None. review show prints it. A thumbs-up whose proposal cannot be filed is logged; feedback.record still returns the stored rating.
  • Tests. tests/unit/test_review_queue.py (every Q1 test the row names, and the CLI); test_only_accept_writes_a_persons_file in tests/architecture/test_boundaries.py, which also lists review/queue.py among the access decisions that ask a Scope.

Built: knowledge in the prompts (K2)

Knowledge reaches the planner's and the refiner's prompts; the index is K3's. Exact names, and where the code differs from this page:

  • Matching and rendering. nl2sql/knowledge/match.py: match_terms(terms, texts, *, sources, top_k) -> List[TermMatch] (NAME_SCORE 1.0, SYNONYM_SCORE 0.9, normalize(text)) and rules_for(rules, tables, snapshot, *, sources) -> List[RuleUse]. nl2sql/knowledge/render.py: render_business_context(terms, rules) -> str, fit_business_context(terms, rules, *, max_chars) -> (terms, rules, dropped) (the cut is its own function, so rendering stays pure) and business_context_of(state), which the planner and the refiner both call. The block carries a term's term, definition, columns and tables (no synonyms, as the example above), a rule's id and text; an empty list is left out.
  • The retriever. schema_knowledge(knowledge, datasource_id, snapshot, scope, dialect) -> SchemaKnowledge (in schema_retriever/node.py) filters with K1's visible(..., deny_names(scope)) and resolves descriptions, roles, units, grains, values and glossary joins per snapshot table key; _build_tables_from_snapshot(..., knowledge=) puts them on Table and Column (extra fields role, unit, grain, values; a relationship gains "source": "glossary"). A database comment that mentions a denied table is dropped too, as show drops it. resolve_join(join, snapshot, *, dialect) was added to K1's resolve.py (a join is used only when problems would not report it). knowledge_used is None when no term or rule matched, and for a pinned plan. The denied-name pattern is built once per sub-query (denied_pattern, mentions in knowledge/scope.py) and only readable tables' comments are checked.
  • The planner. The chain's structured output is PlannerAnswer; each alternative passes plan.after in checked_alternatives(state, alternatives). ASTPlannerResponse.alternatives_offered (added here, after L1's review) keeps every alternative the answer carried, before plan.after or any filter; the no-cache rule (D47) in graph_utils reads it, with alternatives and ambiguous_phrase, so a plan whose readings were all dropped for one caller is still never cached. It carries over to a retry, so an ambiguity an earlier attempt flagged is never forgotten. It is the canonical field; L1 (#339) rebases onto it.
  • knowledge.used is published by the planner, once per sub-query, on the first prompt that carries the block, not by the retriever: a plan-cache hit sends no prompt, publishes nothing, and its SubQueryResult.knowledge_used is None. JSON blocks escape U+2028, U+2029 and U+0085 (one_line in knowledge/render.py).
  • The cache. PlanCache(..., knowledge=) appends | knowledge=<Knowledge.digest(datasource_id)> to every key (the digest of no knowledge when there is none); plan_cache_for(ctx) passes the run's pinned ctx.knowledge.
  • The explanation. caller_knowledge(ctx, state) in nl2sql/knowledge/scope.py is the scope-filtered knowledge, per datasource the run planned on, for X1's result_from_state(..., knowledge=), read from the runtime the run pinned (run_with_graph returns it as state["pinned_runtime"]); QueryAPI.run_query, QueryAPI._stream, evaluation/run.py, tracing/replay.py and tracing/trace.py pass it.
  • Fakes and the recording. nl2sql.testing.fake_llm.as_planner_answer wraps a bare plan as {"plan": ...} for a PlannerAnswer rule; the gold plan fake answers {"plan": ...} itself. The demo recording was converted by the one-off script (17 entries), which was not committed.

The demo recording. K2 changes the planner's structured output from PlanModel to PlannerAnswer, and the replay provider keys on the structured output's name. K2 converts cli/demo/recordings/chinook.json mechanically, with a one-off script: each PlanModel entry is renamed PlannerAnswer and its payload wrapped as {"plan": <payload>}. No model is called, no key is spent, and every replayed answer is byte-identical to today's, which test_converted_recording_replays_every_guided_question holds.

Built: knowledge in the index (K3)

  • The entries. SchemaChunkBuilder(ds_id, snapshot, schema_version, questions, knowledge=None, dialect=None) (indexing/chunk_builder.py) takes the datasource's merged DatasourceKnowledge. A table or column description is the glossary's, else the snapshot's (the database's comment); a column's synonyms are the database's then the glossary's, and it gains ColumnChunk.role (a Role: line) only when the glossary sets one, so a role derived from the schema is not written to an entry. A glossary join that resolve_join accepts is a RelationshipChunk with origin="glossary" and its cardinality (RelationshipChunk.origin is "database" for a foreign key; id schema.relationship:<from>-><to>:glossary:<columns>:<version>). TermChunk (knowledge.term, id knowledge.term:<datasource>:<12 hex of the lower-cased term>:<version>) holds the term, its synonyms and its definition. The glossary's examples are appended to the datasource's sample_questions for build_example_chunks. A name that does not resolve is left out of the entries, as show reports it.
  • Term similarity. Retriever.retrieve_term_candidates(query, datasource_id, k, terms=None) -> list[TermCandidate] (TERM_TYPE in indexing/retrieval.py; TermCandidate(datasource_id, term, score) in indexing/models.py) is a plain similarity search over the live build, and embeds nothing when the datasource has no term entry. match_terms(terms, texts, *, sources, top_k, similar=None, floor=0.6) adds a term whose similarity reaches floor (settings.knowledge.match_floor), scoring that similarity; a lexical match keeps its 1.0 or 0.9. The schema retriever (_similar_terms) asks the search with the sub-query's intent only when the caller sees a term, restricts it to the term names the caller's scope shows (terms=, so hidden terms cannot crowd a visible one out of the top k), and keeps the lexical match when the search fails or the store has no such method.
  • Refresh. IndexingOrchestrator(ctx) (no enrich) has refresh(datasource_id) in place of refresh_curated: it renders every entry from the live build's stored snapshot (LookupError when there is none, naming nl2sql index --datasource), the current curated section and the current knowledge, keeps the stored entry whose id, text and metadata are unchanged, embeds the rest, and commits with curated_hash and knowledge_hash. rebuild_index(ctx, datasource_ids=None, on_progress=None, on_datasource=None, refresh=False); IndexAPI.build(datasource_ids=None, *, on_progress, on_datasource) and IndexAPI.refresh(datasource_ids=None, *, on_progress, on_datasource) (both return a RebuildResult); run_indexing(engine, datasource_ids=None, refresh=False); nl2sql index --refresh. --enrich and --curated-only are gone (a usage error); ENTRY_TYPES gains knowledge.term. review/accept.py refreshes with rebuild_index(..., refresh=True).
  • Health. index_health(..., knowledge_digests=None) compares each datasource's BuildPointer.knowledge_hash (a build made before K3 counts as the digest of no knowledge) with the live Knowledge.digest; a difference is a problem, so the status is stale: "The glossary changed for '' since it was indexed; run nl2sql index --refresh --datasource <id>." IndexAPI.health passes the runtime's digests. The curated.yaml warning now names --refresh.
  • B31, and what P2 uses. The orchestrator never touches a model, so a snapshot holds only the database's text. nl2sql/profiler/drafts.py holds what was moved from the deleted indexing/enrichment_service.py, unchanged: ENRICHMENT_LLM_NAME ("profiler"), DatasourceEnrichment, TableEnrichment, ColumnEnrichment, SchemaEnrichment, ENRICHMENT_PROMPT, build_evidence(snapshot, datasource_description, existing_questions), sanitize_enrichment(snapshot, enrichment, max_questions=100) and their private helpers. apply_enrichment and enrich_schema_snapshot were deleted, not moved: they wrote a model's text into a snapshot and call the model with no budget. P2 wires the moved functions into profile(draft=True).
  • The playground. Its Rebuild no longer takes enrich (POST /api/index/rebuild has no body; rebuild.enrich_available and enrich_reason are gone from GET /api/index), and the checkbox is out of web/playground/src. The committed bundle cli/demo/playground/static/index.html was not rebuilt: until npm run build is run in web/playground, its checkbox is disabled and does nothing.
  • Tests. tests/unit/test_index_knowledge.py (every K3 test the row names except the node-level one, and test_a_glossary_join_that_does_not_resolve_is_not_indexed, test_refresh_swaps_the_curated_entries, test_the_cli_has_refresh_and_not_enrich_or_curated_only); test_terms_are_matched_by_similarity_through_the_index, test_similarity_never_brings_in_a_term_the_caller_may_not_see and test_a_failing_term_search_leaves_the_lexical_match in tests/unit/knowledge/test_knowledge_in_prompts.py; tests/unit/test_profiler_drafts.py (the moved sanitizer). The enrichment tests are deleted with the code.

    • Built (follow-up K3b): the inspector is scoped by caller

    Origin: finding 4 of the K3 review. engine.index.inspect(..., *, user_context) now takes the caller as a required keyword (D60): no default, a missing one is a TypeError. Its pool holds only what the caller's scope reaches, from the same policy_engine.scope the query path reads, and the same visibility engine.knowledge.show applies; there is no second scope implementation.

    • Rules, per hit, in IndexAPI._reachable: a datasource the caller does not reach, or that has no snapshot, shows nothing; a schema.table or schema.column entry needs its table allowed, a schema.relationship both ends; a knowledge.term needs the term to be in knowledge.scope.visible(...) (so a term on a denied table is hidden); datasource, example and metric entries pass; any other type (curated.verified_query) is not shown. Last, an entry whose text names a denied table (knowledge.scope.mentions) is dropped, so a table entry whose glossary description names a denied table is hidden whole, though show would hide only the description.
    • Recall. The store cannot filter by an allowed set per datasource, so Retriever.mmr(..., allow=) asks for SCOPE_OVERFETCH (4) times the candidates, keeps the first fetch_k allowed ones, then runs MMR. A caller for whom most matches are hidden can still get a short pool; one for whom few are hidden gets a full one.
    • The playground. RetrievalRequest.role is required (no default view, as /api/schema, D33: a request without it is a 422), and /api/retrieval searches as UserContext(roles=[role]); Retrieval.jsx sends the role chosen in "Ask as", and the committed bundle is rebuilt. The playground trusts the role the page sends (see the security model), as the Ask page does.
    • Tests. tests/unit/test_index_inspect_scope.py (denied tables, hidden terms, relationships needing both ends, verified queries never shown, an unindexed datasource, the over-fetch at Retriever level) and test_a_search_is_made_as_the_role_asked_and_shows_only_what_it_may_read in tests/unit/test_playground_retrieval.py.

    The waves, with at most four PRs at once:

    Wave PRs Notes 1 B0 Alone and small; everything else branches from it 2 K1, Q1, X1, C1 The four tracks start. K1 merges before Q1 (both edit runtime.py). 3 K2, P1, L1, F1 F1 needs only Q1; it merges after Q1 (both edit api/feedback_api.py, one wave apart). 4 K3, C2, L2 5 P2 Then release 0.8

    Known overlaps, with their merge order: runtime.py (K1, then Q1 in wave 2; C2 in wave 4), api/query_api.py (X1, L1, L2: one track, in order), api/knowledge_api.py (K1, P1, L2: each fills its own methods of B0's class, in wave order), ast_planner/node.py (K2 in wave 3, then L2 in wave 4), nl2sql/knowledge/match.py (K2, then K3), cli/main.py (P1's --profile in wave 3, K3's --refresh in wave 4), observers/audit.py (Q1, then C2), review/accept.py (Q1, then K3's rename), and the boundary test's constant lists.

docs.title: 17. Release 0.8
docs.text:
• release-please opens the release PR as usual. Releasing is the owner's act (see Releasing); no agent merges it.
  • docs/releases/0.8.0.md is written with the release-notes process. Its breaking-changes table covers: the knowledge section and glossary.yaml; the indexing_enrichment agent renamed profiler; nl2sql index --enrich replaced by nl2sql profile --draft, and --curated-only by --refresh (with index.build(curated_only=...) by index.refresh()); model-written descriptions no longer in snapshots or prompts until accepted; nl2sql curated proposals export replaced by the review queue; the new needs_clarification status and QueryResult.clarification and explanation; the planner's structured output (PlannerAnswer); the required caller on the new read methods; the store interface version 3; the plan cache keyed on the glossary (cached plans miss once); and the new knowledge.term entries (run nl2sql index after upgrading).
  • Before tagging, the CI gates are green, the realdb workflow is run on demand on main (the estimates and the profiler's Pagila test), and the owner runs nl2sql eval run --mode full on Chinook, routing and clarify with a key, once, and publishes the record.

docs.title: 18. Open questions
docs.text:
None blocking. Every decision above was made overnight and is marked for the owner to confirm. The ones that most change the shape of the work, if the owner decides otherwise:

  • D42 for curated.yaml. Accept rewrites curated.yaml canonically, which drops the comments people write beside their SQL. The alternative is accept-by-export for verified queries only: the engine writes a file a person merges by hand, as curated proposals export does today, keeping curated.yaml entirely hand-written at the cost of a step after every accept. The glossary, which the engine owns more naturally, is unaffected.
  • D38, nothing generated is used until accepted. The alternative (used at the lowest precedence while proposed) helps a database without comments at once, but needs the queue to feed the knowledge merge and its digest. Batch accept (D61) is how 0.8 covers that case instead.
  • D47, one sub-query only. Clarifying a multi-part question needs the re-ask to pin the whole decomposition, which is Wave C's session state.

docs.title: Wave C: conversation, charts, dashboards, launchpad and MCP over HTTP (design)
docs.text:
Status: design

This page is the design for Wave C of the product redesign, which ships as release 0.9. Nothing on it is built yet. Each pull request in the PR plan adds a "Built" note to the sections it builds, as Phase 1 and Phase 2 did. Phase 1 is Configuration v2 and the extension registry; Phase 2 is Phase 2: test bed, storage, providers, policies and adapter SDK v2. Wave A (0.7: events, observers, hooks, approval, evals, routing, drift, sanity checks, MCP over stdio) and Wave B (0.8: glossary and knowledge sources, the review queue, the schema profiler, clarifications, "why this answer", the cost guard, corrections) are designed on their own pages, architecture/wave_a.md and architecture/wave_b.md, which were not merged when this page was written. Wave C uses the names and shapes those pages give, and lists what it needs from them that they do not yet say in Needs from Waves A and B, rather than redesigning them.

The owner reviewed this design on 2026-10-28. Most decisions are confirmed; chat, dashboards, refresh and access were revised. See Decisions.

docs.title: Principles
docs.text:
The owner set them for the redesign, and they rank above everything below:

  • The package is the product; the playground only demonstrates it. Every capability on this page is a public facade method or an extension point in nl2sql first. The CLI, nl2sql-api, the playground and the MCP server use the public API only. The web UI for conversations, charts and dashboards is Wave D, not here.
  • No active users: design it correctly, not compatibly. No shims, no aliases, no deprecation paths.
  • Never over-engineer. Ship what 0.9 needs; the cut list is part of the design.
  • Configurable in nl2sql.yaml (and its section files) or in code with dependency injection, extensible through the registry, every new action published on the Wave A event bus, and hooks apply to every run this wave adds: a conversation turn, a dashboard tile.

Three older rules decide most of this wave: the model emits a typed plan, never SQL (dashboards build plans in code, and the model never writes a chart); anything the generator can reject, the validator rejects first (a dashboard filter is a predicate added to a plan before the validator, not text added to SQL); and Wave B's Only an Accept Writes a Person's File, which this wave amends, explicitly and narrowly, for the setup workflow (D123).

docs.title: Prior art (unverified, from memory)
docs.text: ChatGPT and Claude let the model decide to chart or to open an artifact, but those artifacts are snapshots. Hex, Databricks Genie and Snowflake show the SQL and lean on trusted example queries. ThoughtSpot, Power BI and WrenAI pin answers to dashboards that re-run the stored query rather than re-asking the question. Tableau Pulse follows metrics. The known complaints are definition drift between chats, silent wrong answers and stale saved charts. This design keeps the typed plan, not the question, so a saved chart cannot drift, and the model never writes SQL, so an answer cannot be silently wrong in a way the validator would not catch. None of this was checked against the products' current documentation.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
The owner was asleep when this design was written and asked that its recommendations be used. On 2026-10-28 the owner reviewed it. Most decisions are confirmed as written. Chat, dashboards, refresh and access were revised: those rows say "revised 2026-10-28 (owner)" and carry the new text. D131 to D135 are new. Wave A uses D9 to D35 and Wave B D36 to D59, so Wave C starts at D100. After an independent review, several were amended earlier; the text shows the amended version. Each decision is written into the section it affects. A builder's call is a choice the owner left to the design; each is marked so and listed under Open questions.

# Decision Status Where D100 engine.conversations is a namespace over ids, not a live session object. A conversation is stored data; every call names it, so the CLI, nl2sql-api, MCP and a Python caller use it the same way, and a server holds nothing between requests. confirmed 2026-10-28 Conversation D101 The model leads the conversation; there is no separate rewrite call. A turn is a bounded loop (D108). The model reads the conversation and, to ask the database, calls the ask tool with a standalone question: that is the rewrite, folded into the loop. A choice from a clarification, a retry and a tool called by name make no model call. The agent is conversation (replacing conversation_rewriter), with the typed output ModelStep. Builder's call: a separate rewrite call would add a second model call to every follow-up and decide nothing the loop's first call cannot; the simplest correct design folds it in. revised 2026-10-28 (owner) The model-led turn D102 The question the model passes to ask is what runs, through run_query, unchanged; the pipeline never sees the conversation. Two conversations that arrive at the same question get the same decomposition, so they share the plan cache as any two askers do (its key is the sub-query's intent, the schema version and the knowledge digest). revised 2026-10-28 (owner) The model-led turn D103 The model sees the last context_turns (3) turns as one JSON block of conversation history, never as instructions: what was typed, each step's tool and arguments, the question that ran, its status, the answer's summary, the result's columns and the tables read, and the model's reply. Result rows are never sent; the summary may quote values from them, as the user already read it. The enabled tools' names, descriptions and argument schemas travel in the same block. revised 2026-10-28 (owner) The model-led turn D104 A Wave B clarification is a step with status needs_clarification, and it ends the turn. The result reaches the model as the tool result, but the model cannot answer for the user. The next turn may name an option (choice=) or be text the model maps to one by calling ask with choice; a choice re-asks with run_query(pending.question, choice=ClarificationChoice(request=pending, option_id=...)). CLARIFICATION_STALE ends that turn error and clears the pending request. revised 2026-10-28 (owner) Clarifications and approvals D105 A conversation belongs to the (tenant_id, user_id) that started it, and every method requires the caller (user_context, keyword, no default). Roles are never stored: each turn runs with the roles the caller passes now. Another user's conversation is "not found". Callers with no user_id share one "no user" owner, which suits a single-user tool only; nl2sql-api must set a user_id before Wave D exposes conversations. confirmed 2026-10-28 Ownership D106 Turns are stored without rows, in the state store, for 30 days by default (conversations.max_age_days), purged by engine.storage.purge(). Rows are read from the result store by trace_id while its own retention keeps them. confirmed 2026-10-28 Ownership D107 A needs_approval step ends the turn and is answered by retry, which re-runs the turn's ask question with the Approvals the asker was given; Wave A's re-run then pins the approved plan. The model never approves. No model call; nothing is stored. revised 2026-10-28 (owner) Clarifications and approvals D108 The model chooses tools in a bounded loop. Like ChatGPT or Claude, the model reads the conversation and decides what to call, after each result. The tools are ask the database (ask), chart, diagram, report, and build or edit a dashboard. The model may also offer a tool in its reply ("want a chart of this?"), as typed offers a client can run in one click. The loop is bounded by conversations.max_tool_calls (12 by default; builder's call: a six-chart dashboard takes six ask calls, one edit and a pin) and ends when the model replies, when a step ends in a clarification, an approval or a stop, or at the bound, after which the model makes one last call with the tools off and must reply. The model still never writes SQL: ask takes a question and goes through the typed plan and the validator unchanged, and the Wave B cost rule applies to every query. chat_tool stays a registry kind, kept tiny. revised 2026-10-28 (owner) Chat tools D109 The registry's tools make no model call, and a tool reaches the engine through the public facade only, as an app does. ask is the conversation's own tool, not a registry tool: it calls run_query, which is where the model is called, as any app would. A tool that puts a chart on a dashboard takes the plan of an earlier ask step by reference, never a question. The runner that builds tools from the config is the conversation's, not the tools'. revised 2026-10-28 (owner) The interface D110 ChartSpec is our own small typed model, with to_vega_lite(). Four kinds: line, bar, big_number, table. Vega-Lite (v5) is the export, not the type. No colour is ever set; the renderer's theme decides. confirmed 2026-10-28 The spec D111 The chart is chosen by rules, from the columns' kinds and the plan, with no model call. The one-line takeaway is a template filled from the data; a model-written takeaway is not offered. confirmed 2026-10-28 Choosing a chart D112 ResultSummary gains column_kinds (number, text, temporal, boolean, other: Wave A's D30 categories), read from the saved result's schema when it is written. The plan refines them only when the run had one sub-query. confirmed 2026-10-28 Choosing a chart D113 Diagrams are Mermaid text with no colour and no %%{init} line. The answer view is drawn from the plans; the schema view is an erDiagram from the snapshot's foreign keys, filtered by the caller's scope (caller required) and capped at 30 tables. confirmed 2026-10-28 Diagrams D114 A report is Markdown assembled from stored turns, with no model call. PDF is out of scope. confirmed 2026-10-28 Reports D115 Fixed dashboard templates stay as the no-model starter dashboard (dashboards.generate, used by nl2sql launch, D124). They work over column roles that the dashboard computes itself: Wave B's role rules (its derived roles and its proposed heuristics) run over the live snapshot, overridden by roles accepted into the glossary; an unaccepted heuristic only picks charts and never reaches a model. Each template carries its own question text and builds a typed plan in code; generating one needs an index, not a profile, and makes no model call. A generated dashboard is an ordinary dashboard: stored plans, workspaces, manual and chat edits. A dashboard a person asks for in chat is built by the model from ask steps (D116), not from templates. revised 2026-10-28 (owner) Choosing the tiles D116 A dashboard is an artifact, saved whole. The model builds it beside the chat as a draft and keeps editing it through the chat. The user pins (saves) the whole dashboard; a single tile is never pinned. Each chart stores the full typed plan that produced it: the run's decomposition (the whole decomposition, combine groups included, plus a plan per sub-query), or a verified query with its params. Several sub-queries are allowed. A refresh re-runs the stored plans through run_query(plan=SuppliedPlan(...)), Wave A's pinned-plan path made public (a need from Wave A). A chart whose plan no longer validates (the schema changed) shows needs_fixing while the others keep working. Fixing it in chat is the only thing that spends tokens. revised 2026-10-28 (owner) Dashboards D117 A dashboard filter is a typed predicate added to each of a chart's stored plans before the validator, applied to the queries that read the filtered table. Values are checked against the column's type category before the plan is built, because the validator does not type-check literals. confirmed 2026-10-28 Filters D118 A dashboard is private to its owner in 0.9, and lives in one of the owner's workspaces. Every run follows the one access rule (D135). Sharing between users waits for the shared workspace (see Later). revised 2026-10-28 (owner) Workspaces and ownership D119 run_query gains answer: bool = True; False skips the answer synthesizer. Refresh uses it: a chart shows a chart, not a paragraph. confirmed 2026-10-28 Refresh and stored results D120 scan() looks in three places, each declared by the adapters: a connection URL the caller passes (nl2sql launch passes DATABASE_URL), database files under the folder by the suffixes adapters declare (two levels deep), and the default ports adapters declare, on 127.0.0.1 only. Nothing in the engine names a database. confirmed 2026-10-28 Finding a database D121 The Connect routes in 0.9 are datasource-types, datasource/test and the existing POST /datasource. No scan route (the server's files and ports are not the user's) and no profile or review routes (Wave B defers them to Wave D, and a profile of a large schema is a job, not a request). confirmed 2026-10-28 Connect a database over REST D122 No secret value is ever written into YAML. The config writer writes every secret field (a connection's secret fields, an LLM or embeddings api_key, a secret provider's credentials) as ${env:NL2SQL_...} and the value into the .env beside nl2sql.yaml, or refuses. .env is written by nl2sql launch, and by the REST route only on the fresh local install nl2sql-api already treats as admin (no role source, loopback client). confirmed 2026-10-28 Writing the config D123 Three writers join accept in Only an Accept Writes a Person's File: write_project (new files only, refuses to overwrite), engine.datasources.save (one datasource file, refused when it changed since the engine loaded it) and write_env_values (the .env). This overrides Phase 1's and Phase 2's "persisting a change is the calling app's job": the web form, the terminal and launch need the same writer, and the package is the product. confirmed 2026-10-28 Writing the config D124 Starter questions are the dashboard templates' questions (five), printed and filed as review-queue proposals (kind example, a need from Wave B); they reach glossary.yaml's examples, and so routing, only through a person's accept. confirmed 2026-10-28 nl2sql launch D125 nl2sql launch does not verify the model key with a call. The first question the user asks is the check. confirmed 2026-10-28 nl2sql launch D126 MCP over HTTP is nl2sql mcp --http, the MCP SDK's streamable HTTP transport in stateless mode, in its own process, with the caller's identity resolved per request. It is not mounted in nl2sql-api in 0.9. confirmed 2026-10-28 MCP over HTTP D127 Authentication is API keys first (bearer); OAuth later. Keys are made by engine.api_keys (an admin caller required), stored hashed in the state store, and each carries the user_id, tenant_id and roles its holder runs as. Binding to anything but loopback without keys is refused. confirmed 2026-10-28 Authentication D128 The hosted demo does not expose MCP in 0.9. MCP is a delivery channel, like the package and the REST API, not a demo feature. The hosted demo serves recorded answers with no key, so an MCP client could ask nothing new; exposing it waits for OAuth and a decision on whose key pays. confirmed 2026-10-28 MCP over HTTP D129 The first PR adds every Wave C shape at once, and the stubs the tracks share: the five facade namespaces (conversations, chat tools, dashboards, workspaces, API keys), the workspace, dashboard-edit, refresh and schedule models, the dashboard edit tools' entry points, the chat-tool entry points, the keys, launch and dashboards commands, the docs pages in the nav and the boundary test's constants, so the parallel PRs touch different files. revised 2026-10-28 (owner) PR plan D130 Every Wave C method that reads or writes something owned, scoped or privileged requires the caller (user_context, or by for a writer), keyword-only with no default, and fails closed: the conversations, workspaces, dashboards (edits, refresh and schedule included) and API-key methods, datasources.diagram, datasources.save and dashboards.suggest_questions. Three methods take no caller: dashboards.run_scheduled, which runs each dashboard as its stored owner (D134); api_keys.verify, a lookup by token that has no caller yet; and chat_tools.list, a list of public tool names. The CLI builds an explicit context (--as ROLE), as Wave B's nl2sql review does. revised 2026-10-28 (owner) Every section D131 Workspaces are named, local groups that categorise dashboards ("Sales", "Ops"). A dashboard lives in exactly one workspace. A user creates, renames, moves dashboards between, and deletes (when empty) their workspaces. In 0.9 a workspace is private to its owner, as D118 says. new 2026-10-28 (owner) Workspaces and ownership D132 Refresh uses no tokens. It comes in three forms: one chart, the whole dashboard, and a schedule. It re-runs the stored plans with answer=False (D119); there is no model call. The last results are stored with a timestamp, so a dashboard opens instantly and says "refreshed 2 h ago". On open, a chart older than the dashboard's schedule refreshes. The cost rule applies to every refresh. A schedule runs only inside a long-running process (nl2sql-api, or a local app process); with nothing running, nothing refreshes, and laptops accept that. nl2sql dashboards refresh serves cron. The minimum interval is dashboards.min_refresh_minutes (15; builder's call). new 2026-10-28 (owner) Refresh and stored results D133 Manual edits need no model call, and every one has chat parity. Reorder or resize charts, rename the dashboard or a chart, change a chart's type, remove a chart, set filters (D117), set the refresh schedule and move to another workspace are public facade methods. The model calls the same edits through the dashboard_edit tool. Changing what data a chart shows (a new question or plan) goes only through chat. new 2026-10-28 (owner) Manual edits and chat parity D134 A scheduled refresh runs as the dashboard's owner, from a saved snapshot of the owner's user_context. Builder's call, resolving D105's "roles are never stored": the snapshot is saved only when a person sets a schedule, lives on the schedule (never on a conversation or a chart), is checked against the current configuration and policies on every run, and expires after dashboards.schedule_identity_max_age_days (30), so a role removed in the identity provider does not outlive it by long. When any check fails or the snapshot expires, the schedule stops with a visible error until its owner sets it again, which saves a fresh snapshot. new 2026-10-28 (owner) Schedules D135 One access rule everywhere. A datasource's stored connection sets the most anyone can see through it; the person's roles and policies (Wave B) narrow that. Chat, dashboard open, manual refresh, scheduled refresh, MCP and REST take the same path and the same checks. Nothing, stored results included, gets a side door. new 2026-10-28 (owner) One access rule

docs.title: What ships in 0.9
docs.text:
Wave C is package first: it ships the engine, the facade, MCP, the CLI and the REST routes listed below. The playground UI for chat and dashboards is Wave D.

Goal What it means Conversation engine.conversations: start, ask, stream, retry, tool, report, get, list, delete. The model leads: it reads the conversation and calls tools (ask the database, chart, diagram, report, build or edit a dashboard) in a loop bounded by max_tool_calls. It never writes SQL; ask runs the question through the typed plan and the validator unchanged. Every turn keeps what was typed, each step, the result and its trace_id. Clarifications and approvals end the turn. Stored per user with retention. Chat tools A small chat_tool registry kind and five built-ins: chart, diagram, report, dashboard_edit, dashboard_pin, plus the conversation's own ask. The model chooses within the bound and may offer one; a client can also call one by name. Auto charts engine.results.chart(...) returns a renderer-neutral ChartSpec (line, bar, big number, table) chosen by rules, with a template takeaway and a Vega-Lite export. Dashboards Artifacts: the model builds a whole dashboard beside the chat, edits it through the chat, and the user pins it whole. Each chart stores the typed plan that produced it. Workspaces group them. Manual edits (arrange, rename, chart type, remove, filters, schedule) need no model call and have chat parity. Refresh (a chart, the dashboard, a schedule) re-runs stored plans with no tokens and keeps the last results. A no-model starter dashboard comes from fixed templates. Launchpad nl2sql launch (and uvx --from nl2sql-engine nl2sql launch): find a database, test it, write the config, set the model key, index, profile and review, five starter questions. Every step is a package method. Connect a database over REST Thin nl2sql-api routes over types() and test(), and a POST /datasource that answers a bad body with a 422 and can save. MCP over HTTP nl2sql mcp --http with API-key auth, per-request identity, and follow-ups and clarifications in ask.
