Where the code and the design differ, the code won:

  • revoke of an unknown id raises ValueError (the design says None); revoking a key that is already revoked changes nothing and publishes nothing.
  • list is newest first and includes revoked keys, which nl2sql keys list marks revoked.
  • create retries a clash of ids (the store's add_api_key raises ValueError) with a new id, up to eight times, then raises RuntimeError; it never overwrites. user_id must not be blank.
  • Roles are checked against policies.roles, with no allow_all exemption: keys outlive the policy, so a key minted with roles=["admin"] under allow_all would become a real admin key once roles are configured. Under allow_all a key carries roles=[] (a role name is a ValueError), which reads everything now and nothing once roles are configured. Under allow_all every caller may still manage keys, as for engine.knowledge.reload and the review queue; the CLI leaves out --as and --role there (caller() refuses every role name when none is defined), so --role is optional.
  • A by that is not a UserContext is a TypeError, one without an admin role a PermissionError (the engine's usual pair), not an ErrorCode.
  • verify checks only the key: it does not check that the key's roles are still configured (the policy engine does that on every run).
  • Tests: test_api_keys.py, test_cli_keys.py. The stub tests moved api_keys and the keys commands out of their tables.
  • For M2: call engine.api_keys.verify(token) with the bearer token (the text after Bearer); None is a 401. verify does not say why, and mcp.denied carries a reason (missing, malformed, unknown, revoked). missing is M2's own (no header). To tell the others apart without reaching into the runtime, M2 adds a method to ApiKeysAPI that returns the reason. Constraints: it compares the secret before reporting revoked (right id with a wrong secret is unknown, so an id alone cannot probe a key's state and the audit log never records a forged token as a revoked key); verify becomes a thin wrapper over it, so there is one code path; and nl2sql.policies.keys.parse stays behind ApiKeysAPI, not imported by mcp/http.py. Not built in M1.

  • pin puts a draft in workspace_id if given, else in the workspace the draft already lives in if that is still the caller's, else in "General" (created on first use). The design says "else the default workspace"; that would undo a move of a draft. A saved dashboard or an empty draft is a ValueError.
  • set_tile_chart checks a forced kind against the tile's last stored result through choose(..., kind=), using the column kinds stored with the result (TileRun.column_kinds, empty for a row stored without them, which falls back to the kinds the chart's encodings carry); a tile with no stored result, or a result that has no chart, takes any kind. auto is always accepted. For D2: fill TileRun.column_kinds (from ResultSummary.column_kinds) whenever it stores a result, or a result last drawn as a table cannot be forced to a bar.
  • edit discards the stored results before it saves the dashboard, so a failing store leaves both as they were. It is still a read-modify-write without a lock. For D2: its refresh lock must also cover edit, so a refresh that finishes after a set_filters cannot store results that ignore the new filters.
  • A missing caller (user_context=None) is a TypeError("user_context is required") on every dashboard and workspace method, never an anonymous owner. pin(title=) checks the title like rename: blank is a ValueError.

Where the code and the design differ, the code won:

  • A tool is handed the conversation with the turn in flight appended (its steps so far, status answered), so chart after ask works in one turn. The report tool covers stored turns only: it calls conversations.report, which reads the store, so it cannot include the turn it is called in.
  • The model sees a tool step as output: a chart is {kind, reason, columns}, a diagram is its text, and a markdown or json body (a report, a dashboard change) is not shown, only its kind, title and refs. The chart's takeaway is withheld too (it quotes values). D4 should show the model what it needs of a dashboard through the [CONVERSATION] block, as its row says.
  • conversations.tool validates the arguments before it opens a turn: an invalid call is a ValueError and stores nothing; only an unknown or disabled name is stored, as an UNKNOWN_CHAT_TOOL step. A tool turn's text is the tool's name.
  • A K1 bug fixed here: a run saves its results under the engine's tenant (settings.tenant_id), whoever asked, so the chart tool no longer reads the conversation's or the caller's tenant (it found nothing for a caller with a tenant_id). The report reads the engine's tenant too.
  • Review fixes: a stored tool output holds no rows (D106). A chart output's data.rows is emptied before the step is stored (a client draws again through engine.results.chart), and the report tool stores the report without row tables and chart takeaways (conversations.report(include_rows=False)); asked for directly, the report still reads the rows from engine.results. engine.results does not check the caller (it reads by tenant and trace id); that gap is a separate row.
  • chat_tools: absent means the default tools the registry has, so an engine on Registry.empty() builds. The defaults are ("chart", "report") only: diagram, dashboard_edit and dashboard_pin are still stubs and stay off by default. K2 and D4 each add their own name to DEFAULT_CHAT_TOOLS (conversations/tools.py) and to the docs when they land. A name listed explicitly must be registered; ask and a plugin whose args_model does not forbid extra keys are config errors.
  • user_context=None, or a context with no user_id, is a TypeError in every conversations method (a shared anonymous owner would see everyone's anonymous conversations). TOOL_FAILED shows the model the exception type only; the log has the full error. The report considers every turn and keeps each successful ask step, so an answer in a turn whose later tool failed is still reported.
  • Names later rows use: ChatToolRunner, build_chat_tools, describe (nl2sql.conversations.tools), build_report (nl2sql.conversations.report), Conversations._tool(run, call), runtime.chat_tools, check_call (renamed from _check_call in agent.py).

The waves, with at most four PRs at once:

Wave PRs Notes 1 C0 Alone; everything else branches from it 2 C1, K1, L1, M1 The four tracks start 3 C2, K2, D1, L2 4 D2, M2 5 D3, D4 Both build on D2 6 L3 Needs D3

Files more than one PR touches, all in wave order or in different waves: api/datasource_api.py (K2's diagram in wave 3 and L2's save in wave 3 fill separate stub methods C0 wrote; L1's scan in wave 2), nl2sql/conversations/api.py and agent.py (C1, then C2), nl2sql/dashboards/api.py (D1, D2, then D3), nl2sql/dashboards/edits.py (D1, then D4), api/dashboards_api.py (D1, D2, D3), nl2sql/mcp/server.py (Wave B's L2, then M2). C0's stubs mean no two PRs add to public_api.py, pyproject.toml, cli/main.py, mkdocs.yml, nl2sql/__init__.py or the boundary test's constants.

docs.title: 15. Release 0.9
docs.text:
• release-please opens the release PR as usual. Releasing is the owner's act (see Releasing); no agent merges it.
  • docs/releases/0.9.0.md is written with the release-notes process. Its breaking-changes table covers: the state store's interface version 4 (an 0.8 file is migrated in place by migration 6), ResultSummary.column_kinds, the new conversation agent (a config that pins every agent's model should add it), the MCP ask tool's choice (an option id with conversation_id, replacing {request, option_id}), MCP's build_server(engine, identity), POST /api/v1/datasource answering 422 for a bad body, and init_project writing through write_project (same files).
  • Before tagging, the owner runs nl2sql launch once against the test bed's PostgreSQL with a key, asks three follow-ups through engine.conversations in a short script (the chat UI is Wave D), has the model build a dashboard for Chinook in that conversation, edits and pins it, refreshes it and sets a schedule, and connects one MCP client over HTTP with a key. The results go in the release notes.

docs.title: 16. Open questions
docs.text:
None blocking. The owner reviewed this design on 2026-10-28: every decision not marked revised or new is confirmed as written, D123 and D128 included. The builder's calls below are the choices the owner left to the design; each is flagged in the decision that makes it, and any can be changed before its PR starts.

Builder's call Decision What was picked No separate rewrite call D101 The conversation agent's loop carries the standalone question in ask; the conversation_rewriter agent and the Rewrite type are gone. max_tool_calls default D108 12, not 5: a six-chart dashboard is six ask calls, an edit and a pin. Loop output is a typed ModelStep D101 The loop uses structured() like every agent, not a provider's native tool-calling, so every LLM adapter works the same way. Minimum schedule interval D132 dashboards.min_refresh_minutes, 15. Schedule shape D132 every_minutes, not cron expressions; cron users call nl2sql dashboards refresh --due. Scheduled-refresh identity D134 A snapshot of the owner's user_context saved on the schedule when it is set, checked on every run, expiring after 30 days; a failed check stops the schedule with a visible error. Default workspace D131 "General", created on first pin or generate. SuppliedPlan shape (A1) D116 C0 widens it to a whole run, shaped on PinnedRun: a DecomposerResponse (combine groups included) plus plans, or a verified ref; exactly one. ChartPlan stores the same. QueryResult.decomposition D116 Set on every run with a decomposition, so a stored turn can rebuild the whole run for add_tile. Verified charts D116 Stay in 0.9, through SuppliedPlan's verified form. Approval on refresh D132 refresh(approvals=) only; scheduled runs and open never approve. MCP ask section 9 Calls conversations.ask_only(...), which runs just the ask tool; named apart because conversations.ask is the model-led turn.

The owner's note that Wave C ships "the REST API" is read as the Connect routes and the schedule runner in nl2sql-api; the conversation and dashboard REST routes stay in Wave D (D121), as the first draft had them. wave_d.md designs those routes and needs a pass to match this page (see its note).

docs.title: Wave D: the apps (API v1, web app, Compose, terminal app) (design)
docs.text:
Status: design

This page is the design for Wave D of the product redesign, the last wave, which ships as the release after 0.9. Nothing on it is built yet. Each pull request in the PR plan adds a "Built" note to the sections it builds, as the earlier phases and waves do. Phase 1 is Configuration v2 and the extension registry; Phase 2 is Phase 2: test bed, storage, providers, policies and adapter SDK v2; Wave A (0.7: events, observers, hooks, approval, evals, routing, drift, sanity warnings, MCP over stdio) and Wave B (0.8: glossary and knowledge, the profiler and review queue, clarification, plan-to-English, the cost guard, corrections) are designed on their own pages. Wave C (0.9: conversations and chat tools, ChartSpec, dashboards, the launchpad, API keys, MCP over HTTP) is designed in architecture/wave_c.md, not merged when this page was written; this page follows its amended version. Wave D renders what the three waves build. Where it needs something they do not provide, the gap is listed in Needs from Waves A to C as a facade method, not designed around.

Wave C was revised on 2026-10-28; this page has not been updated to match

Wave C now has a model-led chat (the model calls tools in a bounded loop; conversation.step replaces conversation.rewritten), dashboards that are artifacts pinned whole (several sub-queries per chart; needs_fixing replaces stale; no single-tile pin), workspaces, manual dashboard edits with chat parity, refresh with stored results and schedules, and one access rule for every entry point. Wave D's dashboard and chat routes, its Dashboards and Chat pages, D224 and the job and fixture tables still describe the first draft and need a pass. The rows below that name a changed Wave C item are corrected; the rest are listed here, not rewritten: the Chat tool buttons (Pin becomes pinning the whole dashboard), POST /dashboards/pin and the tile routes, the Dashboards page (workspaces, arrange, edit, schedule, "refreshed 2 h ago", needs_fixing), and the dashboard job.

The owner set them for the redesign, and they rank above everything below:

  • The package is the product; the playground only demonstrates it. The web app talks only to nl2sql-api's public /api/v1 routes. The terminal app talks only to the Python facade. Neither holds feature logic: a chart is chosen by engine.results.chart, a dashboard by engine.dashboards.generate, a follow-up by engine.conversations.ask. Every gap this page found is a facade method plus a route, listed explicitly.
  • No active users: correct, not compatible. Routes are renamed where their names are wrong, the playground's private server is deleted, and nl2sql demo keeps no flag whose behaviour is gone. No aliases.
  • Never over-engineer. One process, one worker, jobs in memory, one Docker image, one Compose service, plain React and plain CSS. The apps expose what Waves A to C build and nothing they cut. The cut list is part of the design.
  • Both apps have a demo mode and a your-data mode. Demo mode is the sample databases with recorded answers and no key; your-data mode is the caller's nl2sql.yaml.
  • The UI must not look AI-generated. The playground's "Porcelain" design system (web/playground/src/styles.css: its tokens, type scale, the run spine, the raised card, the 44px controls) is the baseline for every new page. No component library, no gradient, no icon font.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
The owner was asleep when this design was written and asked that its recommendations be used, each marked for confirmation. Wave A uses D9 to D35, Wave B D36 to D61 and Wave C D100 to D130, so Wave D starts at D200. After an independent review several were amended; those are marked so. The final redesign's decisions D13 to D16 are cited by the brief for this wave; their numbers collide with Wave A's, so this page calls them final-design D13 to D16 and records how each is applied.

# Decision Status Where D200 The apps hold serving state only. nl2sql-api may keep the job queue, hosted-demo limits and sessions; everything a user would call a feature is a facade method. nl2sql_api imports only the top-level nl2sql, and the web app calls only /api/v1 routes listed in the committed openapi.json. Both are tests. decided overnight, owner to confirm Principles, Boundaries D201 One route convention, applied to the old routes too: plural nouns (/datasources, /conversations, /results), ids in the path, an action on a collection or a resource as a verb sub-path (/proposals/accept), long work as POST /jobs/{kind}. /datasource, /index/{id}, /index-all, /index/status, /llm/{agent} and /query/{request_id}/results/... are renamed or folded with no alias. decided overnight, amended after review, owner to confirm Conventions D202 One error envelope, and only the facade's own exceptions are mapped. {"error": {"code", "message", "fix", "details"}} for every non-2xx response. The facade's named exceptions share one base, nl2sql.NL2SQLError (code, message, fix, status); the API maps that base and nothing else. Any other exception, a built-in ValueError, KeyError or PermissionError included, is a 500 naming a request id, never its text. A pipeline outcome stays a 200 with the QueryResult. decided overnight, amended after review, owner to confirm Errors D203 Every request resolves one full UserContext (user_id, tenant_id, roles) from one configured source, api.auth: api_keys (Wave C's bearer keys), proxy (user, tenant and role headers, trusted only from proxy.trusted_from), static (one role) or none. Anonymous browser sessions exist only inside serve --demo --hosted, never as a config value. trust_body_role, role_header and role are deleted. decided overnight, amended after review, owner to confirm Identity D204 Results and traces are bound to the user who asked (bug B13) in the engine. A run records its asker's (tenant_id, user_id); results.* and traces.get with a user_context answer only that asker, and another user's run is "not found". user_context=None is the trusted in-process operator, as Wave A's D24 and Wave C's keys treat it, so nl2sql trace reads any run. The API, MCP and the terminal app always pass the caller, which a boundary test checks. Every new method this wave adds requires the caller and fails closed (Wave C's D130). decided overnight, amended after review, owner to confirm Results bound to the user D205 Final-design D15, applied safely: with api.auth: none, nl2sql-api refuses to start unless it binds a loopback host, as Wave C's MCP does without keys. It then answers only requests whose Host is localhost, 127.0.0.1 or [::1] (with its port) and refuses any request carrying Forwarded or X-Forwarded-For, so neither a same-host proxy nor a DNS-rebinding page passes for the operator. Such a request is the local operator, with the admin roles. Compose ships with auth: api_keys. decided overnight, amended after review, owner to confirm Identity D206 Jobs run in process, on one worker thread, in memory. A job is one facade call (index, profile, eval, dashboard) with a progress callback; jobs run one at a time in submission order; each caller has at most one job queued or running; the last 100 are kept and lost on restart. nl2sql-api runs one Uvicorn worker. The durable queue is cut. decided overnight, amended after review, owner to confirm Jobs D207 Server-Sent Events carry Wave A's Event as is (event.sse()), through one helper that closes the facade's iterator when the client goes away (and cancels the token where the method takes one), with a heartbeat every 15 seconds. A job's event stream is an async generator, so a waiting browser holds no worker thread. decided overnight, amended after review, owner to confirm Streams D208 /ready is real, and its rule is the engine's: CheckReport.ready(keys_optional=) decides (every required datasource ready, every key resolves unless keys are optional, the index ok or stale). /ready answers status only to an anonymous caller and the report to an admin. The API now starts with a failed required datasource and reports not ready, instead of refusing to start. decided overnight, amended after review, owner to confirm Health and readiness D209 The replay provider is an LLM provider, provider: replay, answering through the normal LLM interface from a recordings file; a question it has no recording for ends with the error code REPLAY_MISS. The demo's local fake HTTP server and its error-string matching leave the demo path. nl2sql demo --record is removed; recording is scripts/record_demo_answers.py, run by the owner. decided overnight, owner to confirm The replay provider D210 A key typed into the web app stays in the browser tab and travels with each request as a per-call LLMOverride (llm_override= on the facade), in every mode. The web app never writes a key to disk. A model the caller chooses runs only on a key the caller sent: X-NL2SQL-Models is honoured only for providers the same request carries a key for, so a caller can never move a step onto the operator's account. Callers may bring a key only where api.request_llm: true; the demo sets it, the default is off. decided overnight, amended after review, owner to confirm Keys and models D211 Final-design D13, applied with one change. The web app ships inside nl2sql-api as package data, served by nl2sql-api serve. It adds no dependency to nl2sql-api, so there is no web extra there; instead the engine's demo extra becomes nl2sql-api, so pip install "nl2sql-engine[demo]" stays the one install line. nl2sql demo is a launcher that runs python -m nl2sql_api serve --demo in a child process; the engine never imports nl2sql_api. The playground server (nl2sql/cli/demo/) is deleted. decided overnight, amended after review, owner to confirm Serving D212 Final-design D14, applied through Wave C's writer: Connect's Save calls Wave C's datasources.save(id, *, by, env_file), which writes datasources/<id>.yaml, with env_file true only for the fresh local install (Wave C's D122). No second save target, no overlay, no new switch. Saving is admin work, so it is off on the hosted demo; where the config is mounted read-only (Docker), save fails with its own message and the datasource stays registered in memory until restart, which the page says. decided overnight, amended after review, owner to confirm Saving a datasource D213 Final-design D16, applied: one Docker image, nl2sql-api, with all five adapters and Microsoft's ODBC driver for SQL Server. The driver and unixODBC are small beside the ONNX runtime and Chroma the image already carries, so slim and full images are not worth two tags. CI builds and tests linux/amd64; arm64 is published only once K1 has checked that msodbcsql18 exists for Debian 12 on arm64. The image job records the size; a split is reconsidered only if the ODBC layers pass 15% of it. decided overnight, amended after review, owner to confirm Docker image D214 Charts are drawn by our own SVG renderer from ChartSpec (four kinds), in Porcelain's tokens; Vega is not bundled, and the Vega-Lite export is a download. Mermaid is loaded on the first diagram as its own chunk (about 2 to 3 MB of the nl2sql-api wheel, recorded by the web job). The single-file build is dropped. decided overnight, amended after review, owner to confirm Charts and diagrams D215 Approval grants are stored by the engine (engine.approvals), amending Wave A's D10 and D24 and Wave C's D107. Over HTTP the approver and the asker are two callers at different times: the asker cannot prove a grant, and the approver must not run the question as the asker, so the approver grants a request by id and the asker's re-run names the id. A grant is reusable until it expires (24 hours), as an Approval is. decided overnight, amended after review, owner to confirm Approvals D216 One React app, in web/app (renamed from web/playground): the existing Vite and React 18 setup, a hash router, plain JavaScript, Porcelain's CSS split per area, the API client split per area. No TypeScript, no state library, no component library. decided overnight, amended after review, owner to confirm The web app D217 Web tests stay what they are, run in CI, and read real shapes: node --test over pure modules, a contract test that every route the client calls is in openapi.json, and golden response files (web/app/src/api/fixtures/*.json) written by the API's route tests and checked like openapi.json, which the node tests read instead of hand-made objects. No browser test runs in CI; the owner runs a short browser pass before the release. decided overnight, amended after review, owner to confirm Testing D218 The terminal app is nl2sql chat, on Textual behind the tui extra, in nl2sql/cli/chat/, on the facade only. Charts become text (a big number, sparklines, bars, a table); diagrams are shown as text. It takes no key: the CLI's environment and .env as everywhere. decided overnight, owner to confirm The terminal app D219 Compose is one service: api (one Uvicorn worker), one data volume, auth: api_keys, a healthcheck on /api/v1/ready. It starts not ready until indexed; /ready says why, and indexing is one command, docker compose run --rm api nl2sql index, so nothing re-indexes on every up. decided overnight, amended after review, owner to confirm Compose D220 Not in nl2sql-api: MCP (Wave C's D126 stands: its own process), the operator event stream (observers are the operator's surface) and a scan route (Wave C's D121 left it to Wave D; the server's files and ports are still not the user's). GET /events/catalog is the one events route. decided overnight, amended after review, owner to confirm Not in Wave D D221 The hosted demo serves the user's side of the web app: chat, tools, charts, diagrams, reports, dashboards and the knowledge view, keyless from recordings or with the visitor's key. Admin work (Connect, review, index, profile, evals, drift, LLM settings, keys) is off because a hosted visitor is never admin, not by a hosted switch. Jobs, streams and questions are capped per session. decided overnight, amended after review, owner to confirm The hosted demo D222 The guided questions are the datasources' sample_questions, which nl2sql init --demo already writes (config/project.py). The only gap is exposing them on DatasourceInfo; nl2sql.datasets.demo stops being imported by any app. decided overnight, amended after review, owner to confirm Demo mode D223 The foundation is three PRs, not one: the CI web job first (bug B202, needs nothing), then the API foundation with every engine shape the gaps need, and the web foundation (shell, shared helpers, the client's transport, the CSS split, the build output) beside it, so the parallel PRs never edit the same file. decided overnight, amended after review, owner to confirm PR plan D224 Dashboards are Wave C's surface and no more: whatever Wave C's engine.dashboards and engine.workspaces offer (open, refresh, edit, arrange, filters, schedule, pin, move, delete, workspaces), as thin routes. Wave C (revised 2026-10-28) builds editing and workspaces in the package; this page's route table has not yet been revised to expose them. decided after review, owner to confirm; superseded in part by Wave C's D116, D131 and D133 Routes

docs.title: Route conventions
docs.text: Rule Detail Prefix Everything under /api/v1; the web page and its assets at /. Nouns Plural collections, ids in the path: GET /conversations/{id}. An action is a verb sub-path on the resource it acts on: POST /approvals/{id}/grant, POST /proposals/accept (the facade takes a list of ids). Long work POST /jobs/{kind} returns 202 and the job; GET /jobs/{id} and GET /jobs/{id}/events follow it (Jobs). No route blocks for longer than a question. Streams A route that streams a run ends in /stream and answers text/event-stream (Streams). Bodies Request models are pydantic, strict (extra="forbid"), declared beside their router. Responses are the facade's own models (QueryResult, Conversation, Dashboard, Proposal, ...), served as they are, so the HTTP shape cannot drift from the package's. The caller Every handler that calls an owned, scoped or privileged facade method passes the request's UserContext as user_context= or, for an admin write, by=. Sync handlers A handler that calls the engine is def, so Starlette runs it in its thread pool, as routes/query.py does today. No services layer nl2sql_api/services/ and dependencies.py are deleted: each wrapper was one line over a facade call. A router calls the facade directly. OpenAPI Every route has a summary, its request and response models and its error statuses. packages/api/openapi.json is committed; test_openapi_snapshot_is_current fails when it is stale and prints the command that rewrites it.

docs.title: The error envelope
docs.text:
# nl2sql_api/errors.py
class ApiError(BaseModel):
    code: str                     # an NL2SQLError's code, or NOT_FOUND, INVALID_REQUEST,
                                  # UNAUTHENTICATED, FORBIDDEN, CONFLICT, LIMIT_REACHED, NOT_READY, INTERNAL
    message: str                  # one sentence a person can act on
    fix: str | None = None
    details: list[dict] = []      # 422: one entry per problem, {"loc": [...], "msg": ...}; never a value
    request_id: str | None = None # 500 only: the id in the server log

class ErrorBody(BaseModel):
    error: ApiError

One base class (D202). The engine gains nl2sql.NL2SQLError(Exception) with code, message, fix and status (the HTTP status it means: 404, 409, 422 or 403). The facade's named exceptions derive from it as well as from the built-in they are today, so a Python caller's except LookupError still works:

Exception (from) Status Code ConversationNotFound, DashboardNotFound (Wave C), ResultNotFound, JobNotFound, DatasourceNotFound, ApprovalNotFound (new) 404 NOT_FOUND ConversationBusy (Wave C); ReviewError(FILE_CHANGED) (Wave B) and Wave C's save that reuses it 409 CONFLICT, FILE_CHANGED NoTiles, WorkspaceNotEmpty, ScheduleTooFrequent, NotIndexed, SecretValueInConfig (Wave C); MissingProviderKey (G2); a facade argument check that raises its own subclass 422 the exception's code ReviewError(NOT_AUTHORIZED, NOT_WRITABLE) (Wave B); a caller without an admin or approver role where the facade checks it (NotAuthorized, new) 403 the exception's code Raised Status Code A request body or query that does not validate 422 INVALID_REQUEST, each problem by path and message; the input is never echoed (the playground's _invalid_request handler, generalised) No identity 401 UNAUTHENTICATED, with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer under api_keys A hosted limit 429 LIMIT_REACHED, with Retry-After Not ready 503 NOT_READY Anything else: a built-in ValueError, pydantic.ValidationError, KeyError, PermissionError or OSError from anywhere 500 INTERNAL; the message is "Something failed on the server. Request id: ...", and the exception is logged with that id and the run's trace_id (Wave A's log correlation)

A pipeline outcome is not an error: POST /query answers 200 with a QueryResult whose status is error, needs_clarification, needs_approval or stopped, as today. D0a removes the per-route except Exception blocks of the old routes so the one handler applies to every route from then on. test_no_route_returns_exception_text raises, through every registered route with a stub engine, a ValueError, a pydantic.ValidationError (with an input_value), a KeyError and a PermissionError, each carrying a fake connection string, and checks that each is a 500 whose body holds no part of it (B200).

docs.title: Identity and auth
docs.text:
nl2sql_api/identity.py replaces auth.py. One dependency, caller, resolves the request's UserContext; admin adds the role check.

# nl2sql.yaml (the api section; the engine validates it and never reads it)
api:
  auth: api_keys              # api_keys | proxy | static | none (default: none)
  proxy:                      # auth: proxy only
    trusted_from: [127.0.0.1/32, "::1/128"]   # CIDRs the proxy connects from
    user_header: X-Forwarded-User
    tenant_header: null
    roles_header: X-NL2SQL-Roles
  static_role: analyst        # auth: static only
  request_llm: false          # callers may send their own key and models (D210)
  cors_origins: []
api.auth The caller Admin api_keys Authorization: Bearer <token>, verified by Wave C's engine.api_keys.verify; the key's user_id, tenant_id and roles. Missing or invalid: 401. A key whose roles include one of policies.admin_roles proxy The headers the proxy sets on every request: the user, the tenant (else settings.tenant_id), the roles (comma-separated). Honoured only when the connecting peer is in proxy.trusted_from; from any other peer, or with no user header, a 401. The roles, as above static user_id: "static", static_role. For a single-user deployment on a private network. Only when static_role is an admin role none Refuses to start unless the bind host is loopback (D205). A request whose Host is localhost, 127.0.0.1 or [::1] (with the port) and that carries no Forwarded or X-Forwarded-For header is the local operator, user_id: "local" with the admin roles; any other request is a 403 naming the fix. That operator

The hosted demo's anonymous sessions are not a value of api.auth (D203): serve --demo --hosted installs them itself (The hosted demo). api.trust_body_role, api.role_header and api.role, and the body's user_context, are deleted. The engine's Api model (config/models.py) carries the new fields so nl2sql config check reports a typo.

docs.title: Results bound to the user (B13)
docs.text:
B13 is fixed in the engine (D204), so the facade, the API, MCP and the terminal app all get it:

  1. The result writer records the run's tenant_id and user_id in the result manifest (execution/artifacts/results.py), beside the columns it already records; the trace document records them too.
  2. engine.results.manifest, page, csv and Wave C's chart take user_context=None (replacing chart's tenant_id); with a context, they compare it with the stored pair, and a mismatch raises ResultNotFound. engine.traces.get(trace_id, *, user_context=None) does the same and returns None.
  3. user_context=None is the trusted in-process operator: it reads any run of the engine's tenant, as nl2sql trace <id> (cli/commands/trace.py) and nl2sql run need, and as Wave A's D24 trusts the context an in-process caller passes.
  4. Every app passes the caller. test_apps_always_pass_the_caller scans nl2sql_api/, nl2sql/mcp/ and nl2sql/cli/chat/ (AST) for calls of results.*, traces.get and results.chart without user_context.
  5. Wave C's built-in chart tool and dashboard runs pass the tool's or the tile's caller (nl2sql/chat_tools/chart.py, nl2sql/dashboards/).
  6. Results written before the change have no owner and are read only by None; the release notes say so.

test_another_users_result_is_not_found, test_another_users_trace_is_not_found, test_cli_trace_reads_any_run, test_ownerless_result_is_read_only_by_the_operator (engine) and test_results_route_hides_another_users_rows (API).

docs.title: Streams
docs.text:
nl2sql_api/sse.py is the one place an SSE response is built:

def event_stream(open_events: Callable[[], Iterator[Event]], request: Request,
                 *, token: CancellationToken | None = None) -> StreamingResponse
Rule Detail The wire Each item is Wave A's Event.sse(): event: <name> and data: <json>. No second event vocabulary. Cancellation The iterator runs in the thread pool. When the client disconnects, the helper closes the iterator, which cancels the run for Wave C's conversations.stream (it takes no token and cancels on close), and cancels token too for stream_query, which takes one (cancel_when_disconnected in playground/app.py, moved). Heartbeat A : keep-alive comment every 15 seconds, so a proxy does not close a quiet stream while the planner thinks. Headers Cache-Control: no-cache, X-Accel-Buffering: no (both servers set them today). Refusals Identity, validation and hosted limits are checked before the stream starts and answer with the envelope; once streaming, a failure is the run's run.failed.

The streams: POST /query/stream (Wave A's caller-safe allow-list, ending run.finished with data.result), POST /conversations/{id}/turns/stream (Wave C's run events with conversation.step, ending conversation.turn), and GET /jobs/{id}/events, which is an async generator over the in-memory job and holds no thread.

docs.title: Jobs
docs.text:
# nl2sql_api/jobs.py
JobKind = Literal["index", "profile", "eval", "dashboard"]

class JobProgress(BaseModel):
    at: datetime
    step: str                    # "chinook", "case 12 of 80", "tile 3 of 8"
    done: int
    total: int | None

class Job(BaseModel):
    id: str                      # 22 url-safe characters
    kind: JobKind
    status: Literal["queued", "running", "succeeded", "failed", "cancelled"]
    params: IndexJob | ProfileJob | EvalJob | DashboardJob   # the request body, typed per kind
    created_by: str | None       # the caller's user_id
    created_at: datetime
    started_at: datetime | None
    finished_at: datetime | None
    progress: list[JobProgress]
    result: IndexResult | list[ProfileReport] | EvalReport | DashboardCreated | None   # typed per kind
    error: ApiError | None

IndexResult is the index build's report; DashboardCreated is the new dashboard's id and its first DashboardRun. Each lands in openapi.json, so the web app reads a typed eval report.

Kind Route Facade call Progress from Who index POST /jobs/index {datasource_ids?} engine.index.build(ids, on_datasource=, cancellation_token=) on_datasource admin profile POST /jobs/profile {datasource_ids?, draft, max_cost_usd?} Wave B's engine.knowledge.profile(ids, user_context=, draft=, max_cost_usd=, on_datasource=, cancellation_token=), on the server's key: a key typed in a browser never pays for drafts on_datasource admin eval POST /jobs/eval {suites?, mode, cases?, max_cost_usd?} Wave A's engine.evals.run(..., on_case=, cancellation_token=) on_case admin, in every mode: a report holds every role's cases, plans and SQL dashboard POST /jobs/dashboard {datasource_id, title?, max_tiles?} Wave C's engine.dashboards.generate(..., user_context=, on_tile=, cancellation_token=) on_tile any caller; the dashboard is theirs Rule Detail One worker (D206) One daemon thread takes jobs in submission order. Two index builds never race on the index, and a profile never reads a snapshot an index build is replacing. A question is not a job: it runs on the request's thread as today. One process The queue lives in the process, so nl2sql-api serve and the image run one Uvicorn worker. serve has no --workers; the docs say why. In memory The last 100 jobs. A restart loses them; what they produced (an index build, proposals, a dashboard) is in the engine's stores. One per caller A caller with a job queued or running gets a 409 naming it, so one caller cannot stall the queue. The duplicate check for dashboard is per caller, so two users generating a dashboard for the same datasource never collide. Ownership GET /jobs lists the caller's jobs (an admin sees all); another user's job is a 404, as D204. Cancel DELETE /jobs/{id}: a queued job is removed; a running one has its token cancelled and stops between items (datasources, cases, tiles). Events GET /jobs/{id}/events sends every JobProgress so far, then each new one, then job.finished with the job. These are the API's, not the engine's catalog's. Facade gaps on_datasource exists on index.build and on_case on evals.run; profile and generate gain a callback, and all four gain cancellation_token (G3).

test_jobs_run_one_at_a_time_in_order, test_job_progress_replays_then_follows, test_job_events_hold_no_worker_thread, test_cancel_running_job_stops_between_items, test_second_job_for_a_caller_is_a_conflict, test_two_users_generate_for_one_datasource, test_another_users_job_is_not_found, test_eval_job_is_admin_only, test_api_runs_one_worker.

docs.title: Health and readiness
docs.text:
Route Answers GET /health Liveness: {"status": "ok", "version": {"engine", "api"}}, from process state only. The Space's release check polls it for the version (scripts/fresh_install_check.py). GET /ready The engine's check() report, cached 10 seconds, judged by CheckReport.ready(keys_optional=) (D208): keys_optional is true when api.request_llm is on or every agent is on replay. 200 {"status": "ready"} or 503 {"status": "not_ready"} to everyone; an admin caller also gets CheckReport.problems() (each failing datasource and its stage, each agent whose key does not resolve, the index status), never a secret. An optional datasource that failed is a problem but not "not ready". GET /meta Without a caller: mode (demo, hosted, your_data), the identity source and request_llm, which is what the page needs to show a sign-in. With a caller: also the datasources it may reach with their sample_questions (D222), which of those the replay provider has recordings for, recorded_with, and the hosted limits. GET /about engine.about(): the pipeline's steps and the model each runs on (today's /api/pipeline).

nl2sql-api no longer refuses to start when a required datasource fails: it starts, /ready is 503, and the reason is one admin request away, which an orchestrator's restart loop would otherwise hide.

test_ready_fails_on_a_required_datasource, test_ready_passes_with_an_optional_failure, test_ready_fails_on_a_missing_index, test_ready_passes_with_request_keys, test_ready_details_only_for_admin, test_meta_without_a_caller_lists_no_datasource.

docs.text:
Every route below is new unless marked. "Admin" is the admin dependency; everything else needs a caller. A name in bold in the facade column is a gap (section 11). caller is the request's UserContext.

Questions, results, traces and feedback (routes/query.py)

Route Facade Notes POST /query (changed) run_query(question, user_context=caller, datasource_id=, execute=, choice=, approvals=, llm_override=) Body: question (was natural_language), datasource_id, execute, choice (Wave B's ClarificationChoice), approval_ids (D215). A body with both choice and approval_ids is a 422 CLARIFICATION_INVALID before the engine is called, as Wave B refuses them together. POST /query/stream (changed) stream_query(...) Wave A's Events GET /results/{trace_id} results.manifest(..., user_context=caller) The manifest, without rows GET /results/{trace_id}/{result_id} (moved) results.page(..., user_context=caller) Was /query/{request_id}/results/{result_id} GET /results/{trace_id}/{result_id}.csv (moved) results.csv(..., user_context=caller) GET /results/{trace_id}/{result_id}/chart Wave C's results.chart(trace_id, result_id, kind=, user_context=caller) ?kind=; ?format=vega-lite answers to_vega_lite() GET /traces/{trace_id} traces.get(trace_id, user_context=caller) Today only the playground has it POST /feedback (from the playground) feedback.record(trace_id, rating, *, user_context, note=None) The engine reads the run's own trace; the playground's in-memory "recent runs" goes POST /feedback/correct Wave B's feedback.correct(trace_id, *, user_context=caller, sql=, plan=, question=, note=) Returns the Proposal GET /feedback feedback.list() Admin

Route Facade POST /conversations conversations.start(user_context=, datasource_id=) GET /conversations conversations.list(user_context=) GET /conversations/{id} conversations.get DELETE /conversations/{id} conversations.delete POST /conversations/{id}/turns conversations.ask(id, text=, user_context=, choice=, execute=, llm_override=) POST /conversations/{id}/turns/stream conversations.stream(...) docs.title: Approvals over REST
docs.text:
Wave A's approval holds nothing: the app that asked keeps the ApprovalRequest, and the approver's Approval names who approved. In process that works because one program sees both people. Over HTTP the approver and the asker are two callers, at different times, on different connections: the asker's request cannot prove that someone else approved, and the approver must not re-run the question as the asker (Wave A binds the run to the asker). So D215 keeps the grant in the engine, keyed by the request's id:

# engine.approvals (state store, beside the review queue); the caller is required (D204)
def list(self, *, user_context, status="pending") -> list[ApprovalRecord]: ...
def grant(self, request_id: str, *, by: UserContext) -> ApprovalRecord: ...
def deny(self, request_id: str, *, by: UserContext, reason: str | None = None) -> ApprovalRecord: ...
Rule Detail Submitted by the run A run that ends needs_approval stores each ApprovalRequest as pending; nobody calls a submit. Granted by an approver grant checks that by holds one of the hook's approver roles (Wave A's D24), else NotAuthorized. Used by id run_query(approvals=), stream_query(approvals=) and Wave C's conversations.retry(approvals=) accept request ids beside Approval objects; a granted id becomes the Approval the engine already checks (the request's hash, the asker, the approver's roles, the SQL's hash), so Wave A's checks are unchanged. A denied or unknown id is APPROVAL_NOT_GRANTED on the result. Reusable until expiry A grant answers any re-run of that request (same question, asker, plan and SQL) for settings.approvals.max_age_hours (24), as Wave A's Approval is reusable. Purged by engine.storage.purge(). Amends Wave A's D10 ("nothing is stored") and D24, and Wave C's D107 ("nothing is stored"; retry takes Approvals), listed in Needs.

In the web app the asker sees "Waiting for approval" with the reason; an approver sees the request under Approvals (the plan in English, the SQL, the reason) and grants it; the asker's Run it now calls retry with the id.

docs.title: The replay provider
docs.text:
Demo mode must answer with no key, through the same pipeline a key would use (D209):

# llm.yaml in the demo project
provider: replay
recordings: null        # null: the recordings packaged with the engine (nl2sql/datasets/recordings/)
Rule Detail Where nl2sql/llm/providers/replay.py (from llm/replay.py's ReplayStore and extract_question): a provider in PROVIDER_PRESETS with no key variable, whose chat model answers structured() and plain calls from the store. Matching As today: the structured-output name plus the question the prompt was built around. Wave C's conversation agent prompt gains the same [USER_QUERY] marker so a recorded step matches. A miss The provider raises ReplayMiss; the pipeline ends with REPLAY_MISS (ERROR, not retryable) and "No recorded answer for this question. Add an API key to ask it live." No marker string is matched (REPLAY_MISS_MARKER and finish_question in playground/app.py go). Labelled Each usage call records provider: "replay" and the recording's recorded_with model; the web app shows "Recorded run" from that, not from a flag the server adds. Coverage engine.llm.recorded(questions) -> list[str] answers which questions the store covers, for /meta. Overrides A per-call LLMOverride with a key replaces the replay provider for that call, which is how a hosted visitor goes live. Recording scripts/record_demo_answers.py runs the guided questions, the scripted follow-ups and the clarification question through a real provider with a recording wrapper (nl2sql.llm.replay.Recorder, internal; scripts may import it) and writes the store. nl2sql demo --record, RecordingProxy and the demo's use of FakeLLMServer go; FakeLLMServer stays for tests.

docs.title: Keys and models in the web app
docs.text:
D210 makes one rule for every mode: a key typed into the browser lives in that tab's sessionStorage and is sent with each request; the model per step likewise. The hosted page already works this way (web/playground/src/hostedKey.js, hostedModels.js); the local page's "save key to .env" and "write models to llm.yaml" go. The cost is that a local user types the key once per tab (or puts it in .env once); getting_started/demo.md says so.

Header Holds X-NL2SQL-Api-Key-<provider> One provider's key; one header per key (as today) X-NL2SQL-Models {"ast_planner": "anthropic:claude-opus-5"}, no secret (as today)

nl2sql_api/overrides.py (in D0a) turns the headers into the engine's LLMOverride(keys={provider: key}, models={agent: (provider, model)}) and passes it as llm_override= (a new keyword, so it never means two types beside Wave A's evals.run(llm=)) to run_query, stream_query and conversations.ask, stream and retry.

Rule Detail Off by default With api.request_llm: false the headers are a 403 naming the setting. Never the operator's key A model in X-NL2SQL-Models on a provider the request sent no key for is a 422 naming the step and the provider (MissingProviderKey), even when the server holds that provider's key. Keys without models run the configured models, using the caller's key for its provider, as llm/request_key.py resolves them today. Never written A key is never logged, never in a trace (the redactor already masks request keys) and never in an error. Not for admin work Profiling, evals and dashboards run on the server's configuration; llm_override is on the question and turn methods only.

test_request_key_headers_refused_without_request_llm, test_model_override_without_request_key_is_422_even_when_server_has_key, test_request_key_never_in_a_response_log_or_trace.

docs.title: Saving a datasource (final-design D14)
docs.text:
Connect tests a connection, registers it with datasources.add, and saves it only through Wave C's writer (D212):

Where What Save does nl2sql-api serve on loopback with auth: none, config loaded from a folder datasources.save(id, by=caller, env_file=True): datasources/<id>.yaml, secrets as ${env:...} with the values in .env (Wave C's D122) Any other deployment with an admin caller datasources.save(id, by=caller, env_file=False): a literal secret is a 422 SecretValueInConfig asking for a ${env:...} reference The Docker image, Compose (the config mounted read-only) save fails with its own message; the page shows it and that the datasource is registered in memory until restart, and how to add it to the mounted config The hosted demo Off: Connect is admin work (D221)

docs.title: 4. Serving the web app and nl2sql demo
nl2sql-api serve
docs.text:
nl2sql_api/serve.py, run as nl2sql-api serve (the console script, replacing server.py) or python -m nl2sql_api serve:

nl2sql-api serve [--config PATH] [--host 127.0.0.1] [--port 8000]
nl2sql-api serve --demo [--dir nl2sql-demo] [--host] [--port]
nl2sql-api serve --demo --hosted [--dir] [--host] [--port] [--questions-per-minute 6] [--questions-per-session 30]
Mode What it does your data (default) Builds NL2SQL.from_config(path), serves /api/v1 and the page. Refuses to start under auth: none on a non-loopback host (D205). --demo nl2sql.prepare_demo(dir) writes the demo project the first time (init_project(demo=True)), builds the index if check() says it is missing, and returns the config path. The demo's model is chosen as today's nl2sql demo chooses it: a provider key in the environment or the project's .env, else a reachable Ollama, else the replay provider. The demo config sets api.request_llm: true and api.auth: none. --demo --hosted As --demo, plus: refuses to start when a provider key is in the environment (as today), never uses Ollama, installs anonymous sessions (below) and the per-visitor limits (nl2sql_api/hosted.py, from playground/hosted.py's Limits), and sends the link-preview tags (playground/preview.py, moved).

The page, its chunks, the social card and the clips are package data of nl2sql_api (web/static/, web/assets/), served at /, /assets/, /social-card.png and /clips/{name} (routes/web.py). Any other path under / that is not a file answers the page, so the hash router owns navigation.

docs.title: nl2sql demo, a launcher (D211)
docs.text:
cli/commands/demo.py shrinks to about 40 lines. It checks that nl2sql_api is installed (importlib.util.find_spec), else prints pip install "nl2sql-engine[demo]" and exits 1. It then starts [sys.executable, "-m", "nl2sql_api", "serve", "--demo", ...] with subprocess.Popen, opens the browser unless --no-browser, and waits; a KeyboardInterrupt is forwarded to the child (CTRL_BREAK_EVENT on Windows, SIGINT elsewhere) and the launcher exits with the child's code. Its flags are --dir, --host, --port and --no-browser. --hosted and the limits are gone from it (the Space runs nl2sql-api serve directly), and so are --record, --api-key and --allow-settings, with no alias: recording is a script, a key is typed into the page or put in .env, and the settings gate is D205's loopback rule.

The engine's pyproject.toml replaces demo = ["fastapi", "uvicorn"] with demo = ["nl2sql-api~=X.Y.Z"] (the release-please version marker, as nl2sql-api pins the engine), and drops the package data for nl2sql.cli.demo and nl2sql.cli.demo.playground. The two distributions now depend on each other; publish_pypi.yaml uploads nl2sql-api before or with the engine, so pip install "nl2sql-engine[demo]" never resolves in between, and docs/development/releasing.md says so. The recordings move to nl2sql/datasets/recordings/, beside the sample databases they answer. Wave C's nl2sql launch ends by printing a command that serves the project; that line becomes nl2sql-api serve --config DIR/nl2sql.yaml.

docs.title: The hosted demo
docs.text:
The Space keeps its URL, its limits and its keyless start (D221):

Hosted Identity An anonymous session per browser: a random 128-bit id in the HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax cookie nl2sql_demo_session that playground/hosted.py already sets, as user_id, with policies.default_role. Never admin. Nothing a visitor makes is visible to another. Questions and turns Recorded guided questions and their scripted follow-ups answer with no key; anything else needs the visitor's key (REPLAY_MISS with "Add a key in Settings") Chat tools, charts, diagrams, reports On: no model call Dashboards Generate (one job per session, no model call), refresh, filter, pin, delete a tile: on, per session Knowledge view, "why this answer" On, read-only Evals, drift, Connect, review, index, profile, LLM settings, API keys Off: admin routes, and a visitor is never admin Limits The questions-per-minute and per-session limits apply to questions, turns and POST /jobs/*, keyed as today on the session and on X-Forwarded-For's first hop (the Space's proxy); at most one job and two open streams per session (429) State The Space's disk is ephemeral: conversations and dashboards live until the container restarts, and the page says so

deploy/huggingface/Dockerfile installs nl2sql-engine[demo] (which brings nl2sql-api), builds the demo project and index as today, and runs nl2sql-api serve --demo --hosted --dir /home/demo/demo --host 0.0.0.0 --port $PORT .... Its healthcheck and scripts/fresh_install_check.py move to /api/v1/health, /api/v1/meta, /api/v1/datasources/{id}/schema (with a session) and /api/v1/index; publish_pypi.yaml's space-smoke and test.yml's fresh-install keep their shape. The cutover is rehearsed on a scratch Space before the release (X1).

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  subgraph Browser
    P["Pages: Home, Chat, Dashboards,<br/>Connect, Knowledge, Evals, Settings,<br/>Pipeline, Retrieval"]
    C["src/api/*.js<br/>one file per area"]
    P --> C
  end
  C -->|"JSON, SSE"| API["nl2sql-api /api/v1"]
  API --> F["NL2SQL facade"]
  T["nl2sql chat (Textual)"] --> F
Rule Detail Where web/app/ (renamed from web/playground/, D216). npm run build writes packages/api/src/nl2sql_api/web/static/, committed, so pip install nl2sql-api needs no Node. The single-file plugin goes (D214): the build is index.html plus hashed chunks, and Mermaid is its own chunk. Until X1, nl2sql demo keeps serving the page already committed in the engine. Transport src/api/http.js (D0b): request(method, path, body) adds the identity header (a bearer key held in the tab under api_keys), the key and model headers (D210), and parses the envelope into an ApiError; stream(path, body, onEvent) reads SSE from a fetch body. Client One file per area, each owned by the W-PR for that area: src/api/chat.js (W1), outputs.js and dashboards.js (W2), connect.js and knowledge.js (W3), evals.js, settings.js and meta.js (W4). src/api/routes.test.js reads every src/api/*.js file's paths. Router src/router.js (kept): hash routes #/, #/chat/{id?}, #/dashboards/{id?}, #/connect, #/knowledge, #/approvals, #/evals, #/settings, #/pipeline, #/retrieval, #/trace/{id}. The shell (D0b) lazy-loads a stub per page, which the W-PRs fill. Sign-in Under api_keys, a page that /meta says needs a caller asks for an API key and keeps it in sessionStorage; under proxy and none there is nothing to ask. State React state in each page; the shell holds /meta, the identity and the tab's keys. Nothing else is stored in the browser. Styles src/styles.css is split (in D0b, by moving rules, not changing them) into styles/base.css (tokens, type, the card, controls) and one file per area. New pages use only the base tokens; styles.test.js keeps holding the tokens. No logic A page never computes what the facade returns: the chart kind, a takeaway, a tile, an explanation, a rewrite. Review holds it, and the client files make every server call visible.

docs.title: Pages
docs.text: Page What it shows Client Home (kept) The hero, the path, three features with clips; "Try a sample question" opens Chat with the first recorded guided question meta.js Chat (replaces Ask) The caller's conversations, the transcript, the composer with the guided questions as chips and the datasource switcher. Each turn: the question that ran (with "rewritten from ..." when it was), the answer, the result table (paged, CSV), its chart, warnings, and folded panels: Why this answer (Wave B's explanation: tables, joins, filters, measures, assumptions, terms, the planner's note labelled), SQL, Plan, Trace (the node inspector). Streaming fills the run spine as node.* events arrive. chat.js — tools Buttons on a turn: Chart, Diagram, Report, Pin; or typed ("chart that"). A tool turn renders its ToolOutput through Output.jsx. chat.js — clarification A needs_clarification turn shows the options (label and the option's explanation) as a radio group with Use this reading, plus Remember this meaning (a pick saved as a proposal) chat.js — approval A needs_approval turn shows the reason and the SQL; "Waiting for approval", then Run it now once granted chat.js — correction This is wrong on a turn: a rating with a note, and optionally corrected SQL; the answer is "Sent for review" with the proposal id chat.js Approvals Pending requests with the asker, the plan in English, the SQL and the reason; Grant or Deny. A badge in the nav for an approver. chat.js Dashboards The caller's; Generate for a datasource (a job with progress); a dashboard as a 4-column grid of tiles (big number, line, bar, table), each with its takeaway, "not filtered" when a filter does not apply, stale with Remove, denied as a blank tile; filters as chips (an in filter's values, a between range); Refresh; Delete dashboards.js Connect (admin) Pick an adapter type (installed or not, with its install line); a form generated from the adapter's connection JSON Schema (text, number, boolean, enum, format: password hidden, description as help); Test shows the failed stage and its fix; Add and, where it applies, Save; then Index and Profile as jobs with progress; then the starter questions, filed for review; then Review connect.js Knowledge The merged knowledge per datasource (descriptions with their origin, terms, rules, joins); the schema diagram; Proposals (admin): by kind, each with its evidence and change, Accept (with an edit form) and Reject (with a reason), one or many; Drift (admin): each datasource's DriftReport, its diff and what it breaks knowledge.js Evals (admin) The suites and their case counts; Run (mode, cases, cost cap; full runs on the server's model) as a job with per-case progress; the report: accuracy, accuracy on the generated path, by source and by role, each failing case with its scorer messages evals.js Settings The tab's keys and models (today's hosted cards, now in every mode where request_llm is on); the tab's API key under api_keys; the server's LLM per agent (admin); API keys (admin: create, shown once; revoke); the index panel (health, Rebuild as an index job) settings.js Pipeline (kept), Retrieval (kept) As today meta.js, connect.js

docs.title: The image
docs.text:
packages/api/Dockerfile, one image (D213):

  • python:3.12-slim; Microsoft's package repository for msodbcsql18 and unixodbc with ACCEPT_EULA=Y;
  • nl2sql-engine[postgres,mysql,mssql,duckdb,anthropic] and nl2sql-api from the repository;
  • the three sample databases, written at build time by nl2sql init --demo /opt/nl2sql/samples, and the local embedding model fetched into the image's cache, as the Space's image does;
  • a non-root user, ENV NL2SQL_CONFIG=/etc/nl2sql/nl2sql.yaml;
  • CMD ["nl2sql-api", "serve", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000"], one worker;
  • HEALTHCHECK on /api/v1/ready.

test.yml's api-image job builds it for linux/amd64, imports both packages, runs pyodbc.drivers() to see the SQL Server driver, and records the image size in the job summary. K1 checks the arm64 package before any arm64 image is published (D213).

docs.title: deploy/compose/
docs.text:
# deploy/compose/docker-compose.yml (shape)
services:
  api:
    image: nl2sql-api:local
    build: { context: ../.., dockerfile: packages/api/Dockerfile }
    env_file: .env
    volumes: [ "./config:/etc/nl2sql:ro", "nl2sql-data:/data" ]
    ports: [ "8000:8000" ]
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "python", "-c", "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen('http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1/ready', timeout=4)"]
      interval: 30s
      start_period: 30s
volumes:
  nl2sql-data: {}
Rule Detail One service (D219) api starts and is not ready until the index exists; /ready says so to an admin. Index once with docker compose run --rm api nl2sql index, again only when the schema changes (or POST /jobs/index). Nothing re-indexes on up. One volume storage.path: "${env:NL2SQL_DATA_DIR}" with NL2SQL_DATA_DIR=/data in .env: index, state store, traces, results, audit log. Auth on config/nl2sql.yaml ships with api.auth: api_keys. The first admin key: docker compose run --rm api nl2sql keys create --as admin --user admin --role admin, printed once (Wave C's CLI). The example config One datasource, /opt/nl2sql/samples/data/chinook.sqlite from the image, so the stack answers after one index command; the docs show replacing it with a PostgreSQL datasource. Keys .env.example lists the provider key and NL2SQL_DATA_DIR; .env is git-ignored. TLS A reverse proxy in front, with api_keys (D205 forbids none off loopback); the page shows Caddy's two lines.

docs/deployment/compose.md (new) is the page: up, index, the first key, the web app with the key, connecting your database, backups of the volume, upgrading.

docs.title: 7. The terminal app: nl2sql chat
docs.text:
nl2sql chat [--config PATH | --demo [--dir nl2sql-demo]] [--as ROLE] [--user NAME] [--datasource ID]
Rule Detail Where nl2sql/cli/chat/ (app.py, widgets.py, charts.py), the command in cli/commands/chat.py, which imports the app lazily and prints pip install "nl2sql-engine[tui]" when Textual is missing. import nl2sql still loads no textual (the existing test). Facade only nl2sql/cli/chat/ imports only the top-level nl2sql and textual. The caller is UserContext(user_id=--user or the OS user, roles=[--as or policies.default_role]), passed to every call (D204). Layout Conversations on the left (conversations.list); the transcript in the middle; the composer at the bottom with the guided questions on Tab; a side panel toggled with F2 for "why this answer", F3 for the SQL. A turn Streamed from conversations.stream: a one-line status per step, then the answer, the warnings, and the result as a DataTable (first page; PageDown reads the next through results.page(..., user_context=)). Charts /chart (or "chart that") calls the chart tool; charts.py draws the ChartSpec as text: big_number as a large figure, line as one Textual Sparkline per series with the first and last values, bar as horizontal bars of block characters with values, table as a DataTable. The takeaway under it. Diagrams, reports /diagram shows the Mermaid text in a code block (a terminal cannot render it); /report shows the Markdown in Textual's Markdown widget, s saves it to a file the user names. Clarification A needs_clarification turn opens an option list; the pick is conversations.ask(choice=). r saves the pick as a proposal. Approval A needs_approval turn shows the reason and the SQL. When --as holds an approver role, Approve and run grants (approvals.grant) and retries with the id; otherwise it says who can approve, and /approvals lists pending ones for an approver. Demo mode --demo calls nl2sql.prepare_demo(dir), the same function serve --demo uses. Keys None typed in the app (D218): the environment and the project's .env, as every command. Tests Textual's App.run_test() pilot over an engine with the fake LLM from nl2sql.testing: test_chat_streams_a_turn_and_shows_rows, test_follow_up_shows_the_rewritten_question, test_chart_tool_draws_sparklines_for_a_line, test_bar_chart_text_has_one_row_per_category, test_clarification_pick_asks_with_choice, test_approver_can_approve_and_retry, test_demo_mode_answers_from_recordings, test_chat_imports_only_the_public_nl2sql (architecture), test_importing_nl2sql_loads_no_textual (existing).

docs.text: Rule Change The REST API, the playground and nl2sql demo import only the top-level nl2sql STILL_IMPORTED_FROM_INSIDE is emptied and deleted (X1); the playground is gone; cli/commands/demo.py imports nothing from the engine but nl2sql and nl2sql.cli. The test covers nl2sql_api/, cli/commands/demo.py and nl2sql/cli/chat/. docs.title: 15. Release
docs.text:
• release-please opens the release PR as usual. Releasing is the owner's act (see Releasing); no agent merges it.
  • docs/releases/X.Y.Z.md is written with the release-notes process. Its breaking-changes table covers every renamed or removed route (section 3, /llm/{agent} among them, no aliases), the error envelope, api.auth replacing role_header, role and trust_body_role, results bound to their asker (ownerless old results), feedback.record's new signature, nl2sql demo's removed flags, the engine's demo extra now installing nl2sql-api, the state store's new version, the API starting when a required datasource fails, and /ready failing where it used to pass.
  • Before tagging, the owner checks the scratch Space (keyless and with a key), runs the Compose stack with a key, connects the test bed's PostgreSQL through the web app, asks three follow-ups with a chart and a pin, generates a dashboard, runs the Chinook evals in plans mode, and opens nl2sql chat --demo. After the release deploys, the live Space is checked again.

docs.title: 16. Open questions
docs.text: None blocking. Every decision above is marked for the owner to confirm. Five are worth a look first, because they change what a user or an operator sees: D211 (the web extra moves to the engine's demo extra), D210 (a key typed into the web app is never saved, locally too), D215 (approval grants are stored, amending Waves A and C), D221 (what the hosted demo leaves on) and D224 (dashboards stay at Wave C's surface).

docs.title: Node Catalog
docs.text:
This section indexes all control-graph nodes and SQL agent subgraph nodes. Each node has a dedicated reference page with inputs, outputs, contracts, and limitations.

For pipeline-level wiring, see ../pipeline.md. For subgraph wiring and lifecycle, see ../subgraphs/sql_agent.md.

docs.text:
• CuratedMatcherNode (only when curated answers are configured)
  • DatasourceResolverNode
  • DecomposerNode
  • EngineAggregatorNode

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
• Summarizes aggregated results into a user‑facing response using an LLM.
  • Exists to convert structured results into human‑readable output.
  • Sits after EngineAggregatorNode at the end of the control graph.
  • Class: AnswerSynthesizerNode
  • Source: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/nodes/answer_synthesizer/node.py

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Send the model a preview of each result, never the whole of it: the first settings.results.preview_rows rows (20), the total row count, the column names and a partial flag.
  • Say when a result was cut at the row limit, whatever the model wrote.
  • Include unmapped sub‑queries in the response context.
  • Invoke LLM with structured output schema.

docs.title: Position in Execution Graph
docs.text:
Upstream: - EngineAggregatorNode, after a generated run or a verified one (the curated matcher ran the query)

Downstream: - Graph end.

Trigger conditions: - Executed after aggregation succeeds. When the aggregator fails (AGGREGATOR_FAILED), aggregator_route ends the run instead, so this node never spends a model call on an empty result.

flowchart LR
    Aggregator[EngineAggregatorNode] --> Synthesizer[AnswerSynthesizerNode] --> EndNode[PipelineEnd]

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
From GraphState:

  • user_query (required)
  • aggregator_response.terminal_results (required): the first rows of each terminal result
  • aggregator_response.computed_artifacts: the saved result behind each, for its row count and columns
  • decomposer_response.unmapped_subqueries (optional)
  • subgraph_outputs[<id>].truncated / .row_cap: whether a sub-query's result reached its row limit, and at how many rows.
  • verified_match (optional): set when a verified query answered. Its qualified id and its description (the data team's words for what the query returns, e.g. "invoiced revenue, before refunds") are added to the prompt as a Verified Query section, and the model is told to describe the numbers that way. A generated answer's prompt has no such section and is exactly what it was.
  • warnings (RunWarnings): the sanity checks' VALUE_NOT_FOUND ("There is no Genre with Name 'Polka'."), JOIN_FAN_OUT (a sum a join may have counted more than once) and ALL_NULL_COLUMN warnings (see ExecutorNode). A recovered one (detail.recovered) is not used: a retry replaced that attempt.

Validation performed:

  • If no aggregated result is available, emits INVALID_STATE.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
Mutations to GraphState:

  • answer_synthesizer_response (AnswerSynthesizerResponse): final_answer is the model's AggregatedResponse (summary, format_type, content, warnings) plus truncated, True when a result was cut at the row limit.
  • reasoning summary
  • errors on failure

Side effects:

  • LLM invocation.

docs.title: Internal Flow (Step-by-Step)
docs.text:
1. Resolve aggregated result from aggregator_response.
  2. If missing, emit INVALID_STATE error and stop.
  3. Build the result preview (result_preview()): for each terminal result, its first settings.results.preview_rows rows, row_count, columns and partial (true when rows were left out). The rows are the aggregator's terminal_results, already cut to the preview; row_count and columns come from the saved combined result in computed_artifacts, so they describe the whole result. Serialize it to JSON.
  4. Build the Result Limit note: one line per sub-query whose result reached its row limit ("The result was cut at 10,000 rows, the row limit, so it is incomplete. Narrow the question ..."), or None.
  5. Serialize unmapped sub‑queries to JSON.
  6. Invoke LLM chain with structured output. The prompt's Data Notes lists the sanity checks' notes and asks the answer to say them: that a value does not exist instead of reporting the empty result as a finding, that a total may count rows more than once, that a column has no values. When the run was started by stream_query (configurable.stream_answer), the chain is streaming_structured: the same request with the provider asked to stream, so the run's RunEvents callback publishes each piece of the tool call as an answer.delta event. The answer it returns is the unstreamed chain's (Streaming a run).
  7. Append each data note and each result-limit note to the answer's warnings, whatever the model wrote, set final_answer.truncated, and return AnswerSynthesizerResponse.
  8. On exception, emit AGGREGATOR_FAILED.

docs.title: The model sees a preview, not the result
docs.text:
The user sees the full result as a table; the model's job is to write about it, not to copy it. So the prompt carries a preview, and its instructions say:

  • every number the answer states comes from the preview rows or from row_count;
  • when the preview is partial, do not total, average, rank or count over rows it cannot see;
  • do not reproduce the result: say the full result is in the table, and use format_type "table" only for a few preview rows.

The prompt's size no longer grows with the result, which is what let the row cap rise from 1,000 to a resource ceiling (settings.results.row_limit, 100,000).

docs.title: A result cut at the row limit
docs.text: The generator bounds each sub-query's SQL at its row limit. A result that comes back with that many rows may have been cut, so the subgraph wrapper marks it truncated (SubgraphOutput, QueryResult.sub_queries[].truncated, QueryResult.truncated). The prompt's Result Limit section tells the model the result was cut at N rows and asks it to say so and to suggest narrowing the question; the node adds the same note to warnings itself, so a cut result is never presented as complete even when the model leaves it out. A plan's own top-N (LIMIT 5) is the answer, not a cut, and is never flagged.
