It is applied before results are combined, so a join input that reaches it is refused (RESULT_TRUNCATED) and a union input that reaches it is flagged with a warning; see row cap before a combine.
  • max_bytes: passed to the adapter.

There is one place for each limit: the 0.4 options: bag and the top-level spellings are gone.

docs.title: Index
docs.text:
index says what of the database is indexed. Every key is optional, and an unknown key is an error.

index:
  include_schemas: [public, reporting]
  exclude_tables: ["*.*_audit", "public.tmp_*"]
  exclude_columns: ["public.customers.email"]
Key Default Meaning include_schemas every schema but the database's system schemas Schema globs exclude_schemas none Schema globs, applied after include include_tables, exclude_tables all, none schema.table globs; a pattern with no schema is an error with the fix ('*.tmp_*') exclude_columns none schema.table.column globs: the column is neither indexed nor profiled. This is not access control: use policies. profile stats catalog: names, types, keys, comments and the catalog's row estimates, with no query against table data. stats: also each column's null share, distinct count and min/max. sample_values false Store each text column's values: every one when there are 50 or fewer distinct, otherwise the five most frequent. Off by default, since values reach the index, the prompts and the model provider. The demo (NL2SQL.demo(), nl2sql init --demo) turns it on. max_profile_rows 1,000,000 A table estimated above this is profiled from the catalog only, and the index build reports it

Every glob ignores case, and an exclude wins over an include. A SQLite database has one schema, main.

The scope is applied before any query that reads a schema, so an excluded schema costs nothing. A row count is the catalog's estimate where the database keeps one (PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, DuckDB); otherwise, under stats, the rows are counted. What a table or column was indexed without (a statistics query the database rejected, a table over max_profile_rows) is an issue: nl2sql index prints it, and engine.index.build() returns it in the datasource's stats under issues. See SQLAlchemy adapters for how the built-in adapters read a schema.

docs.title: Preferred tables
docs.text:
The package never creates a view. The data team creates it in the database, lists it under preferred_tables, and runs nl2sql index; every built-in adapter snapshots views as well as tables (PostgreSQL materialized views are not read). At question time the schema retriever lists preferred tables first and marks them "preferred": true in the schema the planner sees, and the planner is told to plan against a preferred table when it answers the question:

  • When the whole schema is sent (settings.retrieval.full_snapshot_max_tables tables or fewer), every preferred table is in it, first.
  • Otherwise the retrieved tables are re-ordered so preferred ones come first, and a preferred table the search scored but did not pick is added when its similarity is within 0.05 of the least similar pick.

RBAC is unchanged: a preferred table the role may not read loses its data like any other table, and the validator refuses a plan that reads it.

A name that is not in the indexed schema is a warning, not an error: nl2sql doctor and the index status (engine.index.health(), GET /api/v1/index/status) print "Preferred table 'v_x' of 'chinook' is not in the indexed schema". The usual cause is a view created after the last index; re-index the datasource.

docs.title: When a datasource fails to start
docs.text:
A datasource the engine cannot build (an unknown type, a missing driver, an invalid connection config, a ${...} reference that does not resolve) stops it: building the engine raises one ConfigError that names every such datasource and the reason. Building never connects, so this needs no database.

A datasource that cannot connect is found by engine.check() (see Public Facade → Lifecycle), and does not stop the engine unless it is required. The others stay routed, and the broken one is marked unavailable:

  • the log has an error: Datasource 'sales' is unavailable: <reason>;
  • check() reports it failed at stage connect, with a fix;
  • engine.datasources.list() (and GET /api/v1/datasource) shows it with status: "failed" and the reason, and nothing is routed to it;
  • the index status (engine.index.health(), GET /api/v1/index/status) carries the same sentence as a warning;
  • a query with datasource_id set to it, and nl2sql index or engine.index.build([...]) naming it, fail with that reason.

check() raises EngineNotReady when a required: true datasource fails, or when datasources are configured and none is ready. A later check(), or engine.datasources.test(id), that connects routes the datasource again.

nl2sql doctor prints the same check() report. After check(), engine.policies.validate() reports a role that names an unavailable datasource as UNAVAILABLE.

A secret provider that cannot start is different: it fails startup. See Secrets → When a provider fails to start.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Use ${env:VAR} for environment variables, or ${provider:key} for a secret from a provider in the secrets section.
  • The keys under connection are the adapter's; see Connection.
  • From Python, engine.datasources.add(Datasource(...)) adds one to a running engine (built, not connected), and engine.datasources.remove(id) takes one out; nl2sql-api's POST /api/v1/datasource takes the same shape as JSON.

docs.title: Embeddings
docs.text:
The embeddings section of nl2sql.yaml chooses how schema entries are embedded during nl2sql index, and how questions are embedded during retrieval. nl2sql init writes the key-free local provider:

# embeddings.yaml
provider: local
Field Default Meaning provider required local, openai, openai_compatible, or a provider a plugin registers. model the provider's default The embedding model. Required for openai_compatible. api_key the provider's standard variable A ${env:VAR} or ${provider:key} reference, resolved when the embedder is built. base_url none The server's URL, for openai and openai_compatible. An error for local. dimension the provider's The model's output dimension. Write it only when the provider does not know it and you want to skip the probe (see Model and dimension).

In Python, Embeddings(instance=MyEmbeddings()) passes a LangChain embeddings object instead of a provider name. Each engine builds its own embedder once.

docs.title: Providers
docs.text:
provider Model Dimension API key base_url local all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (ONNX, bundled with chromadb); the only model 384 none not allowed openai model, default text-embedding-3-small known for OpenAI's own models (1536, or 3072 for text-embedding-3-large) api_key, else OPENAI_API_KEY optional openai_compatible model, required dimension:, else probed api_key if the server needs one required

An openai section with no key resolving, an openai_compatible section without model or base_url, or a local section with a base_url, is a ConfigError when the engine is built, naming the problem.

Notes on the local provider:

  • No extra dependency. The model ships with chromadb, which the engine already depends on for its built-in chroma index store.
  • One-time download. The first indexing run downloads roughly 79 MB of ONNX model files into a local cache directory. Expect a pause of up to a few minutes; a log line is emitted before the download starts.
  • Embeddings only. This removes the API key requirement from the embedding step. It does not make querying key-free: answering a question still needs a chat model (see LLMs).

docs.title: openai_compatible
docs.text:
Any server with an OpenAI-style embeddings API: Azure OpenAI's v1 endpoint, Ollama, vLLM, LiteLLM, LM Studio or a company gateway. There is no Azure-specific provider; Azure uses this one.

# embeddings.yaml: Ollama
provider: openai_compatible
base_url: http://ollama:11434/v1
model: nomic-embed-text
dimension: 768            # optional: skips the probe

# embeddings.yaml: Azure OpenAI's v1 endpoint
provider: openai_compatible
base_url: https://my-resource.openai.azure.com/openai/v1/
api_key: "${env:AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY}"
model: embed-prod          # the Azure deployment name
dimension: 1536
  • No key variable. OPENAI_API_KEY is never read: that key belongs to OpenAI, not to your server. Write api_key (usually ${env:...}) if the server needs one; without it a placeholder is sent, because the OpenAI client refuses to start without a key.
  • Text, not tokens. The text is sent as is. (The openai provider sends OpenAI's token ids, which other servers' models cannot read.)

docs.title: Model and dimension
docs.text:
The engine needs the embedder's model and dimension to know which index it reads and writes. A provider reports them as EmbeddingInfo(provider, model, dimension):

  • local and openai with OpenAI's own models know the dimension.
  • openai_compatible knows it only when you write dimension:.
  • An instance reports its model attribute (or its class name) and the dimension: of the section, if any.

When the dimension is unknown, the engine embeds the text "dimension probe" once, the first time it needs the dimension, and keeps the answer for the engine's life. Building the engine never calls the model. Writing dimension: skips that one call; it must be what the model returns.

docs.title: Writing a provider
docs.text:
A plugin implements nl2sql.embeddings.EmbeddingsProvider, interface version 2, and registers it under the nl2sql.embeddings entry point group or with registry.add_embeddings (see the registry):

from nl2sql.embeddings import EmbeddingInfo


class MyProvider:
    interface_version = 2
    default_model = "my-model"
    requires = ("my_sdk",)
    install_hint = 'pip install "nl2sql-my-embeddings"'

    def create(self, cfg):
        """The LangChain embeddings object for ``cfg``. No model call; ValueError for a bad section."""
        ...

    def describe(self, cfg):
        """What ``create(cfg)`` embeds with. None as the dimension means "probe it"."""
        return EmbeddingInfo("mine", cfg.model or self.default_model, cfg.dimension)

docs.title: Switching providers
docs.text: Switching providers or models needs a re-index, and nothing more. Different embedding models produce different vectors, so each model has its own index namespace, nl2sql__<model slug>__<dimension>. After a change the new model's namespace is empty: check() and nl2sql doctor report the index missing, and nl2sql index builds it. The old model's namespace is kept, so switching back finds it built; nl2sql index prune drops the ones you no longer need. See Storage → The index.

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text:
A hook is your code, called at six fixed points of every run. At each point it may let the run go on, change what the run carries (before the validator only), stop it, or (at execute.before) ask for a person's approval. Hooks apply to every run: a generated answer and a verified query, from the Python API, the CLI and nl2sql-api alike. None ships built in.

The design is Wave A, section 6.

docs.title: The six points
docs.text:
flowchart TD
  Q["question"] --> P1(["run.before"])
  P1 --> CM["curated matcher"]
  CM -->|"no match"| RES["datasource resolver"]
  RES --> P2(["datasources.after"])
  P2 --> DEC["decomposer"]
  DEC --> PL["planner, or the plan cache"]
  PL --> P3(["plan.after"])
  P3 --> VAL["logical validator"]
  VAL --> GEN["generator"]
  GEN --> P4(["execute.before"])
  CM -->|"verified query"| P4
  P4 --> EX["executor"]
  EX --> P5(["execute.after"])
  P5 --> AGG["aggregator"]
  AGG --> ANS["answer synthesizer"]
  ANS --> P6(["answer.after"])
Point When The hook sees (beyond question, user, trace_id) It may answer run.before Once, before the first step datasource_id, execute Allow, Modify(question=...), Deny datasources.after The resolver chose its datasources datasource_ids Allow, Modify(datasource_ids=...) (a subset only), Deny plan.after Per sub-query and attempt, on the planner's or the plan cache's plan sub_query, plan Allow, Modify(plan=...), Deny execute.before Per sub-query, before the adapter runs the SQL datasource_id, sql, params, tables Allow, Deny, NeedsApproval execute.after Per sub-query, after it ran result: columns, row count, truncated; never rows Allow, Deny answer.after The answer is written, before it is returned; with answer=False there is no answer and final_answer is None, but the point still runs final_answer, results (summaries) Allow, Deny

tables are datasource.schema.table. A field a point does not have is None. The context is frozen and holds copies of the run's plan, caller and values: a hook that changes one in place changes nothing. A hook changes the run only through Modify. ctx.conversation_id is set when the run is a conversation's turn.

Modify before the validator, deny only after. A plan a hook changed is validated like any other, so a hook can never slip in what the policies or the validator refuse. datasources.after may only remove datasources; the resolver checks what is left against the caller's role again. After the validator nothing may change the SQL, the plan or the result.

The answer sanity checks' probes are not hooked. After a sub-query runs, the executor may send small checking queries of its own (does a filter value exist, did a join repeat rows; see the executor's sanity checks). They run outside execute.before and execute.after. So when any hook is attached at execute.before, no probe runs at all: SQL a hook gates never has unseen SQL beside it. settings.pipeline.sanity_checks: false turns the checks off entirely.

Eval seeding is hooked; regenerate is not. engine.evals.seed (Benchmark your own database) runs SQL a model proposed, so each draft's SQL passes execute.before and execute.after like a question's: every hook sees it (an approval hook, a cost guard), and a deny, a hook failure or a NeedsApproval drops the draft (dropped_hooked). execute.after gets a summary of the first row only (seeding reads one row to see that the query returns any), so its row_count is a floor and truncated is true. engine.evals.regenerate runs SQL a person reviewed and approved (a suite's gold sql and alt_sql) and calls no hook.

The verified path has no routing and no plan, so only run.before, execute.before, execute.after and answer.after apply. A deny there ends the run; it does not fall back to the generated path. A plan-only run (execute=False) never reaches the execute.* points.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
• Order. Hooks run in the order of the hooks list. A Modify replaces the fields it sets and the next hook sees the result. The first Deny (or NeedsApproval) ends the point; later hooks are not asked.
  • A deny ends the run with the error HOOK_DENIED (never retried), whose message is the hook's reason. A run a hook ended carries none of its data: no answer, no rows, no artifact references, no result manifest, and its saved results cannot be read by its trace_id either (see What withholding guarantees).
  • Streaming. While any hook is attached at answer.after, stream_query does not stream the answer as it is written (no answer.delta events), and holds the result.manifest event until the hooks allowed the answer; on a deny it is never sent. The answer arrives whole in run.finished.
  • A sub-query deny. At a per-sub-query point (plan.after, execute.before, execute.after), Deny(reason, scope="sub_query") drops only that sub-query: the run goes on without it and the answer's warnings say what went unanswered. A sub-query that feeds a join or compare cannot be dropped alone, so its whole group is dropped. If nothing is left, the run ends with HOOK_DENIED.
  • Hooks fail closed. An exception, a return value that is not a decision, or a decision the point does not allow (a Modify at execute.before, a NeedsApproval at plan.after) is a hook error: the run ends with HOOK_FAILED, whose message names only the hook and the point; the exception's text goes to the log and to hook.decision, never to the caller. With on_error: open, an exception is logged and counts as Allow; a disallowed decision still fails, because it is a bug in the hook, not an outage.
  • Approval. NeedsApproval at execute.before (on the generated or the verified path) ends the run with status: "needs_approval", the error NEEDS_APPROVAL and an ApprovalRequest per pending sub-query in approvals_needed. Re-running the question as the asker with approvals=[Approval(request=..., by=<the approver>)] pins what was approved and generates the SQL again; the engine accepts the approval only if the request is unedited, the question and the asker are this run's, the hash of the new SQL matches, and the approver holds one of the hook's approver_roles (by default policies.admin_roles). An accepted approval counts as Allow (hook.decision with decision: "approved" and the approver), and the next hook at the point still runs. A hook also sees the run's approvals as ctx.approvals. See Query API → Approval.
  • Timeouts are the hook's own; the pipeline's timeout_s bounds the run.
  • Events. Every hook asked publishes hook.decision (hook, point, decision, reason, sub_query_id, approver, seconds).
  • The plan cache keeps the planner's plan, never a hook's change of it; plan.after runs on every cache hit, so a change applies afresh on each run and stops the moment the hook config changes.

docs.title: What withholding guarantees
docs.text:
A run a hook ended (HOOK_DENIED, HOOK_FAILED, NEEDS_APPROVAL, COST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED) returns none of its data, and its saved results cannot be read by its trace_id: engine.results.manifest, page, csv and chart and the REST results routes answer ResultNotFound (404), from run_query, stream_query, nl2sql eval and trace replay alike. This holds while the run is still going too, although a streaming caller has the trace_id from run.started.

Every read of a run's results goes through its manifest, and the manifest is written only once no hook can end the run any more:

  • While a hook is attached at answer.after, the aggregator saves the results but not the manifest. The node that asks answer.after writes it when the hooks allow. A run they deny, or that ends earlier, never has one. If that write fails, the run fails.
  • Without such a hook, nothing can end the run after the aggregator, so the aggregator writes the manifest itself, as soon as the results are saved.
  • A hook at any earlier point that ends the run ends it before the aggregator runs, so there is no manifest.

The parquet files of a run with no manifest stay until retention purges them, but nothing reads them. With a hook at answer.after, a run that crashed or timed out before the hooks ruled has no manifest either, and neither has a run whose answer model failed: the hooks never saw its results, so it returns no result_manifest, no artifact_refs and no rows, and stream_query sends no result.manifest event. Without such a hook that run keeps its results, as nothing was left to withhold them for. The run's trace records the error that ended it, without rows. An approved re-run is a new run with a new trace_id, read as any other.

docs.title: Built-in hooks
docs.text: One hook is built in: policy.cost, the cost rule. The engine builds it from policies.cost (or a role's cost), not from the hooks list, and puts it first at execute.before, ahead of every hook you configure, so an over-limit query never reaches your hook. Its approvers are policies.admin_roles. Its Deny ends the run with COST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED rather than HOOK_DENIED, and its hook.decision events name policy.cost. Without a cost block it is not built, and execute.before is as you configured it.

docs.title: Write one
docs.text:
# corp_hooks.py: a hook that keeps the payroll database out of the afternoon.
from datetime import datetime
from typing import ClassVar

from pydantic import BaseModel

from nl2sql.hooks import Allow, Deny, HookContext


class QuietHoursConfig(BaseModel):
    datasource: str                 # the datasource it guards
    from_hour: int = 12             # local time
    to_hour: int = 18


class QuietHours:
    interface_version: ClassVar[int] = 1
    config_model: ClassVar[type] = QuietHoursConfig
    points: ClassVar[frozenset] = frozenset({"execute.before"})

    def __init__(self, cfg: QuietHoursConfig) -> None:
        self.cfg = cfg

    @classmethod
    def from_config(cls, cfg: QuietHoursConfig) -> "QuietHours":
        return cls(cfg)

    def __call__(self, ctx: HookContext):
        busy = self.cfg.from_hour <= datetime.now().hour < self.cfg.to_hour
        if ctx.datasource_id == self.cfg.datasource and busy:
            return Deny(reason=f"{ctx.datasource_id} is closed to questions until "
                               f"{self.cfg.to_hour}:00.", scope="sub_query")
        return Allow()

Register it, either in code or as an entry point in your package:

from nl2sql import NL2SQL, Registry

registry = Registry.default()
registry.add_hook("quiet_hours", QuietHours)       # or @registry.hook("quiet_hours")
engine = NL2SQL.from_config(registry=registry)

[project.entry-points."nl2sql.hooks"]
quiet_hours = "corp_hooks:QuietHours"

docs.title: Configure it
docs.text:
# nl2sql.yaml
hooks: { file: hooks.yaml }

# hooks.yaml: a list; order matters
- type: quiet_hours
  points: [execute.before]        # a subset of the hook's own points; all of them by default
  on_error: closed                # closed (the default) | open
  approver_roles: [dba]           # who may approve its NeedsApproval; default policies.admin_roles
  datasource: payroll             # the hook's own keys, checked by its config_model

A point the hook does not declare, an unknown type or a key its config_model rejects is a ConfigError when the engine is built, naming hooks[<i>]. In code, a HookConfig or any callable object works:

from nl2sql import Config, HookConfig
from nl2sql.hooks import Allow, Modify

def tag_year(ctx):
    return Modify(question=ctx.question + " (calendar year)") if ctx.point == "run.before" else Allow()

tag_year.points = frozenset({"run.before"})
Config(..., hooks=[HookConfig(type="quiet_hours", datasource="payroll"), tag_year])

An object runs at its points (all six when it has none), named by its name attribute or its function or class name.

Kind Entry point group Interface Version Built-ins hook nl2sql.hooks nl2sql.hooks.Hook 1 none configurable; policy.cost is built in from policies.cost

docs.title: Knowledge
docs.text:
The glossary is what people know about their data and the database does not say: table and column descriptions, synonyms, column roles, units, grains and code values, joins the database does not declare, business terms, prose rules and example questions. It is written in glossary.yaml and read by a knowledge source; the knowledge section lists the sources.

Release 0.8

The engine loads, merges, shows and exports knowledge from release 0.8, and the planner and refiner read it (Wave B's K2): descriptions, roles, units, grains, code values and glossary joins in the schema block, matched terms and rules in [BUSINESS_CONTEXT]. It reaches the index too (K3): the chosen descriptions, the terms, the joins and the examples are index entries, and nl2sql index --refresh brings them up to date after an edit without reading the schema. See Wave B, sections 3 and 4, and the schema retriever.

docs.title: The section
docs.text:
# nl2sql.yaml
knowledge: { file: knowledge.yaml }

# knowledge.yaml: a list, in precedence order
- type: yaml
  path: glossary.yaml             # relative to nl2sql.yaml
- type: corp_catalog              # a plugin; its config_model checks the rest
  url: "${env:CATALOG_URL}"

from nl2sql import Config, KnowledgeSourceConfig

Config(..., knowledge=[KnowledgeSourceConfig(type="yaml", path="glossary.yaml"), MySource()])
Rule Detail No section No knowledge: the pipeline is 0.7's. nl2sql init writes knowledge.yaml naming one yaml source and a glossary.yaml with one empty block per datasource; nl2sql init --demo writes the demo glossary. Loaded at build and on reload only Each source's load() runs when the engine is built and on engine.knowledge.reload(), never during a run. Fails closed at build A source that cannot be built or loaded, a missing glossary.yaml, or a text longer than settings.knowledge.item_max_chars is a ConfigError naming the source and the item. Fails open on reload A reload that fails keeps the previous knowledge live; the source's error says why. A config built in code A relative path is read from the current folder. Objects skip the registry A source object in code (one with load) is used as given, named by its type attribute or its class.

docs.title: glossary.yaml
docs.text:
version: 1
datasources:
  chinook:
    tables:
      Invoice:
        description: One row per customer invoice. Total includes tax.
      InvoiceLine:
        description: One row per track sold on an invoice.
        notes: Refunds are not recorded anywhere.     # for people; never sent to a model
    columns:
      Invoice.Total:
        description: Invoice total in US dollars, tax included.
        synonyms: [invoice amount, bill total]
        role: money
        unit: USD
      Invoice.InvoiceDate:
        grain: day                                   # role: date is derived from the type
      Track.MediaTypeId:
        role: enum
        values: {"1": MPEG audio file, "2": Protected AAC audio file}
    joins:
      - from: Track.MediaTypeId
        to: MediaType.MediaTypeId
        cardinality: many-to-one
    terms:
      - term: revenue
        synonyms: [sales, turnover]
        definition: Sum of InvoiceLine.UnitPrice times InvoiceLine.Quantity. Excludes tax.
        columns: [InvoiceLine.UnitPrice, InvoiceLine.Quantity]
    rules:
      - id: no_test_customers
        text: Customers whose email ends in @example.com are test accounts; leave them out of counts and sums.
        tables: [Customer]
    examples:
      - Which genres sell best in Germany?
Item Fields A table description, notes A column (table.column) description, notes, synonyms, role (identifier, enum, money, quantity, date, text), unit, grain (second to year), values (a code, written as a string, and its meaning; on role: enum only) A join from, to (table.column, or a list of them for a composite key), cardinality (default unknown), notes A term term, synonyms, definition, columns, tables A rule id (a slug, unique in its datasource), text, tables (empty: every sub-query on the datasource) An example a question

Every model is strict: an unknown key is an error. Every text is at most settings.knowledge.item_max_chars (500) characters; a longer one is a load error naming the item, so nothing is silently cut. Every name (a table, a column, a code, a rule id, a term's tables and columns) is at most 255 characters, and the yaml source reads a glossary file of at most 5 MB. notes is for people: it is shown by knowledge show and never sent to a model.

docs.title: Names
docs.text:
A table is named as preferred_tables names it: the bare name or schema.table, case ignored. A column is table.column or schema.table.column. Names are resolved against the datasource's indexed schema when the knowledge is used, not when it is loaded:

Case What happens Resolves to one table or column Used Resolves to nothing (a typo, a dropped column) Not used; a problem in knowledge show, never an error in a run A bare name matching tables in two schemas Not used; the problem says to write schema.table A join whose two sides' types cannot be compared (a date against a number or a boolean) Not used; the problem names both types

A schema drift check (engine.index.check) lists the glossary items that named a dropped table or column in its impact's glossary_items.

docs.title: Precedence
docs.text:
Several sources are merged in config order. A single value (a description, a role, a unit) is the first source's that sets it; lists (synonyms, terms, rules, joins, examples) are unioned, a duplicate (the same term name, rule id or join, case ignored) kept from the first. Each item records the source it came from.

A table or column then has at most one description, and each column one role, chosen in this order:

Origin Where it is kept Who wrote it knowledge A knowledge source, in config order A person database The table or column comment the adapter read The data owner, in the database derived Nowhere: computed from the schema. A role only: identifier for a primary or foreign key column, date for a temporal type The schema itself

Each datasource's merged knowledge has a digest (the SHA-256 of its canonical JSON), shown by knowledge show and published by knowledge.loaded.

docs.title: Who sees what
docs.text:
Every method takes the caller as a required keyword (user_context), with no admin default. A caller sees only what its scope reaches: an item that names a table it cannot read (a table, a column of one, either side of a join, a term's or a rule's tables or columns), or whose text mentions such a table by name (a whole word, case ignored), is left out. The texts checked are every free text and every name an item carries, a rule's id and an enum column's codes included. The names checked are the datasource's indexed tables the caller cannot read, plus every table one of its roles denies by name, so a table kept out of the index is covered too. Knowledge therefore never names a hidden table by its exact name.

What the check cannot catch: a paraphrase ("the pay table"), a plural or singular ("salary" for salaries), and a name inside a longer identifier (salaries_history), as well as a table hidden only by a wildcard pattern and not indexed. The validator still refuses any plan on the table.

Checking names against the scope needs the datasource's indexed schema, so a datasource that is not indexed yet shows nothing but that problem.

Knowledge is data, never instructions: it is validated as data when it loads, export writes it with a safe YAML dumper, and it reaches a model only as JSON values, filtered by the caller's scope (see Knowledge Is Data). A glossary join between two tables the caller may read is a relationship the validator accepts, so a database without declared keys can be joined. A changed glossary changes the datasource's knowledge digest, which keys the plan cache: the next question plans again.

docs.title: The facade and the CLI
docs.text:
Method What it does engine.knowledge.sources(*, user_context) Each source (KnowledgeSourceInfo): its type, item counts per datasource the caller reaches (counting what the caller may see), sha256, loaded_at and the last reload's error. The error quotes the file (its path, its lines, the tables it names), so only a caller who may reload (an admin role, or any caller under allow_all) sees it; anyone else gets a fixed text saying the reload failed and an admin can see why engine.knowledge.show(datasource_id=None, *, user_context) The merged knowledge as the engine uses it (DatasourceKnowledgeView): knowledge with derived roles and database comments filled in, origins and sources per item, digest and problems engine.knowledge.export(path=None, *, datasource_ids=None, user_context) The knowledge-source items the caller may see as one canonical glossary.yaml, returned and, with path, written there. It refuses to write over a config file or a knowledge source's own file. Derived roles and database comments are not exported. engine.knowledge.profile(datasource_ids=None, *, user_context, draft=False, max_cost_usd=None) Probes the indexed schema for joins the database does not declare and for column roles, and files them in the review queue; one ProfileReport per datasource the caller reaches. See Schema Profiler. draft=True also drafts table and column descriptions with the profiler model, as proposals, under max_cost_usd. engine.knowledge.reload(*, user_context) Loads every source again and swaps atomically; needs an admin role (policies.admin_roles; any caller under allow_all). Runs in flight keep the knowledge they started with. 
from nl2sql import NL2SQL, UserContext

engine = NL2SQL.from_config("nl2sql.yaml")
analyst = UserContext(roles=["analyst"])
for view in engine.knowledge.show(user_context=analyst):
    print(view.datasource_id, [t.term for t in view.knowledge.terms], view.problems)
Command Calls nl2sql knowledge show [--datasource ID] --as ROLE show: a readable listing, each item with its origin; problems last, exit 1 when there are any nl2sql knowledge export [--datasource ID] [--out FILE] --as ROLE export, to stdout or --out nl2sql knowledge sources --as ROLE sources nl2sql profile [--datasource ID] --as ROLE profile, then the open profiler proposals; nl2sql index --profile --as ROLE indexes first

--as (repeatable) and --user build the caller. Without --as the role is policies.default_role; with neither the command refuses. Under allow_all no role is needed.

docs.title: The canonical form
docs.text: glossary.yaml belongs to people, and the engine rewrites it only when a reviewer accepts a proposal (the review queue). It then writes the canonical form: a fixed header comment, the keys in the models' order, tables, columns and code values sorted by name, lists in their own order. Comments are not kept, so write remarks in a notes: field. The write refuses when the file changed since the engine loaded it, writes through a symlink (the link is kept), and replaces the file atomically: the new text goes to a temporary file, flushed to disk and given the file's mode, which is renamed over it. A file another program holds open (on Windows) is refused with a review error saying to close it. export writes the same canonical form, and the demo glossary is kept in it.

docs.title: The KnowledgeSource interface
docs.text:
A plugin reads knowledge from elsewhere (a wiki, a data catalog). It depends on the SDK only (nl2sql_sdk.knowledge) and is installed under the nl2sql.knowledge_sources entry point group:

from pathlib import Path
from typing import ClassVar
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict
from nl2sql_sdk.knowledge import Glossary


class CatalogConfig(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")
    url: str


class CatalogSource:
    interface_version: ClassVar[int] = 1
    config_model: ClassVar[type[BaseModel]] = CatalogConfig

    @classmethod
    def from_config(cls, cfg: CatalogConfig, *, folder: Path) -> "CatalogSource":
        return cls(cfg.url)

    def __init__(self, url: str):
        self.url = url

    def load(self) -> Glossary:
        return Glossary.model_validate(fetch_glossary(self.url))

A source only reads. The engine checks every text a source returns against settings.knowledge.item_max_chars, and a source that raises is a load error. See The SDK.

docs.title: LLM Configuration
docs.text:
The llm section of nl2sql.yaml names the model every agent uses, and optional per-agent overrides. nl2sql init writes it to llm.yaml with the provider's default model and no key.

# llm.yaml
provider: openai
model: gpt-5.4
temperature: 0.0
# api_key is optional: without it the provider's standard variable
# (OPENAI_API_KEY) is read. Write it to read another one:
# api_key: "${env:TEAM_OPENAI_KEY}"
agents:
  ast_planner:         { provider: anthropic, model: claude-opus-5, temperature: null }
  profiler: { model: gpt-5.4-mini }
prices:
  gpt-4o: { input: 2.5, cached_input: 1.25, output: 10 }

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
The section is flat: its keys are the top-level agent's.

Field Default Meaning provider required openai, anthropic, openai_compatible, its presets openrouter and ollama, or a provider a plugin registers; see Providers. A misspelt or uninstalled one is a ConfigError with "did you mean". model required The model identifier. In Python it may be a LangChain chat model object instead (LLM(model=ChatOpenAI(...))), with no provider. temperature 0.0 A float, or null to send no temperature at all; see Temperature. api_key none Without it, the provider's standard variable (OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY) is read. With it, a ${env:VAR} or ${provider:key} reference (or a literal, which is not recommended). The reference is resolved when the client is built, never at load. base_url the provider's An endpoint override. Required for openai_compatible; see Any other OpenAI-style server. structured_output the provider's tool_calling, json_schema or json_mode: how structured answers are asked for. See Structured output. parse_retries 1 How many times a structured answer that does not parse is asked for again, with what was wrong. 0 asks once. See Parse-and-retry. max_tokens the provider's The most tokens one answer may use. Unset, Anthropic gets 16,000 and the other providers send none. timeout_s the client library's Seconds one request may take. max_retries the client library's Network and rate-limit retries, done by the client library. headers {} HTTP headers sent with every request, such as a gateway's team or routing header. A value may be a ${env:VAR} or ${provider:key} reference, resolved when the client is built. Values never print: not in a repr, a log, engine.llm.list() or the cache key. agents {} Per-node overrides, keyed by node name; see Per-node models. prices {} Per-model prices per million tokens; see Prices.

engine.check() reports every agent whose key does not resolve, without calling a model.

docs.title: Providers and wire types
docs.text:
The engine is model-agnostic. A provider is a preset: an endpoint, the environment variable its key comes from, and the wire type it speaks, which is the HTTP protocol on the wire. Everything that differs between wire types lives in one adapter per wire type, in nl2sql/llm/wires/:

wire type adapter client providers openai wires/openai.py ChatOpenAI openai, openai_compatible, openrouter, ollama anthropic wires/anthropic.py ChatAnthropic (the anthropic extra) anthropic

Each adapter owns four things, so neither the registry nor the nodes know which wire they are on:

openai wire anthropic wire Client ConfiguredChatOpenAI, seed=42 CachingChatAnthropic, max_tokens=16000 unless the agent sets one Structured output the agent's structured_output the agent's structured_output Prompt caching nothing to mark: OpenAI caches long prefixes by itself cache_control on the last system block Usage prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens → cached; no cache writes reported cache reads and writes, see Query API → usage

Both adapters also turn a model's HTTP 400 on temperature into the same "set temperature: null" error (see Temperature).

The built-in providers are deliberately few: openai, anthropic and openai_compatible. openrouter and ollama are named presets of openai_compatible: a fixed endpoint and key variable, and no code of their own.

provider wire type key variable base_url default structured_output openai openai OPENAI_API_KEY optional tool_calling anthropic anthropic ANTHROPIC_API_KEY optional tool_calling openai_compatible openai none: write api_key (usually ${env:...}) if the server needs one required json_schema openrouter preset of openai_compatible OPENROUTER_API_KEY fixed: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 tool_calling ollama preset of openai_compatible none fixed: http://localhost:11434/v1 (a base_url may override it) tool_calling

There is no Azure provider: Azure OpenAI's v1 endpoint is openai_compatible (see the base_url table). Any other name raises ValueError: Unsupported LLM provider, naming the valid providers. Every agent picks its own provider, so one question can use several; see Per-node models.

docs.title: Adding a provider
docs.text:
• Another OpenAI-style server needs no new provider: use openai_compatible with its base_url (see Any other OpenAI-style server).
  • Anything else (Azure with Entra ID sign-in, Bedrock, Gemini) is a plugin: a class implementing LLMProvider (nl2sql/llm/providers.py, interface version 2: interface_version = 2, label, api_key_env, requires, install_hint, structured_output and create(agent)), registered with registry.add_llm or under the nl2sql.llms entry point group. A provider built for another interface version is rejected when it is loaded.
  • A new wire type inside the engine (Gemini, Bedrock) is one new adapter module in nl2sql/llm/wires/ implementing the Wire protocol in wires/base.py (build_client, structured_output_method, mark_cache, read_usage), one entry in WIRES in wires/__init__.py, and presets that name it. Add a case to CASES in tests/unit/test_llm_wire_contract.py. The contract suite then runs every structured-output call, usage, cache and key test against it.

docs.title: OpenAI
docs.text:
nl2sql init and nl2sql demo write gpt-5.4 as the OpenAI default. On the owner's account (probed 2026-09-20) it accepted temperature: 0 with a limit of 500,000 tokens per minute, against 30,000 for the previous default gpt-4o - less than one question with a single retry needs (about 33,500 tokens).

Every node asks for structured output as a tool call, OpenAI's default structured_output: it is what OpenRouter's and Ollama's models support most widely too. See Structured output.

provider: openai
model: gpt-5.4
temperature: 0.0

docs.title: Anthropic (Claude)
docs.text:
Claude runs on Anthropic's own API through ChatAnthropic, not through an OpenAI-compatibility shim: prompt caching and reliable structured output need Anthropic's native API. langchain-anthropic is an optional extra:

pip install "nl2sql-engine[anthropic]"

Selecting provider: anthropic without it fails on the first LLM call with ValueError: ... Install the anthropic extra: pip install "nl2sql-engine[anthropic]", and nl2sql doctor reports the missing extra.

provider: anthropic
model: claude-opus-5
temperature: null          # Claude Opus 5 and Sonnet 5 reject any temperature

nl2sql init --provider anthropic and nl2sql demo write claude-opus-5 as the Claude default, with temperature: null. Current models:

model temperature minimum cacheable prefix claude-opus-5 rejected (HTTP 400): use null 512 tokens claude-sonnet-5 rejected (HTTP 400): use null 1,024 tokens claude-haiku-4-5 accepted, e.g. 0.0 4,096 tokens

These come from Anthropic's documented model rules, not from a probe on a real account. A rejected temperature fails with the same "set temperature: null" error as OpenAI (see Temperature).

How the engine uses it:

  • Structured output is a forced tool call (with_structured_output's function_calling method, structured_output: tool_calling), for every node. Anthropic's native JSON outputs (output_config.format) do not accept recursive schemas, and the planner's PlanModel is recursive; neither does strict tool use (strict: true). Claude now and then nests a tool call's arguments one level down under a key of its own choosing ({"input": {...}}, {"query": {...}}, {"dtype": {...}}). Recording runs on claude-opus-5 failed the decomposer this way on up to 9 of 20 questions, and no other node. The root cause was the decomposer's tool: it went out with an empty description and no field descriptions, while its prompt asked for "JSON only" rather than a tool call. DecomposerResponse now describes itself and each top-level field ("call this tool with the decomposition itself as the arguments ... do not wrap them"), and the prompt asks for the tool call. As a safety net the wire also unwraps that shape before any node parses it: a dict with exactly one key the schema does not declare, holding an object with every required field and at least one declared one. Any other malformed answer still fails validation as before. A new node's response model should carry a docstring and field descriptions for the same reason.
  • Prompt caching. The resolver, decomposer, planner and refiner send a stable system message and a variable human message. On the anthropic wire only, the last system block carries cache_control: {"type": "ephemeral"} (a 5-minute cache). Anthropic renders tools, then system, then messages, so the breakpoint caches the tool schema and the system prompt; the question follows it. The answer synthesizer sends no system message, so nothing is marked. Other providers send no cache_control.
  • Whether a prefix clears the minimum. On Chinook the planner's cached prefix is its system prompt (about 3.5k tokens, most of it the retrieved schema) plus the PlannerAnswer tool schema (about 2k): above every model's minimum. The decomposer's (about 0.7k of system prompt plus a 1.4k tool schema) and the refiner's (about 2.7k, no tool) clear Opus 5's 512 and Sonnet 5's 1,024 but not Haiku 4.5's 4,096, so on Haiku they are silently not cached. The resolver's answerability check (datasourceresolver) is marked the same way, but its prefix (about 260 tokens of system prompt plus a small tool schema) is below every Claude model's minimum, so it is never cached. The decomposer's prefix is the same for every question; the planner's and refiner's include the retrieved tables, so they hit when a sub-query retrieves the same tables again (a retry, or a similar question).
  • max_tokens is 16,000 per call unless the agent sets max_tokens: every node call but the streamed answer is non-streaming, and the SDK refuses a non-streaming call whose max_tokens could outlast its timeout.
  • Usage. Cache reads and writes are reported as cached_input_tokens and cache_write_input_tokens, with each input token counted once (see Query API → usage). A cache write costs 1.25x the model's input rate (Anthropic's price for a 5-minute write, the only kind the engine asks for): the price table's Claude rows say so, and an llm.prices row without its own cache_write gets it from the wire.

nl2sql demo --record records Claude too: with an Anthropic key the recording proxy speaks Anthropic's Messages API to https://api.anthropic.com, and stores each answer under the same name and question an OpenAI one would get, so replay (which answers on the OpenAI wire) serves it unchanged. The hosted demo's shipped recordings are made this way; see Hosted demo.

docs.title: OpenRouter
docs.text:
A preset of openai_compatible. OpenRouter is an OpenAI-compatible gateway: a single API key reaches Anthropic, Google, Meta and hundreds of other models. Models are named <vendor>/<model>, for example anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5 or google/gemini-2.5-pro.

provider: openrouter
model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5
temperature: 0.0

docs.title: Ollama
docs.text:
A preset of openai_compatible. Ollama exposes an OpenAI-compatible API on http://localhost:11434/v1, so it needs no api_key and no base_url: start the daemon, pull a model, and point llm.yaml at it.

provider: ollama
model: llama3.1
temperature: 0.0

Set base_url if the daemon is not on localhost:11434 (a remote box, or a different port).

Ollama is supported at the transport level, not guaranteed end to end

The pipeline drives every model through with_structured_output, and the AST planner's target is PlannerAnswer, whose PlanModel is a recursive Pydantic schema whose Expr references itself. That is a demanding structured-output target, and small local models often handle it poorly: expect malformed plans, empty fields or repeated refiner loops depending on the model you choose. Whether a given local model works is a property of that model, not of the transport. Prefer the largest instruct model with reliable JSON-schema/tool-calling support that your hardware allows, and validate against your own questions before relying on it.

Ollama also does not make the demo run fully offline: embeddings are a separate path (see below), and the demo's other steps are unchanged.

docs.title: Temperature
docs.text:
Each agent sends exactly the temperature its config names, and seed=42:

  • Omitted, it is 0.0, sent with every call. This reduces variance; it does not make output reproducible (see Determinism).
  • temperature: null sends no temperature parameter at all, so the model uses its own default.

Use null for models that accept only their default. Probed on 2026-09-20 with the engine's parameters of the time (temperature=0, seed=42, strict json_schema; the planner now sends a tool call instead):

model temperature: 0 gpt-5.4, gpt-5.4-mini, gpt-4.1, gpt-4.1-mini, gpt-4o accepted gpt-5.5, gpt-5-mini rejected: HTTP 400 "Unsupported value: 'temperature' does not support 0.0 with this model. Only the default (1) value is supported."

The rejected models accepted the same call without temperature (still with seed=42), so only the temperature needs to go. When a model rejects it, the first LLM call fails with an error that names the model and the agent and says what to set, instead of the provider's raw response:

ValueError: Model 'gpt-5.5' (LLM agent 'default') rejected the temperature
parameter (HTTP 400: Unsupported value: 'temperature' does not support 0.0 with
this model. Only the default (1) value is supported.) Set 'temperature: null'
for agent 'default' in the LLM config file so no temperature is sent to this
model.

Nothing is retried without the parameter: what the config says is what is sent.

langchain-openai would drop it silently

langchain-openai removes any temperature other than 1 from a model whose name starts with gpt-5 before the request is built, so gpt-5.4 would never receive the 0.0 it accepts. The registry sets the configured value after the client is constructed, so the config - not the model name - decides what is sent.

docs.title: Per-node models
docs.text:
The six pipeline nodes that call a model, the profiler's drafts, eval seeding and the conversation each have an agent. An agent not under agents runs on the top level:

agents key node curated_matcher picks the verified query that answers the question, if any (one short call; only when curated answers are configured and a candidate clears the floor) datasource_resolver checks that the connected data can answer the question at all (one short call; refuses with QUESTION_NOT_ANSWERABLE) decomposer splits the question into sub-queries ast_planner writes the query plan (the largest prompt: it carries the schema) refiner explains a failed plan so the planner can retry answer_synthesizer writes the final answer from the rows profiler drafts table and column descriptions as proposals for review, never written into the index or the schema (optional; nl2sql index calls no model; only nl2sql profile --draft or profile(draft=True) runs it, under profiler.max_cost_usd, and its model must have a price in llm.prices) eval_seeder drafts eval questions with typed plans during nl2sql eval seed (Benchmark your own database) conversation leads a conversation turn: reads the history and either replies or calls a tool, one call per step (Conversations): it chooses a reply or the ask tool, never writes SQL and never sees rows. A small model is enough. A config that pins every agent's model should add it.

Any other key is an error with "did you mean". An agent takes every field it sets (provider, model, temperature, api_key, base_url, structured_output, parse_retries, max_tokens, timeout_s, max_retries, headers) and inherits the rest from the top level. Inheritance follows which fields were written, so temperature: null on an agent still means "send none". Each node can be on a different provider, and so a different wire type. For example, plan on Claude and run everything else on OpenAI, with one cheaper node that only accepts its default temperature:

provider: openai
model: gpt-5.4
temperature: 0.0
agents:
  ast_planner:
    provider: anthropic
    model: claude-opus-5
    temperature: null        # Claude Opus 5 rejects a temperature
  answer_synthesizer:
    model: gpt-5-mini        # on OpenAI, inherited
    temperature: null        # gpt-5-mini rejects temperature=0

Here curated_matcher, datasource_resolver, decomposer and refiner run on the top level. With no api_key, the planner reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and the others OPENAI_API_KEY. Each node keeps its own key, endpoint and cache behaviour: the planner's system prompt is cache-marked for Anthropic, the others are sent unmarked to OpenAI. The model each call actually used is recorded per node in QueryResult.usage.calls and in a run trace's llm.by_node (see Debugging).

In the demo, the playground's Settings page writes exactly these entries into the demo folder's llm.yaml. Choosing a provider and a model for a step adds an agents: entry with provider, model and the temperature that model takes: 0.0, or null for gpt-5.5, gpt-5-mini, claude-opus-5 and claude-sonnet-5. A step on the default's provider takes the default's base_url and api_key; a step on another provider names no key (its standard variable is read) and no base_url. A key saved on the page goes to the demo's .env. Choosing "Default" removes the entry. The running engine reloads its llm section from nl2sql.yaml, so the change applies to the next question. The page offers the providers and models in VERIFIED_MODELS (nl2sql/llm/providers.py), OpenAI and Anthropic for now, and a provider only once its key is saved. See the Settings page.

The playground's Pipeline page reads the same configuration back: it lists every step of a run and, for each of the six a model decides, the provider and model it is set to use, then what it actually spent once a question has been asked. It is served by GET /api/pipeline from engine.about(), whose steps (nl2sql.pipeline.steps) take their six model steps from LLM_AGENTS rather than repeating the table above. See the Pipeline page.

On the hosted demo (nl2sql demo --hosted) the same choice is offered and nothing is written at all. The visitor keeps one key per provider and a model per step in their own browser tab, and both travel with each question: a key per provider in a header of its own, and the choices in one compact X-NL2SQL-Models header, {"astplanner": "anthropic:claude-opus-5"} (the header names a step by its registry agent name, LLM_AGENTS in nl2sql/llm/providers.py). The server validates every name against LLM_AGENTS and VERIFIED_MODELS, builds each step's client for that one request from the key for the provider it names, caches none of them, and refuses with 400 -- naming the step and the provider -- when a step is on a provider the request brought no key for. See Hosted demo.

When nl2sql demo picks replay or live mode at start-up it points the top level of llm.yaml at the chosen provider. In replay and record mode every agents: entry follows, with the local replay server or recording proxy as base_url and the placeholder api_key (replay, proxy) it accepts, because one fake or proxy serves every call; no key goes into the environment. In live mode a step keeps the provider it was given; only an entry with no provider, or one left on the replay endpoint, follows the top level, and no api_key is written. Moving an entry between OpenAI and Anthropic replaces a model the new provider does not serve (a gpt- model on Anthropic, a claude- one on OpenAI) with that provider's default and its temperature. Every provider key saved in the demo's .env is loaded at start-up, so each step finds its own.

docs.title: Any other OpenAI-style server (openai_compatible)
docs.text:
openai_compatible is any server with an OpenAI-style chat API. Its base_url is required, and it reads no key variable: write api_key (usually ${env:...}) if the server needs one. Without one it sends a placeholder, because the OpenAI client refuses to start without a key; it never sends OPENAI_API_KEY, which belongs to OpenAI.

# llm.yaml
provider: openai_compatible
base_url: http://vllm:8000/v1
model: qwen3-32b
api_key: "${env:VLLM_KEY}"          # optional for this provider
structured_output: json_schema      # the default for openai_compatible
max_tokens: 8000
timeout_s: 60
max_retries: 2
headers: { X-Team: analytics }
agents:
  answer_synthesizer:
    provider: openai_compatible     # Azure OpenAI's v1 endpoint
    base_url: https://my-resource.openai.azure.com/openai/v1/
    api_key: "${env:AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY}"
    model: gpt-5-4-prod             # the Azure deployment name
    structured_output: tool_calling
Server provider base_url model Notes Azure OpenAI (v1 endpoint) openai_compatible https://<resource>.openai.azure.com/openai/v1/ the deployment name api_key: "${env:AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY}"; set structured_output: tool_calling vLLM openai_compatible http://<host>:8000/v1 the served model, e.g. qwen3-32b json_schema works with its guided decoding Ollama ollama preset: http://localhost:11434/v1; set it for another host a pulled model, e.g. llama3.1 no key LiteLLM proxy openai_compatible http://<host>:4000/v1 a model name the proxy routes api_key is the proxy's key, if it has one OpenRouter openrouter preset: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 <vendor>/<model> OPENROUTER_API_KEY

LM Studio, llama.cpp's server and a company gateway are openai_compatible too.

docs.title: Structured output
docs.text:
Every node asks for a typed answer (the plan, the decomposition, the answer). structured_output says how:

structured_output What is sent Use it for tool_calling a forced tool call whose arguments are the answer OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure, OpenRouter, Ollama json_schema a response format carrying the JSON schema, which the server decodes against local servers with schema-guided decoding (vLLM, LM Studio) json_mode JSON mode, with the schema added to the prompt, since JSON mode alone does not carry it a server with neither of the above

Unset, an agent uses its provider's default (the table under Providers). The method is never switched automatically: the agent's setting is what runs.

docs.title: Parse-and-retry
docs.text:
An answer that does not parse (the parser fails, it does not validate against the schema, or the model made no tool call) is asked for again, up to the agent's parse_retries times (default 1). Each retry adds the model's answer and what was wrong with it to the messages:

Your answer did not match the schema: `steps[0].op`: Field required. Answer again with only PlanModel.

If the last answer still does not parse, the node reports MODEL_OUTPUT_INVALID, whose message names the agent and suggests another structured_output or a stronger model; see Error handling.

  • Each retry is a model call of its own, so it is in the run's trace (one more entry in the node's llm_calls) and in its token usage and cost.
  • A streamed answer (the answer synthesizer's, when the run streams) that does not parse is retried without streaming.
  • parse_retries is separate from max_retries, which is the client library's retry of network errors and rate limits.

docs.title: Timeouts, retries and headers
docs.text: timeout_s, max_retries and headers go to the client library (ChatOpenAI or ChatAnthropic) as its timeout, max_retries and default_headers; max_tokens as its max_tokens. Left unset, the client library's own default holds (for Anthropic's max_tokens, 16,000). These retries are the client library's, for network errors and rate limits.

docs.title: Clients are built when the LLM is set
docs.text:
The engine builds every agent's client when it is created, and again when the LLM is replaced, without calling a model. Each engine keeps its clients in its own cache (an LRU of 16), keyed on the agent's resolved settings: every field of the agent, and the API key. The key and each header value enter the cache key only as a SHA-256 digest, so a cache key can be logged and never holds a secret. Agents with equal settings share one client: seven agents on one model build one client.

A missing key does not stop the engine from starting:

  • Building the engine (which nl2sql index, the API and the demo all do) does not require a chat provider key. A machine with no key can still run key-free work such as indexing with embeddings: {provider: local}. That holds for indexing because the profiler pass is genuinely optional: it is skipped, not merely deferred to a later failure.
  • engine.check() reports every agent whose key does not resolve, without calling a model. Using that agent raises the same error, naming the agent, the provider and the environment variable to set:
ValueError: LLM agent 'default' uses provider 'openai', which requires an API
key, but none could be resolved. Set OPENAI_API_KEY ... or in the environment,
or give the agent an 'api_key' in the LLM config file.

The key is read when the clients are built. A key set in the environment after the engine started is used only once the LLM is set again.

Genuine misconfiguration fails immediately: an unknown provider, or an agent with no model.

docs.title: Replacing the LLM at runtime
docs.text:
engine.llm.replace swaps the whole llm section at once, while the engine runs:

from nl2sql import LLM, AgentLLM

change = engine.llm.replace(
    LLM(provider="anthropic", model="claude-sonnet-5-5",
        agents={"ast_planner": AgentLLM(model="claude-opus-5-5")}),
    by=user,          # optional: the UserContext making the change
)
print(change.changes)  # {"default": {"old": "openai/gpt-5.4", "new": "anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5"}, ...}
  • Validated like the file. The new section is checked as the llm section of nl2sql.yaml is: every provider must be registered and installed, and every agent's API key must resolve. If anything is wrong it raises ConfigError and nothing changes. No model is called.
  • Atomic. The new clients are built first, then the engine's LLM and engine.config.llm are swapped together. A query reads the engine's LLM once, when it starts: queries already running finish on the old LLM, and every query that starts afterwards uses the new one. No query mixes the two.
  • Logged and audited. One INFO line on the nl2sql.llm logger and one llm.changed audit record name who made the change (by's user and roles when given, otherwise the entry point, python by default) and, for each agent whose provider or model changed, the old and the new one. They never hold a key, a key reference or a header.
INFO nl2sql.llm: LLM replaced by user=u42 roles=[admin] via api: default: openai/gpt-5.4 -> anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; ast_planner: openai/gpt-5.4 -> anthropic/claude-opus-5-5
  • Not saved. Nothing is written to disk, so a restart goes back to the config file.
  • Cached clients. Swapping back to an earlier LLM reuses the clients built for it. A client that falls out of the cache is closed (its close(), when it has one) once no running query uses it.
  • Plans follow the model. The plan cache key includes the planner's provider and model, so after a swap a plan written by another model is never served. Swapping back hits the old plans again. See Determinism → The plan cache.

replace also takes the section as written in nl2sql.yaml, as a mapping, checked by the same rules as the file. A ${...} reference is kept in a secret field (api_key, a headers value) and is an error anywhere else, so data that did not come from your files never reads the environment. nl2sql-api serves it as the admin-only PUT /api/v1/settings/llm: the body is the section as JSON, and a bad one is HTTP 422 with the ConfigError text. The playground's model switch calls replace too. engine.llm.list() shows the model each agent runs on.

docs.title: Embeddings are a separate path
docs.text: None of Anthropic, OpenRouter or Ollama covers embeddings — they are not routed through LLMRegistry at all. Each engine builds its own embedder from its embeddings section: {provider: local} embeds with the key-free ONNX all-MiniLM-L6-v2 model bundled with chromadb, and {provider: openai} reads OPENAI_API_KEY (or embeddings.api_key). Switching embedding providers requires a re-index.

docs.title: Prices
docs.text:
Every model call is priced, so QueryResult.usage reports a cost, from a dated price table the engine ships (nl2sql/llm/prices.py, USD per million tokens, each row with its source), with prices in the config adding a model or replacing a row (a negotiated rate, a fine-tune):

prices:
  gpt-4o: { input: 2.5, cached_input: 1.25, output: 10 }
Model Input Cached input Cache write Output gpt-5.4 2.50 0.25 2.50 15.00 gpt-5.4-mini 0.75 0.075 0.75 4.50 claude-opus-5 5.00 0.50 6.25 25.00 claude-sonnet-5 2.00 0.20 2.50 10.00 claude-haiku-4-5 1.00 0.10 1.25 5.00

The Claude rows match Anthropic's first-party prices, with the 5-minute cache write (1.25x input; the engine never asks for the 1-hour cache, which costs 2x). The OpenAI rows still need verifying against OpenAI's published prices (owner to confirm); put a row in llm.prices if yours differ.

The table was checked on 2026-09-21; engine.llm.prices() returns it as the engine uses it, llm.prices applied: checked_on, and per model the four rates, verified, source (table or config) and citation.

  • Exact names, overrides first. A call is priced from llm.prices by the model name the provider reports, then by the name configured, and only then from the table, by either name. So a negotiated rate for a deployment alias (acme-gpt) holds even when the provider reports a table model (gpt-5.4), and a dated snapshot the provider reports (gpt-5.4-2026-03-05) is priced by its configured name. Matches are exact: gpt-5.4 never prices gpt-5.4-mini. A rate is never negative.
  • Unknown is null, never zero. A model neither lists has a null cost, and so does any total that includes one of its calls. A token count the provider did not report (a cache read, reasoning tokens) is null too.
  • Each part at its own rate. Cache reads at cached_input, cache writes at cache_write, the rest of the prompt at input, and the output, reasoning tokens included, at output. In a prices row, cached_input defaults to input, and cache_write to input times the wire's write premium: 1.25 for Claude (provider: anthropic, whose 5-minute cache write Anthropic bills at 1.25x input) and 1 for the OpenAI wire.
  • A cost cap needs prices. With settings.pipeline.max_cost_usd set, every model the llm section names must have a price, or the engine does not build (a ConfigError naming each model, with the fix add llm.prices.<model>); engine.llm.replace refuses such a model the same way.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• agents overrides give individual nodes, or the profiler's drafts, their own model and temperature; see Per-node models.
  • profiler is optional and runs only when asked for. nl2sql index and engine.index.build call no model, so indexing works without it; what the profiler drafts is a proposal in the review queue and never replaces a comment read from the database or a description in the glossary.
  • nl2sql init --provider takes openai, anthropic or openrouter, the providers with a default model, and writes no key. For openai_compatible or ollama, edit llm.yaml as shown above. nl2sql demo --api-key picks the provider from the key's shape (sk-ant- is Anthropic, sk-or- is OpenRouter, anything else is OpenAI).

docs.title: Observers
docs.text:
An observer receives the engine's events: every run's steps, model calls, policy and hook decisions, and the engine's own events (an LLM swap, a purge). Where they go is the observers section of nl2sql.yaml: a log, an audit trail, an OpenTelemetry collector, or a plugin of your own.

# nl2sql.yaml
observers: observers.yaml

# observers.yaml
- type: log
  level: INFO                     # node.started and answer.delta are logged only at DEBUG
- type: audit
  max_age_days: 90
- type: otel                      # needs nl2sql-engine[otel]
  endpoint: http://collector:4317
- type: corp_siem                 # a plugin; its config_model checks the rest
  url: "${env:SIEM_URL}"

from nl2sql import NL2SQL, ObserverConfig

engine = NL2SQL(config.model_copy(update={"observers": [ObserverConfig(type="log"), MyObserver()]}))
Rule Detail No section The engine runs log and audit. observers: [] runs none. Order Observers are subscribed in the section's order and receive each event in that order. Validation type names a registered observer (nl2sql.observers), with "did you mean" for a typo. The observer's config_model checks the other keys when the engine is built; a ${provider:key} reference is resolved then. Every problem is in the one ConfigError. Objects An object with on_event in the list is used as given. Closing engine.close() closes every observer, which writes what it still holds.

docs.title: Observers fail open and never block
docs.text:
An exception from an observer is logged once per observer and event name, at WARNING on logger nl2sql.events, and skipped; it never fails a run. The bus counts it (EventBus.failures).

on_event is called on the thread that published the event, which may be one of a run's worker threads, and a run's events are delivered one at a time so that run.finished is always its last. So an observer must return quickly: anything slow (a network export, a disk write) belongs on a queue of its own. The audit observer writes on its own thread, and otel records in memory while the OpenTelemetry SDK exports in its background thread.

docs.title: log
docs.text:
One line per event on logger nl2sql.events, at level: the event's name and a short summary of its data (run.finished status=success duration_s=1.2 ...). Under DEBUG it logs every event; at any other level it leaves out node.started and answer.delta, one line per step and one per token.

Key Default Meaning level INFO DEBUG, INFO, WARNING or ERROR events every event but node.started and answer.delta; every event at DEBUG The names to log; each must be in the catalog

The run's trace_id and tenant_id reach the line through the context, as they reach every line the engine writes during a run; with nl2sql --log-format json each line carries them as fields.

docs.title: audit
docs.text:
JSON lines in <storage.path>/audit/<date>.jsonl, one file per UTC day. Each line is the event as JSON: name, at, trace_id, tenant_id and data.

Written Why run.finished, run.failed One summary line per run: the user, roles, datasources, tables read (datasource.schema.table), status and source. Never rows. "Who read payroll.salaries" is a search for that table. policy.decision A denial at an enforcement point hook.decision Only deny, needs_approval, approved and error; an allow or modify is not run.limit_reached A question stopped at its cost or call cap llm.changed engine.llm.replace: who, and each agent's old and new provider and model; never a key index.swapped, schema.drifted, retention.purged Changes to the index and to what is kept

The lines are written on the observer's own thread. Its queue holds up to 10,000 lines: when the disk cannot keep up, a line is dropped rather than holding a run, counted in AuditObserver.dropped, and warned about once. engine.close() writes what is queued, and so does the process's exit when nothing closed the engine (a script or a notebook).

The list is the event catalog's: an event is audited when its catalog entry says so (EventInfo.audit), and audit_only narrows it to some values of a field (hook.decision's decision). An event added to the catalog later joins the log through its own entry.

Key Default Meaning max_age_days 90 At least 1. engine.storage.purge() (and nl2sql storage purge, and nl2sql-api once a day) deletes the day files older than this, and reports how many as audit

docs.title: otel
docs.text:
OpenTelemetry metrics and traces, from the bus. Install the extra:

pip install "nl2sql-engine[otel]"

Without it, an otel observer is a ConfigError naming that command. Only this observer imports opentelemetry, and only when it is built.

Metric Kind Attributes From nl2sql.node.duration histogram, s node node.finished nl2sql.token.usage counter node, model, type (input, cached_input, cache_write_input, output, reasoning, total) llm.call nl2sql.plan_cache.lookups counter result (hit, miss), datasource_id plan_cache.lookup nl2sql.run.cost histogram, USD status run.finished, when the run was priced

Traces: one span per run, nl2sql.run, from run.started to run.finished or run.failed (an error status), with the attributes nl2sql.trace_id, nl2sql.status, nl2sql.source and nl2sql.datasources; and a child span per step, nl2sql.node.<node>, with nl2sql.node and nl2sql.sub_query_id.

The observer makes its own MeterProvider and TracerProvider and never sets OpenTelemetry's process-wide ones, so two engines in one process can export to two collectors. engine.close() gives each provider 5 seconds to flush, so a collector that is down does not hold the shutdown longer; what was not sent by then is dropped.

Key Default Meaning endpoint http://localhost:4317 The OTLP collector (gRPC) exporter otlp otlp, or console to print to stdout metrics true Record and export the metrics traces true Record and export the spans service_name nl2sql The service.name resource attribute

docs.title: Writing an observer
docs.text:
An observer depends on the SDK alone (nl2sql_sdk.events). Declare it under the nl2sql.observers entry point group of your package:

from pathlib import Path
from typing import ClassVar, FrozenSet, Optional

from pydantic import BaseModel
from nl2sql_sdk.events import Event


class SiemConfig(BaseModel):
    url: str


class SiemObserver:
    interface_version: ClassVar[int] = 1
    config_model: ClassVar[type[BaseModel]] = SiemConfig
    events: ClassVar[Optional[FrozenSet[str]]] = frozenset({"run.finished", "policy.decision"})

    @classmethod
    def from_config(cls, cfg: SiemConfig, *, folder: Path) -> "SiemObserver":
        return cls(cfg.url)            # folder is storage.path, for anything it writes

    def __init__(self, url: str) -> None:
        self.url = url

    def on_event(self, event: Event) -> None:
        ...                            # put it on a queue; never block

    def close(self) -> None:
        ...                            # flush the queue

[project.entry-points."nl2sql.observers"]
corp_siem = "corp_siem:SiemObserver"

engine.events.catalog() lists every event with its data's JSON Schema; an event never carries result rows (see the invariant Events Carry No Rows).

docs.title: Policies Configuration
docs.text:
The policies section of nl2sql.yaml decides who may read what. nl2sql init writes it to policies.yaml.

On your own machine, one line is enough: every caller may read everything.

# policies.yaml
allow_all: true

For anything shared, write roles. Each role allows and denies tables with patterns over datasource.schema.table:

# policies.yaml
default_role: viewer
admin_roles: [admin]
refusal_names_tables: false
roles:
  admin:
    description: Everything
    allow: ["*"]
  analyst:
    description: Sales, except the audit schema and PII tables
    allow: [sales]
    deny:  [sales.audit.*, "sales.*.*_pii"]
  viewer:
    description: Reporting views and support tickets
    allow: [sales.reporting.*, support.public.tickets]

The same in Python:

from nl2sql import Policies, Role

Policies(default_role="viewer", admin_roles=["admin"],
         roles={"analyst": Role(description="Sales", allow=["sales"], deny=["sales.audit.*"])})

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Default Meaning allow_all false Every caller may read everything. It cannot be combined with default_role or roles. Policies.allow_all() is the Python shorthand. default_role none The role used when the caller gives none. It must name one of roles. Without it, a question with no role is refused. admin_roles [admin] The roles nl2sql-api lets through on the routes that change datasources, LLMs or the index. See REST API. refusal_names_tables false Name the role and the forbidden table in the refusal the user sees. Off, the message is "You do not have permission to see the data this question requires."; the table, the role and the rule that denied it are always in the log and the run trace. The demo (nl2sql init --demo) sets it, since showing a refusal is its point. See Security Model. roles {} Role name to its description, allow patterns and deny patterns. cost none The cost rule: a limit on the rows a query is estimated to read. Absent, no estimate is ever asked for. Valid beside allow_all. check none A policy check: {type: <name>, <its keys>} naming a registered one, or, in Python, a check object. What it grants is intersected with the roles.

docs.title: Cost
docs.text:
A query that reads a billion rows can be cheap to ask and expensive to run. The cost rule asks the database what a query is expected to read, before it runs, and acts when that is over a limit.

# policies.yaml
cost:                            # absent: no estimate is ever asked for
  max_estimated_rows: 5000000    # null: no limit
  over_limit: confirm            # allow | confirm | refuse
  unknown: allow                 # no estimate: allow | confirm | refuse
roles:
  analyst:
    description: Sales
    allow: [sales]
    cost: { max_estimated_rows: 1000000, over_limit: refuse }
  admin:
    description: Everything
    allow: ["*"]
    cost: { max_estimated_rows: null }
Field Meaning max_estimated_rows The most rows a query may be estimated to read: the rows its scans visit, not the rows it returns, so a LIMIT does not hide a full scan. null is no limit, and no estimate is asked for. over_limit What to do over the limit. allow runs it. confirm ends the run needs_approval, as a hook's NeedsApproval: a person with a role in admin_roles approves, and the same SQL then runs. refuse ends the run with COST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, which is never retried. Default confirm. unknown What to do when there is no estimate: the datasource's adapter does not declare ESTIMATES_COST (SQLite), the estimate failed (SQL Server without the SHOWPLAN permission, say) or it reported no rows. The same three actions. Default allow.

A role's cost replaces the top-level fields it sets, for that role. A caller with several roles gets each field's most permissive value across them: the highest max_estimated_rows (null, no limit, wins) and the weakest of over_limit and unknown (allow over confirm over refuse). The values may come from different roles, as grants add up across roles. A cost on a role with no top-level cost starts from no limit.

It is a built-in hook, policy.cost, that runs first at execute.before (see Hooks), so it applies to generated SQL, to verified queries and to the check run of a correction alike, and under allow_all: true, which opens tables, not cost. One estimate is asked for per sub-query. QueryResult.sub_queries[].estimate carries it, and cost.estimated is published for each (Events).

docs.title: Patterns
docs.text:
Pattern Matches * every table in every datasource datasource every table in every schema of one datasource datasource.schema.table the tables whose datasource, schema and table each match

Each part is an fnmatch glob, so sales.audit.* is every table in the audit schema of sales, sales.*.*_pii is every table ending in _pii in any schema, and sal* is every datasource whose id starts with sal.

Rule Detail Two parts Rejected when the config loads, with the fix: "'sales.orders' has two parts: write 'sales.<schema>.orders', or 'sales.<schema>.*'". A two-part pattern could mean a table in any schema. Case Matching ignores case, so a deny cannot be dodged by Orders against orders. Schemas SQLite and DuckDB tables are in main. A plan table with no schema is in the adapter's default schema: the one an unqualified name resolves to (public on PostgreSQL by default, dbo on SQL Server, the connected database on MySQL, main on SQLite and DuckDB; main when the adapter cannot say). Within a role Deny beats allow. Across roles A caller may read a table if some role allows it and that same role does not deny it. One role's deny never takes away what another role allows. Datasource access Implied: a role reaches a datasource when one of its allow patterns can match inside it, unless it denies the whole datasource.
