Unknown datasources A pattern naming a datasource that is not configured is reported by nl2sql policy validate, not refused at startup, because datasources can be added at runtime.

Access is decided on the schema as well as the table. The plan names the schema a table is read from, and the SQL is written with it, so an allow of warehouse.sales.orders does not let a plan read warehouse.audit.orders.

docs.title: Denied tables are hidden
docs.text:
A table the caller may not read never reaches a model. The schema retriever searches only the readable tables, so the planner's prompt is filled with tables the caller can use, and a denied table's name, columns, keys, relationships and data are not in it. The answerability judge and the decomposer see only the readable table names too.

So a question that needs only denied tables gets "no data for that question" rather than a refusal. A plan that names a hidden table anyway is still refused by the logical validator with SECURITY_VIOLATION; with refusal_names_tables: true the refusal names the table, for debugging.

docs.title: One Scope everywhere
docs.text:
Every place that decides access asks the same Scope: what one caller may read in one datasource, built by PolicyEngine.scope(user, datasource_id) from the roles, allow_all, default_role and the policy check, if there is one. The datasource resolver, the curated matcher, the schema retriever, the logical validator, the executor's value check and engine.policies.allows() all ask it, so they cannot disagree. A run builds each datasource's scope once and keeps it, so every step of the run decides the same way.

scope = engine.policies.scope(UserContext(roles=["analyst"]), "sales")
scope.reaches_datasource()          # True
scope.allows("audit", "log")        # False
scope.rule_for("audit", "log")      # "role 'analyst' denies 'sales.audit.*'"

docs.title: A policy check
docs.text:
When access is decided somewhere else (an IAM service, OPA, Cedar, OpenFGA, Unity Catalog), a policy check asks it. A check is a plugin: it gets the caller and a datasource id, and returns a Grant of allow and deny patterns, written exactly like a role's.

# policies.yaml
roles:
  analyst:
    description: Sales
    allow: [sales]
check:
  type: corp_iam               # a registered policy check
  url: "${env:IAM_URL}"        # the check's own keys
Rule Detail Intersection A table is readable only if the roles allow it and the check's grant allows it and does not deny it. Neither can widen the other. With allow_all: true and a check, the check alone decides. Fails closed Any exception from the check, or anything it returns that is not a valid Grant (a pattern with two parts, say), denies that datasource for the run. The failure is logged as a warning with the check's name. There is no fail-open option. How often Once per caller and datasource per run. Nothing is cached across runs, so a change in the outside service applies to the next question. Timeouts The check owns them, as an HTTP client timeout for example. The pipeline's timeout_s bounds the run anyway. The log When the check is what refuses a table, rule_for names it: "policy check 'corp_iam' does not allow 'sales.audit.log'".

No check is built in. A check implements nl2sql_sdk.policy.PolicyCheck (interface_version = 1, a config_model for its block, from_config(cfg) and grant(user, datasource_id)). Register it in code with registry.add_policy_check(name, cls) or @registry.policy_check(name), or publish it in the nl2sql.policy_checks entry point group. An unknown type, or a misspelt key in the block, is a config error that names policies.check. In Python, Policies(..., check=obj) uses a check object as given.

A check that asks an HTTP service:

import httpx
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict

from nl2sql_sdk.policy import Grant, UserContext


class CorpIamConfig(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")
    url: str
    timeout_s: float = 2.0


class CorpIam:
    interface_version = 1
    config_model = CorpIamConfig

    def __init__(self, cfg: CorpIamConfig):
        self.client = httpx.Client(base_url=cfg.url, timeout=cfg.timeout_s)

    @classmethod
    def from_config(cls, cfg: CorpIamConfig) -> "CorpIam":
        return cls(cfg)

    def grant(self, user: UserContext, datasource_id: str) -> Grant:
        # Any error here (a timeout, a 500) denies the datasource for this run.
        response = self.client.get("/grants", params={"user": user.user_id, "datasource": datasource_id})
        response.raise_for_status()
        return Grant.model_validate(response.json())  # {"allow": [...], "deny": [...]}

Publish it in the package that ships it:

[project.entry-points."nl2sql.policy_checks"]
corp_iam = "corp_nl2sql.iam:CorpIam"

docs.title: Checking the policies
docs.text:
nl2sql policy validate checks that every pattern a role names matches a configured datasource, against the config --config names:

nl2sql --config nl2sql.yaml policy validate

A pattern that matches no configured datasource is MISSING, and the command exits 1. From Python, engine.policies.validate() returns the same report; after engine.check(), a pattern that matches only a datasource that failed to connect is UNAVAILABLE.

docs.title: The Review Queue
docs.text:
Every change the engine suggests to a person's knowledge or curated answers is a proposal in one queue, kept in the state store (storage.state). A thumbs-up on a generated answer files a proposed verified query, and so does a checked correction (engine.feedback.correct, origin correction); the schema profiler files its join candidates and column roles the same way (nl2sql profile, and with --draft the descriptions the profiler model drafts), a saved clarification pick files a proposed term. Nothing in the queue reaches a prompt, the index or a file until a person with an admin role accepts it.

nl2sql review list --as admin                     # what is waiting
nl2sql review show 3f9a0c1e5b7d2a44 --as admin    # one, beside the current value
nl2sql review accept 3f9a0c1e5b7d2a44 --as admin  # write it
nl2sql review reject 9b1e44c07a2d1f30 --as admin --reason "Not USD."

docs.title: Proposals
docs.text:
A proposal is the SDK's Proposal (from nl2sql import Proposal), so a third-party state store can keep it:

Field What it holds id 16 hex characters: SHA-256 of kind, datasource_id, target and the canonical JSON of change kind join, column, table or term (the glossary), or verified_query (curated.yaml) target What it changes: Invoice.Total, Track.MediaTypeId->MediaType.MediaTypeId, a term's name, a question change The fields it would set, in glossary.yaml's or curated.yaml's shape tables Every datasource.schema.table its target and change name, for the scope filter. Filing completes it: a table, a column's table, both sides of a join, a term's tables and columns' tables, and the tables a verified query's SQL reads are always listed origin thumbs_up, profiler, draft, correction or clarification evidence Counts and checks (a thumbs-up's trace id and role; a correction's trace id, original SQL, ran, row_count and columns); never rows status proposed, accepted, rejected or superseded created_at, created_by, decided_at, decided_by, reason, wrote Who and when; a rejection's reason; the file an accept wrote Rule Detail One change, one row The id hashes the change, so filing the same change again updates the open row's evidence and adds any tables the new filing names. A rejected change keeps its row and is never proposed again; a different change for the same target is a new row. Supersede A new change for a kind, datasource and target that already has an open row marks that row superseded: the queue holds one open item per target. Accepted and rejected rows are never superseded. Retention Decided rows (accepted, rejected, superseded) are kept for settings.review.max_age_days (365) and deleted by engine.storage.purge() (nl2sql storage purge, and nl2sql-api once a day). Open rows are never purged.

docs.title: Who sees and who decides
docs.text:
Reading the queue takes the caller, with no default (as every Wave B read does): a caller sees a proposal only when their scope reaches its datasource and every table in its tables, and get of one they cannot see is "not found", the same answer as an id that does not exist.

Accepting and rejecting take by, a UserContext holding one of policies.admin_roles (["admin"] by default); anyone else gets ReviewError with code NOT_AUTHORIZED. Under policies.allow_all there are no roles, and every caller may decide. Like an approval, by is trusted as far as the caller's UserContext is.

docs.title: The facade
docs.text:
from nl2sql import UserContext

admin = UserContext(user_id="ada", roles=["admin"])
waiting = engine.proposals.list(user_context=admin, kind="verified_query")
report = engine.proposals.accept([p.id for p in waiting], by=admin,
                                 edits={waiting[0].id: {"description": "Revenue by month."}})
report.accepted, report.files_written, report.warnings, report.refused
Method What it does list(*, user_context, kind=None, status="proposed", datasource_id=None, limit=None) The proposals the caller may see, newest first; status=None lists every status get(id, *, user_context) One proposal; ReviewError(NOT_FOUND) when it is missing or hidden current(id, *, user_context) What the proposal would replace: the glossary item as the caller sees it, or the curated query with the same id. None when there is none, or when the caller's scope does not reach every table that query reads accept(ids, *, by, edits=None) Accepts one id or a list; edits maps an id to a dict merged over its change. Returns an AcceptReport reject(ids, *, by, reason=None) Rejects one id or a list; every id must be proposed, or nothing is rejected (NOT_FOUND) export(path, *, user_context, kind=None, datasource_id=None) Writes the open proposals the caller may see as a review file; returns how many. Never over nl2sql.yaml, a section file or a knowledge source's file apply(path, *, by) Reads a review file: accepts each accept (the file's change replaces the stored one, so a key can be removed) and rejects each reject (with its reason)

AcceptReport has accepted and (from apply) rejected, the proposals now decided; files_written, each file written once, relative to the folder of nl2sql.yaml; warnings; and refused, an id to why it was left as it was: unknown, no longer proposed, or a change that failed its checks.

docs.title: Saving a clarification pick
docs.text:
When a question asked which reading was meant (Asking again), the pick can be kept:

proposal = engine.knowledge.save_choice(choice, user_context=ana)

It files a term proposal with origin clarification: the phrase (or term=, with the phrase as its synonym) as the term's name, the chosen option's label as its definition, and the columns the chosen plan's select items read and the tables it reads. Anyone whose scope reaches the option's datasource and tables may save a pick (otherwise ReviewError NOT_FOUND); a request that was changed, or has no such option, is a ValueError. It reaches the glossary only when an admin accepts it. A term of that name that already exists is replaced, and nl2sql review show shows it beside the proposed one first. Once accepted, the phrase is a term's name or synonym, which settles it: the planner's flag on it is dropped and the question is no longer asked.

docs.title: Accept: the only writer
docs.text:
Accept is the only code that writes a file a person owns, and it writes two:

Kind Writes Then join, column, table, term The first yaml knowledge source's glossary.yaml, each change merged in. A term whose name exists replaces that term. The knowledge is reloaded: the items are in the next run's prompts. verified_query The curated section's own file (curated: {file: curated.yaml}), the query added under its datasource The curated checks run first, on the edited section. Then the engine's curated answers are swapped and the datasource's curated index entries refreshed (as nl2sql index --refresh does), so the next question can match it. Rule Detail One write per file The accepted items are grouped by file; each file is locked, checked, applied, written and reloaded once. Accepting a thousand column roles is one write. Locked Each file's write holds the state store's lock accept:<real path>, so two accepts in two threads or processes cannot both pass the check and lose a write; one waits up to 10 seconds for the other. Each file's items are recorded as accepted under the lock, right after its write, and reject takes the same locks, so an id is never accepted twice, nor rejected while an accept is writing it. Changed underneath Each file's SHA-256 is recorded when the engine loads it; for curated.yaml, only when the file still holds the section the config loaded (otherwise every accept refuses). When the file on disk no longer matches, accept refuses with FILE_CHANGED: reload the knowledge (engine.knowledge.reload) for the glossary, or load the config again and build a new engine for curated.yaml. Every file is checked before the first write, so a call refused by these checks writes nothing. If a later file's write fails after an earlier one succeeded, the earlier file's items stay accepted and the later file's stay proposed. A ${...} reference in curated.yaml reads as a change: keep the file literal. Where Without a yaml knowledge source, a glossary accept is NOT_WRITABLE. A curated section written inline in nl2sql.yaml, or in a config built in code, is never written (NOT_WRITABLE: move it to its own file, or export and edit by hand); a missing section is refused with the fix "add curated: {file: curated.yaml}". Per item An item whose change fails its checks (the glossary's validation, the curated checks, a verified query id that is taken) stays proposed and is named in refused; the rest are written. Canonical rewrite Both files are rewritten in canonical form: the models' key order, mappings sorted by name, lists in their own order, SQL and multi-line text as literal blocks, under a fixed header. Comments are not kept: write remarks in notes: (glossary) or description: (curated). Atomic, through links The real path is resolved first, so a symlinked file is written through and the link kept; the new text goes to a temporary file beside it, renamed over it. The proposals are marked accepted, with wrote, after the rename. Shadowed A knowledge source listed before the glossary that sets the same item wins the merge; accept still writes, and says so in warnings.

proposal.created is published when a proposal enters the queue and proposal.decided (decision, by, wrote) for each accept and reject; the audit observer keeps proposal.decided. See Events.

docs.title: The review file
docs.text:
The queue's export and import format, for deciding in a pull request:

# review.yaml: written by `nl2sql review export`, read by `nl2sql review apply`
version: 1
proposals:
- id: 3f9a0c1e5b7d2a44
  decision: accept            # accept | reject | (empty: leave proposed)
  reason: null
  kind: join
  datasource_id: chinook
  target: Track.MediaTypeId->MediaType.MediaTypeId
  change: {from: Track.MediaTypeId, to: MediaType.MediaTypeId, cardinality: many-to-one}
  evidence: {name_match: exact, types: [number, number], sampled: 347, matched: 347, overlap: 1.0}
  origin: profiler

A reviewer sets decision and may edit change and reason. apply reads back only id, decision, reason and change; it accepts each accept with the file's change in place of the stored one, rejects each reject, leaves an empty decision proposed, and names in refused each id that is unknown or no longer proposed.

docs.title: The CLI
docs.text:
Every command reads as the caller --as ROLE (repeatable) and --user ID build; without --as, the role is policies.default_role.

Command Calls nl2sql review list [--kind K] [--datasource ID] [--status S] list; --status all lists every status nl2sql review show ID get, with current beside the proposed change nl2sql review accept ID... [--all --kind K --datasource ID] accept; --all accepts every open proposal the caller sees. Exits 1 when an item is refused nl2sql review reject ID... [--reason TEXT] reject nl2sql review export --out FILE [--kind K] [--datasource ID] export nl2sql review apply FILE apply; exits 1 when an item is refused

A refusal (ReviewError) prints its message and fix and exits 1.

docs.title: Secrets Configuration
docs.text:
The secrets section of nl2sql.yaml is optional. It lists secret providers that the rest of the config can reference as ${provider_id:key}. The env provider (${env:VAR}) is always there without it.

# nl2sql.yaml
secrets: { file: secrets.yaml }

# secrets.yaml
providers:
  - id: aws-main
    type: aws
    region_name: "us-east-1"

providers may be omitted or left empty: both mean "no secret providers configured".

docs.title: Providers
docs.text:
Each provider has:

  • id: unique provider ID used in secret references (e.g. ${aws-main:db_password})
  • type: aws, azure, hashicorp, or a provider a plugin registers. The id env is reserved for the built-in provider.

Every other key is the provider's own setting:

type Settings Extra to install aws region_name, profile_name, both optional (boto3's own lookup fills them in) nl2sql-engine[aws] azure vault_url (required), client_id, client_secret, tenant_id. Without all three credentials the provider signs in with DefaultAzureCredential. nl2sql-engine[azure] hashicorp url and token (both required), mount_point (default secret) nl2sql-engine[hashicorp] env none none 
providers:
  - id: vault
    type: hashicorp
    url: "https://vault.internal:8200"
    token: "${env:VAULT_TOKEN}"

The settings are strict. An unknown or misspelt key, or a missing required one, fails when the config loads, and the message names the key.

A provider reads its settings from its entry only. It never falls back to an environment variable such as VAULT_ADDR, VAULT_TOKEN or AZURE_KEYVAULT_URL: when a value comes from the environment, write the field as an ${env:...} reference, as token does above.

The HashiCorp key is the secret's path and, after a colon, the field: ${vault:apps/sales:password} reads the field password of apps/sales in the KV version 2 engine at mount_point. Without a colon it reads the field value.

Each provider implements the SecretProvider interface from the SDK; see SDK reference → SecretProvider.

docs.title: Secret references
docs.text: Use ${provider_id:key} to resolve a secret from a provider, and ${env:VAR} to read an environment variable. A reference is the whole value. Every api_key and every value under a datasource's connection keep the reference until the component is built, so engine.config, logs and errors never hold the secret. Inside secrets: itself only ${env:...} is allowed: one provider cannot depend on another. See Configuration System → references.

docs.title: When a provider fails to start
docs.text:
A provider in the secrets section that cannot start fails startup at once: building the engine raises a ConfigError naming secrets.providers[i] (the CLI, nl2sql-api and nl2sql doctor print it). The error names the provider and the reason:

Secret provider 'vault' (type 'hashicorp') failed to start: Missing dependency 'hvac'.
Install 'nl2sql-engine[hashicorp]'. Fix or remove this entry in the secrets config.

The usual reasons are the provider's extra not being installed (nl2sql-engine[aws], [azure], [hashicorp]), a ${env:VAR} credential whose variable is not set (the message names the variable), or the provider's own client refusing the config. Credentials are masked in the message.

This is deliberate: every ${vault:...} reference depends on the provider, so starting without it only moves the error to the first lookup, where it reads as "Unknown secret provider ID". A config without a secrets section and the built-in env provider are unaffected. A datasource that fails to start, by contrast, leaves the others running: see Datasources → When a datasource fails to start.

docs.title: Secrets never print
docs.text:
A credential written as a value never prints: repr, str, log lines and tracebacks of the config show ********** instead. A ${provider:key} reference is not a secret and is shown as written. This covers:

  • api_key in llm, in each of llm.agents, and in embeddings, including a key the demo gives the engine in memory (nl2sql demo --api-key, or one saved in the playground's settings panel): repr(engine.config) never shows it;
  • in the secrets section, every provider setting whose name contains password, secret, token or api_key (client_secret for Azure, token for HashiCorp); the URL and the other settings still show;
  • in a datasource's connection, every field whose name contains one of the same words;
  • the resolved key the LLM registry builds a client from (AgentConfig, a pydantic SecretStr), including model_dump(mode="json") and model_dump_json().

The config's own fields stay plain strings, so the engine (and config.model_dump()) reads the real value; only printing masks it. A config built in code that fails validation never echoes its input either: the error names the field and the problem, not the value.

The real value is read only where it is used: building the LLM or embeddings client, a database connection, the artifact store's storage options or a secret provider's client. nl2sql init never writes a key: a key belongs in the environment or the .env next to nl2sql.yaml. The demo and the playground's Settings page save a key to that .env only, with its real value.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
The settings section of nl2sql.yaml holds the tuning knobs. It is optional, and every field has a default, so most configs leave it out. Each value is the engine's own: two engines in one process can run with different settings.

# settings.yaml (every value shown is the default)
tenant_id: default_tenant
pipeline:
  timeout_s: 60
  plan_cache: true
  strict_columns: true
  today: null                 # pin the run date: 2013-12-31
  retries: { max: 3, base_delay_s: 1.0, max_delay_s: 10.0, jitter_s: 0.5 }
  max_llm_calls: 60           # model calls per question, parse retries included; null: no cap
  max_cost_usd: null          # dollars per question; null (the default): no cap
  sanity_checks: true
retrieval:
  full_snapshot_max_tables: 15
  table_k: 8
  planning_k: 12
  decomposer_tables: 30
routing:
  candidates: 3
  max_datasources: 3
  max_sub_queries: 6
  floor_ratio: 0.5
results:
  row_limit: 100000
  fetch_batch_size: 10000
  preview_rows: 20
traces:
  mode: on_failure            # off | on_failure | always
  sample_rows: 50
  max_field_chars: 20000
schema:
  max_versions: 3
curated:
  match_top_k: 5
  match_floor: 0.6
feedback:
  enabled: true
knowledge:                    # read from release 0.8 (Wave B)
  item_max_chars: 500
  block_max_chars: 4000
  top_k: 8
  match_floor: 0.6
clarify:
  enabled: true
profiler:
  sample_rows: 1000
  max_probes: 200
  time_budget_s: 60
  min_overlap: 0.9
  enum_max_distinct: 50
  max_cost_usd: 0.50
review:
  max_age_days: 365
charts:                       # read from release 0.9 (Wave C)
  max_points: 1000
  max_categories: 20
  max_series: 5

Unknown keys are errors, as everywhere in the config. The demo (nl2sql init --demo) writes a settings.yaml with pipeline.timeout_s: 300 (a live run makes six model calls; one OpenAI run took 136 s) and traces.mode: always (the playground's Debug drill-down reads every run's trace).

In Python, the groups are Settings, PipelineSettings, RetrySettings, RetrievalSettings, RoutingSettings, ResultSettings, TraceSettings, SchemaSettings, CuratedSettings, FeedbackSettings, KnowledgeSettings, ClarifySettings, ProfilerSettings, ReviewSettings and ChartSettings in nl2sql.config.

Where the engine's events, logs and metrics go is not a setting: it is the observers section of nl2sql.yaml. The 0.6 observability group (exporter, otlp_endpoint) is gone; an otel observer takes its place. The schema group is the attribute schema_ (cfg.settings.schema_.max_versions), because schema would shadow a pydantic method; the YAML key is schema.

docs.title: tenant_id
docs.text: The tenant id for requests that name none. Result files are kept per tenant.

docs.title: pipeline
docs.text: Key Default Description timeout_s 60 Timeout in seconds for one question. The caller is answered within about a second of the limit; the run's worker thread winds down in the background (see isolation). plan_cache true Reuse a plan that already passed validation and executed, for the same normalised sub-query intent, datasource and schema version on the same run date, instead of calling the planner LLM. The cached plan is validated again on every use, so RBAC and policy changes still apply. Stored in <storage.path>/state.db; nl2sql cache clear empties it. See Determinism → The plan cache. strict_columns true Treat a column the plan names but the retrieved schema does not have as a blocking, retryable COLUMN_NOT_FOUND error, so the planner is asked again instead of the plan reaching the database. false downgrades it to a warning that lets the plan through once retries are spent. today none The date the planner and refiner are told it is, as an ISO date (2013-12-31). Unset, it is the real date in UTC. Pin it for tests and gold runs whose questions say "this year" or "the last 30 days". A trace records the date its run used, and nl2sql trace replay pins it. It is part of the plan cache key, so a plan made on another date is not reused. retries.max 3 Retry attempts for the SQL agent's refinement loop. retries.base_delay_s 1.0 Base delay between retries, in seconds. retries.max_delay_s 10.0 Longest delay between retries. retries.jitter_s 0.5 Most jitter added to a delay. max_llm_calls 60 The most model calls one question may make, parse retries included; null turns the cap off. 60 covers the largest legitimate run: the resolver, the decomposer, six sub-queries each with a planner call and three refiner and planner retries, the answer, and parse retries. See Per-question caps. max_cost_usd none The most one question may spend, in dollars; null (the default) is no cap. With a cap set, every model the llm section names must have a price, or the engine does not build. See Per-question caps. sanity_checks true The answer sanity checks after each sub-query runs (join fan-out, all-null columns, missing filter values). false turns them all off. Read from release 0.7's sanity checks (Wave A).

docs.title: Per-question caps
docs.text:
Both caps are checked before each model call, by the question's budget: a call that would be the 61st, or that would start once the question has spent max_cost_usd, is never sent. The calls already in flight finish, so a question can pass the cost cap by the calls in flight: at most one per running sub-query.

A question that reaches a cap ends with status: "stopped", never as a planner error to retry: QueryResult.stop is {limit, value, spent} (limit is max_llm_calls or max_cost_usd), the one error is RUN_LIMIT_REACHED (not retryable) naming the limit and the setting, and the answer says so: "This question reached its limit of 60 model calls (settings.pipeline.max_llm_calls)." The run publishes run.limit_reached, which the caller's stream carries and the audit log records.

nl2sql.limits.Budget(max_llm_calls=..., max_cost_usd=...) is the same check for work that is not a question: make the model calls with budget.callbacks(), and a call over a cap raises LimitReached (with the RunStop in .stop) before it is sent.

docs.title: retrieval
docs.text:
Key Default Description full_snapshot_max_tables 15 When a datasource's schema has at most this many tables, the schema retriever skips vector retrieval and passes the full schema snapshot (every table, every column) to the planner. 0 always uses vector retrieval. table_k 8 Table entries the schema retriever's search keeps for a sub-query (and column entries, when no table matches). planning_k 12 Column and relationship entries of those tables the planner is shown for a sub-query. decomposer_tables 30 Table names the decomposer is shown per datasource; the rest are counted.

table_k, planning_k and decomposer_tables replace the constants the schema retriever and the resolver had before 0.7 (TABLE_K, PLANNING_K, MAX_DECOMPOSER_TABLES).

docs.title: routing
docs.text:
Cross-database routing: which datasources a question goes to, and how far it may spread. The resolver reads candidates, max_datasources and floor_ratio (Routing); the decomposer reads max_sub_queries (Wave A, Limits).

Key Default Description candidates 3 Datasources routing keeps for the answerability check, best by fused score first. max_datasources 3 Datasources one question may use: of those the answerability check accepts, the resolver forwards at most this many, best first. max_sub_queries 6 Sub-queries one question may have. A decomposition over it ends the run with QUESTION_TOO_BROAD. floor_ratio 0.5 A candidate whose best index-entry similarity to the question is under this share of the most similar candidate's is dropped, between 0 and 1. It is on similarity, not on the fused score: with a handful of datasources every reciprocal-rank score is within a few percent of the best. 0 keeps every candidate up to candidates.

docs.title: results
docs.text: Key Default Description row_limit 100000 The most rows one sub-query returns: a resource ceiling baked into the SQL as a LIMIT. A datasource's own limits.row_limit applies when it is lower (the demo datasources set 10000). A result that reaches it is flagged as truncated (QueryResult.truncated, sub_queries[].truncated) and the answer says it was cut. fetch_batch_size 10000 Rows fetched from the database and written to the sub-query's result file at a time, for an adapter that streams (every built-in SQL adapter does). At most one batch is held in memory. See Artifact Store. preview_rows 20 Result rows the answer model sees, with the total row count and the column names. The model writes about the result; it never copies it. See AnswerSynthesizerNode.

docs.title: traces
docs.text: Key Default Description mode on_failure When to write a run trace to <storage.path>/traces/: off, on_failure (errors, a retry, or an incomplete run) or always. See Debugging a Run. sample_rows 50 Result rows kept in a trace. max_field_chars 20000 Longest string kept in a node's recorded inputs and outputs; LLM prompts and responses are never cut.

docs.title: schema
docs.text: Key Default Description max_versions 3 The newest schema snapshots kept per datasource in the state store, besides every version a build pointer names and the one a build just replaced.

docs.title: curated
docs.text:
Key Default Description match_top_k 5 Verified query candidates a question's search returns, one per query. match_floor 0.6 Cosine similarity the best verified query candidate must reach before the model is asked to choose one. Below it the question is answered by the normal pipeline with no model call. See Curated Answers.

Whether curated answers are on is not a setting: the curated section is present or absent.

docs.title: feedback
docs.text: Key Default Description enabled true Let the playground record a thumbs up or down, with an optional note, for a run. Stored in <storage.path>/state.db: question, role, status, SQL, the datasources it ran on, whether the answer was verified or generated, error codes, the model per node and the engine version, never result rows or sample values. nl2sql feedback clear empties it. See Feedback and Signals.

docs.title: knowledge, clarify, profiler and review
docs.text:
Four groups for release 0.8 (Wave B). They are accepted and validated now; the Wave B change named with each reads it.

Key Default Description knowledge.item_max_chars 500 The longest one glossary text may be; a longer one is a load error naming the item, so nothing is silently cut (K1). knowledge.block_max_chars 4000 The longest the [BUSINESS_CONTEXT] block of a prompt may be; the lowest-scored terms, then rules, are dropped, and the trace records what was (K2). knowledge.top_k 8 Matched glossary terms kept per sub-query (K2). knowledge.match_floor 0.6 Similarity a term's index entry must reach to the sub-query's intent to match, between 0 and 1 (K3). clarify.enabled true Ask which reading was meant when the planner flags a real ambiguity, instead of guessing (L1). profiler.sample_rows 1000 Distinct values one join-overlap probe reads (P1). profiler.max_probes 200 Overlap probes per datasource; the remaining candidates are proposed without one (P1). profiler.time_budget_s 60 Seconds per datasource after which no probe starts (P1). profiler.min_overlap 0.9 A measured overlap under this drops a join candidate, between 0 and 1 (P1). profiler.enum_max_distinct 50 The most distinct values a column proposed as an enum may have (P1). profiler.max_cost_usd 0.50 The most one profile(draft=True) call may spend drafting descriptions (profile(draft=True), nl2sql profile --draft). review.max_age_days 365 Decided proposals older than this are purged by engine.storage.purge() (Q1).

docs.title: charts
docs.text:
Release 0.9 (Wave C). engine.results.chart reads it (Charts).

Key Default Description charts.max_points 1000 The most rows charted. A longer result is read up to this and flagged truncated; a line chart becomes a table rather than drop points silently. charts.max_categories 20 The most categories a bar chart draws; more is a table. charts.max_series 5 The most lines in one line chart (measures, or values of a category split into lines).

docs.title: conversations and dashboards
docs.text:
These two are sections of nl2sql.yaml of their own, not groups of settings: see Conversations, chat tools, dashboards and MCP.

Key Default Description conversations.context_turns 3 Turns of history the model sees. conversations.max_tool_calls 12 Tool calls the model may make in one turn; after the last it makes one more call with the tools off and must reply. conversations.max_turns 50 Turns in one conversation; the next is refused with CONVERSATION_TOO_LONG. conversations.max_age_days 30 Conversations, and draft dashboards, not updated for this long are deleted by engine.storage.purge(). null keeps them. dashboards.max_tiles 10 Charts in the starter dashboard. dashboards.min_refresh_minutes 15 The shortest refresh schedule; a shorter one is refused. dashboards.schedule_identity_max_age_days 30 A schedule stops when the owner identity saved with it is older than this, until the owner sets it again.

docs.title: Storage
docs.text:
The storage section of nl2sql.yaml says where the engine keeps its data, and which store keeps each part of it. Only path is required:

# storage.yaml
path: .nl2sql          # or "${env:NL2SQL_DATA_DIR}" in a container

A relative path is relative to nl2sql.yaml in a file, and to the working directory when the Config is built in code. nl2sql init writes .nl2sql and adds .nl2sql/ to .gitignore.

Everything the engine writes lives under it:

Under path What Was (0.4) index/ The vector index (Chroma), one collection per embedding model: nl2sql__<model slug>__<dimension>. VECTOR_STORE, VECTOR_STORE_COLLECTION state.db SQLite: schema snapshots, the plan cache and playground feedback. SCHEMA_STORE_PATH traces/ Run traces (settings.traces.mode), kept 14 days by default. TRACE_DIR results/ Result files, <tenant_id>/<request_id>/<sub_query_id>.parquet. Kept 7 days by default. See Artifact Store. RESULT_ARTIFACT_BASE_URI

docs.title: The four stores
docs.text:
Each part of that data has a slot, and each slot a store, named by type. Every sub-block is optional; left out, a slot uses its built-in store, so the section above is the same as:

path: .nl2sql
index:   { type: chroma }    # <path>/index/
state:   { type: sqlite }    # <path>/state.db
traces:  { type: files, max_age_days: 14 }    # <path>/traces/
results: { type: local, max_age_days: 7 }     # <path>/results/
Slot Built-in Holds index chroma The vector index, one namespace per embedding model, and each datasource's live build state sqlite Schema snapshots, the plan cache, feedback traces files Run traces results local Result files

A store's other keys are its own, checked by the store when the engine is built, so a misspelt key is an error. They may be ${provider:key} references, resolved through the secret providers when the store is built:

index: { type: qdrant, url: "http://qdrant:6333", api_key: "${env:QDRANT_KEY}" }

Store names share one entry point group, nl2sql.stores, so a name is unique across the four slots. A store in the wrong slot is refused with the stores installed for that slot: "'chroma' is an index store; results needs a results store. Installed: local."

In code, a slot takes a StoreConfig or a store object, used as given:

from nl2sql import Storage, StoreConfig

Storage(path=".nl2sql")
Storage(path=".nl2sql", traces=StoreConfig(type="files", max_age_days=30))
Storage(path=".nl2sql", index=my_index_store)   # any object whose slot is "index"

The store interfaces are in nl2sql_sdk.stores. A plugin registers a store in the nl2sql.stores entry point group, or in code with registry.add_store(name, cls).

Every slot is read through its interface, so a plugin store works in any slot it fills.

docs.title: Retention
docs.text:
The files trace store and the local results store take max_age_days, 14 and 7 by default (at least 1). It is a key of those two stores, not of every store.

traces:  { type: files, max_age_days: 30 }
results: { type: local, max_age_days: 2 }

engine.storage.purge() deletes the traces and result files last written before that age, and the audit observer's day files older than its max_age_days (90 by default), and the review queue's decided proposals (accepted, rejected, superseded) decided more than settings.review.max_age_days (365) ago, and the conversations last updated more than conversations.max_age_days (30) ago, and the draft dashboards last edited more than that long ago (saved dashboards are never purged), and returns the counts, {"traces": 3, "results": 12, "proposals": 4, "conversations": 2, "dashboards": 1, "audit": 1} (no audit when the engine runs no audit observer, no conversations or dashboards when max_age_days is null). Open proposals are never purged. It publishes the counts as the retention.purged event, which the audit observer writes. A plugin trace or results store is purged when it has a max_age_days attribute, and left alone when it does not (a bucket with its own lifecycle rule, say). Three things call it:

  • nl2sql storage purge, by hand or from cron;
  • nl2sql-api, at startup and then once a day while it serves (a failed purge is logged and tried again the next day);
  • your own code.

Feedback and schema snapshots have no age limit: feedback is cleared by hand (nl2sql feedback clear), and after each index build the snapshots nothing can read any more are deleted (see The state).

docs.title: What is where: engine.storage.info()
docs.text:
engine.storage.info()
# {"index":   {"type": "chroma", "location": ".../.nl2sql/index"},
#  "state":   {"type": "sqlite", "location": ".../.nl2sql/state.db"},
#  "traces":  {"type": "files",  "location": ".../.nl2sql/traces", "max_age_days": 14},
#  "results": {"type": "local",  "location": ".../.nl2sql/results", "max_age_days": 7},
#  "namespace": "nl2sql__local-all-minilm-l6-v2__384"}

type is the store's name, or the class name of a store object; location is its folder or file, or None for a store that does not have one.

docs.title: The state
docs.text: The state store keeps the schema snapshots (immutable, one row per version), the plan cache, the playground's feedback, and the lock that lets one index build run at a time. The engine applies the store's pending migrations when it starts; the built-in sqlite store adopts a 0.5 state.db as it is, and applies them in one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction, so engines or CLI runs opening a new state.db at the same moment apply each one exactly once. A store with nothing pending takes no lock, so a read-only state.db opens. See The state store.

docs.title: The index
docs.text:
The engine embeds; the index store keeps entries and vectors in a namespace per embedding model, nl2sql__<model slug>__<dimension> (for example nl2sql__local-all-minilm-l6-v2__384), filters them, and records each datasource's live build as a BuildPointer (its build_id and the schema_version it was made from). Switching a pointer is the commit, and a run reads the pointers once when it starts. See Indexing.

  • Changing the embedding model opens a new, empty namespace: check() reports the index missing, and nl2sql index builds it. Switching back finds the old namespace still built.
  • nl2sql index prune (engine.index.prune()) drops every namespace but the current model's, including 0.5's nl2sql_store collection, which 0.6 never reads. Run it once after upgrading, and after settling on a new model.
  • The chroma store opens index/ on the first build; reading a missing folder or namespace creates nothing.

docs.title: Sharing
docs.text:
Two engines with different paths share nothing. The commands that only read these stores (nl2sql cache clear, nl2sql feedback, nl2sql trace show, nl2sql storage purge) find them from the same config, so run them with the same --config.

There is no built-in S3 or ADLS results store. The ResultStore interface is four methods; Artifact Store has an S3 example.

In a container, mount a volume and point the path at it:

path: "${env:NL2SQL_DATA_DIR}"

docker run -e NL2SQL_DATA_DIR=/data -v nl2sql-data:/data ...

docs.title: Configuration System
docs.text:
nl2sql reads one config: nl2sql.yaml and the files it includes. Loading it gives one typed Config object, and building that same Config in Python gives exactly the same engine. Everything the engine needs is in it. Only the config path and the provider key variables are read directly (see Environment variables); any other value from the environment is written in the YAML as ${env:VAR}.

The design and its reasoning are in Configuration v2. This page is the reference.

docs.title: nl2sql.yaml
docs.text:
nl2sql init writes a new project, with each section in its own file:

nl2sql init my-project              # an example SQLite datasource, allow_all policies
nl2sql init my-project --demo       # the demo: three sample databases, roles, verified queries
nl2sql init my-project --provider anthropic

nl2sql.yaml            # the table of contents
datasources/
  example.yaml         # one file per datasource (--demo: chinook.yaml, support.yaml, webanalytics.yaml)
llm.yaml               # provider + model; no key, the provider's standard variable is read
embeddings.yaml        # provider: local
policies.yaml          # allow_all: true            (--demo: admin, analyst, viewer roles)
storage.yaml           # path: .nl2sql
knowledge.yaml         # one yaml knowledge source: glossary.yaml
glossary.yaml          # one empty block per datasource (--demo: the Chinook glossary)
curated.yaml           # --demo only: the demo's verified queries
settings.yaml          # --demo only: the demo's tuning knobs
data/                  # --demo only: the three SQLite files, copied
.gitignore             # .nl2sql/ and .env

init refuses to overwrite a file without --force, never writes a key, and checks what it wrote with load_config.

# nl2sql.yaml
version: 2
datasources: { file: datasources/ }      # a folder, one file per datasource
llm:         { file: llm.yaml }
embeddings:  { file: embeddings.yaml }
policies:    { file: policies.yaml }
storage:     { file: storage.yaml }
curated:     { file: curated.yaml }      # optional
secrets:     { file: secrets.yaml }      # optional
settings:    { file: settings.yaml }     # optional
api:         { file: api.yaml }          # optional, read by nl2sql-api only
observers:   { file: observers.yaml }    # optional: where events, logs and metrics go
hooks:       { file: hooks.yaml }        # optional
evals:       { file: evals.yaml }        # optional
knowledge:   { file: knowledge.yaml }    # optional: where the glossary comes from (0.8)
conversations: { file: conversations.yaml }  # optional: follow-up questions (0.9)
chat_tools:  { file: chat_tools.yaml }   # optional: which chat tools are on (0.9)
dashboards:  { file: dashboards.yaml }   # optional (0.9)
mcp:         { file: mcp.yaml }          # optional: nl2sql mcp --http (0.9)

A small project can write every section inline instead. This file builds the same Config as a split layout would:

version: 2
datasources:
  - id: shop
    type: sqlite
    connection: { database: shop.db }
llm:        { provider: anthropic, model: claude-sonnet-5-5 }
embeddings: { provider: local }
policies:   { allow_all: true }
storage:    { path: .nl2sql }
Section Required Page Notes version yes 2. Anything else, or none, is an error that points to the 0.4 mapping. datasources yes Datasources A list; [] is enough. llm yes LLMs The model every agent uses, and per-agent overrides. embeddings yes Embeddings {provider: local} is a complete section. policies yes Policies {allow_all: true} is a complete section. storage yes Storage {path: .nl2sql} is a complete section. curated no Curated Answers Present means curated answers are on. secrets no Secrets The env provider is always there without it. settings no Settings Tuning knobs; every field has a default. api no REST API nl2sql-api's own settings; the engine ignores them. observers no below A list. Absent means the default observers, log and audit; [] means none. hooks no below A list, run in its order. evals no below The eval suites, scorers and regression gate. knowledge no below A list of knowledge sources, in precedence order. Absent (or []) means no knowledge. conversations no below How a model-led turn is bounded and kept. Every field has a default. chat_tools no below A list of chat tool names. Absent means chart and report, if registered; [] means none (ask stays). dashboards no below The starter dashboard's size and the refresh limits. Every field has a default. mcp no below nl2sql mcp --http: where it listens and how it authenticates. Every field has a default.

From Python:

from nl2sql import NL2SQL, load_config

engine = NL2SQL.from_config("nl2sql.yaml")        # path=None: NL2SQL_CONFIG, then ./nl2sql.yaml
cfg = load_config("nl2sql.yaml")                  # the Config, to change in code first
engine = NL2SQL(cfg.model_copy(update={"settings": cfg.settings.model_copy(update={"tenant_id": "acme"})}))

See Public Facade → Creating an engine.

docs.title: file: includes
docs.text:
Rule Detail Shape A section is either inline, or exactly {file: <path>} with no other keys. Relative paths The path is relative to nl2sql.yaml, not to the working directory. One level Only nl2sql.yaml includes. An included file holds the section's body and includes nothing itself. No version Only nl2sql.yaml has version:. Datasource folder datasources: {file: datasources/} names a folder. Every *.yaml in it, sorted by name and not recursive, holds one datasource. id may be left out and defaults to the file name; if it is given, it must equal the file name. Datasource file datasources: {file: datasources.yaml} names a file whose body is the list. List sections observers, hooks, knowledge and chat_tools are lists too: their file's body is the list. Literal paths file: values are never interpolated. Each file once Including the same file twice is an error.

Other relative paths are relative to nl2sql.yaml too: storage.path, and a SQLite or DuckDB database. The engine can be run from any working directory.

docs.title: Secret and variable references
docs.text:
${env:SALES_DB_PASSWORD} reads an environment variable; ${vault:apps/sales:password} reads a secret from the provider whose id is vault (see Secrets). env is built in.

Rule Detail Whole value only A reference is the entire string. "postgres://${env:U}@db" is an error, and there is no default syntax. Secrets resolve late Every api_key, the secret providers' credentials and every value under a datasource's connection keep the reference. It is resolved when the component is built, so engine.config, logs and errors never hold a plaintext secret. Everything else resolves at load Any other field, for example storage.path: "${env:NL2SQL_DATA_DIR}", is resolved by load_config. A variable that is not set is an error naming the field. Inside secrets: Only ${env:...}: one provider cannot depend on another.

docs.title: Observers, hooks and evals
docs.text:
Three sections added in release 0.7 (Wave A). They are accepted and validated now; the engine runs the hooks and the observers, and reads evals from the Wave A change named below. The observers are documented on their own page, Observers.

# observers.yaml: where the engine's events go
- type: log
  level: INFO
- type: audit
  max_age_days: 90
- type: otel                      # needs nl2sql-engine[otel]
  endpoint: http://collector:4317
- type: corp_siem                 # a plugin; its config_model checks the rest
  url: "${env:SIEM_URL}"

# hooks.yaml: code that sees every run at fixed points, in this order (see Hooks)
- type: corp_sql_review
  points: [execute.before]        # a subset of the hook's own points; all of them by default
  on_error: closed                # closed (the default) | open
  approver_roles: [dba]           # who may approve its needs_approval; default policies.admin_roles
  url: "${env:REVIEW_URL}"        # the hook's own keys

# evals.yaml: the suites engine.evals.run runs, and how they are scored
suites: [evals/chinook.yaml]      # relative to nl2sql.yaml
scorers: [result_match, outcome, faithfulness, retrieval_recall, routing]   # the default: all five
curated: true
max_cost_usd: 5.00                # across a run in mode full; required for it
gate:
  max_regressions: 2
  alpha: 0.05
  max_cost_increase: 0.20
Section Item Rule observers {type: <name>, ...} (ObserverConfig) or an observer object in code type names a registered observer (nl2sql.observers); its config_model checks the other keys, and keeps their ${...} references until it is built. Without the section the engine runs log and audit; observers: [] runs none. hooks {type: <name>, points, on_error, approver_roles, ...} (HookConfig) or a hook object in code points takes run.before, datasources.after, plan.after, execute.before, execute.after and answer.after; any other is an error. on_error is closed or open. The hook's config_model checks its own keys. A point the hook does not declare is an error. See Hooks. evals EvalsConfig Strict keys. suites are files of cases, read when a run asks for them, not when the engine starts. gate.alpha is between 0 and 1. See Evals. 
from nl2sql import Config, HookConfig, ObserverConfig

Config(..., observers=[ObserverConfig(type="log"), MyObserver()],
       hooks=[HookConfig(type="corp_sql_review", points=["execute.before"]), MyHook()])

docs.title: Knowledge
docs.text:
The knowledge sources the glossary comes from, in precedence order (release 0.8, Wave B). The engine loads them when it is built and on engine.knowledge.reload(); see Knowledge for the glossary, precedence and who sees what.

# knowledge.yaml: a list, in precedence order
- type: yaml
  path: glossary.yaml             # relative to nl2sql.yaml
- type: corp_catalog              # a plugin; its config_model checks the rest
  url: "${env:CATALOG_URL}"
Section Item Rule knowledge {type: <name>, ...} (KnowledgeSourceConfig) or a knowledge source object in code (one with load) type names a registered knowledge source (nl2sql.knowledge_sources); its config_model checks the other keys and keeps their ${...} references until it is built. A source only reads; glossary.yaml itself is data, not a config section. 
from nl2sql import Config, KnowledgeSourceConfig

Config(..., knowledge=[KnowledgeSourceConfig(type="yaml", path="glossary.yaml"), MySource()])

docs.title: Conversations, chat tools, dashboards and MCP
docs.text:
Four sections for release 0.9 (Wave C). They are accepted and validated now; the Wave C change named with each reads it. Each is optional, and absent, the defaults shown apply. Chart limits are settings.charts (Settings).

# conversations.yaml (every value shown is the default)
context_turns: 3        # turns the model sees
max_tool_calls: 12      # tool calls per turn; the model then makes one last call, tools off
max_turns: 50           # the 51st turn is refused
max_age_days: 30        # null keeps conversations; also bounds draft dashboards

# chat_tools.yaml: a list of registered names (the nl2sql.chat_tools entry point group)
# absent: chart and report (those the registry has); diagram, dashboard_edit and dashboard_pin wait for K2 and D4
- chart
- report

# dashboards.yaml (every value shown is the default)
max_tiles: 10                        # the starter dashboard's size
min_refresh_minutes: 15              # a schedule below this is refused
schedule_identity_max_age_days: 30   # a schedule stops when its saved identity is older

# mcp.yaml (every value shown is the default)
http:
  host: 127.0.0.1
  port: 8765
  path: /mcp
  allowed_hosts: ["127.0.0.1:*", "localhost:*"]   # Host headers accepted
  allowed_origins: []                              # browser Origins accepted
auth: api_keys            # api_keys | none (none: loopback only)
Section Rule conversations Conversations: strict keys; every count is at least 1, and max_age_days: null keeps conversations. Read by engine.conversations (C1). The conversation agent that leads a turn is one of the LLM agents. chat_tools A list of names: none twice, each a registered chat tool (registry.add_chat_tool, or an entry point). An unknown name is an error when the engine is built (chat_tools[i] in the report), with the closest registered name; ask and a plugin whose args_model does not forbid extra keys are errors too. Absent means the default tools (chart and report) that the registry has, so an engine on Registry.empty() starts with none and needs no chat_tools: []; a name you list must be registered. [] means none; ask is the conversation's own tool and is always on. Read by engine.conversations and engine.chat_tools (C2); see Chat tools. dashboards Dashboards: strict keys; every value is at least 1. Read by engine.dashboards (D1 to D3). mcp Mcp: strict keys. http.port is 1 to 65535 and http.path starts with /. auth: none is for loopback only: the server refuses to start on any other host. Read by nl2sql mcp --http (M2). 
from nl2sql import Config
from nl2sql.config import Conversations

Config(..., conversations=Conversations(context_turns=5), chat_tools=["chart", "report"])

docs.title: Strict keys and errors
docs.text:
Every section forbids unknown keys and suggests the closest known one. Names resolved through the registry (type:, provider:) suggest from the installed names. load_config and NL2SQL(...) collect every problem before raising one ConfigError, each naming the file it is in (an included file, not nl2sql.yaml):

nl2sql.yaml has 2 problems:

  datasources/sales.yaml → preferd_tables
    Unknown key. Did you mean 'preferred_tables'?

  llm.yaml → provider
    'antropic' is not an installed LLM provider. Did you mean 'anthropic'?

A secret is shown as its reference, never as its value. A 0.4 file (version: 1) gets one message pointing to the mapping.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Only these are read directly:

Variable Read by Purpose NL2SQL_CONFIG load_config() with no path, the CLI, nl2sql-api Path to nl2sql.yaml. Without it, ./nl2sql.yaml. NL2SQL_LOG_LEVEL configure_logging() The log level when the caller passes none (DEBUG, INFO, ...). Without it, INFO. NL2SQL_LOG_FORMAT configure_logging() text or json (one JSON object per line, with its trace_id) when the caller chooses neither; the CLI's --log-format chooses for any command. Without it, text; any other value is an error (ValueError; the CLI prints it on one line and exits 1). OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY nl2sql/llm/ The fallback key when llm.api_key (or an agent's, or embeddings.api_key) is not set.

Anything else from the environment is written in the YAML as ${env:VAR}. There are no generic overrides such as NL2SQL__SECTION__KEY. Third-party libraries (the OpenTelemetry SDK) still read their own standard variables, the trace redactor scans the environment for values to mask. Nothing in nl2sql writes the environment: a key the demo is given travels in the engine's LLM config, and only the .env loading below adds variables. The architecture tests enforce both (invariants).

docs.title: .env files
docs.text:
Only the entry points load a .env file: the CLI, nl2sql-api and nl2sql demo load the .env next to nl2sql.yaml into the process environment at startup. A variable that is already set always wins; the file never overrides it. Each loads the .env before it configures logging, so a NL2SQL_LOG_LEVEL written there applies (nl2sql demo reads the demo project's .env, except with --hosted, which reads none).

The library itself never reads a .env file. A Python caller that wants one loads it before building the engine:

from dotenv import load_dotenv
from nl2sql import NL2SQL

load_dotenv("my-project/.env")   # or nl2sql.load_env_file("my-project/nl2sql.yaml")
engine = NL2SQL.from_config("my-project/nl2sql.yaml")

nl2sql init adds .env to .gitignore. Keep keys there, or in the environment, never in the YAML.

docs.title: The CLI
docs.text:
Every command reads the same config, named once, before the subcommand:

nl2sql --config prod/nl2sql.yaml index
nl2sql --config prod/nl2sql.yaml run "Top 5 customers by revenue"
NL2SQL_CONFIG=prod/nl2sql.yaml nl2sql curated validate
nl2sql run "..."                       # ./nl2sql.yaml
nl2sql --log-format json run "..."     # JSON log lines, for any command

There are no per-command path flags. Commands that query or index build the engine and call engine.check() first (see Startup). nl2sql cache, nl2sql feedback and nl2sql trace show only need the store paths under storage.path, and build no engine.

docs.title: Checking a config: nl2sql config check
docs.text:
nl2sql config check checks the whole config without starting the engine, so it fits a CI job or a pre-deploy step:

nl2sql --config prod/nl2sql.yaml config check            # files, names, drivers
nl2sql --config prod/nl2sql.yaml config check --connect  # and connect to every datasource

It does what building the engine does, short of the stores:

  • reads nl2sql.yaml and every file it includes, and resolves ${env:...};
  • loads every name the config uses through the registry (type:, provider:, the secret providers): the name is installed, implements the interface version this engine needs, and its drivers are installed;
  • builds the components, which resolves each datasource's connection references, without connecting or calling a model.

With --connect it also connects to every datasource, as engine.check() does, and a datasource that fails is a problem (required or not).

Problems are printed by the file they are in, then a line per secret:

datasources/sales.yaml
  type
    Unknown adapter 'postgress'. Did you mean 'postgres'? Registered: duckdb, mssql, mysql, postgres, sqlite.

llm.yaml
  provider
    Unknown LLM provider 'antropic'. Did you mean 'anthropic'? Registered: anthropic, ollama, openai, openrouter.

Secrets:
  ${env:SALES_DB_PASSWORD} missing (datasources/sales.yaml → connection.password)

prod/nl2sql.yaml: 2 problems in 2 files.

A secret is reported as present or missing, never printed. Where the llm section names no api_key, the provider's standard variable is listed. A missing LLM key is reported but is not a problem, as for the engine: a CI job rarely holds the production key, and engine.check() reports it at startup. Any other secret that does not resolve stops the engine from building, so it is a problem.

Exit code Meaning 0 No problems. 1 One or more problems, or the config was not found. 2 A usage error: an unknown option.

The check creates no file under storage.path. From Python, the same check is nl2sql.config.check.check_config(path, registry=..., connect=...), which returns the problems, the secrets and the datasource statuses.

docs.title: Startup: check() and required
docs.text:
Building the engine never connects to a datasource or calls a model: every problem it can find without a connection is one ConfigError. engine.check() then connects to each datasource, checks that every agent's API key resolves (no model call) and reports the index status.

The CLI, nl2sql-api (in its lifespan, before it accepts requests) and nl2sql demo call check() at startup:

  • A datasource with required: true that fails, or datasources configured and none ready, raises EngineNotReady: the entry point prints the report and refuses to start (the CLI exits 1).
  • An optional datasource that fails is printed, left out of routing, and the entry point runs degraded.
# datasources/sales.yaml
type: postgres
required: true           # without it, nothing works: refuse to start
connection: { host: db.internal, database: sales, user: nl2sql, password: "${env:SALES_DB_PASSWORD}" }

A Python caller decides for itself. Without check(), a broken datasource fails the first query that targets it, with its reason.

docs.title: From 0.4
docs.text: 0.5 reads only nl2sql.yaml. There is no migration command: map each 0.4 file, variable and flag with these tables. nl2sql init writes a fresh layout to start from.

docs.title: Files
docs.text: 0.4 0.5 configs/datasources.yaml (DATASOURCE_CONFIG) datasources:, one file per datasource in datasources/. connection.type moves up to type; options: and the top-level limits become limits: {row_limit, timeout_ms, max_bytes}. configs/llm.yaml (LLM_CONFIG) llm:, flat: default:'s keys are the top level; agents: are keyed by node name (ast_planner, not astplanner); name: and version: are gone. configs/policies.json (POLICIES_CONFIG) policies:, in YAML; the role: field that repeated the key is gone. configs/secrets.yaml (SECRETS_CONFIG) secrets:, without version. hashi is now hashicorp. configs/curated.yaml (CURATED_CONFIG) curated:, without version. Present means on. configs/sample_questions.yaml (SAMPLE_QUESTIONS, ROUTING_EXAMPLES) sample_questions: on each datasource. .env, .env.<name> (ENV, APP_ENV, ENV_FILE_PATH) The .env next to nl2sql.yaml, loaded by the entry points only. .env.demo and configs/*.demo.* nl2sql init --demo (and nl2sql demo, which runs it): nl2sql.yaml, its files, and .env.

docs.title: Settings variables
docs.text: 0.4 variable 0.5 OPENAI_API_KEY llm.api_key / embeddings.api_key, or the fallback variable above VECTOR_STORE storage.path (the index is <path>/index/) VECTOR_STORE_COLLECTION removed (an internal constant) EMBEDDING_PROVIDER embeddings.provider EMBEDDING_MODEL embeddings.model TENANT_ID settings.tenant_id CURATED_ENABLED removed: the curated section is present or absent CURATED_MATCH_TOP_K settings.curated.match_top_k CURATED_MATCH_FLOOR settings.curated.match_floor GLOBAL_TIMEOUT_SEC settings.pipeline.timeout_s RESULT_ARTIFACT_BASE_URI storage.path (<path>/results/) RESULT_ARTIFACT_PATH_TEMPLATE removed: a fixed layout under <path>/results/ RESULT_ARTIFACT_BACKEND, RESULT_ARTIFACT_S3_*, RESULT_ARTIFACT_ADLS_* removed: results are local; the S3 and ADLS backends are deleted SCHEMA_STORE_BACKEND removed: SQLite at <path>/state.db SCHEMA_STORE_PATH storage.path (<path>/state.db, which also holds the plan cache and feedback) SCHEMA_STORE_MAX_VERSIONS settings.schema.max_versions SCHEMA_VERSION_MISMATCH_POLICY removed: a run reads the schema version its index build was made from PLAN_CACHE_ENABLED settings.pipeline.plan_cache FEEDBACK_ENABLED settings.feedback.enabled SCHEMA_RETRIEVAL_FULL_SNAPSHOT_MAX_TABLES settings.retrieval.full_snapshot_max_tables LOGICAL_VALIDATOR_STRICT_COLUMNS settings.pipeline.strict_columns RBAC_REFUSAL_NAMES_TABLES policies.refusal_names_tables SQL_AGENT_MAX_RETRIES settings.pipeline.retries.max SQL_AGENT_RETRY_BASE_DELAY_SEC settings.pipeline.retries.base_delay_s SQL_AGENT_RETRY_MAX_DELAY_SEC settings.pipeline.retries.max_delay_s SQL_AGENT_RETRY_JITTER_SEC settings.pipeline.retries.jitter_s LLM_PRICES llm.prices TRACE_MODE settings.traces.mode TRACE_DIR storage.path (<path>/traces/) RESULT_ROW_LIMIT settings.results.row_limit RESULT_FETCH_BATCH_SIZE settings.results.fetch_batch_size ANSWER_PREVIEW_ROWS settings.results.preview_rows TRACE_SAMPLE_ROWS settings.traces.sample_rows TRACE_MAX_FIELD_CHARS settings.traces.max_field_chars NL2SQL_TODAY settings.pipeline.today OBSERVABILITY_EXPORTER an otel observer in the observers section (0.7) OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT the otel observer's endpoint (0.7)

docs.title: Other variables
docs.text: 0.4 variable 0.5 NL2SQL_API_ROLE_HEADER api.role_header NL2SQL_API_ROLE api.role NL2SQL_API_TRUST_BODY_ROLE api.trust_body_role NL2SQL_API_CORS_ORIGINS (comma-separated) api.cors_origins (a list) NL2SQL_API_ADMIN_ROLES policies.admin_roles NL2SQL_DEMO_HOSTED nl2sql demo --hosted NL2SQL_DEMO_QUESTIONS_PER_MINUTE, NL2SQL_DEMO_QUESTIONS_PER_SESSION nl2sql demo --questions-per-minute N --questions-per-session N VAULT_ADDR, VAULT_TOKEN secrets.providers[].url / .token (write ${env:VAULT_TOKEN} to keep reading the variable) AZURE_KEYVAULT_URL secrets.providers[].vault_url ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY unchanged: the fallback key variables

docs.title: CLI
docs.text: 0.4 0.5 nl2sql setup nl2sql init [DIR] [--provider NAME] [--force]; the guided flow comes in a later release nl2sql setup --demo nl2sql init --demo [DIR] (or just nl2sql demo) --env NAME, --env-file PATH removed: the .env next to nl2sql.yaml is loaded --config PATH (the datasource file), --llm-config, --secrets-config, --policies-config, --vector-store the one global nl2sql --config PATH/nl2sql.yaml curated validate/test --curated --config --secrets nl2sql --config ... curated validate/test policy validate --config --policies --secrets nl2sql --config ... policy validate nl2sql --env demo <command> (from the demo folder) nl2sql --config nl2sql-demo/nl2sql.yaml <command>, or run it from inside nl2sql-demo/

docs.title: Source references
docs.text:
• Models and load_config: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/config/
  • init_project, demo_config: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/config/project.py
  • The runtime built from a Config: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/runtime.py
  • The CLI's --config: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/cli/common/engine.py
  • nl2sql config check: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/config/check.py, printed by packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/cli/commands/config_check.py

docs.title: Conversations
docs.text:
Wave C, 0.9

start, ask, stream, retry, ask_only, tool, report, get, list and delete work, with the chat tools chart and report. The design is Wave C, section 3.

A conversation is a chat over the database. The model decides, step by step, whether to answer or to ask the database a question through the same typed plan and validator as run_query. It never writes SQL and never sees result rows.

conversation = engine.conversations.start(user_context=me)
turn = engine.conversations.ask(conversation.id, "How many customers are there?", user_context=me)
print(turn.reply)                       # the model's closing message
print(turn.steps[0].result.sub_queries[0].sql)   # what ran; the rows are not stored
follow_up = engine.conversations.ask(conversation.id, "and by country?", user_context=me)

Every method takes the caller (user_context, keyword-only and required). The methods are listed in Conversations API.

docs.title: A turn
docs.text:
flowchart TD
  IN["ask(text) or ask(choice=...)"] --> K{"choice?"}
  K -->|yes| RE["ask step: the pending question, with the choice"]
  K -->|no| M["model call: reply or tool call"]
  M -->|reply| ST["store the turn"]
  M -->|"ask"| RUN["run_query: typed plan, validator, cost rule"]
  M -->|"chat tool"| TOOL["registry tool: no model call"]
  RUN -->|"clarification, approval or stop"| ST
  RUN -->|"ok or error"| M
  TOOL --> M
  M -->|"bound reached"| LAST["one last call, tools off"]
  LAST --> ST
  RE --> ST
  • The model chooses. Each step is one structured call (ModelStep): a reply, or one call of the ask tool with a question that stands alone, or of an enabled chat tool (a chart, a report). A reply may carry offers: tools it suggests, which run only when a client calls tool. The model sees the last context_turns turns as one JSON object (the questions that ran, each answer's summary, the columns, the datasources and tables read), never rows. Everything earlier said, the new message included, reaches it as a JSON string value: text in the history cannot pass for an instruction or a section marker.
  • The bound. At most max_tool_calls tool calls per turn, then one more model call with the tools off. A turn makes at most max_tool_calls + 1 model calls. They count against settings.pipeline.max_llm_calls and max_cost_usd; a refusal ends the turn stopped.
  • A step the model got wrong (an unknown tool, a bad argument, an option id that is not pending) is sent back with what was wrong. After the parse retries the turn ends error with MODEL_STEP_INVALID (Turn.error) and the reply "I could not tell what to do with that. Please ask it as a full question."
  • Each ask step is a run of its own, with its own trace_id, events and result pages, and the cost rule, scope and hooks of any run. A hook at run.before sees conversation_id.

docs.title: Clarifications and approvals
docs.text:
• A run that ends needs_clarification ends the turn and sets Conversation.pending. The next turn can pass choice="b" (an option id; the turn is of kind choice, its text the option's label, and no model is called) or text the model maps to an option by calling ask with choice. Either way the pending request's own question is re-asked with the choice. Any next turn clears pending. A choice with nothing pending is a ValueError.
  • A run that ends needs_approval ends the turn. An approver acts on each ApprovalRequest in turn.steps[i].result.approvals_needed outside the conversation; the asker then calls retry(conversation_id, user_context=..., approvals=[...]), which re-runs the last ask step's question as a turn of kind retry, with no model call.
  • ask_only(conversation_id, question, user_context=..., choice=None) runs just the ask tool (a turn of kind tool, no model call) and returns the full QueryResult with its rows. MCP's ask will use it.

docs.title: Streaming
docs.text: stream(...) takes the same arguments as ask and yields the caller-safe run events of each ask step (run.started to run.finished), conversation.step after each step and, last, conversation.turn whose data["stored"] is the stored Turn as JSON. Ownership and the arguments are checked at the call; a conversation that is already running a turn raises ConversationBusy from the first next. Closing the iterator early cancels the turn and stores nothing.

docs.title: Ownership and retention
docs.text: Rule Detail Owner start records the caller's tenant_id (else the engine's) and user_id. Any other caller gets ConversationNotFound, as for an id that does not exist. Roles Never stored. Each turn runs with the user_context passed to that call, so a role taken away applies at the next turn. No user_id Allowed, and owned by "no user": every caller without one in that tenant sees those conversations. Fine for a script, not for a server. One turn at a time A turn holds the state store's lock conversation:<id>; a second ask, retry or stream raises ConversationBusy. Limits conversations.max_turns (50): the next turn, whichever of ask, stream, retry or ask_only it is, is a ValueError naming CONVERSATION_TOO_LONG and the fix, "Start a new conversation." Results A stored step keeps its question, plan, SQL, explanation and summary, never the rows. Read them with engine.results.page(step.trace_id, ...) until they are purged. Retention engine.storage.purge() deletes conversations last updated more than conversations.max_age_days (30; null keeps them) ago and reports conversations in retention.purged.

docs.title: Events
docs.text: conversation.started (from start), conversation.step (after each step, in the turn's scope, with the tool, the status and the argument names, never values) and conversation.turn (once the turn is stored; it closes the turn's scope). The turn's trace_id carries the loop's own llm.calls, and Turn.usage holds their usage.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: conversations: in nl2sql.yaml (context_turns, max_tool_calls, max_turns, max_age_days) and the conversation agent in llm.yaml; see Configuration System and LLM.

docs.title: Chat tools
docs.text:
Wave C, 0.9: the runner, chart and report are built

diagram arrives with K2 and dashboard_edit and dashboard_pin with D4; until then each raises NotImplementedError, which a conversation reports as a failed step, so they are off by default. The design is Wave C, section 4.

A chat tool turns something a conversation already has into something else, with no model call of its own. The five built-ins:

Tool Does Filled by chart Draws an answer's data as a line, bar, big number or table (Charts); args turn, step, result_id, kind K1 (built) diagram Draws the tables of an answer, or of a datasource, as Mermaid (Diagrams) K2 report Writes the conversation's answered turns up as Markdown; args turns, title C2 (built) dashboard_edit Builds or changes a dashboard (Dashboards) D4 dashboard_pin Saves the dashboard being built, whole D4

docs.title: Which tools are on
docs.text: chat_tools: in nl2sql.yaml lists registered names. Absent, the default tools are on: chart and report, those of them the registry has (an engine built on Registry.empty() has none). diagram, dashboard_edit and dashboard_pin are off until K2 and D4 make them real; name them in chat_tools: to try them. [] turns every registry tool off and leaves ask, the conversation's own tool, which is always on. A name you list that the registry does not know is a config error when the engine is built, and so is ask (it is not a registry tool). engine.chat_tools.list() returns the enabled tools (ChatToolInfo: name, description, JSON Schema of the arguments); it takes no caller, as it lists names.

docs.title: Three ways a tool runs
docs.text:
• The model calls it. In a turn the model may call an enabled tool after any result. Its arguments are checked against the tool's args_model before it runs, and a bad call goes back to the model with what was wrong. The tool sees the conversation including the steps already taken in this turn, so a chart of the answer just asked for works in one turn. The model gets the step back as a short description (a chart: its kind, why and its columns; a diagram: its text; a report or JSON: its title only) and never the data. max_tool_calls bounds ask and tools together.
  • The model offers it. A reply may carry offers, tools it suggests (Turn.offers). Nothing runs; a client shows a button and, on a click, calls conversations.tool.
  • A client calls it by name. engine.conversations.tool(cid, "chart", {"turn": 3}, user_context=me) runs one enabled tool as a turn of kind tool, with no model call. Arguments that do not validate raise ValueError and store nothing. A name that is not enabled is stored as a failed step.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
A step that does not succeed has status error and ToolStep.error = {"code", "message"}; the model sees it and may go on.

Code When TOOL_FAILED The tool raised, or returned something that is not a ToolOutput. The message gives the exception type only, since its text can quote data; the full error is in the log. TOOL_NOT_APPLICABLE The tool raised ToolNotApplicable(message): it cannot apply to that turn (no answer to chart, rows expired). UNKNOWN_CHAT_TOOL The name is not enabled; the message names the enabled tools.

Every call, successful or not, publishes chat_tool.called (tool, conversation_id, turn, ok, seconds, error_code).

docs.title: The report
docs.text: engine.conversations.report(cid, user_context=me, turns=None, title=None) returns Markdown assembled from the stored turns, with no model call: for each answered question its summary, the plain-English explanation, the first 20 rows, the takeaway of the chart the data is drawn as (unless it is a table), the SQL in a <details> block and the trace id. Rows are read back through engine.results; once they are purged the section says "Results expired." and keeps the text, the SQL and the trace. turns picks turn numbers (an unknown one is a ValueError); the default is every answered turn. A conversation with nothing answered is a ValueError. Every turn is considered, and a question counts when its ask step succeeded, even if a later tool step in that turn failed. The report tool is the same call, so it covers earlier turns, not the one it is called in. A stored tool output never holds row data (D106): the report tool stores the report without its row tables and chart takeaways, and a stored chart output has its spec and columns but data.rows is empty. Ask conversations.report again for the full report, and engine.results.chart to draw a chart; both read the rows from the results while their retention keeps them.

docs.title: Writing one
docs.text:
A tool is a class with interface_version = 1, a one-line description the model reads, an args_model (a pydantic model that must forbid extra keys, or the engine refuses it when it is built; its JSON Schema is shown to the model) and __call__(ctx: ToolContext, args) -> ToolOutput. It is built with no arguments. It reaches the engine only through the public NL2SQL facade in ctx.engine, and may import only the top-level nl2sql and nl2sql.chat_tools. Register it under the nl2sql.chat_tools entry point group, or with registry.add_chat_tool(name, cls), and name it in chat_tools: in nl2sql.yaml. The name ask is taken.

from typing import ClassVar

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict

from nl2sql.chat_tools import ToolContext, ToolNotApplicable, ToolOutput


class CountArgs(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")


class QuestionCount:
    interface_version: ClassVar[int] = 1
    description: ClassVar[str] = "Say how many questions this conversation has answered."
    args_model: ClassVar[type[BaseModel]] = CountArgs

    def __call__(self, ctx: ToolContext, args: BaseModel) -> ToolOutput:
        asked = sum(s.call.name == "ask" for t in ctx.conversation.turns for s in t.steps)
        if not asked:
            raise ToolNotApplicable("Nothing has been asked yet.")
        return ToolOutput(kind="markdown", title="Questions", body=f"{asked} questions so far.")


registry.add_chat_tool("question_count", QuestionCount)

ToolOutput.kind is chart (a ChartSpec as JSON), mermaid, markdown or json; refs carries ids a client needs ({"dashboard_id": ...}). A tool makes no model call. ctx.conversation is a copy, so a tool cannot change it.

docs.title: Dashboards
docs.text:
Partly built (Wave C, 0.9)

Workspaces, the dashboard store, pin, move and the manual edits work (D1). Refresh, filters and schedules (D2), the starter dashboard (D3) and building in chat (D4) have their signatures and raise NotImplementedError naming the pull request that fills them. The design is Wave C, section 6.

A dashboard is a set of charts, each holding the typed plan that produced it, saved whole into a private workspace. Opening one serves stored results after the access check; refreshing re-runs the stored plans as the caller with no model call. The methods are in Dashboards API.
