The engine's own observers (log, audit, otel and plugins) subscribe the same way, from the observers section: see Observers.

docs.title: Logs carry the run's trace_id
docs.text:
Every log line written while a question runs carries its trace_id and tenant_id, on the caller's thread and on every graph worker thread, so a trace, its events and its log lines join on one id. nl2sql, nl2sql demo and nl2sql-api configure logging with the filter that adds them (--log-format json, or NL2SQL_LOG_FORMAT=json, writes them as fields). A library caller who configures logging their own way adds nl2sql.TraceContextFilter to their handler:

import logging
from nl2sql import TraceContextFilter

handler = logging.StreamHandler()
handler.addFilter(TraceContextFilter())
handler.setFormatter(logging.Formatter("%(asctime)s [%(trace_id)s] %(name)s %(message)s"))
logging.getLogger().addHandler(handler)

docs.title: The trace
docs.text: A run's trace lists its events (every one but answer.delta) under events.

docs.title: Feedback and Signals
docs.text:
Nothing in the engine can tell on its own whether a live answer was right. Two small signals help: a person's rating of an answer in the playground, and the guardrail rates the engine already records for every run. nl2sql feedback reads both. Thumbs-up runs can then be exported as draft entries for the gold set, and thumbs-up generated answers as proposed verified queries.

The playground and nl2sql feedback are both built on engine.feedback (record, list, stats, export, clear, correct), which any Python caller can use too: see the public facade.

docs.title: Rating an answer in the playground
docs.text:
After a run, below Cost & time, the playground asks Was this answer right? with two buttons, 👍 Right and 👎 Wrong. A click saves the rating at once. A note is optional: pick Wrong number, Wrong table, Wrong filter or Missing rows, or type a few words (up to 280 characters), then Save note. Rating the same run again replaces the earlier rating.

The page sends only the run's trace id, the rating and the note. The server stores what it answered for that run, from its own copy of the last 200 runs, so a page cannot put a question or SQL into the table that the engine never produced. A run the playground did not answer is refused with 404.

Route Gate GET /api/feedback Whether feedback is on (and why not), the counts and the last 50 ratings. The ratings are returned only where the gate below passes. POST /api/feedback {"trace_id", "rating": "up" \| "down", "note"}. Local only, the same gate as Settings, Rebuild and the Retrieval inspector: on a non-loopback --host it answers 403 unless nl2sql demo --allow-settings, and it refuses another site's page (a foreign Origin), a non-loopback hostname and anything but JSON.

Feedback is available in the playground that nl2sql demo starts, and on by default. settings.feedback.enabled: false turns it off: the control then says so and POST /api/feedback answers 403.

docs.title: What is stored
docs.text:
One row per run, kept by the engine's state store (storage.state) beside the schema snapshots and the plan cache. The built-in sqlite state store keeps it in a feedback table of <storage.path>/state.db (nl2sql-demo/.nl2sql/state.db in the demo). No new service or file. The engine builds each row (nl2sql.feedback.rated_row) and hands it to StateStore.add_feedback, so a plugin state store keeps the same row.

Column Holds trace_id The run's id (primary key), the same id as its trace file. created_at Unix time of the rating. rating, note up or down, and the optional note. question, role, status The question as asked, the role it ran as, and the result status (success, plan_only, error). sql The generated SQL per sub-query, as a JSON list. Empty for a run the role was refused (SECURITY_VIOLATION). error_codes The blocking error codes, as a JSON list. Codes only, never messages. retries, validator_failures, plan_cache_hits, sub_queries The run's guardrail counters (below). models The provider and model each LLM node ran on, as JSON. engine_version The nl2sql-engine version, plus the git commit when run from a checkout. datasource_ids The datasources the run's sub-queries ran on, each once, as a JSON list. source Where the answer came from: verified (a verified query from curated.yaml) or generated.

datasource_ids and source were added after the table first shipped. A state.db from before them gains both columns, empty, through the state store's migrations when the engine next starts; the rows already in it keep their ratings and read the two as null. See The state store → Migrations.

Privacy. A row never holds result rows, the written answer, sample values, error messages or keys. It holds only what the run showed the role it ran as: the SQL of a refused run is dropped, and error messages (which can name a forbidden table) are not kept. nl2sql feedback clear deletes every row.

docs.title: Guardrail rates: nl2sql feedback stats
docs.text:
nl2sql feedback stats          # a table
nl2sql feedback stats --json   # the same numbers as JSON
nl2sql feedback stats --traces other/traces

stats counts every recorded run once, keyed by trace id: the feedback rows, plus every trace in <storage.path>/traces when settings.traces.mode kept them (the demo's config sets always). When a run has both, its counters come from the trace, which also sees a validator rejection a retry then fixed, and its rating from the row.

Signal Counted as Thumbs up / down Ratings; the rates are over rated runs. Refused, by code Runs that ended with SECURITY_VIOLATION or QUESTION_NOT_ANSWERABLE. Refiner retried Runs with at least one retry (retry_count summed over sub-queries). Validator rejected a plan Runs where the logical validator rejected a plan at least once. Errored, by code Runs with any other blocking error code. Plan cache hits Sub-queries whose plan came from the plan cache, over all planned sub-queries.

Every other rate is over all runs. From canned data (four rated runs, three more traces):

7 runs, 4 rated (feedback table plus traces in traces)

  Signal                                 Runs             Rate
 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Thumbs up                                 2   50.0% of rated
  Thumbs down                               2   50.0% of rated
  Refused                                   2            28.6%
    SECURITY_VIOLATION                      1            14.3%
    QUESTION_NOT_ANSWERABLE                 1            14.3%
  Refiner retried (3 retries)               2            28.6%
  Validator rejected a plan (2 times)       2            28.6%
  Errored                                   1            14.3%
    DB_EXECUTION_ERROR                      1            14.3%
  Plan cache hits (2 of 5 sub-queries)      2            40.0%

nl2sql feedback list prints the ratings, newest first, with their notes.

docs.title: Growing an eval suite: nl2sql feedback export --good
docs.text:
nl2sql feedback export --good                     # feedback_gold_drafts.yaml
nl2sql feedback export --good --out drafts.yaml

Each thumbs-up run becomes a draft eval case, written to a suite file of its own:

  • status: draft and origin: feedback;
  • the question, the run's SQL as the sql candidate, and the datasources it read;
  • outcome set to allowed for the role it ran as;
  • no rows.

A run with no SQL, or with more than one statement, is skipped: a case's sql is one query. Drafts never replace reviewed cases. export refuses an --out that is:

  • a suite the package ships;
  • a suite evals.yaml names;
  • an existing file that holds an approved case.

A person must review every draft before it runs. A thumbs up says an answer looked right, not that its SQL is the reference answer. To promote a draft:

  1. Check that the SQL answers the question.
  2. Fill in difficulty, tags, tables, columns and outcome (add the roles that must be refused).
  3. Set status: approved.
  4. Write its rows:
engine.evals.regenerate("feedback_gold_drafts.yaml")

docs.title: Proposing verified queries: the review queue
docs.text:
A thumbs-up on a generated answer also files a verified_query proposal in the review queue: engine.feedback.record(..., rating="up") keeps the rating and, when the run qualifies, proposes the question and the run's SQL for curated.yaml. Nothing is written until an admin accepts it:

nl2sql review list --kind verified_query --as admin
nl2sql review accept <id> --as admin

Runs answered by a verified query, failed runs, runs on more than one datasource, runs with no SQL or more than one statement, and rows rated before the table recorded the datasource file nothing. The same change is one proposal however often it is rated; a thumbs-up therefore influences routing only after a person accepts it. See From feedback to verified queries.

docs.title: Correcting an answer: nl2sql feedback correct
docs.text:
A thumbs-down says an answer was wrong; a correction also says what was right. engine.feedback.correct takes the run's trace id and exactly one fix, the right SQL or the right plan, and files it as a verified_query proposal (origin correction) in the review queue:

nl2sql feedback correct 7c0e2f4a-... --sql revenue.sql --note "Revenue is invoiced, not gross." --as analyst
nl2sql feedback correct 7c0e2f4a-... --plan revenue.yaml --question "What was revenue last year?" --as analyst

from nl2sql import UserContext

analyst = UserContext(user_id="bob", roles=["analyst"])
proposal = engine.feedback.correct(result.trace_id, sql="SELECT SUM(Total) AS revenue FROM Invoice",
                                   note="Revenue is invoiced, not gross.", user_context=analyst)

The fix is checked as the corrector before anything is queued, and a check that fails raises CorrectionRefused (a ValueError) with a code and the check's own messages; the command prints them and exits 1.

Step What happens Refused as The run Its kept trace gives the question (question overrides it), its datasource and its SQL; without a trace, its rating does. First, the corrector's role must reach every datasource the run read and every table its SQL read; the refusal names none of them, and the run's rating is left as it was. Then a run on several datasources is refused (a verified query answers from one), and the run is rated down with the note unless it already is. no_run, denied, multi_datasource A plan fix Runs as a pinned plan with execute=False: plan.after, the logical validator and the generator, under the corrector's scope, with no model call. The SQL is the engine's rendering. invalid_plan, with the validator's messages A SQL fix Must parse as exactly one read-only query in the datasource's dialect (the curated config's own check; a trailing ; and comment are fine), with no :name placeholders. It reads plain tables only, never a table-valued function, and calls only the functions a plan may call plus CAST, CASE, EXISTS and the current date and time. It reads only tables the corrector's role may read. not_read_only, denied The hooks The SQL passes the execute.before hooks with the corrector as the caller. A deny or a failed hook refuses it, and so does a request for approval: a correction is never run with an approval. hook_denied, needs_approval The check The SQL runs once through the adapter, as nl2sql curated test runs a verified query: read-only, under the datasource's limits, reading the first batch of rows and keeping none. An empty result is allowed. failed, with the adapter's message (an error it did not wrap is named by its type only) The proposal change is in curated.yaml's shape: an id slugged from the question, the question as its one phrasing, the SQL, and the note as its description (a placeholder without one). tables lists every table the fix and the original SQL read; evidence holds the trace id, the original SQL, ran, row_count and columns.

Nothing is written to curated.yaml (or any file a person owns) until an admin accepts the proposal, usually with edits: a better id, more phrasings, and :name params in place of the literal values. Only a caller whose scope reaches every table in tables sees the proposal. Keep traces (settings.traces.mode: always) to correct runs that succeeded and were not rated; the default keeps only failed runs' traces.

docs.title: Turning it off and clearing it
docs.text:
• settings.feedback.enabled: false stops the playground recording ratings.
  • nl2sql feedback clear deletes every rating (--yes skips the prompt). Schema snapshots and the plan cache are kept, and nl2sql cache clear never touches the ratings.

docs.title: Observability Stack
docs.text:
NL2SQL provides structured logging always, per-question token and time telemetry on every run, and events that observers turn into logs, an audit log and OpenTelemetry metrics and traces.

  • Every run reports its cost and timings in the result. run_with_graph() always attaches NodeTimingCallback (wall-clock seconds per node, into QueryResult.timings) and TokenUsageCallback (LLM calls, input / cached / output / reasoning tokens and model seconds per node and per question, into QueryResult.usage). That covers the Python API, the REST API, the CLI and the demo playground. Every call is priced from the dated price table and llm.prices (Prices), so usage.cost is the question's cost whenever every model it called has a price. See the query API.
  • Every question runs under caps. settings.pipeline.max_llm_calls (60) and max_cost_usd (none) are checked before each model call; a question that reaches one ends stopped and publishes run.limit_reached, which the audit log records (Per-question caps).
  • Everything else is an event, and observers decide where it goes. A run publishes its steps (node.*), each model call (llm.call, from TokenUsageCallback), each plan cache lookup (plan_cache.lookup) and its summary (run.finished); engine.llm.replace publishes llm.changed. The observers in the observers section receive them: by default log and audit.
  • OpenTelemetry is an observer, and an extra. An otel observer (with pip install "nl2sql-engine[otel]") records the metrics below and one span per run with a child span per step, on providers of its own, exported over OTLP (gRPC) or to the console. Without one, nothing exports to OpenTelemetry.
  • The audit log is the audit observer's. JSON lines under <storage.path>/audit/, one summary line per run plus the denials, approvals, limits and changes; 90 days by default, purged by engine.storage.purge().

docs.title: Telemetry flow
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant Pipeline as run_with_graph()
    participant Usage as TokenUsageCallback
    participant Bus as The engine's bus
    participant Observers as log, audit, otel
    participant Result as QueryResult

    Pipeline->>Usage: always attached
    Usage->>Result: usage
    Usage->>Bus: llm.call
    Pipeline->>Bus: node.started, node.finished, run.finished
    Bus->>Observers: each event, in config order

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
The otel observer records:

  • nl2sql.node.duration (histogram, seconds), attribute node, from node.finished.
  • nl2sql.token.usage (counter), attributes node, model and type: one point per LLM call for each of input, cached_input, cache_write_input, output, reasoning and total, from llm.call.
  • nl2sql.plan_cache.lookups (counter), attributes result (hit or miss) and datasource_id, from plan_cache.lookup. The per-question view is QueryResult.usage.plan_cache_hits and sub_queries[].plan_source; see Determinism → The plan cache.
  • nl2sql.run.cost (histogram, USD), attribute status, from run.finished when the run was priced.

The 0.6 datasource_id attribute on nl2sql.token.usage is gone: llm.call does not carry it. Token usage is not kept in a process-wide list; read it from QueryResult.usage.

docs.title: Audit logging
docs.text: The audit observer writes <storage.path>/audit/<date>.jsonl, one JSON line per audited event: one summary per run (run.finished or run.failed: the user, roles, datasources, tables read, status and source; never rows), and each policy.decision, hook.decision that denied, asked for or carried an approval or failed, run.limit_reached, llm.changed, index.swapped, retention.purged and schema.drifted. llm.changed names who made the change and each agent's old and new provider and model, never a key. See Observers → audit.

docs.title: Structured logging
docs.text: The library does not configure logging on import; the application entry point calls nl2sql.configure_logging after loading the .env next to nl2sql.yaml, so a NL2SQL_LOG_LEVEL there applies (the REST API does it in its lifespan, the CLI before every command, nl2sql demo again once the demo project's .env is loaded). JSON lines are chosen with nl2sql --log-format json (any command) or NL2SQL_LOG_FORMAT=json (any entry point); text is the default. Every question's RunScope sets the run's trace_id and tenant_id in the context TraceContextFilter reads, inside the run's worker, so a log line written during a run carries them, on LangGraph's worker threads too.

docs.title: Source references
docs.text:
• Observers: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/observers/ (log.py, audit.py, otel.py)
  • Events: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/events/
  • Token usage: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/services/callbacks/token_handler.py
  • Logging: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/common/logger.py

docs.title: Releases
docs.text:
What each release is for, in plain words. The full list of commits is in CHANGELOG.md. How a release is cut is in Releasing.

  • 0.8.0: Wave B: business knowledge in the index and prompts, a review queue, a schema profiler, clarifying questions, "why this answer" and a cost guard.
  • 0.7.0: Wave A: events and observers, hooks and approval, nl2sql eval with a regression gate, five-signal routing, answer sanity checks, cost caps, schema drift and an MCP server.
  • 0.6.0: a real-database test bed, adapter SDK v2 and its conformance kit, four storage slots, OpenAI-compatible providers and allow/deny policy globs.
  • 0.5.0: Configuration v2, one nl2sql.yaml, an extension registry, a namespaced Python API and per-engine config; a clean break from 0.4.
  • 0.4.1: admin-only REST routes, opt-in enrichment, schema-aware policies and a datasource that fails no longer stops startup.
  • 0.4.0: curated answers, where a question that matches a verified query runs its reviewed SQL and is labelled verified.
  • 0.3.0: results at any size, paged and downloadable, with a 20-row preview for the answer and a streamed run.
  • 0.2.4: a cached plan is reused only on the day it was made, so relative dates stay current.
  • 0.2.3: the model knows today's date and its data, and wrong or empty queries are retried or explained.
  • 0.2.2: correct answers or clear refusals for multi-sub-query questions, and the demo at nl2sql.codewithnk.com.
  • 0.2.1: the release image on Python 3.12, and a reliable Space deploy.
  • 0.2.0: the hosted demo, with or without a key, and pip install "nl2sql-engine[demo]".
  • 0.1.2: a merged release PR publishes to PyPI on its own.
  • 0.1.1: fixes for nl2sql doctor, the Docker demo, pipeline errors and the API image.
  • 0.1.0: the first release, as three packages on PyPI.

docs.title: NL2SQL 0.1.0
docs.text:
The first release: the NL2SQL engine, its REST API and the adapter SDK on PyPI as three packages that share one version.

Released 2026-08-28.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• pip install nl2sql-engine gives you the engine and the nl2sql CLI. nl2sql-api serves it over REST, and nl2sql-adapter-sdk is what a third-party database adapter builds against.
  • The model writes a typed plan, never SQL. The plan is checked against the schema and your role before any SQL is generated.
  • A DuckDB adapter joins PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server and SQLite.
  • The Docker demo now starts the application as well as its databases, so it can answer a question with nothing else installed.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• A DuckDB adapter, installed with the nl2sql-engine[duckdb] extra (#57).
  • The Docker demo runs the application next to its databases. SQL Server is now opt-in, so the first start skips a 1.6 GB download (#59).
  • Releases are automated: release-please writes the changelog, and a merged release PR publishes to PyPI (#58).

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text:
• Cancelling one run no longer cancels every other run in the process (#48).
  • The REST API needs its CORS origins listed. It no longer accepts any origin together with credentials (#49).
  • The minimum versions of pydantic, langgraph and chromadb are now correct (#50).
  • Importing nl2sql no longer changes your application's logging setup (#51).
  • The NL2SQL facade builds its settings API correctly (#52).

docs.title: Docs
docs.text: • The README and architecture docs now describe only code that exists (#54), and the docs cover the three-package layout (#60).

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• No API image was published to GHCR for 0.1.0, because the image build failed. 0.1.1 fixes the build.
  • The project is pre-1.0, so the API can still change between minor versions.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
pip install "nl2sql-engine==0.1.0"

Breaking changes: nine earlier distributions are now three, nl2sql-engine, nl2sql-api and nl2sql-adapter-sdk, and the dialect adapters ship inside the engine (#56). The import name is still nl2sql.

docs.title: What's next
docs.text:
Next: 0.1.1, with fixes for the CLI, the Docker demo and the release pipeline.

Full changelog: CHANGELOG.md

docs.title: NL2SQL 0.1.1
docs.text:
A fix release for 0.1.0: nl2sql doctor, the Docker demo and pipeline errors now work as documented, and the API image builds.

Released 2026-09-07.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• nl2sql doctor, the command you run when something is wrong, no longer crashes.
  • The Docker demo can reach its databases and survives a terminal that cannot show prompts.
  • A question that no subgraph can answer ends with a clear error code, not a crash.
  • The API image builds and is published to GHCR.

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text:
• nl2sql doctor checks connectivity again instead of failing on an import (#72).
  • A secrets config with every provider commented out is read as "no secret providers", not an error (#73).
  • The Docker demo's datasources are reachable: only passwords are treated as secrets when a config is resolved (#74).
  • nl2sql setup --demo --docker no longer crashes under Git Bash on Windows (#79).
  • When no subgraph matches a question, the pipeline raises a real error (#75), and its error code reaches the caller (#78).
  • The API image is built from the repository root, which fixes the GHCR publish that failed on 0.1.0 (#70).

docs.title: Docs
docs.text: • The docs match the code again (#77).

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• Tagging 0.1.1 did not publish it, because the PyPI upload failed in CI. The packages and the image went out about an hour later, by a manual re-run once the fix that shipped as 0.1.2 was on main.
  • The project is pre-1.0, so the API can still change between minor versions.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
pip install --upgrade "nl2sql-engine==0.1.1"

docs.text:
A release-pipeline fix: a merged release PR now reaches PyPI on its own. The packages are the same as 0.1.1.

Released 2026-09-07.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Merging the release PR publishes all three packages to PyPI with no manual step. On 0.1.1, that upload failed.
  • Library code has not changed since 0.1.1.

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text: • The release workflow publishes without PEP 740 attestations. Through the called workflow, PyPI rejected them (#80).

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• Released packages have no PEP 740 provenance attestations. That is the cost of this fix.
  • The project is pre-1.0, so the API can still change between minor versions.

docs.text:
pip install --upgrade "nl2sql-engine==0.1.2"
