docs.title: NL2SQL 0.2.0
docs.text:
The hosted demo release: try NL2SQL in a browser, without a key or with your own, or run the same playground locally with pip install "nl2sql-engine[demo]".

Released 2026-10-10.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• A public demo on Hugging Face Spaces (https://nadeem4nk-nl2sql-demo.hf.space). It asks three linked sample databases in plain English and shows the plan, the checks, the SQL and the rows.
  • No key needed to start. Twenty guided questions replay real recorded answers. For anything else, bring your own key; it stays in your browser tab and is used for that one request only.
  • pip install "nl2sql-engine[demo]" and nl2sql demo run the same playground on your machine. It has a home page, an answer-first Ask page, a Pipeline page and a Retrieval inspector.
  • Claude is supported natively alongside OpenAI-compatible providers, and each step can use its own model.
  • A release now runs end to end on its own: tag, PyPI, a fresh install check, then the Space at the same version.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Hosted mode: a public demo where each visitor brings their own key and the server holds none (#165), plus the Dockerfile and Space config to run it (#168).
  • Try the hosted demo without a key, on recorded runs (#197), with real recorded answers for the 20 guided questions (#205).
  • The React playground and nl2sql demo (#93), now with a home page (#198), an answer-first Ask page (#186) and a Pipeline page (#171).
  • Support and web-analytics sample databases, linked to Chinook customers (#157).
  • Native Claude support, and a provider per pipeline step (#124). In the hosted demo, each step can use its own model, with a key per provider (#173).
  • QueryResult exposes the plan, the validation checks, a row sample, the status and timings (#88).
  • Every run can be recorded to a trace file, viewed, and replayed without the model (#104).
  • Validated plans are cached by question and schema version, and checked again on every use (#122).
  • An evaluation harness: a Chinook gold dataset (#114), a tier 1 check on every PR (#119) and a tier 2 benchmark against real models (#126).
  • Each tagged release deploys the Space, pinned to the version on PyPI (#196).

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text:
• The validator rejects a plan whose tables cannot be joined before SQL is generated, so the model can try again (#161). Only known function names are allowed in plans (#137).
  • Role checks refuse without leaking data from forbidden tables, and deny unknown or empty roles cleanly (#112).
  • API keys and connection secrets are held as SecretStr, so they never print (#113).
  • When a sub-query fails, you get a structured result, not a crash or a loop (#84). The pipeline timeout is enforced (#87).
  • The aggregator combines sub-query results correctly when join keys carry a prefix (#144, #162).
  • Many smaller fixes to the generator, the decomposer, the CLI and the demo. See the changelog below.

docs.title: Docs
docs.text: • The README is organised around a quickstart, results, the CLI, the REST API and screenshots (#131), and links the live demo (#191).

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• No API image was published to GHCR for 0.2.0: its Dockerfile used Python 3.11. The first Space deploy also failed, on a PyPI index that had not caught up. Both are fixed in 0.2.1.
  • Without a key, the hosted demo only answers the 20 guided questions it has recordings for.
  • A question that needs several sub-queries can be answered wrong without an error. 0.2.2 fixes the known cases.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
pip install --upgrade "nl2sql-engine[demo]==0.2.0"

Breaking changes: Chinook is now the only demo dataset. nl2sql setup --demo --lite, --demo --docker and nl2sql demo --dataset are removed, and nl2sql setup --demo sets up Chinook (#98).

docs.title: What's next
docs.text:
Next: 0.2.1, which fixes the release image and makes the Space deploy reliable.

Full changelog: v0.1.2...v0.2.0

docs.title: NL2SQL 0.2.1
docs.text:
A release-pipeline fix for 0.2.0: the API image is built on Python 3.12, and the hosted demo deploys reliably. The library is unchanged.

Released 2026-10-10.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• ghcr.io/nadeem4/nl2sql-api is published again. 0.2.1 is the first image of the 0.2 line.
  • The Space deploy waits until PyPI serves the new version, and retries its install.
  • A Space deploy only passes when the Space is actually running.

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text:
• The release image moves to Python 3.12, which every package requires. A new PR check builds the image, so a broken Dockerfile fails before release (#208).
  • The Space deploy waits for PyPI to list the version before it pushes, and the Space's install retries up to ten times (#208).
  • A redeploy that pushes nothing asks for a rebuild, and the job fails unless the Space ends up running (#208).

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• There is no nl2sql-api:0.2.0 image. Use 0.2.1 or later.
  • Without a key, the hosted demo only answers the 20 guided questions it has recordings for.
  • A question that needs several sub-queries can be answered wrong without an error. 0.2.2 fixes the known cases.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
pip install --upgrade "nl2sql-engine[demo]==0.2.1"

Breaking changes: none.

docs.title: What's next
docs.text:
Next: 0.2.2, with correctness fixes for questions answered from several sub-queries.

Full changelog: v0.2.0...v0.2.1

docs.title: NL2SQL 0.2.2
docs.text:
A correctness release: a question answered from several sub-queries now gets the right answer or a clear refusal, never a silently wrong one. The live demo also moves to https://nl2sql.codewithnk.com.

Released 2026-10-11.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Each sub-query writes its own result file. Before this, two sub-queries of one question could overwrite each other, and a join could combine a result with itself.
  • A join or compare is refused if it lost one of its inputs, for example to a role restriction, instead of being answered from the side that remained.
  • A join or compare is refused if one input was cut short by the row cap. Missing rows mean missing matches.
  • The hosted demo has its own domain, https://nl2sql.codewithnk.com.

docs.title: Features
docs.text: • The link preview and the release checks use nl2sql.codewithnk.com, the Space's custom domain (#212).

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text:
• One result artifact per sub-query, at <tenant_id>/<request_id>/<sub_query_id>.parquet. A failed aggregation now ends the run instead of asking the model to explain an empty result (#213).
  • A join or compare that lost one of its inputs is refused with PLANNER_FAILED, before any query runs. The message does not name the restricted datasource (#214).
  • A join or compare on a sub-query that hit the row cap is refused with RESULT_TRUNCATED. A union on a capped input still runs, with a warning (#215).

docs.title: Docs
docs.text: • The README and docs link the live demo at nl2sql.codewithnk.com (#210).

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• Questions across several databases are not yet supported end to end. Each database answers its own sub-query and the results are joined in memory. This release makes that safer, not complete.
  • Each sub-query returns at most 1,000 rows by default (the datasource's row_limit). A join over a larger input is refused rather than answered.
  • Without a key, the hosted demo only answers the 20 guided questions it has recordings for.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
pip install --upgrade "nl2sql-engine[demo]==0.2.2"

Breaking changes: none. The default result artifact path gains a <sub_query_id> level. A custom RESULT_ARTIFACT_PATH_TEMPLATE keeps working: the sub-query id is added to its file name.

docs.title: What's next
docs.text:
Next: cross-database queries, so one question can be answered from several databases.

Full changelog: v0.2.1...v0.2.2

docs.title: NL2SQL 0.2.3
docs.text:
A correctness release: the model now knows today's date, what values a column holds and where its data starts and ends, and a query that comes back wrong or empty is retried or explained instead of answered as fact.

Released 2026-10-12.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• "This year" and "the last 30 days" are resolved against today's date, not a year the model guessed. When the period falls outside the data, the planner uses the latest period the data has and says so.
  • A filter on a value the column does not hold, such as 'Metal' for 'Heavy Metal', no longer turns into a confident "none". A close match is retried once; a missing value is named as a warning in the answer.
  • A query the database rejects as wrong (an unknown column, a type mismatch, bad syntax) goes back to the refiner for another try, instead of ending the run.
  • A column the plan names but the schema does not have is caught before the query runs, and the planner is asked to fix it.

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text:
• Strict column checking is on by default: an unknown column is a retryable COLUMN_NOT_FOUND. LOGICAL_VALIDATOR_STRICT_COLUMNS=false restores the old warning (#219).
  • The plan's offset is rendered, so "rows 11 to 20" no longer returns rows 1 to 10. An offset without an order is refused before generation (#221).
  • A query the database rejects as wrong is retried through the refiner. A refusal (permission, timeout, connection) still ends the run. Retry feedback carries only the latest error, with no SQL echo or stack trace (#223).
  • An empty result that filtered on a missing value is checked: a close stored value sends the plan back once, otherwise the answer carries a warning such as "There is no Genre with Name 'Polka'." (#226).
  • DATE and DATETIME leave the function allow-list, which now matches the planner prompt. STRFTIME is still accepted as a legacy name (#218).
  • The planner and refiner are told today's date. NL2SQL_TODAY pins it; unset, it is the UTC date (#220).
  • A text column with 50 or fewer distinct values keeps all of them in the index, not five samples (#222).
  • Date and numeric columns carry their data range in the prompt, with a rule for relative periods outside it (#224).
  • Two gold questions cover data ranges and value matching. The gold set is now 47 questions (#225).

docs.title: Docs
docs.text: • Every version has a release page, written by a skill and required in CI before a release (#216).

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• Each query returns at most 1,000 rows by default, and the answer model sees the whole result.
  • A cached plan for a relative-date question ("this month") can be reused on a later day. 0.2.4 fixes this.
  • "Rows 11 to 20" reaches the planner only through the question text.
  • Questions across several databases are still limited.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
pip install --upgrade "nl2sql-engine[demo]==0.2.3"

Breaking changes: none. Two behaviour changes: an unknown column is now a retried error rather than a warning (set LOGICAL_VALIDATOR_STRICT_COLUMNS=false for the old behaviour), and a plan calling DATE or DATETIME is refused. Re-index an existing demo folder to pick up the full column values: nl2sql setup --demo or nl2sql --env demo index.

docs.title: What's next
docs.text:
Next: 0.2.4, starting with cached plans for relative-date questions.

Full changelog: v0.2.2...v0.2.3

docs.title: NL2SQL 0.2.4
docs.text:
A cache fix: a cached plan is now reused only on the day it was made, so a relative-date question such as "the last 30 days" is never answered with an earlier day's dates.

Released 2026-10-12.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• "This year", "the last 30 days" and "yesterday" are planned against today's date, even when the same question was asked on an earlier day. Before this, the plan cache could serve an earlier day's plan with that day's dates.
  • Every cached plan carries the date it was made, not only plans that look date-relative, because nothing reliably tells which plans depend on today. A plan is reused for the rest of that day, or for as long as NL2SQL_TODAY pins the date.

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text: • The plan cache key includes the run date (#228).

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• Each query returns at most 1,000 rows by default, and the answer model sees the whole result.
  • "Rows 11 to 20" reaches the planner only through the question text.
  • Questions across several databases are still limited.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
pip install --upgrade "nl2sql-engine[demo]==0.2.4"

Breaking changes: none. Plans cached before the upgrade no longer match and are planned again once.

docs.title: What's next
docs.text:
Next: 0.3.0, starting with larger results.

Full changelog: v0.2.3...v0.2.4

docs.title: NL2SQL 0.3.0
docs.text:
Results at any size: a question can now return up to 100,000 rows by default, the whole result is saved and can be paged through or downloaded as CSV, and the answer model reads a 20-row preview instead of every row.

Released 2026-10-12.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• The default row cap rises from 1,000 to 100,000 (10,000 in the demo). A result that hits the cap is flagged, and the answer says it is incomplete and asks you to narrow the question.
  • The answer model sees the first 20 rows and the total count, not the whole result, so a large result no longer fills the prompt.
  • Every run's result is saved whole. Page through it or download it as CSV from the SDK, nl2sql-api or the playground, where each result gets its own tab and every sub-query is shown.
  • A run can stream its progress and its answer as Server-Sent Events. The playground lights up each step as it finishes and writes the answer as it arrives.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• The answer model gets a 20-row preview and the row count (ANSWER_PREVIEW_ROWS). RESULT_ROW_LIMIT (default 100,000) replaces the 1,000-row cap, and a result cut at the cap is flagged in truncated and in the answer's warnings (#231).
  • Results are fetched in batches of RESULT_FETCH_BATCH_SIZE rows through a new optional StreamingAdapterProtocol; adapters without it work unchanged. Each run's combined result is saved as parquet in its artifact folder (#234).
  • A run writes a manifest.json of its results, returned as QueryResult.result_manifest. get_result_manifest, get_result_page and export_result_csv read a result back, and nl2sql-api and the playground serve the same as page and CSV routes (#235).
  • The playground pages through the saved result 100 rows at a time, shows a tab per result, downloads the full CSV and shows every sub-query in the Plan and SQL steps (#236).
  • NL2SQL.stream_query, POST /api/v1/query/stream and the playground's /api/ask/stream send a run's progress, its result manifest and its answer token by token as Server-Sent Events. The playground falls back to the non-streaming call if the stream fails (#237).

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text: • A datasource's row_limit, statement_timeout_ms and max_bytes written beside connection, as the docs show, are now honoured; they were silently ignored. If a limit is set both there and under options, the lower wins (#233).

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• Anyone with a role who knows a run's id can read its saved result. There is no access check beyond the tenant's folder.
  • The downloaded CSV does not guard against spreadsheet formulas in cell values.
  • A join, sort or group-by across results may still hold its inputs in memory (as polars columns, not Python rows).
  • When a stream breaks, the playground asks the question again without streaming, so it is run a second time.
  • Questions across several databases are still limited.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
pip install --upgrade "nl2sql-engine[demo]==0.3.0"

Breaking changes: none. Three behaviour changes:

  • The default row cap is 100,000, not 1,000. To keep a lower cap, set RESULT_ROW_LIMIT or a datasource's row_limit.
  • terminal_results now holds only the 20-row preview. The full result is the saved artifact; read it with get_result_page or export_result_csv.
  • Every run writes its combined result as parquet and a manifest.json in its artifact folder. On S3 or ADLS, the manifest needs s3fs or adlfs installed.

docs.title: What's next
docs.text:
Next: 0.4.0.

Full changelog: v0.2.4...v0.3.0

docs.title: NL2SQL 0.4.0
docs.text:
Curated answers: a data team can write verified queries, reviewed SQL with typed parameters, and when a question matches one the engine runs that SQL with the values bound instead of generating new SQL, and labels the answer as verified. Any other question is answered by generated SQL, as before.

Released 2026-10-13.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Write verified queries in configs/curated.yaml: a description, the phrasings people ask, typed parameters and the SQL. When a question matches one, its reviewed SQL runs with the values bound by the driver, never pasted into the text.
  • An answer from a verified query says so. QueryResult.source is verified or generated in the SDK, the REST response and the trace, and the playground shows a "Verified" badge with the query's id and values.
  • Point the planner at the tables your team trusts with preferred_tables in datasources.yaml. The built-in adapters now index views as well as tables.
  • Thumbs-up feedback on generated answers can become proposed verified queries with nl2sql curated proposals export, for a person to review and commit.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• configs/curated.yaml, its settings CURATED_CONFIG and CURATED_ENABLED, and nl2sql curated validate, which checks every verified query, its parameters and its SQL against the indexed schema (#240).
  • nl2sql index indexes each verified query's phrasings, nl2sql index --curated-only refreshes only those after an edit, and nl2sql doctor warns when curated.yaml changed since the last index (#242).
  • A new first step, the curated matcher, picks a verified query and its values, checks the values and the role's access in code, and runs the saved SQL with bound parameters; anything else goes to the generated pipeline with a reason in the trace (#243).
  • preferred_tables in datasources.yaml puts those tables first in the schema the planner sees, and the SQLAlchemy-based adapters now snapshot views (#244).
  • The playground's "Verified" badge, six verified queries in the demo, and nl2sql curated test, which runs every verified query once with its defaults or examples (#245).
  • Feedback records the datasources a run used and the answer's source, and nl2sql curated proposals export turns thumbs-up feedback into proposed verified queries (#246).

docs.title: Docs
docs.text: • The design for curated answers: verified queries, preferred tables and feedback proposals, with business metrics deferred (#239).

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• Matching runs once, on the whole question. A question with two parts falls back to generated SQL, even if one part matches a verified query.
  • A question missing a value a verified query needs falls back to generated SQL; it does not ask a follow-up question.
  • The match threshold (CURATED_MATCH_FLOOR) was calibrated with the local embedding model only.
  • Business metrics are parsed and checked in curated.yaml but not used yet.
  • PostgreSQL materialized views are not indexed.
  • Feedback given before this release cannot become a proposal, because it did not record its datasource.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
pip install --upgrade "nl2sql-engine[demo]==0.4.0"

Breaking changes: none. Curated answers are off unless a curated.yaml exists at the default path or CURATED_CONFIG names one. Two behaviour changes:

  • Views now appear in the schema snapshot of the built-in adapters, so a re-index picks them up.
  • If CURATED_CONFIG points at a missing or broken file, startup fails with a message naming every problem.

docs.title: What's next
docs.text:
Next: 0.5.0, questions across several databases.

Full changelog: v0.3.0...v0.4.0

docs.title: NL2SQL 0.4.1
docs.text:
A hardening release: the REST routes that change the server need an admin role, indexing no longer calls the model unless you ask it to, table access is checked by schema as well as table, and one broken datasource no longer stops the engine from starting.

Released 2026-10-13.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Adding or removing a datasource, changing the LLM and rebuilding the index over REST now need an admin role. With no role source configured, only clients on the same machine may call them.
  • nl2sql index and the indexing SDK calls no longer spend model tokens by default. Ask for descriptions with --enrich or enrich=True, and the comments already in your database are never overwritten.
  • Policies can name a schema: ds.schema.table and ds.schema.*. A grant on sales.orders no longer lets a plan read audit.orders.
  • A datasource that fails to start is marked unavailable and the rest keep working; a secret provider that fails to start stops startup with a message saying which one and why.

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text:
• Passwords and user names with @ : / # % now work for PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQL Server, and statement_timeout_ms is now enforced on SQL Server and DuckDB too (#249).
  • The REST admin routes require an admin role, a failed POST /datasource no longer echoes the connection string, and nl2sql-api pins the engine release it ships with (#250).
  • A secret provider that cannot start fails startup with a clear error; a datasource that cannot start is listed by list_unavailable_datasources() and in index_health() warnings instead of stopping the engine (#251).
  • Routing respects the answerability check's choice of datasources, and the decomposer now sees each datasource's description and table names (#252).
  • Enrichment is opt-in for every indexing entry point, only fills blank descriptions, logs a failure as one line, and a datasource added in code keeps its description (#254).
  • Tier 2 benchmarks run with curated answers off unless --use-curated is passed, and each case records whether its answer was verified or generated (#255).
  • Indexing profiles each column on its own, so a boolean, UUID, JSON or date column, or one failing query, no longer fails the whole datasource (#256).
  • Table access is decided on datasource, schema and table, the same way in the validator, schema retriever, executor and curated matcher (#257).
  • nl2sql setup checks and offers the right driver for bring-your-own PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server and DuckDB databases, offers DuckDB as a type, and nl2sql install postgres installs the right extra (#258).

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• A reverse proxy on the same host makes every request look like it comes from loopback. Set NL2SQL_API_ROLE_HEADER in that case.
  • The REST indexing routes do not take an enrich parameter, so they always index without enrichment.
  • There is no strict mode that fails startup when one datasource cannot start. Use nl2sql doctor as a deploy check.
  • The SQL Server timeout counts whole seconds, so statement_timeout_ms is rounded up.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
pip install --upgrade "nl2sql-engine[demo]==0.4.1"

Breaking changes / behaviour changes: four, each of which needs a look before you upgrade.

  • REST admin routes need an admin role (#250). POST /datasource, DELETE /datasource/{id}, POST /llm, POST /index/{id}, POST /index-all and DELETE /index now need a role listed in NL2SQL_API_ADMIN_ROLES (comma-separated, default admin). With no role source configured, only loopback clients are allowed. What to do: set NL2SQL_API_ROLE_HEADER behind a proxy, or NL2SQL_API_ROLE=admin for a single-user deployment. In Docker, requests arrive from the bridge gateway rather than loopback, so one of these is needed.
  • Indexing enrichment is opt-in (#254). index_datasource, index_all_datasources and nl2sql index no longer call the LLM unless you pass enrich=True or --enrich, and enrichment never overwrites table or column comments from the database. What to do: if you relied on generated descriptions, add --enrich or enrich=True to your indexing calls.
  • Two-part policy entries mean the default schema (#257). ds.table now grants that table in the datasource's default schema only (public on PostgreSQL, dbo on SQL Server, the connected database on MySQL, main on SQLite and DuckDB). Three-part ds.schema.table and ds.schema.* entries are supported. What to do: for a table outside the default schema, write ds.schema.table or ds.schema.*. Policies on SQLite datasources, including the demo's, mean what they did before.
  • Startup failures (#251). A configured secret provider that fails to start now stops startup with an error naming it and the reason. A datasource that fails to start no longer stops the engine; it is reported as unavailable. What to do: fix or remove a broken entry in the secrets config, and check list_unavailable_datasources(), GET /api/v1/index/status or nl2sql doctor for datasources that did not start.

docs.title: What's next
docs.text:
Next: 0.5, Configuration v2 and the extension registry.

Full changelog: v0.4.0...v0.4.1

docs.title: NL2SQL 0.5.0
docs.text:
Configuration v2: one nl2sql.yaml configures the engine, the CLI, nl2sql-api and the demo, an extension registry loads adapters, LLM, embeddings and secret providers by name, and every engine owns its config. This is a clean break from 0.4, with no compatibility layer: read Upgrading before you install it.

Released 2026-10-14.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• One config file. nl2sql.yaml replaces the 0.4 files and about 48 environment variables. It can be one file or split into datasources/, llm.yaml, embeddings.yaml, policies.yaml and storage.yaml. nl2sql init writes that layout for you (--demo adds the demo databases). nl2sql config check checks every file, name, driver and secret without starting the engine, and with --connect it also connects to each datasource. It fits a CI job.
  • An extension registry. Registry.default() finds adapters, LLM providers, embeddings providers and secret providers through entry points, and imports none of them until the config uses one. Register your own with add_adapter, add_llm, add_embeddings, add_secrets or a decorator (@registry.adapter("name")). A wrong interface version, a missing driver or a misspelled name is reported when the engine is built, with the fix. The SDK they build against is now nl2sql-sdk (import nl2sql_sdk).
  • A tidier Python API, with a model switch at runtime. run_query and stream_query stay at the top level. Everything else is in namespaces: engine.datasources, index, llm, policies, curated, results, traces and feedback, plus about(), check() and close() (or with). engine.llm.replace(...) and the admin-only PUT /api/v1/settings/llm swap the model in a running engine. Queries already running finish on the old model, and the change is logged without keys.
  • Each engine owns its config. There are no process-wide settings and nothing writes os.environ, so two engines in one process share nothing. import nl2sql takes about 15 ms instead of about 2.2 s, because it loads no heavy library.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• nl2sql-adapter-sdk is renamed nl2sql-sdk, with the import package nl2sql_sdk (#262).
  • import nl2sql loads no database driver, vector store or model library, and a test holds it under budget (#263).
  • The typed config models, load_config, file: includes, ${env:...} references, strict keys with "did you mean", and one ConfigError that lists every problem (#264).
  • The SDK defines the adapter and secret provider interfaces, with interface versions, driver lists and install hints. Secret provider settings are checked strictly (#265).
  • The extension registry: Registry.default(), add_*, decorators, and the entry point groups nl2sql.adapters, nl2sql.llms, nl2sql.embeddings and nl2sql.secrets (#266).
  • nl2sql init [DIR] [--demo] [--provider NAME] [--force] writes the split config layout and checks it (#267).
  • The engine is built from a Config: NL2SQL(config), NL2SQL.from_config(path), NL2SQL.demo(), check() and close(). Building never connects, and all results are written under storage.path (#268).
  • The pipeline reads its settings from its own engine, so two engines in one process each keep their own row limit, plan cache and model (#269).
  • engine.llm.replace, with LLM clients cached per engine, and a plan cache key that includes the planner's model (#270).
  • Indexing, tracing, replay and benchmarks run on run-scoped settings and never change the engine they run on (#271).
  • The CLI, nl2sql-api and the demo start from nl2sql.yaml with a single --config flag. nl2sql setup and every 0.4 config path are removed (#272).
  • nl2sql config check [--connect], which is also callable from Python as nl2sql.config.check.check_config (#273).
  • The namespaced facade and PUT /api/v1/settings/llm. The CLI now uses only the public API (#274).
  • engine.feedback, engine.traces.get, engine.about() and engine.llm.providers(). The playground now uses only the public API (#275).
  • The process-wide settings object is deleted. The library writes no environment variables and reads only an allow-list of them (#276).

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text: • Secrets in the config are masked when it is printed, NL2SQL_LOG_LEVEL set in .env takes effect, and the scripts no longer write the environment (#277).

docs.title: Docs
docs.text: • The design for Configuration v2 and the extension registry (#260). The Configuration pages are rewritten for nl2sql.yaml in the PRs above.

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• Running several nl2sql-api replicas is not supported for a model switch. PUT /api/v1/settings/llm changes only the process that receives it, and the change is not saved: a restart reads llm.yaml again.
  • There is no migration command. You map 0.4 files and variables by hand, using the table.
  • Results are stored locally only. The S3 and ADLS backends are gone until the results-store interface in Phase 2.
  • nl2sql init is not interactive, and its --provider accepts openai, anthropic and openrouter only (Ollama has no default model). The guided setup flow comes in Phase 4.
  • A datasource's connection block is checked by the adapter only, not by a typed model, and check() gives a generic reason when a connection fails. Typed connection models and connection-test stages come with SDK v2 in Phase 2.
  • After engine.datasources.remove(id), the datasource's index entries stay until the next full index.build or index.clear.
  • This release is Phase 1 of five. Phase 2 brings SDK v2, storage interfaces and policy globs, Phase 3 the event bus and evals, Phase 4 the guided setup and the web app on nl2sql-api, and Phase 5 glossaries and knowledge sources.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
pip install --upgrade "nl2sql-engine[demo]==0.5.0"

Adapter and secret provider authors: pip install "nl2sql-sdk==0.5.0" and uninstall nl2sql-adapter-sdk.

Breaking changes: many. 0.5 is a clean break with no compatibility layer, and the engine refuses a 0.4 config. Start with nl2sql init, then move your values across with the 0.4 to 0.5 mapping.

  • One config file (#264, #272). configs/datasources.yaml, llm.yaml, policies.json, secrets.yaml, curated.yaml, sample_questions.yaml and about 48 environment variables are no longer read. What to do: run nl2sql init (or nl2sql init --demo) and move each value to its new place using the mapping table. Sample questions now sit on each datasource, policies are YAML, and LLM agents are keyed by node name (ast_planner).
  • Environment variables (#276). Only NL2SQL_CONFIG, NL2SQL_LOG_LEVEL and the provider keys (OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY) are read directly. What to do: write any other value in the YAML, as ${env:VAR} where it should come from the environment.
  • .env loading (#272). Only the CLI, nl2sql-api and nl2sql demo load a .env, and only the one next to nl2sql.yaml. They never override a variable that is already set. The library never reads .env. --env, --env-file, ENV, APP_ENV and ENV_FILE_PATH are gone. What to do: put .env next to nl2sql.yaml. From Python, call nl2sql.load_env_file(path) before building the engine.
  • nl2sql setup is removed (#272). What to do: use nl2sql init, or nl2sql init --demo in place of setup --demo.
  • One CLI flag (#272). nl2sql --config PATH/nl2sql.yaml <command> (or NL2SQL_CONFIG, or ./nl2sql.yaml) replaces every per-command path flag (--llm-config, --secrets-config, --policies-config, --vector-store, and the curated and policy path flags). What to do: pass --config once, before the command.
  • nl2sql-api settings (#272). The NL2SQL_API_* variables are removed. What to do: set api.role_header, api.role, api.trust_body_role and api.cors_origins (a list) in an api: section, and the admin roles in policies.admin_roles. The API image reads NL2SQL_CONFIG=/etc/nl2sql/nl2sql.yaml, so mount your config folder there.
  • REST LLM route (#274). POST /api/v1/llm is replaced by the admin-only PUT /api/v1/settings/llm, whose body is the llm section as JSON. A bad body gets a 422 with the config error. POST /api/v1/datasource takes the datasource in the nl2sql.yaml shape, and the datasource routes return DatasourceInfo. What to do: update your clients.
  • Result storage (#268). The S3 and ADLS backends and the RESULT_ARTIFACT_* settings are removed. Results are written under storage.path/results/. What to do: set storage.path and copy anything you need from a remote store yourself.
  • Secret providers (#265). hashi is renamed hashicorp, with no alias. The VAULT_ADDR, VAULT_TOKEN and AZURE_KEYVAULT_URL fallbacks are removed, and an unknown provider setting is an error. What to do: write type: hashicorp and give url and token (for example token: "${env:VAULT_TOKEN}"), or vault_url for Azure, in the provider's block.
  • The SDK package (#262). nl2sql-adapter-sdk / nl2sql_adapter_sdk is now nl2sql-sdk / nl2sql_sdk. Adapters also declare interface_version, driver_modules and install_hint (#265). What to do: rename the dependency and the imports, add the three class attributes, and register through the nl2sql.adapters entry point or Registry.add_adapter.
  • The Python facade (#274, #275). The flat methods, engine.context, engine.query, get_adapter, configure_llm, reload_llm_config, the auth, settings, policy, indexing and datasource sub-APIs, and the QueryAPI/DatasourceAPI/LLM_API/... exports are removed. NL2SQL() is built from a Config or NL2SQL.from_config(path). What to do: call the namespaces (engine.datasources.add, engine.index.build, engine.llm.replace, engine.policies.validate, ...). The public facade page lists them.
  • Hosted demo (#276). nl2sql demo --hosted refuses to start if OPENAI_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set in its environment. NL2SQL_DEMO_HOSTED and NL2SQL_DEMO_QUESTIONS_* are replaced by --hosted, --questions-per-minute and --questions-per-session, and the demo's key file is <dir>/.env instead of .env.demo (#272). What to do: remove provider keys from the hosted server's environment and use the flags.
  • Startup errors (#268). Anything wrong that can be found without connecting is now a ConfigError when the engine is built. This includes an unknown datasource type and a secret that does not resolve, which in 0.4 only marked that datasource unavailable. A datasource that cannot connect still runs degraded unless it is required: true. What to do: run nl2sql config check before you deploy.

docs.title: What's next
docs.text:
Next: 0.6, datasources and adapter SDK v2, then the web app on the API and Docker Compose.

Full changelog: v0.4.1...v0.5.0

docs.title: NL2SQL 0.6.0
docs.text:
Phase 2: every built-in adapter is now tested against real PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQL Server servers, adapters are built on SDK v2 with a conformance kit, storage has four pluggable stores, LLM and embeddings providers take any OpenAI-compatible server, and policies gain allow and deny globs. Several config keys and interfaces change: read Upgrading before you install it.

Released 2026-10-15.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Tested on real databases. A test bed runs PostgreSQL with Pagila, MySQL with Sakila and SQL Server with AdventureWorksLT, plus a generated schema of 1,200 tables. It runs in CI on every PR that touches database code, and on a GCP VM on demand. The VM run found three bugs that CI had hidden, all fixed in this release.
  • Adapter SDK v2 and a conformance kit. Each adapter has a typed connection model, so a misspelt key gets "did you mean". You can choose which schemas and tables to index (IndexScope). Row counts come from the database catalog. A table that cannot be read becomes an issue in the index build instead of a crash. Read-only sessions and statement timeouts are enforced where the database allows it and reported where it does not, and a failed connection test names the stage that failed. The SQLAlchemy base is public in nl2sql-sdk[sqlalchemy], and nl2sql-sdk[testing] is the kit that all five built-in adapters pass.
  • Four storage slots. storage has index, state, traces and results, each a built-in or a plugin store. The index's build pointer is now the commit, so a failed build leaves the previous index live. Each embedding model gets its own namespace. Traces and results are deleted after a set number of days.
  • Providers and policies. openai_compatible with a base_url works with any OpenAI-style server, with openrouter and ollama as presets of it. Each agent can set structured_output, max_tokens, timeout_s, max_retries and headers, and a malformed answer is retried with the error. Policies use allow and deny globs on datasource.schema.table, the planner never sees a denied table, and a PolicyCheck plugin can add your own access rules. engine.datasources.types(), test() and add() are the methods a Connect-a-database form needs.

docs.title: Real-database results
docs.text:
• The CI realdb job passed on every PR that touched database code.
  • The run on the GCP VM on 2026-10-14 (python scripts/testbed.py run -- pytest -m realdb): 110 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed. The four skips are expected. SQL Server does not declare ENFORCES_READ_ONLY (2 tests), and the 60-second target for reading the wide schema is measured on PostgreSQL only (2 tests).
  • Runs on the real VM found and fixed three problems. MySQL 8 logins needed cryptography, and SQL Server used a hard-coded ODBC driver (#303). The test bed also had Windows problems (#299, #301, #302, #304).

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Embeddings providers v2: openai_compatible, base_url on the hosted providers, a known dimension for each model, and one probe call when the dimension is unknown (#281).
  • Store interfaces in nl2sql_sdk.stores, the four storage slots and the store registry kind (#283).
  • LLM providers v2: openai_compatible, with openrouter and ollama as its presets, and the agent fields structured_output, max_tokens, timeout_s, max_retries and headers. Header values are never printed (#284).
  • Policy allow and deny globs, one Scope wherever access is decided, and denied tables hidden from the planner (#285).
  • The real-database test bed: a Docker Compose file, the realdb pytest marker and a CI workflow (#286).
  • A malformed structured answer is sent back to the model with the error, up to parse_retries times. After that the run fails with MODEL_OUTPUT_INVALID (#287).
  • The PolicyCheck extension point. Its grants are intersected with the YAML roles, and it denies if it fails (#288).
  • The index store: one namespace per embedding model, the build pointer as the commit, and nl2sql index prune (#289).
  • scripts/testbed.py starts, uses and stops the GCP test-bed VM through IAP (#290).
  • Adapter SDK v2: DatasourceAdapter, strict connection models with "did you mean", and IndexScope (#291).
  • Trace and result stores with max_age_days retention, engine.storage.info() and purge(), and nl2sql storage purge (#292).
  • The sqlite state store: snapshots that are never changed, migrations that adopt a 0.5 state.db, and a lock during index builds (#293).
  • The SQLAlchemy base in nl2sql-sdk[sqlalchemy]. It reads the schema once, takes row estimates from the catalog, collects sample values only when asked, and reports index issues (#295).
  • engine.datasources.types(), test(Datasource) without registering it, and add() checking the index scope (#296).
  • Read-only sessions and statement timeouts on every adapter that can enforce them, and connection tests that name the failed stage (#297).
  • The adapter conformance kit, nl2sql-sdk[testing], run on all five built-in adapters (#298).

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text:
• The SDK docs page no longer has leftover merge-conflict markers, and CI now fails on any it finds (#294).
  • DuckDB schemas are read from DuckDB's own catalog, so indexing works on SQLAlchemy 2.1 (#300).
  • nl2sql-engine[mysql] installs cryptography for MySQL 8 logins. SQL Server uses the newest installed ODBC driver, with a clear message when none is installed (#303).
  • Fixes to the test bed on Windows and on the VM: passwords, Docker start-up, SQL Server start-up, and stopping cleanly (#299, #301, #302, #304).

docs.title: Docs
docs.text: • The Phase 2 design: test bed, storage, providers, policies and adapter SDK v2 (#279). The test bed, storage, policies and adapter SDK pages are written or rewritten in the PRs above.

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• SQL Server does not make the session read-only. check() warns about it, so connect with a login that can only read.
  • The built-in stores are for a single replica. A PostgreSQL state store and a pgvector index, for several replicas, come later.
  • There is no built-in S3 or ADLS results store. Write one as a ResultStore plugin; the Artifact Store page has an S3 example.
  • Policies go down to tables. Column denies, row filters and user attributes come later.
  • engine.datasources.types(), test() and add() are Python only. The REST routes and the Connect-a-database form come in Phase 4.
  • There are no Snowflake or BigQuery adapters yet.
  • The 60-second target for reading the 1,200-table schema is measured on PostgreSQL only. Retrieval limits as settings and incremental re-indexing come after 0.6.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
pip install --upgrade "nl2sql-engine[demo]==0.6.0"

Adapter, store and policy-check authors: pip install "nl2sql-sdk==0.6.0" (add [sqlalchemy] for the SQLAlchemy base, [testing] for the conformance kit).

Breaking changes: several. Each needs a look before you upgrade.

  • Storage sub-blocks and a new index namespace (#283, #289, #292). storage has index, state, traces and results sub-blocks. path on its own is still valid. The index now lives in one namespace per embedding model, and 0.6 never reads 0.5's nl2sql_store collection. Traces are deleted after 14 days and results after 7 by default. What to do: run nl2sql index after upgrading, then nl2sql index prune to drop the 0.5 collection. Set max_age_days on traces or results if you want them kept longer. A 0.5 state.db is adopted as it is.
  • Policy patterns (#285). allow and deny replace allowed_datasources and allowed_tables. A pattern is *, datasource or datasource.schema.table. A two-part pattern such as sales.orders is rejected when the config loads, and matching ignores case. What to do: rewrite each role, for example sales.orders as sales.<schema>.orders or sales.<schema>.*.
  • Denied tables are hidden from the planner (#285). A table a role cannot read never reaches the model. A user who asks about one sees "can't be answered from the connected data". A plan that still names a hidden table is refused by the validator. What to do: check that each role allows the tables its users need.
  • sample_values is off by default (#295). Column values are no longer collected into the index and prompts unless index.sample_values is on. The demo keeps them on. What to do: set index: {sample_values: true} on a datasource whose answers need its values, then run nl2sql index.
  • Strict connection keys (#291). An unknown key in a datasource's connection block is now an error with a "did you mean" hint. It used to be ignored. What to do: run nl2sql config check and fix what it reports.
  • Adapter interface version 2 (#291, #295). DatasourceAdapter replaces DatasourceAdapterProtocol, with no alias, and a version 1 adapter is refused when it loads. What to do: port your adapter to DatasourceAdapter, ideally on nl2sql_sdk.sqlalchemy.SQLAlchemyAdapter, and run the conformance kit. See Adapter development.
  • LLM and embeddings provider interface version 2 (#281, #284). A version 1 LLM or embeddings provider is refused when it loads. What to do: add structured_output to an LLM provider and describe() to an embeddings provider, and set interface_version = 2.
  • Deleted index arguments and setting (#289). index.build(full=..., switch_guard=...), nl2sql index --full and settings.schema.version_mismatch are gone. What to do: drop them. A failed build now leaves the previous build live, so there is nothing to guard.
  • engine.policies.allowed() is now engine.policies.scope() (#285). A flat table list cannot express a deny. What to do: call scope(user_context, datasource_id) and ask it allows(schema, table).
  • S3 and ADLS results only through a plugin (#292). What to do: implement the ResultStore interface and set it as the results store.
  • SQL Server always connects with Encrypt=yes (#303). ODBC Driver 17 did not encrypt by default. What to do: for a server with a self-signed certificate, set trust_server_certificate: true in its connection block.
  • nl2sql-engine[mysql] installs pymysql[rsa] (#303), which brings in cryptography. What to do: nothing, unless you pin dependencies, in which case allow cryptography.

docs.title: What's next
docs.text:
Next: Phase 3, hooks, observers and evals.

Full changelog: v0.5.0...v0.6.0

docs.title: NL2SQL 0.7.0
docs.text:
Wave A of the redesign: every run publishes typed events that observers log, audit or export, hooks can change or stop a run and ask for a person's approval, evals become engine.evals and nl2sql eval with a regression gate, routing votes across five signals, and answers are checked for join fan-out and empty columns. It also adds per-question cost caps, schema drift checks and an MCP server. Several APIs and config keys change: read Upgrading before you install it.

Released 2026-10-15.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Events, observers and hooks. Every run publishes typed events on one bus: run, node, answer, LLM call, policy denial, index and drift events, each in a catalog. stream_query yields those events from a caller-safe allow-list, ready for SSE. The observers section sends them to a log, a JSON-lines audit log under storage.path, or OpenTelemetry. Six hook points let your code modify a run before the validator and deny it after, and a hook can stop a run as needs_approval until an approver re-runs it.
  • Evals as a product. engine.benchmark is now engine.evals, and nl2sql benchmark is now nl2sql eval. One case format, five scorers and three modes (full, plans, retrieval), with the Chinook gold set moved unchanged and pinned by its digest. A regression gate on execution accuracy runs in CI, a new routing suite of 78 cases covers the demo's three databases, and nl2sql eval seed drafts cases from your own database.
  • Better routing and safer answers. Each example question is its own index entry. Routing fuses five signals (description, examples, verified queries, tables, columns) by rank and drops a datasource far less similar than the best. A question that needs too many sub-queries is refused as QUESTION_TOO_BROAD. Join keys of different types are converted before a cross-database join. A count inflated by a join is caught and retried (JOIN_FAN_OUT), and a column that came back all null is flagged.
  • Cost caps, drift and MCP. settings.pipeline.max_llm_calls and max_cost_usd stop a question before the call that would cross them, with status stopped. nl2sql index --check reports schema drift and what it breaks, without re-indexing. nl2sql mcp serves the engine to MCP clients over stdio, as one role.

docs.title: Real-database results
docs.text:
• The CI realdb job passed on the PRs that touched database code.
  • The run on the GCP test bed against main at 5920d3f1: 111 passed, 9 skipped, 0 failed, in 9.5 minutes.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• The foundation: the event bus and catalog, the run scope, the observer, hook and scorer registry kinds, the new config sections and settings, the RunStatus values and nl2sql --log-format text|json (#313).
  • Run events on every run, stream_query yielding Events from a caller-safe allow-list, engine.events.subscribe() and catalog(), and the run's trace_id on every log line (#314).
  • Hooks: six points (run.before, datasources.after, plan.after, execute.before, execute.after, answer.after), run in config order, failing closed unless a hook sets on_error: open (#315).
  • Routing: one index entry per example question, five signals fused by rank, a similarity floor, and the settings.routing and settings.retrieval limits (#316).
  • engine.evals: the suite format, the Chinook suite, five scorers, modes full, plans and retrieval, and regenerate through the datasource's adapter (#317).
  • The log, audit and otel observers, with llm.call and llm.changed on the bus. The audit log moves under storage.path (#318).
  • Approval: a hook can ask for one, the result is needs_approval with a request, and an approver's re-run pins the same plan. run_query(plan=SuppliedPlan(...)) runs a plan you already hold (#319).
  • nl2sql eval run, regenerate and publish, and engine.evals.gate(), a regression gate on execution accuracy, with records kept by mode and suite (#320).
  • The Phase 2 events are published: index builds, failed datasource checks, parse retries, policy denials and purges (#321).
  • A limit on sub-queries per question (QUESTION_TOO_BROAD), join keys converted to one type before a cross-database join, and a validator check for join keys of incompatible types (#322).
  • The routing suite of 78 cases over the demo's three databases, and its gate on top-1 and shortlist recall in CI (#323).
  • Answer checks for join fan-out and all-null columns, closest values from the index's sample values, and typed RunWarnings (#324).
  • nl2sql mcp, an MCP server over stdio with ask, list_datasources and describe_table, all limited to the caller's role (the new mcp extra) (#325).
  • The dated price table in llm/prices.py, every LLM call priced, engine.llm.prices(), the per-question caps and a Budget you can use outside a question (#326).
  • Schema drift: engine.index.check(), versions() and diff(), nl2sql index --check, and the verified queries and policy rules a change affects (#327).
  • engine.evals.seed() and nl2sql eval seed: draft eval cases from your own datasource, as typed plans the engine validates and runs read-only, under a cost cap (#328).
  • SQL Server connections take encrypt: false for a local server without TLS. Encryption stays on by default (#307).

docs.title: Docs
docs.text:
• The Wave A design (#308), and the designs for Waves B, C and D (#310, #311, #312). New pages: Events, Observers, Hooks, Evals, Seeding, Schema drift and MCP.
  • Two rules in CLAUDE.md corrected to match the code (#306).

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• Routing is not perfect. On the routing suite, top-1 is 76 of 78 and the shortlist 77 of 78. "Which customers complained most about refunds?" and "How many purchases were there per month in 2013?" go to Chinook first.
  • Approvals are not stored. The caller keeps the request and sends the approval back with the re-run. Stored approvals come with the REST API in Wave D.
  • needs_clarification is a reserved status. Nothing returns it until Wave B.
  • MCP runs over stdio only, as one role. MCP over HTTP with API keys comes in Wave C.
  • Schema drift is measured, not acted on. Nothing re-indexes or fixes a verified query by itself.
  • When a hook is attached at execute.before, the value and fan-out checks run no probe query. Only the all-null check runs.
  • While chromadb is a core dependency, it brings OpenTelemetry with it, so the otel extra installs nothing new yet.
  • Seeded drafts have no rows. Run nl2sql eval regenerate after you approve them.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
pip install --upgrade "nl2sql-engine[demo]==0.7.0"

Add [otel] for the OpenTelemetry observer and [mcp] for nl2sql mcp. Third-party store authors: pip install "nl2sql-sdk==0.7.0".

Breaking changes: several. Each needs a look before you upgrade.

  • engine.benchmark is now engine.evals, and nl2sql benchmark is now nl2sql eval (#317, #320). There is no alias. The gold files are now suites/chinook.yaml with renamed keys (expected is outcome, gold_sql is sql, alt_gold_sql is alt_sql), and the gate reads execution accuracy. What to do: call engine.evals.run() and gate(), or nl2sql eval run. Move your own gold files to the case format. A 0.6 record starts a new series in the gate.
  • QueryEvent is gone; stream_query yields Events (#314). The stream carries run.started, node.*, answer.delta, result.manifest, sanity.flagged, run.limit_reached, then one run.finished (with the QueryResult in data.result) or run.failed. Policy, hook and LLM call events never reach it. Each SSE data line of POST /api/v1/query/stream is now the whole event: name, at, trace_id, tenant_id and data. What to do: read events by name, and take the result from run.finished. See Events.
  • QueryResult.warnings are typed RunWarnings (#324). Each is {code, node, message, sub_query_id, detail}. Over REST, error_code is now code, and severity is gone: an earlier attempt that a retry replaced has detail.recovered: true. What to do: read code instead of error_code, and detail.recovered instead of severity.
  • QueryResult.status is a RunStatus (#313, #319, #326). Beside success, plan_only and error, a run can now end needs_approval (with approvals_needed) or stopped (with stop, at a cost or call cap). What to do: handle the two new values.
  • engine.datasources.schema() requires user_context (#325), and drops the tables the caller may not read. engine.index.check(), versions() and diff() take it too (#327). What to do: pass the caller's UserContext.
  • settings.observability is gone; use the observers section (#313, #318). A config that still sets it fails to load. By default the engine runs the log and audit observers, and the audit log is now <storage.path>/audit/<date>.jsonl, not logs/audit_events.log. What to do: move exporter and otlp_endpoint to an otel observer. See Observers.
  • OpenTelemetry is the otel extra (#318). It has left the core dependencies, and an otel observer without it is a ConfigError. What to do: pip install "nl2sql-engine[otel]" if you export to a collector.
  • TABLE_K, PLANNING_K and MAX_DECOMPOSER_TABLES are settings (#313, #316): settings.retrieval.table_k, planning_k and decomposer_tables, with the same defaults. What to do: if you patched the constants, set the settings instead.
  • Routing changed (#316). settings.routing.candidates now defaults to 3, a datasource far less similar than the best is dropped (floor_ratio, 0.5), and Retriever.route() replaces retrieve_datasource_candidates. What to do: run nl2sql index after upgrading, so each example question gets its own entry. Until you do, routing has no example votes.
  • A question needs at most settings.routing.max_sub_queries sub-queries (#322), 6 by default. More ends the run with QUESTION_TOO_BROAD. What to do: raise the setting if your users ask wider questions.
  • Store interface version 2 (#327). StateStore gains put_schema_diff and get_schema_diff, and a version 1 store is refused when it loads. The built-in sqlite store migrates itself. What to do: third-party state stores add the two methods and set interface_version = 2.
  • The price table moved to nl2sql/llm/prices.py (#326). nl2sql.evaluation.prices is gone, with no alias. A model the table does not know now costs None, not 0, and a token count the provider did not report is None. What to do: import from nl2sql.llm.prices, price your own models with llm.prices, and handle None in usage and cost. With max_cost_usd set, an unpriced model is a ConfigError.
  • The mcp extra (#325). nl2sql mcp needs pip install "nl2sql-engine[mcp]".

New, not breaking: run_query(plan=SuppliedPlan(...)) runs a plan you hold, through plan.after and the validator, with no planning (#319).

docs.title: What's next
docs.text:
Next: 0.8, Wave B: business knowledge, the schema profiler, clarifying questions and a cost guard.

Full changelog: v0.6.0...v0.7.0

docs.title: NL2SQL 0.8.0
docs.text:
Wave B of the redesign: business knowledge (a glossary and other knowledge sources) now reaches the index and the prompts, a review queue holds every proposed change until someone accepts it, a schema profiler proposes joins, roles and drafted descriptions, ambiguous questions can be re-asked with a choice, every answer can say why, and a cost rule can refuse or confirm an expensive query. A few APIs and flags change: read Upgrading before you install it.

Released 2026-10-28.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Business knowledge. Knowledge sources (the yaml glossary first) are merged, filtered by the caller's scope and shown or exported with engine.knowledge. Descriptions, synonyms, roles, units, joins and rules now go into the index and into the planner's prompt, and a changed glossary marks the index stale. nl2sql index --refresh re-renders the entries from the stored snapshot with no schema read and no model call.
  • A review queue and a profiler. Every proposed change (a profiler finding, a thumbs-up, a correction, a chosen reading) is filed in one queue, and accepting it is the only way anything is written. engine.knowledge.profile() proposes joins and column roles from bounded probes, and with draft=True the profiler model drafts missing descriptions under a cost cap (nl2sql profile --draft --max-cost).
  • Clarifying questions, and why an answer is what it is. A question that can be read more than one way ends as needs_clarification with up to three options, each explained. run_query(choice=) runs the chosen plan, and a pick can be saved as a glossary term proposal. Every successful answer carries an explanation, written from the typed plan, not from model text.
  • A cost guard and corrections. policies.cost is enforced: over the limit, a query is allowed, held for approval or refused as COST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, using a rows-read estimate from PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server and DuckDB. engine.feedback.correct() checks a fixed plan or SQL and files it as a verified-query proposal.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• The shared shapes for knowledge, review, profiler, clarify, explain and cost, and store interface version 3 (#329).
  • Adapters: estimate (rows read) on PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server and DuckDB, and probe_overlap on all five built-ins (#332).
  • explanation on QueryResult: why this answer, rendered from the typed plan (#335).
  • Knowledge sources, merge, scope filter, show and export, and the yaml source with a checked, atomic writer (#336).
  • The review queue: one way to file a proposal, accept as the only writer, and thumbs-up proposals (#337).
  • The clarifier and the needs_clarification result (#339).
  • Knowledge in the planner's prompts, and the terms and rules used on each answer (#340).
  • engine.feedback.correct(): a checked fix filed as a verified-query proposal (#341).
  • The cost rule, enforced by the built-in policy.cost hook (#342).
  • The profiler: join and column-role proposals from bounded probes (#343).
  • The glossary in the index, index --refresh, and no model text written into the index (#344).
  • Clarifications: choice= on run_query and stream_query, save_choice, settled phrases, a prompt in nl2sql run on a terminal, and choice on the MCP ask tool (#345).
  • Drafted descriptions under a cost cap, filed for review (#347).
  • The retrieval inspector shows only what the caller's scope reaches (#348).

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• The playground and the REST API trust the caller-supplied role. See the security model.
  • The retrieval inspector over-fetches to apply a caller's scope, so a caller for whom most matches are hidden can see a short list (#348).
  • Business metrics are still deferred. A glossary term with columns is the prose half of a metric.
  • SQLite has no cost estimate, so the cost rule treats its queries as unknown.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
pip install --upgrade "nl2sql-engine[demo]==0.8.0"

Third-party store authors: pip install "nl2sql-sdk==0.8.0".

Breaking changes: a few. Each needs a look before you upgrade.

  • nl2sql index --enrich, --curated-only and their enrich= and curated_only= parameters are gone (#344). The index no longer calls the model to write descriptions, and the playground's "write descriptions with the LLM" option is gone. What to do: use nl2sql profile --draft for drafted descriptions, which are filed for review, and nl2sql index --refresh after a glossary change.
  • engine.index.inspect() requires user_context (#348), and shows only the entries that caller's scope reaches. The playground's /api/retrieval takes a role. What to do: pass the caller's UserContext.
  • Store interface version 3 (#329). StateStore gains five proposal methods. What to do: third-party state stores add them and set interface_version = 3.
  • A new QueryResult.status, needs_clarification (#339), and a new error code, COST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED (#342). What to do: handle both. nl2sql run exits 4 when it needs a choice and has no terminal.

docs.title: What's next
docs.text:
Next: 0.9, Wave C: conversations, chat tools, charts, dashboards, the launchpad, and MCP over HTTP with API keys.

Full changelog: v0.7.0...v0.8.0

docs.title: Schema Drift
docs.text:
A database changes after it is indexed: a column is added, a table dropped, a type widened. The engine keeps answering from the schema its build was made from until the next nl2sql index. Schema drift is measured, not acted on: nothing here re-indexes, schedules a build or changes what a question reads. You decide when to rebuild.

There are two measures:

  • A check: the live database against its live build, now (engine.index.check(), nl2sql index --check).
  • The stored diffs: what each build changed against the one it replaced (engine.index.versions(), engine.index.diff()).

docs.title: The check
docs.text:
nl2sql index --check                  # every datasource
nl2sql index --check -d shop --json   # one, as JSON

For each datasource it reflects the live database with the datasource's index scope and no profiling (only the catalog is read), and compares its structural fingerprint with the fingerprint of the snapshot the live build was made from. It writes nothing.

Exit code Meaning 0 Nothing drifted (a datasource never indexed is reported and does not change the code) 1 At least one datasource drifted 2 At least one check failed (the database could not be read, or the config did not load), or nothing was checked (no datasource is configured, or the role reaches none); wins over 1

So a cron job or a CI step can act on it. --role (repeatable, default admin, as nl2sql run) is the role the check runs as; drift shows only in the tables it may read. A role that reaches no datasource checks nothing and exits 2, so a gate never passes on a check that did not run. --json prints the reports.

From code:

from nl2sql import UserContext

for report in engine.index.check(user_context=UserContext(roles=["admin"])):
    print(report.datasource_id, report.status)
    if report.status == "drifted":
        print(report.diff.counts(), report.impact)

Each DriftReport has:

Field Meaning datasource_id The datasource status unchanged, drifted, not_indexed (no build yet) or failed live_version The live build's schema_version checked_at When (UTC) diff With drifted: a SchemaDiff from the live build (from_version) to the live database (to_version is None) impact With drifted: what the diff breaks (below) error With failed: why, redacted (a password in a connection string never shows)

docs.title: The diff
docs.text:
SchemaDiff (nl2sql_sdk.schema, also exported from nl2sql) compares exactly what the fingerprint covers:

Field Meaning tables_added, tables_dropped TableRefs. A table added or dropped is listed once, without its columns columns_added, columns_dropped ColumnRefs, in tables on both sides columns_changed ColumnChange: table, column, changes such as {"type": ["INTEGER", "BIGINT"]}; the keys are type, nullable and pk foreign_keys_added, foreign_keys_dropped ForeignKeyRef: table, columns, referred_table, referred_columns engine_type (old, new) when the datasource's engine type changed (its type), else None

diff.counts() is the number of each, and diff.is_empty() is true exactly when the two fingerprints are equal. Statistics, descriptions and sample values are not structure: a build whose statistics alone changed has no diff.

A rename is a drop and an add. Nothing can tell a renamed column from a dropped one and a new one without asking someone, so the diff does not guess.

docs.title: Stored diffs
docs.text:
When a build's new snapshot differs in structure from the version it replaces, the diff between them is stored beside the new version in the state store (see Schema Store) and schema.drifted is published with detected_by: "build". It is pruned with its snapshot.

Method Returns engine.index.versions(datasource_id, *, user_context) Each stored version, newest first: schema_version, fingerprint (of the schema as the caller may see it), live, has_diff engine.index.diff(datasource_id, schema_version=None, *, user_context) The diff that introduced the version (the live one by default), or None

Reading these is the measurement: how often a datasource's structure changes between builds, and how far the live database is from the build at a check.

docs.title: Impact
docs.text:
A drifted report's impact (DriftImpact) lists what the diff breaks, from data the engine already has:

Field What verified_queries Each verified query (datasource_id, query_id, reasons) whose SQL reads a dropped table, a dropped column, or a column whose type changed. A column is matched by its table (its qualifier's alias, or the only table read); an unqualified column in a query of several tables is reported as one it may read policy_rules Each role's allow or deny pattern (role, kind, pattern) that matched a dropped table and now matches nothing preferred_tables The datasource's preferred_tables that were dropped glossary_items Each glossary item (tables.orders, columns.orders.note, terms.revenue, rules.pay_private, joins.a.id->b.id) that named a dropped table or column, of those the caller may see

The plan cache needs no entry: it is keyed on the schema version, so a rebuild already makes its old plans unreachable.

docs.title: Who sees what
docs.text:
user_context is required on all three methods. A caller sees drift only in the tables its scope may read:

  • A table its roles deny is left out of the diff, and so is a foreign key that refers to one; the impact is computed from what is left, against the tables it may read.
  • The fingerprint versions() shows is of the schema without the denied tables, so a change only to a denied table looks like a statistics-only rebuild.
  • Drift only in denied tables is unchanged for that caller, and such a stored diff reads as None (has_diff false).
  • A datasource it cannot reach is left out of check(); named, it is a ValueError worded exactly like an unknown datasource.

schema.drifted is an operator event: it is on the engine's bus (engine.events.subscribe) and in the audit log, never on a caller's stream_query. It carries the versions and the whole diff's counts, and no table names. A check publishes a drift once: while the same drift of the same build stays, later checks (by any caller) publish nothing, so a check every few minutes writes one audit line per change. This is remembered in memory per engine, so a new process publishes it once more. A build publishes each diff it stores. See Events.
